comment: Everything revolved around 3 tests. Loved the structure, but didn't like when the tests were harder than any of the work we did before. Everything can be done online, and all from the textbook, word for word. He has a lot of passion for his field, I just don't think a blanket intro class is where he thrives.

Dr seplaki is amazing and so passionate about public health. Lectures are CRUCIAL to attend if you want to succeed since the class is graded by two tests and a few low weighted homework assignments. Two exams make up 70% of your grade, so it's really hard to get a good grade if you don't do well on the exams. Lectures are pretty boring and not really anything new if you've taken PH classes before. Tests aren't super difficult, but hard to study for because questions are a little random and tricky. HW is long but easy and graded easily.

Once in a while, we had an interesting lecture. But overall, the lectures were boring, and the test questions were unfair. He asks very specific questions about a quote that a guest lecturer had on their slides. He also gives very time-consuming assignments that require us to write several paragraphs, and we usually only get five points for them.

HWs are stupid easy, tests are specific and difficult. He provides no materials to study, is barely at lecture at all because of guest lecturers. Course policies are insane, 89.99% gets rounded down. Late HW by 1 min is 0. Only way to get an extentino is providing DOCUMENTED proof of an illness or family emergency. Overall, very unpleasant class.

grading system = absurd. Students can only get 100 points TOTAL in the class: 2 exams 40 points each and 4 homework assignments 5 points each. Leplaki

He literally is the least flexible professor I have ever had at the UofR. He gives no feedback on his grading and does not allow any extra credit or help. He didn't even show up for like 4 weeks because there were guest lecturers. Unfortunately, this class is required for public health majors but take it with caution.

He is very clear about grading policies from the start, and encourages lots of questions regarding class guidelines. I took 102 online and I think the open note and open book policies during tests were great, I recommend watching the lectures too b/c 70-80% of exams are based on lecture material (including guest lectures!). Overall, pretty easy.

I wasn't a fan of her teaching style (not sure if it's the blackboard or the way she explains things), but she's very nice. She provided an online link to the textbook, but reading isn't mandatory. The point system allows you to pick and choose what assignments you want to do. Practice exams are very similar to real exams.

She is truly an amazing person. Although people think freshmen orgo is hard, it's very easy to get an A becuase of the point system. the class is interesting and the workshops are great. She's very empathetic and helpful.

Very good lectures and was willing to help outside of class. Problem Sets and Midterm practice tests were very helpful. Tests were hard, but the class is graded on a points system, so getting a good grade isn't that difficult. She really emphasizes fundamentals instead of mechanism memorization, and she is an overall caring person and great teacher

Great person but not great at teaching. Class is a points system, making it easier to get a good overall grade in the class. Every assignment is optional and basically graded on participation. Lectures are confusing and I only learned the material by reading the textbook and watching videos on my own. Be prepared to do a lot of self learning.

While many don't love her lecture style, I was a fan. Orgo can be hard, but thanks to her giving more points available than possible (ie 625 points out of 500 total) it will not tank my grade. In addition when I came to her about being unsure where I'm missing understanding she offered to review my exams personally and give me feedback.

Dr Jacobs was always very helpful and always able to be reached. There were 3 main coding homeworks which were not too bad if you give time to work through them and 2 multiple choice exams which weren't the worst. Overall I would definitely take this class again, as well as any other classes he teaches.

Dr. Jacobs is very nice and passionate about the material. Perception and cognitive modeling are his field so he is very knowledgeable in the field. No tests, 6 coding homeworks, and short final paper. Perfect class if you don't want to stress about exams and don't mind coding.

This course is Prof. Jacobs specialty. If you are interested in computational methods and Bayesianism, take this from him. All the readings are recent publications in the field so it's a great way to get exposed to the research going on. There are no exams, just some tricky homework coding assignments and a final essay.

Professor Jacobs is really interested in the subject and you can tell he's just a big nerd about the material. There is a lot of readings to do, but the lectures cover a lot of the readings. There are no exams, but the homeworks can be quite difficult. I think his lectures are fairly interesting, but sometimes they are heavy on the math.
Helpful and competent, but unfortunately a very dry lecturer and confusing test-writer.

So amazingly boring. If you need to take this class do not take it with him as a professor. The only grades are all multiple choice tests-all of which are super confusing. He is also confusing during class. The only reason to truly go to class is for the review questions.

Boring boring boring. Probably can do without attending the lectures. The things that he says are often confusing. The review sessions were helpful though and he often told you things to focus on while studying at them.

He's a wonderful professor! Very clear in what he expects of you. His exam questions all come directly from lectures, there is no textbook. He is so helpful during office hours, and the class before a midterm is always a review session. Great professor! Midterms are fairly easy if you study, the material is interesting/ fun to study.

Really clear and used great examples to relate the material to every day things. Also, extremely nice and kind to students. Tests are difficult, but he normalizes grades, so all you have to do is score higher than average (average is usually ~70%), and you'll get a good grade! Also, no textbook and no hw. No outside work... just learn the material.

HORRIBLE! Just reads from Powerpoints which are full of jargon and don't clarify anything. He might add an example here or there, but it's usually vague and doesn't help. The teacher no longer uses a real textbook - instead, articles from various books accompany the powerpoints. He isn't a great professor, but he isn't horrible, either.

Prof Bernal was really great. He prepared for lectures well and poured a lot of effort into preparing slides and code for lecture. Do not take this class. He is not even a professor. Worst course ever! Grading is very subjective. he is busy with rationalizing the grading. Prof. Pye is genuinely such a nice guy. The biggest thing is he gives exams every 2-3 weeks which can be a pain. There's a lot of work for Spanish 101 but I learned a LOT. No final and its a fairly easy class if you stay on top of the work.

The lectures for BUS118 are pretty chill. Professor is also a very nice person and classes tend to be interactive. He grades the homework and exams VERY generously. I loved this man's lectures. He was slightly unorganized at times, and had a habit of going on tangents unrelated to the class, but his lectures were still easy to understand, and that's how my brain works. He was very willing to help students outside of class times and very approachable.

This class is an easy A; he goes over the exact questions that will be on the final (take-home), so it's stress-free and you can just learn for fun.

Professor Abramson is fine. His lectures can be rather boring but they're fairly straightforward. The problem sets were confusing but the final wasn't bad. As long as you look at the slides (which he usually posts before lectures) and do the readings you'll do just fine.

A good professor. Disorganized at times, but very passionate for his subject matter, and a very fair grader. He is very kind, and if you go to his office hours, you will do well. Dr. Basu is a VERY intelligent person. Of course you will read alot on your own. Read the chapter before coming to class. The tests are easy if you study. TA's do EVERYTHING! they take the test and make the key, so hope it matches theirs. prepare for long nights in lab and hours studying. HE LOVES CHARTS! MUST MEMO

Dr. Basu is a very interesting lecturer, passionate about his subuject. However he is a little disorganized in his lecture style. Overall enjoyed the class.

Absolutely terrible! relies so heavily on technical jargon, its easy to get confused. Not clear about expectations for exams. Will take points off if your answer is not framed exactly the way he wants it, even though the questions are broad/vague. Class average was at a 60% immediately before the final. Worst professor I've ever had!

Extremely knowledgeable instructor. Intimidating at first, but really a nice and caring person if you get to know him. The material is memorization heavy, so be prepared to study. But it is very interesting. And always ask questions in class.

his enthusiasm and clear teaching method make the class better :D I really enjoy his math jokes
He made math entertaining. Super funny guy in like an awkward way. Highly recommend

His enthusiasm makes the class better, This is a hard class but he is extremely accessible outside of class. He will give you hints for the problems and not just straightly tell you the answers, which is great! It's a pity he had a haircut though.

This was Carney's first semester teaching and overall did a good job. Very helpful and wanted you to know the material. -danc 202- Very caring professor, expectations are clear and homework is graded mainly on completion. Show a little bit of thoughtfulness/care while you are in her class and you will do well.

I looooooove Mariah! She's really nice and she always encourages us to share our ideas. Though there were various tasks, they weren't hard, and Mariah gives us chance to earn credits back. Ok so I can't say what class it is because it will just give away who I am but i sincerely wish I read all of these comments before. She is the reason why I've been so miserable this semester. Very friendly and enjoyable to talk to. Very helpful one on one, a bit confusing with the organization of lecture notes. Good jokes.

He is really easy.  Really nice guy.  He will help you all the way through the class. Not a ton of work. Slides posted online.  Kinda boring at times, but it's a good A.

The book is helpful for the first half of the class! The second half you have to read his lecture notes and go to class. The professor himself is not really interesting or exciting at all. My Dutch GOAT! Love him!

comment: One of the best teachers I have had in my life. The class is more difficult than other mechanics courses I have taken however, his is by far the most helpful and comprehensive. Very very good Professor, helped me a lot.

You should definitely not take PHYS141 if you don't have previous physics experience. Amazing. He doesn't waste time in trivialities and obvious physics (good!). Provides derivations for theorems that were just accepted in previous physics courses. Very funny; free pack of sparkling water per person every course. Lab reports are fair (8-10 pages), exam questions parallel recitation/homework problems. Always willing to help.

"Class average was 50" 

If this reviewer had went to recitations, they would've been fine. The test was very easy, don't let them scare you.

comment: 50.8 average score on the midterm... Good luck taking his class

The professor is a good man. But the course is extremely difficult. His PowerPoint don't help usually and you need to figure
something out by yourself. The lab sucks most. You need to write a 10 pages long lab report each time. The homework is very tough and usually covers things not

His Labs are the worst. There are much better introductory physics textbooks out there like Young&Freedman, Serway & Jewett, Giancoli , Resnick & Halliday, so many more. Somewhat intimidating, but a good teacher if you put in the effort. 237 is, in principle, a difficult course, but it is easy to do well. His expectations are very clear for exams. Helpful, but can be intimidating. High expectations, but will help you meet them. Labs are very important to your grade.
Very challenging class, but he really helped make it possible to succeed.  HW was near impossible, but he will help. He is nice and a great lecturer.
Fun class, fun guy. Perfect science course for non-science majors.

Had him for astronomy, awesome teacher. Great sense of humor and really cares about his students. Takes time to think about and answer the questions posed to him. An extremely organized and thoughtful man, always planning ahead. Very patient as well. Dope accent.

Professor Wolfs is one of the best teachers I have ever had. He truly cares about every one of his students and everything in his class is geared towards their success. The subject material is hard at times but he presents it in a clear, organized way and is always willing to help.

Brilliant professor and truly the best kind; He expects a lot from his students and does everything he can in his power to get you there. Go to his office hours and USE THE TEXTBOOK! He pulls problems from the textbook for exams and if you can do them on your own you can knock them out of the park test day. One of the best teachers I've ever had.

Prof. Wolfs definitely knows his stuff, and makes himself very available for extra help. He rode around in a fire extinguisher powered wheelchair, if that doesn't want to make you a physicist, you should gain knowledge.
He's tough, but he knows this and adjusts his grades accordingly.

Wolfs is an excellent professor. Some comments on this website are too harsh. It is true that powerpoint is his mode of teaching but all of his lectures are online. He really makes this a fun class. Fantastic Professor, one of the best I have had yet at U of R (I'm in my 3rd semester now)

Great guy, homework and tests can be long or difficult but overall a great class and professor. Very organized and concerned for his students.

Uses Powerpoint religiously, and can be difficult to understand due to his accent.  However, he is a fair grader and teaches well.  Makes physics students right up their labs rather than doing cookie-cutter "do the lab, write data down, answer a question" format.
Very tough class but extremely nice professor.  Very will to help and seems to genuinely care about his students.  Does fun demonstrations in lecture.  Good sense of humor and sweet accent.

He has a tendency to repeat things when he speaks, but his attitude towards teaching is great. The tests are nice and challenging, but it's relatively easy to get an A, even if you mess up a problem. An 80's an A.

Very tough teacher but he is a great guy. If you go in to ask for help he definitely will help you. Very encouraging and never acts like your questions are too stupid to answer. Just be ready to work your butt off!!!

He is serious in trying to teach basic physics and will have great classroom demonstrations. He is a fun professor but his heavy accent may discourage some to go to lectures. Whatever you get out of Reichman's class is proportional to the amount of work you put into his class. Lectures cover engaging material, there are weekly group discussions if that's more of your thing + there's room for extra credit even if the exams and paper are very fairly graded. Reichman is relatable and interesting. The material for the class was applicable and the books were worth reading. He is a pretty hard grader though. Very hard to get an A.

Professor is really nice and understanding. Make sure you don't fall behind bc the material piles up real quick.

lovely man. subject is tough if you don't like circuits and if you're a bad test taker. he is really willing to help students out and genuinely cares about students success -- great professor overall.
He explains material well and his class is really interesting. Hes my favorite professor here at U of R! Big recommend.

Very good class. BME 210 is great for biomedical engineers. The course is rock solid, prepare to learn a lot of things. Lalor is great at teaching and a very chill dude. Pretty chill professor and always available for help. DON'T SKIP CLASS. Before exams, do as many book questions as you can then do more.
Prof Lalor is great. A good communicator and very responsive to questions and requests for help. Cares a lot about the students.

John Nichol(s Wilder) is god's gift to 123. Couldn't have taught it better myself.

Professor Nichol's PHYS 246 was definitely one of the top three physics classes I have ever taken in college. PHYS 246 was challenging. Prof. Nichol explains things so well for quantum theory (PHYS 246). He's not a good professor; he really doesn't know how to teach. The one redeeming thing about him is that if you talk to him outside of class, you'll see that he's super nice and wants you to know the material. He just can't teach it.

Professor Nichol does not care for teaching this class well nor does he care about his students doing well and understanding the material. comment: The lectures were mundane and the class itself lacks enough information to be interesting - it's literally too easy. Taking it felt like a chore.

Professor Yang gives fun, interesting lectures if you enjoy the subject material. Your grade is determined by quizzes, discussions, and homework, and the quizzes/tests are not difficult if you review the lecture slides. Lectures are also recorded. Yang gives a good amount extra credit near the end of the semester too. I enjoyed the class.

He is very nice, but he is also incredibly boring. The lectures are hard to pay attention to, given his monotone voice and the pacing of the material. The class is in a large space and he has a microphone, however it doesn't really work. He also has a lot of memes on his slides. Genuinely such a sweet guy tho.

Dr. Martin Yang might seem a little monotone at first, but his dry humor is actually so good. On Black Friday, he posted a “Black Friday Deals” and gave a bunch of extra credit. Absolute angel. If you actually study, the exams are not tricky at all. One word of advice; this class is lecture heavy. Make sure you understand everything on the slides.

Extremely knowledgable professor who is great at breaking down complicated theories into more digestible concepts. He records his lectures which is extremely helpful. One of my favorite professors here-- encouraged me to pursue a minor in BCSC

While he is a very nice professor, he is probably the most difficult professor to understand. He teaches in a large lecture hall, and has his microphone volume very low. He also has a very thick accent with not great pronunciation, so when he discusses more in-depth topics with complicated(ish) vocab, it gets really muddled.

Dr Yang is a well-versed and dynamic researcher, as well as a caring and proficient teacher. He is excited about the material and is approachable. Class expectations are clear and fair. I knew I could go to him during office hours with any questions. He has been my favorite during my university experience.

Seems like it will be a demanding class but it's very manageable. The big assignment is broken down into components over the semester. Small assignments throughout. 3 quizzes you will do well on if you just listen in class. The lab assignments are very easy if you just follow what he does in class. Dr. Yang is very available for extra help.
dreaded this class, by far the most MUNDANE prof at uofr. never take this prof again

Prof Yang is so very sweet and reaches out if he sees you are struggling. However, his lectures are a snooze fest- he speaks very quietly and he puts a lot of memes on the slides but then doesn't explain the actual concepts very well. From a learning perspective, it's frustrating. This is a class that you pretty much need to teach yourself.
great prof ever!

Very caring professor. He was clearly willing to assist me when I asked him for help and responded email quickly. Also, there were multiple opportunities (Optional Quiz/Discussion + Extra Credit) to help us make up for our mistake. I enjoyed this course and was glad to be in his class in my 1st year. Looking forward to having him again in BCS152.

Martin explains things clearly and there's lots of opportunities to do well. Quizzes, homework, midterm + final, and discussions. Well balanced and easy to do well, the only reason I got a B was because the topic of the class was boring to me and I wasn't motivated, but I wouldn't say this class was hard.

Dr. Yang is a really nice and caring professor. I appreciate how he grades us by more than just quizzes/exams; homework is 25% and there's a redo quiz. However, his lectures aren't great. It is hard to understand him from a language prospective and he explains the content terribly. The basics are even unclear. It's too bad, as he's a great guy.

great guy but an average professor at best. lectures have slideshows with 50-60 slides and he does not explain very well. quizzes aren't too bad but you need to teach yourself everything, going to lecture does not help that much
One of the sweetest profs ever, brought candy to class a few times, tried to keep lecture entertaining      -not always succeeding though-, still one of my favorites
Dr. Yang is so cute. I want to put him in my pocket. Chill class.

Super clear about what you need to do well in the class! Lectures are informative and to the point + recorded. Genuinely a good guy who wants you to do well. Decent amount of assignments (HW + discussion posts) but boost your grade. Wish he taught more classes!
A bit quiet but lectures are interesting and informative overall!

If you're looking for an easy class, take one with Professor Yang. If you're looking to actually be challenged and learn, find a different professor. He's a nice guy, but his lectures are super boring - he basically regurgitates the textbook - and the exams are silly. They are all multiple choice but super specific and full of grammar mistakes.

Yang is very easy. Tests and quizzes are multiple choice, lowest quiz score gets dropped. Lectures are a little boring but they are all recorded. I will say that the only downside of the recordings is that it's hard to see things he directly references on slides. Not many people attend lecture, so if you go consistently he will recognize you.

Although his lectures can be boring, he is a very caring professor that has a passion for what he teaches. I loved taking courses with him because his structure was always straight-forward. Also, he records lectures, which makes it easier if you need to miss a class.

Really sweet professor. Lectures may be boring but quizzes and exams are very doable (you still need put in the effort and study). Not the best office hours because it's 1 on 1 and there is usually a really long line with people just hogging and taking 20 minutes of his time. Multiple choice tests, content on the slides. lectures are recorded.

Great guy, super nice. Low maintenance class. Gives quizzes that are supposed to help boost your grade. A lot content to remember for the 2 exams but not difficult. Gives easy hw to help boost grade as well. Personally didn't find the course content as interesting, but people who like linguistics like this course. Love Dr. Yang.

He clearly wants everyone to succeed in this course. He gave optional quiz, optional discussion and extra credit to help us get higher grade. Lecture is a little bit boring but very clear. If you miss classes, you can still know what the contents are by watching recordings which is useful for both learning new things and reviewing.
Very hard to understand (spoken and written language), predictable with all class criteria (BCS 111 compared to 152), easy points for HWs and Discussions

Super nice guy. Also took his 111 class. He can be a bit dry and boring, but if you just pay attention to the lectures and have a reasonable understanding of what is going on, his classes should be an easy A. Tests are easy and his "participation" points just involve writing your thoughts on a certain topic.

Martin was an great professor. This was my second class with him and I enjoyed both of them. His exams and quizzes require you to know specific examples from his lectures so make sure to go to class. Some questions can get challenging so make sure to look over your notes. Very accommodating and offered extra credit to boost your grade.

Oh Martin...

I have had this man for 3 classes now, and can't even begin to describe him. He's such a sweet man and genuinely cares about his students. However, so boring. So so boring. BUT, once you figure out his classes it is easy enough to do well in them. Martin truly is the BCS department here, so just get used to him. 

Live love martin

Dr.Yang is super nice, and very helpful. I've been in 2 of his courses (111 and 152) and is now in BCSC153. I'm very glad that so many of my courses are teached by him. He is creative and leads us to think and discuss on class. Provides clear recordings and crateria of exams. Likes him a lot!

Dr. Yang is one of the nicest professors at UofR. He is a very caring man and he'll often wave to you on campus or in the dining halls. The class material is easy and as long as you attend lectures and read the textbook, the class should be an easy A. He also gives optional quizzes and extra credit.

Martin is a really great professor, and super nice and funny during lectures. All the quizzes and midterms are multiple choice, and the final wasn't cumulative. He really knows the subject and breaks it down so that everyone can easily understand. The homework was also very easy. I highly recommend his classes!

I absolutely love Dr Yang. His grading system is one of the better ones I have seen. He offered a bonus quiz to have our lowest quiz grade replaced which he did in my class last year as well. He also added some extra credit if you submitted discussions early. Sometimes I take the silver line with him (he parks down there & I live in southside) :)
If you're struggling with a topic, Dr. Yang will make time to help you outside of class. His quizzes are fairly easy because everything is mentioned in the lectures.

The class is so much smoother compared to 110. The content is digestible and you can almost always see how they relate to each other. The homeworks (which are just experiments to do on your friends) are always fun and an easy way to get an A.

Nice and approachable. Reply email quickly even at midnight! Very generous with HW extensions! Give information about career paths or research opportunities in certain lectures. His wording on the slides may be confusing, but if you go ask him he will clarify or paraphrase! Exams are MCQ or T/F questions, revise the notes and you'll be fine.
Very nice professor.

Never went to class and studied strictly from the textbook and slides. It probably would have been more helpful if I studied before class to solidify material, but I have a learning disability so I struggled with paying attention during his lecture (it was very boring for me so I struggled to follow along) but the material itself was interesting.
This was my second class with Martin. He's a very nice man but his tests are nothing like his lectures are difficult to understand.

Martin is one of those professors that, at the beginning of the course, seems kind of boring, but he has this sort of dry humor that makes the class really enjoyable. All of the homework assignments and discussion assignments were easy points, but midterm and final were a bit difficult. Depending on how well the class does, he will scale the exam.
The midterm and final are pretty easy, the quizzes are a lot harder! The class is pretty easy but definitely boring. Dr. Yang is really accommodating and understanding!

Dr. Yang is EXTREMELY understanding of extenuating circumstances. He became one of my favorite professors and really pushed me to continue BCS. I loved this professor and you can tell he cares for his students. He checks up on those who fall behind or have failed a quiz. He holds office hours and the TA's in this class are super nice. Study and look over lectures to do well on his exams and quizzes. Understanding the concepts is important. Sit in the front because he can be hard to hear.
This class isn't too difficult as long as you review the slides before the quizzes. I took 3 BCS classes with Yang for my cluster and found him to be fair and consistent with grading.

Prof Yang's lectures are generally pretty engaging! He cares about how successful students are and is flexible in terms of quiz or exam make-ups. The homework's were very clear and pretty easy. Quizzes and tests are all multiple choice (at least for BCS152) - tests are important for your grade, but as long as you pay attention in class you're fine

Professor Yang is one of the kindest and most caring professors here. He really cares that you learn the material and there's a strong initiative seen from him. He's passionate about his subject and makes the lectures a little humorous and interactive. Absolutely recommend him.
Enjoyable lectures. It should be an easy-A- class as long as you don't miss homework like me (6.5% each!)

This is my 5th class with Dr. Yang, super awesome instructor! I had office hours with him to discuss about applying for grad school and about my participation in class. He was always helpful, super flexible during COVID, and gave us make up opportunities/extra credit. BCS 261 is a seminar based class, so readings and discussions are a must.

Martin Yang is an amazing professor who gives awesome lectures. The scores are determined basically by quizzes and exams. There will be study guides provided before each exam that would be extremely helpful.
Nice professor, he is funny and try to make the class engage. Had him for BCS111 and 153, will sign up for his experiment class

Dr Yang is a very nice professor and cares about his students. I took BCS 153 with him in person and BCS 152 with him online. He wants his students to do well and always makes time for their questions and sometimes offers easy extra credit. Overall good guy

comment: This was my second course with Kegl and she's become one of my favorite professors. She makes even the driest material entertaining with her easy-going personality. Participation is important and she gives awesome feedback on essays. Lectures are always interesting.

Prof Kegl managed to make an interesting subject, Shakespeare, incredibly tedious. Her class was also lecture style, which I found to be a poor choice for an English class. Attendance and turning in papers on time is a must.

Professor Kegl is a very fair, honest, grader. Was consistently late to class and often was late on giving us an assignment. I could tell she was passionate about Shakespeare, but her lectures were thoroughly unengaging - if not for mandatory attendance, I probably would have never come to class.
Really knowledgeable, really nice. Sometimes got off topic, but usually not too bad. Just repeat back what she says in class in your papers and you'll do great!
Definately fell asleep during many of her classes. She knows her stuff and is passionate about it. Might wanna look into someone else to teach Shakespeare though.

"Meh" is the best expression to describe Kegl. She's clearly passionate about her work, but the material was just a hair away from being painfully basic (even for an intro class). I had Prof. Kegl for many classes, and her courses always held my interest. She was especially helpful to me during a thesis paper. I always found her comments on papers especially helpful, and she was always willing to meet with students.

A very unhelpful and mean woman. Unable to meet students needs. Grades tough and often arbitrarily. Recommend avoiding.

He's a very detailed professor. He teaches every step of Python, which has definitely helped me build a strong foundational understanding of the language.He also focuses on using real-life examples, which makes the lectures not boring at all. I attend all of his lectures because he's such a great professor. Highly recommend taking his class.
Terrible decision to use paper exam for a coding class. As with any professor that do exams for coding, does not understand that coding is a language and how to teach coding effectively.

He taught introductory programming extremely well. His lectures were very clear and organized, and had lots of examples. He made class super fun and easy. I still program a lot today and he set a very strong foundation.
He is a nice person but the class is difficult and the grading is not clear
Very approachable and a nice professor. Explain things in an elegant and concise manner. Would take again.

The course is difficult, the readings are not easy to understand. But prof weslake is a very nice person, very friendly and approachable. The workload also is okay.Come to his office hours if you have any questions, communicate more and you should be fine
Very strict grading, unclear grading criteria.
Took his Global perspective on society at NYU Shanghai. Prof. Weslake is nice and approachable. The ideas in his lecture are thought-provoking, but are not that easy to understand.

I have taken a LOT of philosophy classes and Brad is probably the best professor I've had in any of them. awesome proff!! reason why I am a Philosophy major!

Stunningly boring, but she's clearly knowledgeable on the subject matter, which is a shame considering her teaching style is about at interesting as watching paint dry. Probably good idea to go to class--I did--but you can just as easily learn the philosophy from the internet with ease.

She's enthusiastic but her teaching style (direct from overheads) can be dull at times.  I found that the individual tests are graded somewhat harshly but she was forgiving in the overall course grade.

She is the most boring professor ever. You'll hate going to class, but you have to or you won't be prepared for the tests. She knows her stuff, but it was painful being in her class due to how she lectures.
Ancient Philosophy is really boring but she is really nice and does her best to get discussions going. very nice, helpful and understanding.
Clear, understandable, and overall just a good professor.

i love how he does a bonus program at the end of the course so you can give your grade an extra boost. i dont love how the exams were tough, this is universally one of the most difficult undergraduate finance courses so keep that in mind.
Take this course
I don't think he explained stuff very well and most of time I just google and ask GPT. Tests are easy

Incredibly boring professor who rambles during lectures and it's honestly a waste of time to go. 5 assignments total, one due every few weeks or so (takes the best 4/5 for hw grade). His exams are just like practice exams, and he even takes questions from them.

While it is incredibly difficult to listen to this professor for more than a few minutes at a time, the material is important, and he makes it somewhat relevant. His lectures are so boring, Mohr does not care about the material he is teaching! I wish I took this course with a different professor. DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASSES WITH HIM!

Lectures are boring, and questions on tests/homework are often hard to read. He does less teaching and more of expecting you to know the material. Most lectures are not worth going to. The only important parts are when he gives you excel formulas.

there is no clear grading rubric for homeworks, he does give you 2 extra credit opportunities, he doesnt teach from the slides, he basically doesnt use them at all, he talks as he goes. hes pretty boring and attendance isnt mandatory so you can watch the recordings on 2x speed. if you can, dont take him, if you have to, youll be fine

Professor Mohr clearly wants students to do well in his class, by giving plenty of extra credit and fairly straightforward assignments, but it is hard to stay engaged in his lectures. Literally the worst professor at the business department. if the class is offered with anyone else - take it with them. He is simply not a good lecturer, gets lost in his words, makes finance an even drier subject than it needs to be. He schedules exams right after fall break and thanksgiving, so you can't spend time with your family. Beware!!!!!!!

Not a good professor, doesn't really teach much, but not terrible. Gives lots of practice tests so you just have to master those and you'll do well on exams. His lectures are do droney and he hardly gets through any important material per class. gets distracted easily. will spend all class on yahoo finance rather than teaching us the material. he skips around slides and is not organized.

Super boring during class. Don't even bother going to his class because you won't learn anything. Ridiculous professor

I don't know whether Derek Mohr really cares about his students. I makes tons of mistakes on both slides and handouts. Most of his class time would go off topic. There is no way to learn something during his office hour since he always skips it.

His way of teaching is pointless. It's hard to keep notes because he always jumps in between slideshows. He claims there are problems with them so he would not teach in sequence but a comment in 2019 stated the same exact thing: he knows and never fixes these issues. great professor
He is a really nice person who provides sufficient materials for students to prepare for the exams. Extra credits also provided.
Great Professor, very fair grading and lectures are clear and interesting.

There are other professors at UR teaching fin213. If you really want to lay a solid foundation with the corporate finance material, don't choose his class. Derek doesn't respond to email, and yes, he neither appear in his office hour in most cases. Tests are fair, 65% related to homework and past exam, 15% lecture content, 20% from nowhere

I don't know why his rating is such high. I took the course this year, and he is one of the most irresponsible professors I ever had. He never replied to the email and he never appeared during his office hour. The tests are extremely hard and the contents are totally unrelated to his lectures.
Tests are usually very fair and not really difficult

Great professor! Really cares about his students. Sure the lectures can be boring at times but hes very knowledgeable about finance and often talks about finance in the current news. His grading is very lenient and offers extra credit. Will take him again!
You will learn everything by searching investopedia. His lectures are boring and won't help you do well on the homework or exams. The textbook is confusing and doesn't help too.
Best prof ever, loved lecture
Best professor ever. Could listen to him all day. Very organised, respectful and educated. Every student loves him. Amazing slides and best lectures ever.

Curves exams. generous Extra Credit.

This professor frequently will read off slides ( he uses the ones provided by the book) and every class he says there's issues with the slides but after years of teaching it seems like he doesn't care enough up to update them. I found him unclear and very difficult to reach. It seems like he just doesn't care.
Professor Mohr is hands down the best professor that I've had at the University of Rochester since coming here. He's respected by his students and deserves to be recognized for his work.
Easy class, clear expectations

Perhaps one of the best professors you will ever come across. Focuses on learning and scoring a great grade (which you can easily manage if you follow instructions). Super easy-going and friendly, he welcomes seeking help/discussing ideas beyond the classroom. I also highly recommend taking the course as it is extremely interesting and unique.

I was in 181 (not listed). Probably the best math professor I've had, he's caring, gave very helpful examples, helped us through homework problems and gave enthusiastic explanations of mathematical principles. He also made himself very available outside of class. I'm sad to see him have to leave, I hope he comes back to RIT to teach in the future.
Shashank is the best professor I've had. He was always available to meet outside of class and help with practice problems. The lectures were very clear and he demonstrated a lot of practice problems.

I got an A in this class but only bc he MAAD curved our grades at the end of the course. he seems to care for his students but mans just did NOT convey the subject material well. I don't think I learned enough in this course as I should've but it's his first semester at RIT so I can forgive some of the stuff? just don't take him for multivar/vect

Professor Chorge was really helpful in me understanding and learning calculus for the first time. His lectures are not bad if you pay attention and follow his work. He is a little unorganized when he works out a problem but he explains everything clear. He was one of my favorite instructors I had this semester and I recommend him to anyone.

In this class I ended up having to teach myself most of the material. I got little to no feedback from him on exams or quizzes.

Chorge is very nice, but  I would not recommend this taking this class.

Can be a little hard to understand, but is fun if you get to know him. Homework every class but it takes 5 minuets to do and is graded on completion. If you show up and pay attention in class its a easy A or B
He wasn't the best but was by no means the worst. Just wanted his students to do their best and made himself super available in order to help!
I don't understand why this professor rated so low, but he is the best professor I have ever met in the university. He answers every question thoroughly, and I can understand his lecture.

Professor Gresens is one of the nicest professors I've ever met. If you show interest in the material he will bend over backwards to help you and support you. He is also just a great person who you can trust with personal information and life advice. Amazing professor.

Best professor I've ever had. Funny, engaging, extremely knowledgeable, genuinely passionate. The only time I've ever seen a professor's eyes literally light up when I asked a good question. Accessible and cares about students. Lots of reading but you don't really have to do it, fair grader but you do have to try to do well.
Honestly, I am inept and do not understand Greek, but Professor Gresens has been understanding from the beginning and has pushed me to do better but is extremely gentle
Just a good professor and a good guy. He expects a lot but is available for help. My favorite prof so far.

He's probably the best professor I've ever had. He's so understanding and genuinely wants the students to succeed. He's incredibly helpful and that's made it so I've done better in this class than any other language classes I've taken

He's my favorite professor I've ever had. He's made it so that I want to learn the language for the language itself rather than wanting to learn it just so I could read things. He's also incredibly kind and understanding. Attendance wasn't mandatory but I know I wouldn't be able to pass the class if I didn't actually go to class

I usually HATE language classes but his Classical Greek class was awesome! I did better in that class than I've ever done in a language class because he made things actually make sense. He's also really understanding and just generally great overall
Prof G is the best! Lectures are super fun and casual, and he really cares about both students and the material. Lots of interesting and relevant tangents.

This class comes with a lot of work --hw assignments due every class, vocab every week, with 2 mini quizzes but all are necessary to keep up with learning Latin and are definitely manageable! Gresens is a very nice, caring and understanding professor and I am definitely taking more courses with him :)
Professor G is really nice, and he won't call on you in class if you don't raise your hand first (so don't worry about getting anxiety over not knowing answers).

Took two classes with him. Gave a lot of reading, but I did extremely well just by listening in class. Flexible: Gives multiple options about when to write essays. Lectures are extremely interesting, and he likes to connect the ancient world to the present. Really nice guy who actively tries to learn everyone's name and is extremely approachable.

The majority of classes focused on translating passages from the book, and the rest were devoted to learning grammar. Incredibly passionate about what he teaches, engages the class in inspirational and interesting discussions and, above all, best dad jokes.

Really enjoyed taking a class on Catullus from Prof G! He expects a lot from his students but doesn't overload on the work. Very smart, friendly, and open to new ideas and perspectives. Would definitely take again!

An all around great guy and prof! Class is fast-paced and there is a lot to memorize. Very willing to hold individual office hours to help one-on-one. Best professor I have ever had.Funny. Smart. Makes material interesting and exciting. Always available to help his students.

really nice guy, good lecturer, he also gives you the test questions before the test so that definitely helps.  you don't always have to go to class either which is kinda nice.

Adequate.  Don't expect any inspiration or anything, though.

He is a sweet guy but rather unapproachable and awkward. He is a stickler for grammar which can be really annoying if you have to write papers for him. If you are an IR or PSC major, you should really take a class with him. He is very informative and explains examples very well. He makes sure you will get a good grade too if you put in effort
Much more work in this class than you word expect for an elective political science course, prepare to do a lot of writing (even if you're not taking it as a writing course). Otherwise interesting.
SO BAD!  he is full of himself and boring to listen to.  I would never take a class with him if its not required

My course was taught by both Niemi and Linda Powell.  This was the funniest ****ing class I've ever had.  Dick is hilarious (in that old style grandfather way). the best poli sci prof at the place.  I LEARNED SO MUCH, more than i expected to.
probably the best professor i've ever had.  a lot of fun, makes class interesting.  always available for questions.
great guy, very knowledgeable but nice, not stuffy or arrogant, great with discussions, even when working with boring material,

I was literally so lost on the material days before finals -- TAs and friends couldn't help. Joined an hour-long office hour with Professor Gregory the day before the exam? understood everything. Really good professor. If you are fine to attend the lecture, definitely a great choice to take her class.

Highly caring professor who is a joy to be around. Highly knowledgeable of music theory. Outstanding Professor!

I enjoyed Prof Gregory and her Musc 101 class. If you went to class and stayed on top of the homework (1 short assignment per class), it is hard not to do well in her class. She's super sweet, passionate, and always willing to help outside of class.
She is so good. Friendly professor. Easy grading, and easy exams. But mandatory attendance and need to buy textbook.
She's good. I feel like even if you only wrote name on your exam you would still pass it.
AMAZING PROFESSOR. Accessible outside of class and will remember your name in a room of a hundred students.

This is an OUT OF MIND extremely hard course. I know it's the minor requirement but this class is definitely not for people who have only taken theory 1&2. What not to say about Oberly. One of my favorite math teachers of all time and I also believe he is one of the smartest teachers I have ever had. He is an amazing lecturer, and although attendance isn't mandatory, I encourage everyone to go to an Oberly lecture.
Best 162 prof by far.
Best math teacher I've ever had. His course covered difficult material, but workshop and homework helped a lot. Fair grader, if you put in the work you are guaranteed a good grade.

Explains concepts clearly, but speeds through them because there's a lot of content to cover. Very caring, and accessible for help if you reach out. Definitely go to workshop (graded on participation)/study groups because those TAs have a lot of good info to share. Look over/practice with past tests before exams, similar material will be covered.

His lectures were good, but he could have went through more practice problems for each topic. Small mistakes were worth a lot of points on the midterms and final, so make sure you check your work multiple times. Highly recommend doing the practice exams before the exams.

Poberly is actually the goat. His lectures really clearly outline the content you need to know, and he's such a chill whimsical guy. Definitely the best 162 professor by far out of the bunch, so take it with him if at all possible.

I love Poberly so much I wanna be like him when I grow up. Don't miss the lectures because the content is much harder to learn on your own. Exams were pretty easy compared to the practice exams/questions that we did. I love the brain breaks as well.

In Math 162, I thoroughly enjoyed all of my lectures throughout the semester, regardless of the material being covered. I took math201 with him. he explained stuff very well and always ready to answer questions we have

This class flat out stinks. You will fail tests and it will be okay. This professor's lecture were too much and confused everyone. A charismatic professor who gives amazing lectures and provides useful notes. He definitely has the personality to teach. Choose him!
He is very considerate and caring. I registered for the course late, and he offered to walk me through the topics I had missed. 
I will definitely take his other math classes.

Oberly was a great professor and very caring! The class itself was very difficult, especially the second half. Oberly was very helpful during office hours though. I also recommend going to study group and tutoring through the learning center if you need help with webwork problems.
Awful course, but a great professor. If you have to take Math 162, take Oberly.
Tough course but he is always available to answer questions and enthusiastic

Challenging class consider if you have ap calc ab and jump straight into college level calc 2, a lot of students I know have bc or equivalent IB background. I recommend watching corresponding lessons from professor V on youtube before coming to class.

Big difficulty spike in the second part of class with series. I recommend going to office hours, the 162 study groups, and finding a (free) tutor through the learning center. Oberly is a caring and available professor even if his lectures sometimes drag on, and if you do the webwork consistently then you should be on track for a good grade.

I thought he did a great job with teaching this class and his lectures were genuinely helpful. Otherwise, he is an approachable professor and I highly recommend asking questions!

Oberly is a kind professor who takes time to answer your questions and teaches in a good manner. Sometimes he skips a few steps or goes a bit too quickly but overall, he is pretty good. Out of all the math 162 teachers, I recommend him because when talking to my peers, he seems to be the best. But math 162 as a class is hard and tests are unfair.

Peter is super accesible outside of class, passionate about teaching, and welcoming! Lectures can feel a little dense and overwhelming, but overall a great class!

Super knowledgable and cares for his students a lot! His lectures are quite content heavy but that's expected for any math course. Not necessary to read the textbook but it makes the lectures easier to understand if you skim beforehand.

He is a very engaging lecturer, and the course overall is very interesting. Would strongly recommend knowing linear algebra before this course as I feel you get a lot more out of it if you do.
Great class
He is such an amazing professor, he was so caring that he gave us 50 extra points on the final because our TA did not give us enough time to complete the exam.

Tough content but he is a great professor. He adjusts his teaching to fit the understanding of the class. For Spring 2025, there was three problem sets, one midterm and one final. Hard class but really interesting. Attend lecture and don't be lazy.
Very smart guy

amazing professor. talk to him in office hours, he is super duper cool, chill and smart!

Amazing and brilliant professor. Highly recommend talking to him in office hours as he has lots of interesting information and knowledge to share.

really great guy. super accessible, easy to digest lectures with ample help and assistance. if you're thinking about or are already majoring in political science or international relations i highly recommend taking any class with professor stu, just an overall good-hearted empathetic guy with tons of expertise and connections to help you succeed.

LOVED THIS CLASS AND STU. Definitely get the W credit because it's really easy and you do fun activities in the Rochester community. Stu is super caring and is more than accommodating with his students. 10/10

Stu is an absolutely amazing guy. He has a tendency to be very redundant with the material, but he does make it extremely clear. Although you don't have to go to lecture, the work really comes in outside of class, so be prepared for that. I thoroughly enjoyed this class despite its simplicity.
Lovvveeed this class, local gov is the best. Really easy to get the W credit and has fun OTB activities around the Rochester community. Stu is also a great guy and professor.

Local govt has been my favorite class at Rochester so far. Class has very clear syllabus. Professor Jordan is great. He's very intelligent, clear with his requirements, and the nicest guy you'll ever meet. Any class he teaches is worth taking

Stu is the best. I took PSC 280W with him and it was the best W class I could have ever hoped for. Instead of having to write a 25p research paper like most W classes. We wrote 5 5p papers. It was awesome. I highly recommend all of Stu's classes.
He is a great professor. Extremely nice. Very clear. And he teaches you stuff you will actually use.

Professor Jordan is just a great guy.  Its a pleasure to be in his classes and he is always willing to lend a helping hand upon request.  If you're a poli sci, I suggest taking as many classes with him as possible.

Best professor I've ever had so far! Whoever has a problem with his teaching style in PSC 202 is one who expects the professor to feed him all the class material. Amazing professor!  So helpful and friendly. Lecture could drag on so bring a computer.

Ridiculously good with names.
awesome professor, funny guy, makes some small mistakes but manages to correct himself, & engages all of the students in discussion
Excellent professor. I actually looked forward to going to class. He makes the discussions very thought provoking.

Homework 20% / Exam 80%. Good professor teaching a tough course. Little to no opportunity for partial credit, which motivated a strong curve but stings when the average for an exam might be between 50-60%.

Stefankovic is passionate about the class and its material. Solve extra problems outside of class and do HWs on your own. Exams are hard but not very challenging.

My favorite prof in the CS dept. Great lectures, really cares about the material, and is great to explore ideas more in depth with in office hours. Had her as my PI for a research class. She's incredibly helpful.
Giving low scores. Compared to other professors in the writing department, Kara really disappoints students a lot. I will never recommend this professor at all.

She's an absolutely wonderful professor. She teaches with great interest and skill. I want to study medieval literature because of this class now! She makes class interesting and fun. You will grow a lot in English writing after a class with McShane.

comment: Professor Blackman stands out in the way that he wrote homework/test questions. In principle, they were never difficult, but they tested the fundamentals of a subject at a very deep level. Homework, and exams especially, were fantastic learning experiences. He's also a very kind person and amazing to chat with. Stand-up guy and brilliant physicist.

Prof. Cook is such a huge role model of mine and 350 characters isn't nearly enough to explain how incredible she is! She is so kind and truly cares about her students. She sat with me for hours answering all my questions without making it feel like an imposition. 201 is hard, but she makes it manageable. I will miss her next semester :')

Good with lectures but exams are unnecessarily hard and not reflective of Webworks. Partially reflective of Gradescopes, but not really. Exams are graded on a curve because of this and everyone scores pretty much the same so there's not really a way to get an A.
Reallllllly nice professor
Very harsh

She is just so nice 😭 I had a panic attack during the exam and I had to leave. She was just so caring and so helpful throughout the whole process. I love her😭 Thanks to her, otherwise I wouldn't have passed the course.

Great lectures, and cares a lot about making sure everyone understands the concepts. I never liked probability in the past but found this class interesting, especially once we got into more complicated math.

Mary Cook is one of the best math professors I ever had! She was accommodating and accessible outside of class. Dr. Cook is an amazing professor. She is patient and explains things clearly. She's accessible outside of class and always willing to provide support if you ask. Her lecture notes are extremely well-organized, just like her lectures. Def attend her classes. Her office hours are incredibly helpful too. Don't hesitate to ask for help if you need it.

Dr. Cook has extremely concise lectures, but even more concise complimentary notes. I didn't go to class much because the notes were so good, but I definitely recommend going to recitation or study hours. Great professor!

She is a very nice professor who lectures well but the math department at this school is just awful. The exams are difficult and the webwork is harder than 141. She records lectures which is nice and she is accessible outside of class. She also posts filled-in notes and blank notes. Definitely try to get 100% on the webwork and workshop.

I was never able to get above a B+ in a calc class, finally was able to after taking 164 with her. She is so clear and concise when teaching. Everything was thoroughly explained. Exams were difficult though, review her in class examples when studying for an exam.
Mary Cook is a good professor, explains topics well and is very approachable. If she is teaching multi you are in good shape.

Cook is a great professor, the class is quite difficult tho. All of her examples come directly out of the book. The Webwork is quite challenging. Recommend using prof Leonard on YouTube for help to make the class more manageable.

Coming into college,I thought I wanted to be a math minor. To say the least, I never plan to take another math class again. He was the best professor anyone could have asked for.
Dr. Dietsche is an amazing professor. I miss his class so much!!!

Dietsche is my most memorable UR prof - you will never forget this guy! He is the best ever! He tells many stories about the time he served in the navy, and those are so much fun to listen in class. Tests are very straight forward, but doesn't mean they are easy. Nobody could teach physiology better than him!
Best teacher ever. This is a class about taking notes and memorizing. you would be surprised how many people havent developed these skills by the time they enter college

Not a bad teacher, tough class especially over the summer.  Tends to not be the most organized guy but could be worse.  His stories were great.  Tests are short but are hard.  Teacher recommended summer class is not (to much info to fast).

Very unorganized.  Though he is a very charismatic man, he fails at being a good lecturer.  He doesn't even bother to let us have access to the slides he puts up and his tests are quite difficult compared to what he teaches.

Excellent lecturer.  Very fast paced.  Straight from the book and lectures.  Glad to see he's still teaching.  I had him in 91/92 and I kept my binder from that class because I was so amazed (and still am) at how much I learned.
Awesomeness incarnate. Tough class, but he keeps the material interesting with his personality and stories. Very friendly and personable.

This man is one of the most caring professors I've had.  Makes a point to meet every student during lab (and remember names) and give them on the spot advice for life.  Lectures are fast paced, but the tests are very basic and easy to pull an A.

The class was rough with the amount of material that you were expected to memorize.  All tests were multiple choice and non-cumulative but really specific.  He was a very good teacher though and extremely funny.  The little annecdotal stories he told during lectures definitely helped with remembering material for the exams.
No Comments

****ing awesome- bitter divorcee, proud ****, ex-farmer, vietnam navy veteran, outright crazy and one hella charming man.  Teaches each lecture with a moral for life, and gives you a lot of other valuable life lessons along the way, mostly through didactic horse breeding stories. Take the class
this man, while hillarious, has no sense of organization. I'm also pretty sure he does no preparation for this class... i mean honestly is an overhead with some key terms to much to ask for?
He's quite literally very very crazy, but entertaining. And the class is relatively easy too
Fantastic lectures, I didn't skip a single one.  The guy is hysterical.  Painful amounts of memorization, but all tests are non-cumulative.

I really enjoyed this class and professor.  There is alot of memorizing in this class, although it's an easy course concept-wise.  A few students do comment that he doesn't have much organization within his lectures, but I didn't find this the case.
I love this man.  I am a man myself.  Boy that is wierd.  Anyway, an amazing teacher who can make even physiology a fun and interesting class.
Very direct - brute memorization class ... great naval stories

can be very sarcastic if you match his energy. Solid lectures, entertaining, clearly passionate about the material. Does a decent job explaining things. Accessible outside class and cares about his students. The homework is a bit tedious. The exams are hard, but study and you'll probably be fine. Fairly lenient grader, you can often convince him to give you a few extra points if you go to OH.

His lectures were great, he had many "hands-on" examples throughout the semester and even if you can't go to class his online notes are great (class is better though). This was my first real physics course, and although it's not my strong suit at all, it went much better because of him. Legitimately a great prof and I'd take him if you can.

Professor Manly was inspirational to me this semester. 123 was the first physics class I took at UR, and he certainly continued to inspire the love of physics that I got from a good teacher in high school. The tests are difficult, but doing the problem sets and practicing from old exams makes them absolutely doable.

Manly is a good prof. Lectures are energetic and entertaining but he would often miss a week of classes at a time do to research commitments. Exams were tough and given in a 50 minute time period so you had to race against the clock. All in all the guy is a good prof but the logistics of the class could be much better.

Manly was the professor for my E&M class that was self-paced. At first, he seems really helpful and genuinely interested in the students. Soon, it became clear that was not the case. He and his TA would send emails weeklysaying that he would "laugh in our faces" if we didn't get all the work done and needed help. The emails really put students down

Genuinely invested in teaching and really wants you to understand physics, but not always great at explain things - lecture is often unhelpful. Tests are really tough but fair, and he let's you bring in a formula sheet. Going to workshop and doing the problem sets are essential to passing. The book is super helpful - definitely a must have.

I have a love hate relationship with him. Love him until an exam then hate a few days after exam then I forgive him. You will literally not pass if you don't study and actual learn. You can't just pattern match the problems with how he writes his exams. Very conceptual and creative with writing problems. But I still love him

Manly is funny, interesting, and wholly devoted to his students. There were moments in lecture where he'd lose track of a problem he was doing, but he'd always inform us of the right solution once he'd worked it out properly. His tests are fair, but they're definitely difficult. One of the most dedicated teachers I've had here in a long time.
Great class, don't be concerned about his curve. He respects the effort the class requires and grades accordingly. He's also pretty funny.

He is a funny guy and know the material very, very well. But, if you were not studying regularly, it's very hard, i mean VERY hard, to keep up with. His exams are conceptual and tricky. Understand the concept is a key to do well in his class.

He's pretty interesting in class.  Sometimes he slips into just showing lots of slides in a row, making me painfully aware of the clock above his left shoulder.  His curve doesn't really make sense to me (normalizes all tests to an 70% mean, even if it means students losing points) but my grade in the class turned out alright, so I can't complain.

Took 113 as a freshman. Not a phsyics person but pulled off a B. Manly is a good prof. Exams are hard but not impossible. He curves (even if that means curving DOWN). Graded homework is a booster.  Don't skip lecture.  Workshop was alright.  Labs are easy.

Very enthusiastic and clear. Lectures are usually interesting. 142 was a very challenging course. My average test score was in the 40's but I got a B in the course. Homeworks aren't worth very many points but DO THEM. They will help you more than anything else.

EXCELLENT communication--he e-mailed us constantly with corrections, helpful hints, & other info, and he always added bits of humor to keep things entertaining.  He used a light saber as a pointer, and his method of using a tablet PC projected onto a big screen for lectures was perfect.  Demos were exciting and lectures were interesting. Great guy!

Seems nice, but can turn on you.  Is a bit full of himself. Lecture was at times entertaining. Exams are difficult.  (but people still got 100s, I have no idea how).  Workshop was somewhat helpful.  At least he renormalizes the grades.
What a terrible teacher! And he thinks he's funny too.
best prof in the physics department
Great Guy.  Definitely knew how to party back in his time!
Learned a lot.  Great professor.

Excellent professor.  Very clear/Instructs well.  Uses effective in-class demonstrations.  Instituted small groups which really help learning the material.  Tests are generally fair, and well representative of material that was supposed to be learned.
Manly's awesome!  Good natured, and a great professor.  Makes a painful course slightly easier.
Eager for the students to do well without being overly easy.

Although I did not take any courses in person with this professor, his lecture slides are the most structured and logically comprehensible I have ever seen in any other course here at UR, and I have been taking tons of Bio and Econ courses with both Scientific and Statistic contents. Highest admiration and respect to him! Thank you!
Best Prof in Stat Department
Good class. It requires good math skills. I wish it could include broad topics in regression. eg, non-linear regression, ridge, lasso, etc.

I have taken multiple classes with Professor Ciminelli, and he is the best professor I have had at u of r. He is extremely knowledgeable and caring. best prof ever
taken STAT216, best professor ever met

To say that he is a good professor is an understatement. Unlike most of the others I have had, Professor Ciminelli explains concepts extremely well and is always willing to help students who are struggling. Would strongly encourage any CS or stats majors to take a course with him.

Ciminelli is genuinely one of the best professors I've had here. While the content for the class can be quite challenging, his lectures are extremely clear and break everything down. He recognizes when we're not understanding a topic and adjusts accordingly. He genuinely wants you to succeed.
Best professor ever. Amazing lectures. Reasonable and helpful homework. Clear class notes. Students can really learn solid knowledge from his class.
This is a relatively hard course, but prof. Ciminelli is really helpful!

comment: Best professor ever and STAT 218 is relative easy.
The reviews are true, Dr. Cimminelli is a great professor and will help you outside of class when you need it. Workload is kind of heavy, so get started on assignments in advance.

Fantastic lectures, very passionate and caring. Will respond to emails quickly and is very generous and respectful. 262 was very easy, but stats is not a difficult subject. Prof Ciminelli was a pleasure all semester.

Joe is the best professor in terms of teaching not only in U of R, but also in my grad school. I took his STT218 in Fall 2018 and STT223 in Spring 2019. Rarely do you see a professor that's both a nice and easy-going person while at the same time also a great instructor. One or the other is usually what you hope for.
Good

He is probably one of the best professor at U of R. Not only does his class is super organized and the lectures are very informative and useful. He is very helpful after class and supporting his students. Fantastic teacher!

He is one of the nicest professor I had for my undergraduate.

He really is one of the best professors at the University. Caring, gentle, takes time to get to know you. Interesting and really great introduction to statistics. You can't really go wrong with him. Was struggling a bit in the class and he set me up with a great tutor. Great guy.
Professor Ciminelli is a gem at U of R, one hw assignment per week and gives out practice tests that are very similar to the actual ones.

Ciminelli is by far the best professor I've ever had at UR. He truly cares about how his students are doing , and does his best to make sure no one is left behind . The way he approaches the material is easily comprehendible. There is one homework assignment each week , but I feel the assignment directly reflects the types of questions on tests .
He goes above and beyond as a professor. He is very sweet and is always willing to help students out.

Professor Ciminelli is hands down the BEST Professor Ive ever met. Though our class became online, he is very responsive and caring to his students. His tests are reasonable and gives opportunity to correct for credit. His lectures are also super coherent and organized. Simply a great person and lecturer! Thanks for everything Professor Ciminelli!

Super good and helpful prof. Really detailed, clear, and organized slides. Lectures are boring but not required. He often uploads supplemental videos of him solving problems if he thinks he didn't explain something well in lecture. He also made cookies for us on the last class!
He is one of the best professors I have ever had. He is an amazing professor and cares about his students.
He is just amazing. The only bad thing is at the end you realize how BAD your other professors are.

Really nice professor in Statistics Department! For students planning Data Science major: if you haven't decided which course to take among 212/213/262, then 262 can be the best choice for you, which is also the best connection to DSC265!

Easily best professor I've ever had. The material isn't particularly difficult, but if you ever have any troubles with it, Joe is there to help you at almost any hour of the day. And he makes cookies for all his classes. <3 Joe

Professor Ciminelli is the best teacher i've had at the university so far and is my favorite teacher ever. He genuinely cares about his students understanding the material and enjoying his class. His lectures are interesting and he makes sure the students understand the material before they leave each day.

Amazing, amazing, amazing professor! He's one of the most caring and thoughtful people I have encountered at the UofR. He's fully devoted to the class and will try his best to get you to understand this stuff! He was of great help! 100% deserved his Professor of the Year award!

Dr. Ciminelli is literally my absolute favorite teacher. He really wants his students to succeed and works really hard to make sure that his students understand his material. He's extremely accessible and makes stats interesting to learn (he is very knowledgeable). He got the professor of the year award for a reason. TAKE STATS WITH HIM!
I love ciminelli so much that I created an account so that I can hype this man up. TAKE HIS CLASS

One of the best professor Ive had in college. He cares about students and is approachable outside class. The homework needs some time work but its doable. Class was very helpful in learning RStudio. Definitely recommend to take his class.

Definitely one of the best professors I had in u of r. Always care about his students and respond emails super fast. He even baked cookies himself for 6 hours for us during final week. Strongly recommend to take his class.

He's really approachable and easy to talk to. The homework is challenging, but it makes you to learn the material. This class is awesome if you enjoy statistics and learning more about different tests and models used by statisticians.

He really cares about his students and so far one of the most amazing professors.

Joe is by far the best professor I've had at UR, I've taken STT212 and STT218 with him and thoroughly enjoyed both (never in a million years thought I would enjoy stats). Professor Ciminelli is one of my favorite professors. He is very friendly and approachable and will respond to emails very very quickly! He makes statistics easy to understand and he explains concepts extremely well. Highly recommend Ciminelli for any Intro Stats courses!!

OK SO- Dr. Ciminelli actually is easily the most accessible and well-read professor I have come across at U of R. Easily the hottest professor here!
Inspiring teacher!

He is an excellent teacher. Materials are clear and organized. And he goes through everything in great details! I asked for several office hours l, and he made great efforts to cooperate. Good teacher!

He is a fantastic teacher. Very funny. Did some reviewers confuse him for somebody else? He never gave extra credit
His lectures are disorganized and the slides dont help in the slightest. However, he offers up to 2% extra credits. If you only want a good grade and dont expect to learn much, take his class.

The lectures were not very clear and Professor Yang sometimes rambled on about a study or an example that wasn't making sense to the students. Prof. Chaves is a bore to listen to lecture and does not do a great job of explaining material. Like all math courses here they are ungodly difficult for no reason. has got to easily be one of the worst professors here at u of r.

MATH 200: Easily worst professor and class Ive ever taken. He does not care about his students. Contents in lecture and hw do not match, sometimes hw has content not in textbook. Professor chaves has one of the best methods of going throught examples. His notes are also a piece of art, more than enough to study everything with examples and be able to answer questions in homework and lectures. He made discrete math an easy A for me!
This guy is great. He's a talented mathematician and can cast light on some really difficult topics. The class is difficult, but he does a great job of showing the more beautiful side of mathematics.
really good!! hard to pay attention in class, because its pretty boring/monotone, so its easy to doze off
Laura is a gentle and interesting professor. Her classes are very relaxed, but attendance is very important. Only when you attend classes on time can you gain a lot.
Pretty solid professor. Not much to say because this class isn't very demanding. If you go to class and put in 40% effort you should be fine.

She's a great person—as long as you complete and submit assignments on time, you're guaranteed an A. She'll also help you with any questions about papers. I'd absolutely take her class again if I had the chance.
nice instructor, just select her course without worry

Laura is a very nice professor who gives clear and useful feedbacks to students. She is good at teaching too. I'm not a fan of writing, but I enjoyed writing in her class. She is a fair grader that if you have done your work well, she would give you the grade that you deserve.

I absolutely loved professor Whitebell for my required writing class this semester. She was super flexible with my schedule and was understanding about extensions. I'm not a huge fan of writing in general, but I'd take this class again with her any semester. Would definitely recommend!

I am the one who got an A from WRTG 105A on 1/20/21. Everything is similar. She is always respectful, kind, and structural in teaching. I would love to take a future writing course with her if I have a chance.
