comment: Although the readings she assigned weren't all that in-depth, I thought the provided material was still interesting enough to have a pretty fun class. Lectures weren't too heavy, so long as you participate in discussions and submit the papers on time, the class is not too difficult.

For her 105A, what really matters are the two formal assignments (two roughly 5-pages papers), which add to 60% of the grade. As long as you do all the homework, you will get the rest 40%. She is very caring and serious about academics. She is open to paper extensions as long as you are hard-working and respectful. Sincere thanks to her.

Awesome teacher. She is naturally funny and will always give super helpful feedback. Her style of teaching is very collaborative (making sure you get feedback from different sources), and she's always available if you need to talk to her about something.
Takes herself very seriously and has no sense of humor, which is probably why she didn't get that 273 is a joke. It's an easy class though so it doesn't really matter that she's not great.
She's a really caring professor and is very open and wants to make sure that her students succeed. While she is a tough grader in my opinion, she gives good feedback. Really great class.

She chose super boring readings and topics for the course. Was forcing us to do a lot of group work, during which she was doing her own stuff and didn't even pay attention to us. Surprisingly, the requirements were more harsh in this  class than in WRT 105 (according to my friends' feedback). Laura is nice as a person though and gives extensions.
Best professor I had in this university yet; love her.
Super nice, really into her class. Had some great discussions. I would recommend if you are picking a WRT105E class.

If you just read the syllabus for this course, you will quickly understand who your dealing with, "You may consider the reading load for the course to be totally unreasonable! My response? Too bad!" he genuinely cares about his students and his lectures are full of wisdom

I've never had a professor phone it in this hard. Johnson is crazy disorganized, unfocused, uninteresting, and clearly not trying. I can't believe he has so many positive ratings. Nice guy though. Very easy class. But, you won't learn anything.

Amazing professor with really insightful lectures. Likes to go on tangents but he's funny. The readings are fairly dense but definitely manageable and engaging. Very lenient grader and super flexible with extensions too; he definitely cares about his students. Also really helpful if you go to his office hours if needed.

Took during covid. Lectures are him talking about the reading the whole time (great if you don't get the readings or if it was really dense) I skipped like the whole class the entire semester (it was rough okay) and I still passed with just skimming the reading. He was amazing though. So kind and understanding please talk with him if you need help.
Professor Johnson's class was really good which I learned a lot from. There is not much reading, approximately 50 pages per week. Recommend this class!

James Johnson was a fantastic professor, he was interesting to listen to and he was understanding of difficulties caused by life. The paper at the end was challenging, but also fun because of how much freedom you have with it

We love Professor Johnson for his humor. He can always keep students awake--even when I'm taking his class in the middle of the night! He loves reading, and he makes sure his students love reading as well. So get ready to read a lot, otherwise you won't understand what he's talking about. Very relaxed class. All discussion based with a lot of reading but not a lot of assignments. Very understanding of students and flexible around certain things. He just wants his students to learn and grow and doesn't care about grades, which is scary but it works out in the end. Course is really unique and changes your perspective, highly recommend

Terrific guy! Down to earth, is there for the students, humble, and makes the dull subject matter (e.g. 17th century political philosophy) understandable and, somehow, interesting.  My favorite professor this semester and would definitely take another class with him again.  You really only need to hustle for the three big papers he assigns.
He is a good professor who really cares about the students.

Johnson is a character. He likes to be agreed with so don't argue, he has favorites, he expects a lot of "smart" comments but if you try, pay attention and care about the subject you will be fine.  I really actually like him, he's  kinda disorganized but i'm being negative, he is actually really good, so overall i think you should take his class.

Prof Johnson is extremely good at getting you to understand political philosophy, and teaches the "lectures" in a seminar style that allows people to really get to the heart of an issue. He can be redundant but that helps drill crucial points in. I will try to take another of his classes ASP.

Prof. Johnson is amazing! Really smart and eager to help students out. I've never found him to be arrogant, for being as brilliant as he is, he is really down to earth. His classes can be easy, but he always assigns great readings and offers great insight on them.

Very funny and relaxed, Johnson will keep you somewhat interested in going to class, although his seminar does have a lot of reading and discussion so definitely be prepared for that. He is VERY lenient about time pressures, so gives extensions liberally as long as you're not an atrocious student.
He is very smart, interesting and cute.

Johnson is one of those professors who you'll want to wake up at 9:00 in the morning and listen to. His overwhelmingly benevolent and hilarious nature is what makes his class so honestly enjoyable; don't get a Poli Sci degree at Rochester without taking one of his courses.

Gives great lectures.. If you take good notes it is easy to do well on the writing assignments even if you have not done all the readings completely. Very interesting and well informed professor. I don't see how that other person could have said that he would mark you down for different views. I'm shocked that someone takes marketing—likely one of the first jobs AI will replace—so seriously. She speaks too fast and grades harshly for a social science course. I'm usually a high achiever and enjoy tough professors, but she makes it hard to enjoy her or this subject.

If you want you to take the most pointless class and learn nothing, take this class. If you want to be a walk across campus to sit and do other work and be on your phone, take this class. The choice is yours, where pointless test and assignments are graded like they are going to be the cure to cancer.

genuinely the most stretched out course and aimlessly and pointlessly tedious assignments and tests. Doesn't curve anything and intentionally gives bad grades, especially towards beginning of the year
Great Professor, if you put in effort you will easily finish with an A! amazing lectures and fun projects, Nescio is real and is a wonderful professor
A very kind person and knows a lot about the world of marketing outside the classroom. Does a great job bringing outside examples into class to help students understand the material.

she is not accessible outside of class, she takes everything so seriously, attendance is mandatory and if you miss you have to show a drs notes to have it excused, tests are mainly based on textbook readings and her lectures, she has some extra credit opps but i just can't stand her, she is rude to students and classroom management

Professor Nescio is one of the best professors that I have had at the U of R. She is very knowledgable, and organizes her class in a manner that enables her students to fully apprehend the subject. comment: She's very direct, and is very clear that she treats us like adults, rightfully expecting us to behave accordingly. She can come off as strict, but in my experience it's usually deserved. Grading criteria can be a little fuzzy, but never felt unfair. Lectures are very well organized and engagingly delivered.

She is a good lecturer and really demonstrate her identity as a coach. Assignments are graded tough and tests are kinda hard too. Definitely not an easy A. Not really accessible outside of the classroom but I enjoy her class.

Great professor. Describes herself as a coach, and it's very accurate. Super helpful and incredibly knowledgable and confident. A lot of work, but the simulation at the end is fun, and the grading is not too bad if you put the work in. Overall a smart and caring person.

Professor Nescio is the best professor I have had, she is very smart and an amazing lecturer! At first I didn't like the class but then it really grew on me, I ended up really loving the course and the professors teaching style. If you put in the effort you will get an A
Shes tough, and abrasive. It is difficult to receive a high grade in her class. I would rather take the course with a different professor
final project is 30% of your overall grade. if anything wrong happened your grade is over.
Too much homework. If you miss one, you will fail the class.
Professor Nescio was the best Professor I've ever had! Her lectures are super clear, helpful, and she has a great grading system! I wish I could take her class again
One of the best professors I've ever had! Highly recommend her classes.

Too much work to be done in this class. The grading is very ambiguous so don't expect to get an A that you actually deserve. It is most likely that you will get an A- no matter how much harder you work than other people do. Better take this intro class with another professor.
She is a really good professor and she is easy to reach out to
super kind and always approachable

Take self paced if you care about your grade, class is hard. Howell does really want students to succeed but he is very busy outside of this class. Thinking about retaking physics in self paced. Tests for this class were the hardest I've ever experienced.

Not enough emphasis on examples, too many derivations. That's just not my learning style, I struggled with the class. Others talk about how workshops were so helpful, my TA didn't really facilitate a learning environment-everyone just sits there and does HW.  I'm not just bitter I didn't do well, I really actually did not learn well w his style.

Professor Howell really wants to help. He's well-prepared for the lecture and he tries his best to help students stay interested. Physics is not easy for most of people, but if you really study for it, go to his office hour as many as possible , you'll eventually ace it. I like pro. Howell and would like to take future classes with him if possible.

I love Prof. Howell! Teaching PHY 121 can be tricky, but Prof. Howell did a good job! He is hilarious and uses real-life examples to make bland subjects interesting. Grading and extra credit are very fair. I only wish that we can have more time in class for the clicker quizzes - I often don't have enough time to react before I answer. Good job!
Horrible teacher. You could tell he is a smart physicist but he just can NOT teach whatsoever. He also fails at putting together tests. I would avoid taking a class with him if I could.

Teaches the concepts quite well, especially entanglement which he knows a lot about.  Tests aren't too bad if you make sure you know the homeworks.  Extremely nice and positive guy too.  Overall a good course; I learned a lot.

I was very lucky to have him teaching PHY407 for the first semester of my PhD. He is a very nice and helpful guy. He is in general very considerate. And he would like to explain again and again if you have difficulty understanding the concept. His tests are the hardest thing in the universe. But he graded them nicely and he has a nice curve as well

My favourite subject so far. Very very good lecturer with very good presentation skills. Lectures well-paced. Used lots of examples from recent research to motivate ideas. Homework questions are hard and long but he is always willing to offer help although he appears to be busy(due to meetings/conferences). Highly recommended!

Howell, an experimentalist, presented a rigorous treatment of fundamental principles while pausing often to develop advanced topics such as coherent states, Peres separability criteria and continuously entangled states.  Additionally, he related many topics to experiments mostly done in his own lab to motivate ideas.  A first rate treatment!

Could tell he didn''t want to teach the class.  Once he changed his teaching style he taught a little better but midterms were unfair.  However he had a huge scale making it difficult not to get a B or higher.

Howell changed the way he ran the class in the middle of the semester, only adding to the confusion he created during lectures.  Take this class if you can study/learn  math/science concepts on your own.  Also, go to workshops, just make sure your TA is helpful (some are self-centered meanies!!!)
He is absolutely HORRIBLE! I wish I didn't take his class.  It was a waste of time and the unfair grading will hurt my GPA.  I learned nothing.  People who didn't go to class were better off.

Prof. Howell, for one reason or another (*cough*doesn't want to teach*cough*) believes that the textbook should teach you and that he should supplement it, not the other way around.  As a result, he lectures on things nobody has heard of, and this leads to mass confusion.  Overall, he's so terrible.
he doesnt like teaching and it reflects in the class...
Doesn't know the material, doesn't know how to teach, go back to grad school (newbie)!!

No exams (phew!) homework assignments are weighted heavily, and pop quizzes. HWs are very long and take around a full days worth of work to complete (if not- longer). This class will make you work for it if you want an A, and there is a group project that is worth 30% of your grade.

Its a bit annoying how there are pop quizzes in class, so you attendance is mandatory. No exams. Homeworks were ok... they were very very long. I remember one assignment took me 9 hours. You do learn a good amount about HCI in this class but its not an easy A.

I enjoyed taking CSC212: HCI with Prof. Yan. He was a good lecturer and the guest lectures at the end of the semester were quite fun with lots of Q&A interactions. My only caveats are the course structure - sometimes materials and grading were messy; but that's understandable, given that it was his first time instructing the course.

Interesting lectures and fun assignments/projects to work on.

There will be pop quizzes that count on your grade.
He give you one week to do an assignment that cannot be don't properly given the time frame. His lectures are not clear and have no structure.

As my first college-level language class, it was very fast paced and took a lot of effort to keep up. She is respectful and helful during her lectures even if she expects a lot out of her students. There is a lot of homework, so try to do around an hour of it per day to keep up with the content.

She is very caring and willing to answer all questions you ask. She always encourages me when I feel nervous about the test or my progress. There is a lot of homework, but they are very helpful for understanding the texts and mastering new knowledge. Tests aren't hard if you put effort into it, and she gave us chance to get extra credit.

Professor Papaionnou's class is very stress free. She promotes an environment where you are allowed to make mistakes, which is imperative for a language course. She is very strict about attendance, which is the only issue I have during the pandemic (of 2020). Nonetheless, If you want to learn french, she is a solid choice.

She's very disorganized and it's sometimes incredibly difficult to find out what's going on in the class. I feel like every time that I show up to class it's a complete gamble on what we're talking about that day. She doesn't really inspire or encourage discussion of topics and the homework is difficult and the workload is heavy.

comment: Professor Papaioannou was a fantastic professor. She's clearly very knowledgeable about the material and values students who make an attempt to care about it like she does. 200 would be a very, very difficult class if you aren't coming in with a good amount of experience, but if that's the case, just start out lower down.

Prof. Papaioannou is a very good professor. It's easy to tell how passionate she is about the course she is teaching. The only thing that is difficult to get over is the grading. Man, she is such a tough grader that I've found myself honestly questioning the fairness of it, something I've never done before.
She is very passionate about the class and the topics at hand, but she can be a bit intense when it comes to perfecting grammar.
She is a caring person and teaches good lectures. If you attend lectures and do some review after class, you will be well-prepared for the exams. There is quite some homework though.

Her class is a challenge, but it's worth it. I've learned more from her than I have in any other French class.  Participation can be a little intimidating when you're first starting her class, but I at least got used to it. She seems to really love what she's teaching and she makes quite a few jokes, so she's made the challenging class fun.

She's a pretty harsh grader and she makes asking questions intimidating in class. You'll see people visibly confused but afraid to ask questions because of the demeaning way she tends to answer them. Overall, she's a nice lady, but she made me want to stop taking French. Also, the textbook doesn't have ANY guides for pronunciation, just listening.

She is wonderful. She's a fun person, and really wants to be there, which shows. She makes everything very interactive, which is fantastic in a language class. She grades fairly and tries to give you as many points as possible. She is really sweet, and very helpful. I've only been to her office hours once so far, but can't wait to go back.

I took the intro ethics class. Easiest A you'll find at Roch.He gave us sheets with the notes on them.   Study for tests and know what's on the guide lines. I know a few people who took it WAY too lightly and got Cs on the first test. Do the reading (it's SO short and interesting), show up once in a while, and study for half an hour; you'll get an

Philosophy of Language is not the most enthralling course but he tries to make it interesting.  He's definitely a nice guy and a pretty good teacher.  Lots of assignments but he's pretty cool about giving you enough time to complete them.  Biggest issue: he doesn't give any comments on assignments, just the grades.
He is very nice and he gives out worksheets that help us.

He asked the class what our favorite disease was.  I want to give him a hug because i feel bad for him, leave because it's terrible to stay in a classroom with him, and then have a beer with him later b/c he's prolly a good guy.
he gives you the notes, i didn't have to open a book...but sooooo boring its ridiculous.  easy class though

He hands you typed copies of the notes but his explanations can be boring and very hard to understand.  Especially when he starts writing on the board.  It is usually illegible and he writes over things without erasing them making it worse.
He is a very nice professor lots of reading and tuff grader on writing but super nice and gives you advice on how to get better
He is very passionate, funny, and knowledgeable. But he is also an extremely tough professor. Tons of readings and papers. Very tough grader on papers. Cares a lot about participation and attendance

comment: He is a good guy and definitely cares about his students and their learning but his expectations are unreasonable. For a class full of non-english majors he expects a level of writing that is unattainable without providing instruction on how to do that. This is not a writing class but he grades as if it was.

He really made me enjoy Spanish writing.  If you go in for office hours he will help you immensely with your compositions.  He improved my spanish proficiency ten fold, but also helped me with my english writing (critiques your thesis, organization of ideas, etc that translate over to English).  I plan on taking future classes with him.

Go to office hours if you're having issues - budget a good amount of time because it's difficult to stop him once he starts talking but he will tell you all you need to know to impress him. Overall he's funny and great and recently got tenured which is very deserving. Also, he hands out chocolate.

Charismatic about the material and quite a funny guy during class. This is a composition class, so be prepared to hand in almost a draft a week. However, he's very open to confer with during office hours and offers a lot of helpful advice. Definitely raised my Spanish proficiency and challenged me to improve my writing ability.
Extremely helpful during office hours. Helped with my writing in Spanish and in English.
VERY intelligent professor. Tough grader - certainly not an easy A. He really knows his stuff and he really wants his students to learn and to leave his class as smarter people.

Brilliant. Can be a little brutal if you debate him in class, but is very intelligent and a tough grader that whips your writing skills into shape. He's very funny. Class is fun and his commentary on texts make it less painful.

This professor is phenomenal. He made me think and helped me improve my writing in Spanish. He has high standards but we are paying 45k+ a year to learn after all. Students who complain about him are lazy and wanted a grade they most likely didn't earn. This prof knows his subject area and grades fairly. He made pre-18th century lit relevant

Professor Prendergast is one of the most helpful professors I have ever taken. Those students who complain about the work load simply feel they have some deserving right to coast through college. Professor Prendergast wants to maximize the learning experience for his students. Does that mean working harder at times? Of course. But it's worth it.

Grades essays really hard and a bit unfairly, takes points off for 'personal peeves' not necesarily for poor writing style.  Class discussion sometimes gets monopolized by him. Very unsympathetic to personal needs of his students.

Ryan is a pretentious ****.  Screams too much about stupid things.  Grades ridiculously hard.  Activities don't support class material.  I would have had a perfect semester gpa if not for this class. This was a complete waste of a class.
Very strange man, has a weird obsession with pop stars. Grades compositions REALLY hard.
An ok prof. He grades compositions pretty hard, and the curriculum of the class could use some work too.  Pretty fair. Not great but not bad.

Nicole is arguably the best and sweetest professor/person I have met in my life. She's very approachable and offer the best advice for your writings. If you planning on taking WRT 105 and is here to figure out which professor you should take it with, take it with Nicole!

I feel like sometimes she treats us like we're in fifth grade and I thought the class would be more interesting. She's not very engaging and we are covering material we have already covered (eg. MLA) I think the class I have learned the most from consisted of a student discussing the history of bananas from a book he read. Discussions  great.

Nicole is one of the nicest people you'll ever meet. She is helpful in and outside of class, and genuinely cares about you as a student. Amazing things she did: canceled class the day before Thanksgiving break so we could go home early, gave multiple pages of amazingly helpful feedback on papers, and let us write about topics we enjoyed. Loved her!
Thinks she is the only important professor on campus and her schedule is the only schedule that needs to be respected.
instructions on assignments are horrible and deducts points on things not listed in instructions
grading in this class is very weird, does not follow a rubric. Professor is not helpful and we just watch clips in class

Class is pretty simple, all you have to do is semester long project where you make an app/web-app that solves a problem and uses HCI principles (doesn't have to be good). Professor is incoherent and doesn't care about or help with anything. Lectures are mind-numbingly boring. Would definitely not trust her to teach a class with actual content.

Lectures are not very well structured; grading rubrics on individual homework do not match the actual grading. It is a big group project that needs a lot of personal research and study. The VR/AR workshop is not that helpful, and YouTube videos will be your friend. However, this course is pretty fun to take.

worst professor ever existed. does not teach anything basically, no code, just playing ytb videos and throwing non-sense ideas. does not seem to understand the theory. TAs teach out-of-date frameworks and code, what a great match! develop unity for final project, taught by studioX guys, they are great btw, help out projects a lot.

She doesn't teach anything useful. She spent the first half of the semester showing is pointless Youtube videos. Then, she dumped a huge project on us without guidance. The project was really annoying. You have to make 30,000 prototypes to satisfy her. When I asked her for help she was vague and unhelpful. Worst class ever.
Professor Sun's class is interesting at beginning, until his midterm test and paper. The average was very low for a introductory history class. His accents need improvements.
I regret taking this class, the teacher's accents too strong, he wasted class time to fix the powerpoint, he graded unfair. hes just ridiculous. do yourself a favor: do not take his class!
yes very very awful~~
Not a good prof.  Unfair grading, not clear, accent problems, can't really teach.  Just bad in general.  Do not take his class, you will regret it forever and ever and EVER.
Not clear, Not helpful, Too much work, Bad Grammar, Hard Grader.

Though Professor Das usually teaches higher level courses, he did an excellent job of explaining the material in this lower level class in a way that anyone could understand. It is obvious that he cares for his students and is passionate about physics.

Professor Das really cares about students and tries to make lectures as helpful as possible. You can tell that he DID really think about the stuff before teaching. Everything is memorised in his mind. He didn't bring anything other than a piece of paper to the class. And I never saw him looking at that piece of paper. First class treatment!
Such a genius. Explains things really well . Highly recommended.

Genius prof. rarely teaches undergrads. His lectures follows his book(s) word for word. We all opened his book and followed along. HW is decent and tests are related to the material taught. But his tests are only 5-10 questions so you better not get any wrong or else your grade is toast! Makes you wonder if you'll ever be as smart as he is.
professor with a decentunderstanding of the topics he is teaching
Really nice teacher

Every class features a group project, and the group members are both variable and randomly assigned. Attendance is mandatory. Additionally, there is a "warm-up quiz" administered at the beginning of every class session.
I liked him, he can be a little difficult to get used to. He has a great understanding of the material and is always willing to answer questions and help.

Hard class, but he's very passionate about Physics and uses demonstrations to explain material. Very helpful in person as well. I see a lot of complaints about his accent but if you mind your professor's having accents, get over it! If you plan on going into research, you're going to be interacting with people from many countries, so get used to it

Bodek tends to mumble and has a slight accent but if you sit in the front, you should be fine. Physics is complicated in itself so it's irrational to expect a complete understanding of the material by just attending lecture. To really understand the material, go to workshop, do the homework, and read the textbook. Otherwise, he's a decent teacher
excellent teacher. I set in the front seats so that I could focus on the lectures.  I liked the demonstrations and the connections that he made to modern physics, e.g. quarks and black holes.
Amazing teacher.  Must have this guy teach physics!!!!  If not for him i dont know where i would be.

As a professor Bodek wasn't good. He is hard to understand and I don't like how he runs the class. If you do go see him in person, though, he is actually a nice guy. I  recommend going to him directly if you are having issues because I have had issues with the TAs and he is usually willing to help. He is just too smart to teach a basic course.

If you used to like physics, don't hang on to that notion for long. Absolutely awful, attendance is "mandatory" because of in-class quizzes that count for 1% of your final grade. The man developed the basis of the quark and should've shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1990, but he can't even get the powerpoint to work half the time.

Abandon all hope, ye who enter here.  Bodek may be a brilliant researcher, but all the dire stuff people have written here is true.  It is kind of hilarious that his demonstrations always fail, though.

He is really, really bad.  Sometimes very difficult to understand and follow due to bad handwriting and a strong accent.  Seems like a nice guy, perhaps, and is extremely intelligent, but just a horrible lecturer.  May god have mercy on your soul if you have him.

Bodek has to be one of the worst professors I have ever met!! Can't even understand him and he wears a microphone. All his in class experiments are a complete fail. He thinks he the Ish!! Don't go to class find someone to do your in-class quizzes. gkll;gslksl if you can understand this then you will do very well!!

I don't know where to begin with this professor. Currently taking this class has diminished my interest in physics. Bodek doesn't even speak a language; he mumbles and stutters for literally the whole class time. He's not accessible and has the worst handwriting. His mini experiments in lecture are always a fail and he's so bad with technology.

Pretty much the worst lecturer I've ever had the misfortune to have.  He's a smart man and he tries very hard, but his convoluted proofs and tangents (which are not and should not be tested) accomplish nothing.  On top of that, he has a nearly indecipherable accent and MUMBLES.  And lecture notes?  Forget it--they look like Rorshach blots.

Worst lecturer I've ever encountered. Mumbles, but the real problem is that he spent lecture time proving various equations (using calculus over many people's heads) and correcting his own algebra, rather than explaining concepts or showing how to do problems. Explained potential energy using subatomic particles and graphs...way to overcomplicate.

Avoid this guy. Can't understand a word he says... and he mumbles. Such a smart man, wants to help, but can't convey it to the students. I have learned everything from the book and my TA and not a single thing from him all semester. Probably the worst course I have taken at UR.
Totally Incomprehensible in class....more like disorganized. Worst online lecture notes ever, it looks like a five year old wrote them.
Professor Gamm is an amazing and enthusiastic professor. His class even though it has a lot of work is well worth it and will expand your knowledge of the US government.

You leave this course feeling like you truly learned. Though this is probably the hardest course in PSCI, I recommend it to every student taking the major. Gamm is super approachable, I enjoy his lectures, and his office hours will direct your essays. Only reason he isn't a 5 is his grading system means you're best doing the minimum amount of work.
Lectures are a waste of time, and classes are boring and unnecessary. I would never take them, if not for credit. He is a good person, but not a good professor.

comment: I love this man. Great lecturer, funny, has great personality. I learned so much about US history and why our country is the way it is. Review for midterm and final.

IT HELPS A LOT WITH THE PAPER) you'll be okay!!

This class was one of my favorites I've taken at UofR! Professor Gamm was a great teacher and I really enjoyed the class with him. comment: Professor Gamm is a fantastic lecturer and a passionate teacher. I never disliked a reading, and the material was relevant. The class consists of around an essay a week plus 100-150 pages of weekly readings. The essays are graded by TA's, so it can be difficult to score well, but the TA's are helpful. It's hard, but a must for any PSCI student.

comment: This is the worst class for the political science major and the hardest class I have ever taken. Too much reading and too many papers imo

comment: A lot of reading and a lot of writing for this course. The grading criteria for the papers, which there's 1 every week, is pretty arbitrary and difficult; it takes a long time to learn how to write about what Gamm is looking for. It's a fascinating class and he's a good lecturer but the TAs are extremely tough, so take the class at your own risk
Extremely tough grader, TAs grading even tougher. Lot of readings and homework. Just don't overestimate yourself. Trust me.
Prof. Gamm is the best political science lecturer I have ever had. Very passionate and bright. Get ready to read and write alot. Exam is difficult, but doable. Great professor!
Too many textbooks and too much reading. Grading is arbitrary and often makes 0 sense at all. Feedback was never useful. That being said the professor is extremely passionate about the subject.

comment: I took 202 and 241W with Gamm and he's truly a professor who deeply values his students' points of view. Though he assigns a lot of reading and is a tough grader, you will become a better writer for it. Utilize his office hours and don't be afraid to speak up.

Professor Gamm is a phenomenal professor. Not only is he brilliant, but he is a passionate professor who  genuinely cares about his students. I would recommend his class to anyone who wants to be challenged, and to anyone who sincerely loves to learn.
His instructions are clear, he's pretty helpful. There's though tons of readings for the class and it is literally VERY hard.

Very good professor, very engaging and passionate and approachable.  The people who complain about him are usually the type who think they deserve an A just for showing up and doing their homework or who whine about having to read --gasp--100 pages a week!  At one of the top Universities in the country?  NOOOO!

Professor Gamm is an extremely good professor because he is extremely passionate about his teachings. However, this class is just awful because of the expected amount of reading. He expects the students to read about 100 pages per week. The TA's are also very tough at grading which makes receiving good grades on papers and tests extremely difficult

Class should be called "History of people who write papers about Political Science."  Lectures are very good, but he expects you to respond to paper questions in a very specific manner. Winds up being more about the reading itself than what the reading is actually about, and this drives me up the wall.

Professor Gamm is fantastic. Have had him for both 202 and 241, Urban Change. I've found him to be extremely interested in his students' thoughts and easy to engage with. 241 has a significant workload but I think it's fair because of how in-depth the course is. His lectures are always insightful, and it's clear he cares deeply about the subjects.

Lectures are ok. EXCESSIVE reading and writing. TAs were extremely tough graders. You'll likely feel you didn't get the grade you deserve on papers. Would never take this class if not required for major - uninteresting and overbearing. Wish Gamm would take a step back and re-examine the course.

His lectures are not great. They are average - starting out pretty good in the beginning of the semester and declining into oblivion and seemingly irrelevant information. TAs are harsh and probably not uniform in grading. WAYYY too much reading - excessive writing. Would never take the class if it weren't required for the major. Ever.

He is an amazing lecturer but if you try to discuss with him outside of class you feel like you are being tested rather than assisted. It is frustrating working so hard and not receiving the grade you think you deserve because of the arbitrary value he puts on certain things over others.

Aloof and above the students, good lecturer but good luck talking to him outside of class.  seems to care about students until he actually has to do something, then his condescending attitude is evident.

Gamm is a good lecturer. BUT he is not very approachable or understanding. He doesn't really care about his students. It is very hard to shake him from his devotion to academia (good and bad) and robot students.
great lecturer, tas are not very helpful and are harsh graders but he is always helpful in office hours, a lot of work but a worthwhile class to take

Really good lecturer though sometimes covers seemingly irrelevant material.  Very very long (but fair and relatively easy) final.  Extremely large amounts of reading (sometimes it's a little excessive and unnecessary).  Grading between sections (by the TAs) wasn't always consistent, and Gamm is very reluctant to override the TAs.

Though not liked by all, Professor Gamm is a very strong teacher and a good person. He's a tough but very fair grader; if you're willing work hard and are interested in the material, you should do well. He runs a very structured course, good for organized people (or people trying to get more organized).
Gamm is a remarkable lecturer.  Truly inspiring.

fantastic lecturer. i think you would have to try to fall asleep. he is always very excited to be there. only downside is his grading. It is pretty easy to get a B but near impossible to get an A. I think he gave only 3 in a class of more than a 100. def recommend taking one of his classes

Amazing lecturer, I have rarely looked at the clock during Gamm's classes. Very friendly and interested in getting to know his students. He expects a lot of work, but grades fairly. Professor Zhang is a nice lady, and she really tries her best to make the class interesting, but I think the course materials should be more organized. The tests are based on lectures and the whole two books and the questions are very specific. It is hard to tell what to concentrate on.

This class is based off 4 tests on readings from 2 textbooks. They ask 8 IDs and 2 short answers. They are hard, and ask very specific questions despite covering like 100 pages of reading each. However, this means there is no final or midterm. Prof Zhang is a nice, no nonsense lady. I respect her a lot. However this does not seem like a 100 level.

Professor Zhang is responsible and knowledgeable, she makes the class really interesting by various materials, and she is native speaker Chinese thus I feel that I learned to view China from a broader mindset and leaned the truest aspect of China without biases from the western ideology. definitely would take her class again.
Very intelligent and interesting, though the workload/expectations/grading didn't seem to match a 100 level course. Otherwise, it was a really great class.
Truly the greatest of all time
Tiger is the goat.

Tiger is so engaging and sweet. He creates an encouraging environment, and if you apologize for messing up he'll tell you not to worry because you're still learning. He's a pretty easy grader, but he shares tons of opportunities to connect with the Deaf community and pushes people to get more involved with ASL outside of class. Amazing prof :)

Professor Balint is a great ASL teacher! I had never taken any sign language courses before so I was nervous walking in that I would fall behind. However, Prof Balint creates a safe space inside the classroom where you feel ok to make mistakes and learn from them. I always felt prepared for exams. Make sure to attend lectures for the practice!

Tiger is super funny and a great professor. The homework was never too difficult and he is a fair grader. I loved his class! 

I recommend going to ASL club in addition to the class to practice signing with others

I honestly don't get the über negative ratings. Sure, he can be a bit dull and his assignments are difficult -- but the essays are mostly graded by the TAs, who are pretty horrible. He seems like a friendly, witty guy who keeps his lectures interesting with subtle wit. He can be a bit foggy sometimes but he is a good man.
Yes, lectures are boring. Yes, they are also essential. Book is the key to success. It IS possible to do well in this class, plenty of extra credit opportunities. Just keep up with the reading.

I really don't understand why he has such a high rating. His lectures are absolutely painful to sit through. He assigns reading that covers very difficult subjects, only to devote a few seconds to in class. I learned more reading the book than from him. His exams are confusing;interpreting the questions are difficult. Worst PSY prof I've had.

Okay, he is just the worst. I don't understand anything he says, and he can't spell, and I have no idea what the prompt for any of his questions mean so I'm so confused and his test questions come out of no where and he makes me cry because I hate him so much and I am crying right now because he is literally ruining my life. He looks like a seahors

McAdam is awesome. He was also my academic adviser. He can be pretty vague and mystic at times, however, he is a great professor with a ton of knowledge about EVERYTHING going on at the university, especially within the psych department. Wish I had taken PSY 101 with him too!
Fun and vibrant.

Great professor!  Very funny guy!  His tests were challenging but if you completed the 2nd answer sheet it certainly made up for it.  Very fair class.  Do the psych studies for extra credit - they are fun and it makes an A very attainable!
He is very funny. But the tests are difficult.

Great guy and a fun class. Tests can be somewhat stressful, but you get two tries so get a fews extra points. Write down notes on stuff he spends a long time on in the lecture, there will probably be a tricky question on it in the next test.
Excellent professor. Quite entertaining- keeps your attention. Fair grader- but tricky tests. Read text and take notes in class and you'll do well.
He's one of the best professors I've had. He keeps your attention during lecture and is very interesting and informative. His tests can be very hard though, so prepare for them well.
If you focus and do all the reading required, you will come out with a very decent work. Watch out for his test, they can be verrrrry tricky. But overall, an amazing professor, very approachable.

This class was challenging, but if you do the work, you'll come out with a good grade and a love of psychology. I'm actually considering it as a minor, or even a double major, after taking this class. Such a great instructor. Two thumbs up!
No Comments
His lectures are very interesting, but his tests are difficult. The course is really informative though.
his tests were soooo hard, but the class was really interesting and he's an entertaining man.

Great in PSY 101,wouldn't take 101 with anyone else.The tests require extra time and effort. HOWEVER-PSY113 is totally different.(relatively new course)but it is one of the worst classes I have ever taken and during this course he is the worst:everything unclear and difficult.nearly impos.to do well

He's got a split-curriculum -what he teaches during lectures, and what's in the book; he tests you on Both.  Context clues were the biggest help on his annoying tests, the less I studied the better I tended to do on them.

I don't know what prof. you all had, but i can't stand this man, or the class.  He tries to be funny, but it's usually just wierd, and 113 is so boring, i would fall asleep even if i wasnt at all tired.  I hated the class with a passion.
Best Prof I had at UR. Engaging lectures...never knew what to expect.
I did not like him, he was unhelpful and cold when I asked him about something on the syllabus which wasnt clear which other people had also had a problem with.
Hilarious guy but if you skip a couple lectures or don't read the book, you're screwed on the tests.
Lectures are great, knows his stuff and makes the material engaging.
Great teacher, very knowledgeable.  Tests weren't hard if you paid attention in class.  Very funny too, one of my favorite classes!
very funny, and a good teach
loved the lectures
No Comments
A great teacher with a great sense of humor that keeps his lectures interesting.
Enthusiastic, funny, great with students.
nice guy, very comfortable teaching
Funny as hell, some of the most enjoyable lectures I've had
tests are too hard
No Comments
my DAD had him for a professor 30 years ago!

good lecturer

Mihai is one of the most enthusiatic math professors i've ever had. He absolutely loves what he does and expresses that during class. The only problem with him is he writes way to fast leaving most of the class in the dust and skips over some steps during a problem that he expects us to know, which some of us dont. Go to his office after hours.

I took Mihai's math 210 1.5 years ago and now I'm taking his math250. He is hot, nice, and funny but honostly he doesn't know what he is teaching at least for math 250... and for math 210, he doesn't explain things clearly but rather gives out how to use formulas. and I saw him several times in gym. Hot and friendly but not that helpful honestly.
Explained the math in class very clearly; Very helpful in office hours; Exams are reasonable.

Mihai very much loves what he does and puts forth an honest effort. That, however, does no coincide with teaching ability. He has a very roundabout way of teaching that never actually teaches you the methods needed. Without fail, my undergrad TA has explained in 50 minutes what Mihai fails to explain in 150. I do not recommend him by any means.
So nice and Super Hot! Really passionate about math.

Sometimes he's too smart for his own good, but he truly cares more about his students than any other professor at UofR. He gladly meets with you outside of class when you're confused and really wants you to learn.

Mihai is a really cute, funny guy, and it's obvious that he is passionate about math and teaching it. He wants students to be passionate too. The problem is that his tests are difficult and he sometimes doesn't understand why a student can't grasp a concept as easily as he can. Overall, great teacher IF you're good at math.
Best math professor I've ever had. Good humor. Actually explains the math well.
Super nice guy, really tries to explain it from a students point of view so you can understand it. Very helpful in office hours too. Exam's aren't too difficult.

A great professor who knows what he is talking about. He really cares about his students and is willing to meet with you outside of class if need be. One of the best math professors I have had thus far at Rochester. The material in the class is difficult, but Mihai does a great job explaining it.

Very entertaining lecturer who's not only hilarious but willing to go over material until students understand it. This is good because there's a lot of readings, many of which are at a higher level than I personally had ever read in Spanish before. Fairly straightforward essays, the partial exams were strange but manageable.

comment: Very rude. Harassed student for registering for his course, which he left open, before the add/drop period ended after only 3 lectures having passed. Complained about being contacted in Spanish for a Spanish class. If he didn't want anyone to add his class anymore, he should have closed the listing with the registrar.

Prof. RH is a good but imperfect professor. While I came out of the class definitely having learned a lot, it wasn't exactly what I expected. He seemed to lose the focus on Latin America midway through and just wanted us to know the details of Freudian thought. As a Spanish major, I was hoping to learn more about its impact on the L.A. world.
Very tough grader and very writing/reading heavy, however he makes lecture super entertaining and is easily available outside of class.
You have to read a lot, it takes forever. It was very stressful for me, but he grades pretty fairly and is patient when you don't understand (esp bc his first language isn't English).

Very, VERY disorganized. Unclear, confusing. It's really difficult to follow what is going on in class. Lots of reading that is over our level. I would not recommend anyone to take this class, or anything else with this professor for that matter. However, if you need extra help he is willing to meet with you. It is very unhelpful because not clear.
I enjoyed this professor and he really knows how to make class fun.
Professor Rodriguez-Hernandez is always very clear with his expectations and is very big on using content specific  vocabulary when it comes to writing essays. He's pretty funny and easy going.

He's hilarious! Class is long so you'll obviously get tired but he does a great job of keeping you interested. He's a very tough grader but pay attention to his edits and edit your papers by yourself a couple of times before submitting and you should be good. Each week you're either writing or editing a paper but it's fun.

He is very funny and makes the 75 minutes bearable. He's a hard grader, but he wants you to improve and understand everything. Tests aren't hard, essays are fun, class is interesting, reading is cool. Raul is great
Very quirky and endearing. Class was a lot of fun, and he does know a lot about spanish literature. Very approachable.
Quirky and likable; take him if you can as soon as you can (his classes tend to fill quickly).
He is simply an awesome, funny, smart man. Also way easier than the other 200 professors. TAKE HIS CLASS!
Definitely knowledgeable on literature and theory, but he can be too specific with the papers making them very difficult. Talks a lot if you don't.
Nice professor, puts forth a good effort, but a little bit confusing sometimes.  Adorably wacky.
very helpful, good professor, very knowledgeable

Not bad as a Spanish prof.  Horrible for the major seminar- he tried to include way too much information and made class a drudgery.  Plus, rumor has it he didn't even read our final papers!
GO AWAY

Interesting course and lecturer, and he talked about some topics in machine learning/neural networks, which was nice. The class felt a bit disorganized sometimes, but I expect that's because it was his first time teaching this course. Exams were very easy.

CSC 171 will be very challenging if you do not have any coding experience. The content seems to be fairly fine, but the exams were incoherent with the slides that he taught through the lectures, making exam tough, though the hw and the project were fine. He changed exam styles frequently,  students may get very different grades at different times.

Class will be difficult if you don't have coding experience. He is clearly knowledgeable about this subject, but this gets in the way of the lectures. He speeds through examples and ends 20 minutes early. Very disorganized and must be reminded to post lectures and review slides. Grading criteria is clear and there is not a great emphasis on exams.

He's a nice professor and covers a lot of AI content, both classic and modern. 
However, his grading scale is tough—an A starts at 94, so missing a couple of quiz questions can cost you. It feels UNFAIR, especially since he's the only CS professor I know who uses such a high cutoff. Students in other professors might have it easier.

comment:
Really cares about the subject and makes learning fun which is my top priority, but he can be messy which can be somewhat hard to follow, but he's super nice.
Rate my Professor is kind of bull, but ill let you know all my friends in his class really like him as a professor

Incoherent shallow lectures that don't touch anywhere near the amount of topic you are expected to know to actually do well in the exams. The slides are incomprehensible and you are given no other material to study with. There is a textbook but he flatly assigns 80+ pages of it per week and gives you no clue as to which parts of it are important.

He just rants about ML topics and doesn't give the backbone to learn this discipline well. There is an attempt to skip a bunch of domain relevant knowledge to get to new methods that are “better” or more “useful”. Projects are confusing and he gets behind; many times there was no submission area for a homework or project due that day.

Non majors or new to coding may find this course difficult as the content is pretty rushed. Prof does good job of giving you opportunities to improve ur grade and truly looks out for students. Recommend reading the txtbook and learning on your own to fill gaps.

Very nice professor, and the course is well-structured. Grading is 100% transparent, so you can easily study by your own too.

Little bit hard to understand sometimes, because of rush. And also there are some mistakes that he does. But overall, good.

Great professor! Machine learning with Purtee was super fair, with assignments graded quite leniently and with extended deadlines for a lot of them. The final exam was all multiple choice and true/false, and was pretty easy. I wish he'd delved even deeper into the math, but I'm pretty happy with the way he taught and structured the course!

You'll only pass if you alr know Java. Bc he's known Java for so long, he assumes everyone else does and the assignments are every two weeks but they're really hard. They will take two weeks. Also, I had a 103 degree fever for a week and had to go to the ER 2 times the week before my midterm on Monday and I asked him for a make-up and he said no.

Love this guy, he cares about his students and the topic. Though his passion for java gets a little in the way of his teaching because he tends to under-explain and over-exemplify topics because he's too eager to show the code and doesn't realize this is an introductory course where students need a slower pace and more explanation to succeed.

You can tell Prof Purtee loves the material and wants you to love it too. Exams are fair as well as the grading for the final project. Avg grade for students was high too.  Be careful to make sure you're doing readings and watching videos about the material because lectures are often unclear due to Purtee's passion.  Always ask what's on exams.

I can tell he's good at programming himself, but he's not a good instructor in teaching. The only reason why I got an A is I took Java during high school so I was fully prepared for this class. You can barely learn anything from his lectures...

Your probably better off teaching yourself using the textbook and Youtube videos than going to lectures. After taking CSC161 with Dr. Polak (absolute queen) last semester and enjoying it, I really wanted to like this class --- HUGE let down.

Nice professor, and he always wants to make the class interesting and not "that" hard to students. To success, need some kind of Calculus (Partial Derivative and Matrix Calculus mainly), Linear Algebra, and probability theory, but not that much. However, if you really want to "learn something", I will still suggest CS 229 from Stanford.

Overall pretty solid professor. Lectures are generally interesting, although sometimes he rushes through information and then ends class 20 mins early. Homework and projects are very fair and honestly fun.

Prior to taking this class I had little experience with CS. His lectures are often not helpful and disorganized. I would recommend self-studying this class. It is the only way to understand what he is saying. He often changes the grading criteria so beware. Overall the class was somewhat enjoyable. He was not good at responding to emails.

Purtee is one of those professors that actually cares a lot and is passionate about what he teaches. Nerdy guy who cares about your learning more than just giving you a grade. Super lenient when it comes to giving extra points on exams. Always accessible outside of class and clearly cares for his students. Great prof for an intro class!

Very disorganized lectures, wish they were recorded cause he doesn't post the code before lectures so it is hard to remember what he says as he is typing out code. As a person with zero coding experience, the class was fair, I did do a lot of reading and watching videos and that's how I mainly learned. Purtee is a nice guy with passion, but not 4me

He's a good teacher, I just think he's teaching style might not be for everyone
Yeah sure he is a bit messy, but he actually likes CS which honestly is super important!
He cares about his students, he makes class funny, his homework while a bit tuff is genuily fun to make and he is very acciseble and receptive to feedback!

I switched to this class about three weeks into the semester. Professor Purtee made sure I could catch up and helped me get on track. He is very kind and cares that the students do well in class. He tries to make lectures entertaining and goes through code in class. Assignments aren't too bad and you can always ask TAs/the prof for help.

I think he is a genuine caring guy who loves Computer Science.

Lectures, however, are a flip of a coin.
Sometimes it's entertaining, fun, and he explains things coherently.
Other times, it feels like he got no sleep or is extremely bored, so he rushes through the material in what feels like five minutes.
He is very docile and generally kind.

If you want an "easy" CS course - take 161. 171 will challenge you if you do not have prior CS experience. Purtee is OK - he cares and wants to help his students but struggles to communicate effectively. The difficulty of the course depends entirely on your prior knowledge. If you are experienced, this is an easy A. If not, get ready to work.

The worst professor I've encountered. He constantly altered the course grading criteria throughout the semester. Many peers were unsure if they could get an A due to his erratic policy changes. It's shocking that such an irresponsible approach exists in an intro CS course, potentially dampening many students' passion.

(Fall 2022 course) 3 homework projects and 3 quizzes, no exams. Projects are easy but quizzes need some effort. He has a slow teaching pace and sometimes makes little mistakes during lectures. But he will adjust the coverage  of quizzes accordingly and curve the final scores to save all students if the average scores look bad. BTW, TAs are nice.

I had Purtee in CSC-171: An Introduction to CS. This course was by no means an introduction. I attended nearly every lecture, read from the textbook, went to labs, & still around a month & a half in I was very lost. I don't know if this is because of flaws in the way the course was designed, or Purtee's teaching. Still, he could have done better.
not very organized, exams are harder than he thinks(in-person paper exams because of chat), free textbooks, and lectures are too complex for beginners. Great guy though, he can be very humorous.

Funny, transparent, and great guy. He's kind of confusing and all over the place, but he's always trying new things and trying to get better. Exams are harder than he expects, but he tries to correct this. Good introduction to CS but not good intro to programming. If you've never programmed I HIGHLY recommend taking CSC 161 before this class.

He modified the whole courses schedule this semester which makes everything more difficult ( not fair at all). Now you have to reach 95 to get an A in AN INTRO CLASS. His lecture was so boring. Have no idea what he is talking about. Will not ever take his class.
He is a typical "CS dude", he has a clear passion for cs but in my opinion, his lectures were very disorganized and is not suited for teaching... at least not an intro course!

I found the class super easy. Students completely new to Computer Science will probably find it difficult. Purtee wants to helpful and teach but often gets mixed up when explaining important topics. He really tries which I appreciate but I feel that he isn't suited to teach an intro course.

I personally found the class very easy. Labs take 1-2 hours to complete and projects may take 6-7 hours. Lectures are sometimes all over the place but Purtee is really enthusiast and eager to help his student succeeds.

Professor Purtee is a nice professor and generally gives decent lectures compared to some of the other professors in the department. That being said, I would not rely on lectures to succeed and like many other CS courses, a lot of the learning is up to you. The class was overall useful and you can get a good grade as long as you put in time.

Professor Purtee is a nice guy and really great with grading criteria (if it works you get an 100) but my god he is a horrible lecturer. This class was not accessible for people who haven't coded before. He doesn't explain concepts well at all, and his coding demos are useless as well because he types so fast that everyone gets lost immediately.

Professor Purtee demonstrates a genuine love for the subject, but does not know how to apply it properly and teach his students in a manner that will help them succeed. The assignments he gives are far more complex than what he says in class, and he isn't lenient at all with extensions, 5 points are deducted per day even if you have a good reason.

He is a funny guy. CSC 171 was really not an intro course, i had no coding experience and it was VERY difficult for me. The lectures aren't that helpful, many people did not go to them. Labs/Projects took approximately 1-3 hours, they were difficult. Quizzes are online through blackboard which was nice.

Clearly loves the subject, not super good at explaining things. CSC 171 is supposed to be an intro class for complete beginners, but if you have no background in CS, expect the homework and projects to take an absurd amount of time. The grading is super straightforward - if your code works, full credit.
So good. Really funny and I learned the fundamentals of Java. Adorable man

Prof. Purtee is a very understanding professor, who usually gave extensions on assignments and offered extra credit on projects. The class was graded very fairly. However, he does go a bit fast in lectures and is a bit all over the place, so be prepared for that.

adam purtee is a funny little man. csc171 lectures arent required, i guess you could pass this course only by the graded zybooks, but the lectures were pretty informative when i ended up paying attention (im sorry for falling asleep in class prof purtee). projects in general were VERY fair, make sure to put in the effort and its an easy 90%+ grade

You get what you put in. Good lectures and organized PowerPoints make the concepts very easy to be understood. The final project is challenging but it pushes you and make you learn. Even though the lectures are said to be "optional", it gives you a different perspective on the same concepts which will help you understand better.
I took CS171 in spring 2021. I never attend lecture, and I basically studied everything myself through zybook. Not a bad class and not a bad professor. Take this class if you need!
Great teacher and very lenient, almost too lenient.

This is not a critique of Prof. Purtee's teaching, but a WARNING to those who want recommendations from him! He tends to overpromise and stands you up right before the application due! So if you really want him to recommend you, be sure to have a backup recommender and cross your fingers.

Professor Purtee is very accommodating. He very frequently extends the deadlines of all types of assignments. Quizzes in this class are very quick and straightforward. The only difficult things are projects, but you have a lot of time to do those
Professor Purtee is a really funny guy. He can sometimes be a bit disorganized in class, but he has a clear passion for the topic and makes class interesting with practical demonstrations
His lecture is important if you want to get good grades.

CSC 246 is quite challenging and you must have strong mastery of linear algebra and multivariate calculus in order to succeed, but it is really worth taking, especially for those who want to explore further in theoretical machine learning and AI.

Adam is very nice. I can't say he is perfect teacher but most of times his lectures were enough for me to understand the topic (except for the graphics part). CSC171 is an easy course overall, just start your projects early and everything will be great. Adam is funny and easy grader.

Prof Purtee was an amazing teacher to have, especially for CSC171. He makes sure that everyone feels included in the class and his lectures are very informing. His office hours are also a great resource to ask questions.

He is a really nice professor who cares about students. However, the class in general is really hard and for students with no CS background it can be very fast so it is highly advised to have a study group for his class. This class will feel like a 6 credit course

Dr. Purtee is a great lecturer. He really cares about students and does his best to help students of varying computer science background. He is extremely helpful outside of class! (GO TO OFFICE HOURS). The homeworks are based off lecture material and he always gives recommended reading for if you aren't sure if you understand the material.

This was my first ever official CSC course, and Prof. Purtee is great at bringing people unfamiliar with Computer Science into the fold. Lectures are often very engaging and the assignments are clear and fairly assessed. Not a test heavy course either. Would recommend to those looking to get into CS.
I have to basically teach myself everything. Don't see the point of taking this class.

Taking professor Purtee's class is extremely miserable. His lectures were completely ambiguous, confusing, and preposterously fast. In the class, he taught how to calculate 2 to the power of 2 is 4, and the homework is programming Angry Bird! Yes, he offered materials, but those are nothing more useful than himself. Self-teaching is the only way.

Has his own online space(Piazza) for students to give feedback and ask questions. Extremely helpful. You can really feel like he wants you to do good and understand everything. Liked his energy, his lectures are fine, homework just enough. Overall? Prof. Purtee is the the definition of a good professor.

Prof Purtee has a pleasant teaching style. His humorous ways of speaking really made the CS lectures less stressful and sleepy. Homework and quizzes are pretty easy to handle. The projects are not very hard, though they did take you some time to figure out and finish. The only things that seem to pull down your grade a bit are the 2 paper exams

I barely learned anything in this class, which was disappointing since it seemed exciting when I signed up. There weren't any exams, so not a lot of incentive to pay attention to the lectures. And the prof seemed unprepared to teach some of the material, so one of the students ended up having to teach everyone how to use the software we were using.

Dr. Hunter was really helpful and informative during class. Her lectures are clear for the most part; the only part of the class I didn't enjoy was the final project. Still, she provided a lot of the materials I requested for the project and went above and beyond to ensure that I knew how to use it. Really great person and teacher.

As a person, she was respectful and approachable. I appreciated the safe space she created around sensitive topics. She was human outside the teacher role. She helped break me free of strict writing rules that I was taught to follow. This new way to write is more liberating and useful to me. I could never thank her enough for being my instructor.

Kate Soules at first grades really really easy, but on the final paper her entire attitude completely changes. I went from getting 100 on all the papers to an 81 on the final paper. The way she grades is so unpredictable. The topics are so abstract and boring. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. If you like zombies and cyborgs then take it.

Kate Soules is the best writing professor ever. I cannot believe how kind and thoughtful she is. She really has our best interest at heart, and is willing to put in the time and effort to make us better writers. Even with so much going on in her personal life, she made sure to help us with our research papers. She is an extraordinary human being.

I love Professor Soules! Whenever I have a meeting with her, or just talk to her, she really works hard to understand our point of view and readers, writers, students and humans. She is extremely respectful and engaging and I would not have had such a great writing experience without her.
She was always kind and helpful and just wanted us to succeed.

Soules, based on what I hear from my friends, is one of the best Writing105 professors at UR. Her rubrics are clear and she will provide you with ample feedback on your rough drafts so you can write and A level final draft. The class was interesting and she is understanding when students do not do their readings. Great professor.

comment: I adored this class because of the instructor! She made an intimidating topic and course structure feel doable, and I am so grateful for her investing so much personal time in making us better writers.

She was engaging, interesting, informative, and most importantly fun. The activities/assignments she made us do felt like they actually mattered and wasn't just busy work. Every formal assignment I actually felt myself growing stronger as a writer.

She is very understanding of unforseen circumstances and was ALWAYS available and willing to help improve my writing or give suggestions. Every assignment given to the class helped me become a better reader/writer in its own unique way. Professor Soules is a gem and finding instructors like her are not easy to find in the world of academia.

Prof. Soules is so kind and caring. She is also very understanding. Although the class had a lot of thought reading assignments, she still discusses them in class and doesn't force you to participate. Very encouraging when it comes to your paper and gives good feedbacks. She is also pretty chill compared to other writing profs I heard from friends.

this class was a bit rough for a summer class. not an easy A. so much reading and participation is really important. that being said i liked the material and i think she made it a good environment even though we were doing hard things and talking about hard stuff like racism. a lot of your grade was the final paper.

Kind, considerate & supportive. Shows empathy towards students, provides in-depth, insightful feedback, & works extremely hard to make sure the course is interesting, varied and engaging. She is personally invested in your learning, & wants to make sure you succeed. Great sense of humor & easy to talk to; exciting and engaging classes.

comment: this class was the hardest thing iv'e done. she makes you write. go to office hours though. i got so much feedback i thought i would fail but she changed my life and i don't love writing but i got a really good grade and i'm waayyyyy mroe confident now.

comment: Kate Soules is one of the most caring professors I've had so far at UR. She understands mental health and prioritizing that over everything. She gives really good feedback. Her class was also really fun which I didn't expect from a writing class. But it's so obvious she cares about the stuff she teaches and about her students. Loved this class.

LOVE soules. i took wrtg105, and she was so lovely to work w. was rly just trying to bang out my writing reqs but ended up enjoying class- its a lot of in depth reading and wrtg, but there were only 3 big essays over the course, which all included a lot of helpful peer and prof review during the assigned period. go to office hours, wonderful advice

comment: I took this as a summer course. We crammed a whole semester into just a couple of weeks and the class meetings were 4 hours long which was h-a-r-d. She was kind and engaging and encouraging during class discussions. We covered some hard material but it was okay if we went off topic a bit. Loved the things we read like Angels in America and stuff.
