comment: She's an interesting combination of Voldemort and Professor Umbridge. But seriously, I would rather go into the Forbidden Forest than take her class.
I didn't wear a seat belt in the car ride to this class because I wasn't sure if I wanted to survive the drive.

She mislead multiple students about the requirements for the final paper (while refusing to admit this) and did not answer questions clearly. The lectures were very interesting, but the assignments are horrible-- page limits are impossibly low, and then she takes off points for not including more specifics. She's smart but needs to learn to teach.

Professor Hazelton is very knowledgeable about her subject but her class has several drawbacks. She tends to heavily penalize anyone who disagrees with her and she refuses to admit a mistake she has made. She is very susceptible to flattery and be ready to do this or you won't do well in her class.

I highly regret taking her class IR228 discuss. She has killed all the passion I had for International Relations. I did not find her helpful. She has made my Spring 2012 semester at the UofR difficult. Very sarcastic too.She is very happy to give you an F even if you show up to class, participate and write your papers.
She is very helpful, but expects you to work very  hard. If you want an easy course, do NOT take a class with her.

If you are interested in international security, Hazelton is the way to go. She expects you to do your reading and come to lecture, but you can learn a lot. She is also great about answering questions outside of class.

Don't take this course! The professor is really bad. It's too much coursework in very little time (although interesting!) and the professor is tone-deaf to the level of intellect of students. There are tests every day on topics taught in the previous class (sometimes for topics taught the same day) and it's all closed book. DO NOT RECOMMEND!
It is a language class so it is very difficult, but she wants you to learn, and she is very patient and caring, and such an amazing person.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: Very unclear lecture. Almost no examples. Handwritings are extremely unclear. Just avoid him otherwise you will be regret hahaha. Avoid avoid avoid. Worst prof I've ever met. Yu can hardly learn anything from him.
Lectures are extremely unclear. Learned all material from outside sources.

Lectures weren't always clear or useful, but he was good with extra help, and the material tested was pretty much the same exact questions as webwork.  The tough webwork assignments were definitely worth it in the end and served as excellent test preparation.  Medium level difficulty.
Reading the book was way more helpful than going to his class

He was more about theory instead of showing examples, so when the online homework came around, it was difficult to finish without going to office hours, which still didn't help me fully understand problems. I did a lot of the problems in the textbook, but that still didn't help, and was a waste of time, becaue the exam problems were different.

He is awful!! I can't follow anything he says and neither can anyone around me. The class is easy so you feel like you don't have to put in a lot of effort, but then the test comes around and you realize that you never really learned the material. Also he won't give you any solutions to workshops or practice tests.

Gage is great.  He focused a lot more on theoretical concepts than applications but if you really paid attention to what he was saying the applications come naturally.  Hard to follow in lecture sometimes.  If you are lost there is a good chance everyone else is as well.  Stop him and ask him to explain something again, it will be good for everyone

Gage is the god of math... He somehow can at least appear to know everything known to man because of a few mathematical properties... I'm suprized that his head isn't 20 feet in diameter... Awesome guy although a little flighty.  I suggest getting help through email.  He's always very quick to respond and almost alwasy can lead you to an answer.

Good lecturer but his WebWork assignments didn't follow the lectures or the tests. If you take good notes you will do well on the WebWork, and if you read the book backwards and forwards you will do well on the tests. He's decent. I give him an A-.
Not really clear, but the content is easy enough for you to teach youself. Ask for help from TAs and not him. Needs to spend more time with examples then deriving random formulas and using variables
No Comments

Incredibly easy class with gage, the tests were mirror images of the practice tests.  Webwork was a b*tch and lectures were boring and didn't follow webwork.  He derives to much in class then showing how to apply the material.  However an easy class nonetheless

Avoid taking this class if Gage is teaching it.  He spends all his time talking theory and not enough time actually teaching the things you need to be learning.  Workshops are horrible and tests follow the same pattern.

Wasn't all to bad.  Too smart for his own good, does a lot of theoretical stuff without actually applying it to anything.  Leaving you with no clue how to do webwork.  Tests were very fair and curved fair.
he starts deriving an equation but never gets to the point where he tells you what the equation is, or shows you how to apply it!  goes off on tangents and never gets to the point....
i may be a moron who can barely take a derivative but that is due to my undiagnosed ADHD definitely not this guys fault he was a really good teacher
I thought he was a great professor.  He was very knowledgable and if you can keep up, you you will do well in the course.  I thought it was very esay to get an A.
An Uber-Geek who was not very approachable

Arguably the worst Calculus teacher on campus.  Knows the subject too well to teach it, i.e. he expects you to know most of the material right off the bat.  Also not very approachable.  You're best off taking another Calculus teacher if you can.

Terrible professor, would talk endlessly about mathematical topics secondary to teaching Calculus--this was supposed to be an application, not a theory course.  Would talk a lot about everything except getting to the meat of how to do problems.

The lectures and homework were fine, the exams were ridiculous. The homework was far easier than the exams, and thus did an awful job of preparing me for them. I failed the final after spending the last week reviewing the lecture material. Also, on short notice he gave a course eval incentive, then released the final grades prior to the deadline.

I have never had a more compassionate and passionate math professor. Belmirio is a stand-up gentleman and cares about the success of his students and the application of calculus to the outside world. Homework isn't overbearing and workshops allow you to apply knowledge in a mini-test format.

technically didn't have him but we had access to recordings of all math 141 professors. he's extremely helpful and his reviews prior to midterms or for webwork help literally saved me I appreciate him so much. only started watching his lectures towards the end, very sad I didn't earlier because they definitely would've helped me do better on exams

Prof. Galo is the man! I listened to the lectures from the other Calc professors to see which professor was the clearest teacher and they weren't even close to on par with him. He responds to emails really quickly and is always ready to help with the webwork. He really wants his students to understand the concepts, and really wants them to succeed.

Professor Galo is a great professor in that he actually works to help you succeed in the class and not only in getting a good grade, which is nice but also in helping you to truly understand the course material. Office hours are extremely helpful. His lectures are also very funny and he gives a lot of example problems that help a lot with webwork.

Professor Galo is a reason why this course was enjoyable to study. He tries to mix humor with his math content and is always open for participation from all students. He was always available to help me after class to provide any feedback. His helpful mentality and clarity in teaching made it easier to adjust to this class.

He is really a great professor. He is respectful, inspirational, and caring. He cares about students' understanding of the course material and their comfortability with math despite their background in math. He uses simple and relevant examples that make students easily understand the course material and concept taught in class.
Belmiro is very enthusiastic and holds workshops, recitations and office hours to help students struggling in Math.
Spends a huge amount of time helping students. Enthusiastic, funny, beautiful, smart, dedicated, exams are easy but always 1 or 2 hard problems. Actually, his accent is his only problem.

Really nice, puts a lot of time into giving feedback, if you go to office hours you will do better. Doesn't give the most clear instructions... so just ask for clarification. You're an adult communicate its not all on the teacher. Once you ask everything will become clear usually, if you TRY you will probably get at least a B in this class.

Great professor! The learning objectives are clear: students learn to analyze research papers. By the end of the course, you will probably become fluent in determining objectives, methods, and interpreting results. And with this comes the necessary workload. Be advised: if you are not interested in research, maybe this is not the professor for you.

This professor is AWFUL. Her lecture are pedantic, and the writing exercises are tedious busy-work that will be very harshly assessed. Only take this if you are taking no other classes besides this because this is how she treats the course. She has absolutely no respect for her students.

Great professor who made learning calc kinda funny/interesting. Would definitely take a class with Prof Chio again. His blackboard notes were easily the best of the 142 professors. Super helpful in class and in office hours if you had any questions

Ivan is one of the better profs I've had. He knows what he's doing, is always prepared, and we usually got out of lecture early. Sometimes I would get confused by his lectures; I think he overcomplicates some things but if you ask he will go back through the problem. I recommend taking his class.

This is the only professor that was able to actually teach me calculus. Calc 2 is an extremely hard subject but Dr.Chio somehow finds a way to make students understand the concepts well. Even if you can't make it to lecture, his notes are extremely thorough and easy to follow. His lectures are fun and interactive as well.

His lectures are a bit confusing because he goes through the material so quickly, but he is otherwise a great professor. If you reread the lecture notes you will usually understand what he is teaching. He is very funny and tries to make class interesting.
He's a great guy, but lowkey a bad teacher. Doesn't explain things very well
His notes are clear. I like him.

Ivan is a pretty solid lecturer, despite English not being his native language. He can get a bit sidetracked sometimes but he makes up for it by trying to stay as engaging as possible. The notes he uses and gives are also amazing. Could do a slightly better job of explaining things.
He is the best math professor I've ever seen in UR.

Calc 2 is a beast on its own, but Ivan made me excited to attend class. He's funny and sympathized with the students about having online class. He's super understanding and caring, I'd definitely take a course with him again. I could have put more effort into the course, so my grade doesn't reflect his teaching ability--that's my bad.

Took multiple classes and unfortunately still haven't learned the material. The lectures are not clear and it's very difficult to follow or actually pick up the language. If you want to learn Arabic, I'd recommend looking for another professor.

She is truly one of a kind and one of the best professors I have ever had! I have taken three classes with her, and she has been amazing every time. She is incredibly kind, understanding, and genuinely cares about her students and their success. Professors like her are so rare. I highly recommend her!

Taking Arabic 101 with Professor Alfatli was very easy. She is very understanding and genuine in her teaching. She cares about her students and wants to see them succeed in her class. There are weekly homeworks, one midterm, and a final exam. Attendance also counts towards your grade.
Amazing love her!!
SHE IS AMAZING! I would recommend!
This professor is a very nice, hardworking professor. As one of her students, I recommend Afrah for your professor.

Shes honestly the best professor Ive ever had ever since I joined this university. Most professors dont care but shes so considerate and caring that I was shocked because of how rare it was in this university. I recommend taking a class with her! Her classes are easy, as long as you have a general idea of the language youll get an A easily.
tags: ['Participation matters', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: She is one of the nicest professor in the university. She is really empathetic and genuinely cares about her students. The classes are extremely easy if you go to classes and listen to her. The exams are basically what she teaches in class which prompts you to not miss a class. A very easy A if you go to all the classes

She's a really nice and caring person who'll go out of her way to help you. The tests are easy and it is easy to do good in this class. She's good for all Arabic levels - 101, 102, and 103. She requires that one participates in the class though.

This professor is very caring. Besides the Arabic language being challenging, she makes it fun and interesting. Very understanding and accessible outside class. There are also conversation hours which are very helpful.
She is extremely nice and a very reasonable person. She cares for her students and tries her best to make learning easier. Would definitely want to take more classes with her.

This course is a bit harder than ARA 101. Knowing all the stuff from ARA 101 would be beneficial. The readings in this course get much longer and some writing is introduced. One also has to pay attention to grammar. The tests are easy though and if one studies, it's not hard to get an A.

She's a great professor for Arabic. 101 was easy and the tests are very easy as well. The class involves some participation so don't expect yourself to just come, sit, and then leave. The course involves some reading and learning of a new script (obv) so if one is completely unbeknownst to that, one has to put in some effort the first few weeks.

I really enjoyed taking ARA 101 with her. She has a humble nature and always facilitates her students in the best possible way. She tries her best to make learning Arabic easy for her students and her tests are easy if you pay attention in class and do the homework.
She is too foreign to understand and speaks too monotone. it usually put me to sleep in the class. it did not help that nobody showed up.

Objectively speaking BCSC 111 should be an easy course. However, this professor is literally the worst. Most of her TAs never took her class before, and her exams are hard (to the point of confusing some of her TAs!) If you try to give her advice or complain about the grade of the course, sorry, you will be rejected. The grading is kind of insane.

She is nice person and always reply to email but I truly don't like her lecture that much. Although she tried to make the classes engaged, it is still overall boring. I'm also not a huge fan to her speaking style. This class is overall very easy but grading is poorly designed. You need > 94 to get an A based on three 50 mcqs tests worth 30% each.

Poletti was a great BCS professor, and I really enjoyed her class. She tries to engage the class and involve us in the lecture which I loved. You do need >94% to get an A, but that is pretty doable as long as you go to class and pay attention.I would definitely take again if I could.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: BCS 111 is much easier than BCS 110, but her lectures are so boring and I definitely learned so much less. Her wording on exams is oftentimes very confusing, and she does not give points back. You need over a 94 to get an A, so while this class is very easy, getting an A is not that easy since you can only get 2 questions wrong on each exam.

Very good teacher, clear material, tests were straightforward, gave freedom of choice for the big end of year assignment which meant we could pick anything we were interested in as long as we could relate it to the general prompt
Ridiculously easy everyone should take it
Extremely easy compared to BCS111 and a nice professor! Not the most interesting class but her tests were fair/easy.

Absolutely nothing like BCSC 110 with Davis. Very relaxed and easy-going lectures. The exams aren't bad either, as long as you take notes and pay attention you'll be all good. She's pretty chill and a solid professor. Definitely would take this class again, easy to understand and learn. Took during COVID over Zoom.
The absolute sweetest, a true gem. Anyway yeah she's super nice and the tests are very straightforward. Just attend the lectures and pay attention and you should be good.
lowkey amazing

One of the best professors I have ever had. I was really dreading physics but the structure and lectures from this class were amazing. Retakes reduce pressure on exams and exams are fair. I could really tell that Mike cares about his students and wants them to succeed and enjoy physics. Sad he won't be teaching 114 next semester!

Best professor I've ever had. I prolonged taking physics as long as I could because I hated the subject. Mike allowed me to leave an exam without thinking how bad I did, but what I needed to do better for next time. I hope he comes back to teach because other people deserve to be taught by him. Sad to see him go :(
He is such a beautiful, kind soul. You will be missed, Mike.

I am not someone who likes physics, but Mike put so much work into this class that I couldn't help but enjoy every lecture. The physics demonstrations were fun and engaging, and lessons were well planned and thoughtfully explained. He's friendly and outgoing and genuinely entertaining to watch. This guy is as good as physics can get.

the course is very test heavy (workshops, hw, all that not graded) BUT every test is split into 3 units and you can retake each unit a week after the test. final was a 5 unit retake. easy to get A.

i hated physics, never touched it before in my life, but i love this guy. really made it interesting, actually cares about students. will miss him :((
I love this guy

Having Professor Verostek is bitter-sweet. He is such an amazing professor and made the class so much more enjoyable. It sucks because I know I will not have another professor like him. He actually cares about us and remembers everyone's name. I walk out of this class actually learning physics. I envy those who get to have him for any class.

Mike is a great professor and everyone knows it, even though he's new to teaching and visibly a bit flustered at times. I hope he comes back to teach more physics! He's made 113 bearable for so many students.

MV? More like MVP (most valuable physicist). Mike is such an incredible lecturer and always keeps things engaging, super accessible outside of class. Incredible course structure that encourages us to learn instead of relying on a curve. He makes physics less scary. I'm praying for a miracle to happen so that he decides to teach 114 next semester.

I have never written a rating on a professor but I had to for Mike Verostek. I am deeply disappointed that Mike will not be able to continue teaching physics at the UofR. He is the best professor that I have had at the UofR. I never liked physics, but after taking his class I can gladly say that this is one of my favorite classes this semester.

Mike is actually the goat. He cares that we know the material and presents plenty of opportunities for students to demonstrate their understanding in case they struggled the first time around. He is very forgiving of mistakes and is an amazing lecturer and person. We love Mike.

Great professor - really knows his stuff. You can tell he cares a lot about students and works really hard to make lectures interesting. Takes feedback well and is very open for office hours. Incredibly well versed in bugs.
Professor provides quality lectures making sure students really understand the material. Occasionally brought up the physics of bugs
Fantastic lecturer; master of physics. Talks about bugs sometimes.

wish I could write more about how bad this class was. Majority of class petitioned to have grades increased due to how little things were explained and how unrelated exams were to course material.Inacessible outside class, actively condescending to students. Described class as "guinea pigs" after 1st exam avg was

Goodman has the unfortunate task of being a first semester orgo professor. He gets a lot of hate. I think I learned more in workshops than in Goodman's lectures but orgo is an interactive learning process and this is unavoidable. Work hard and you'll succeed. Goodman's gruffness will grow on you. Look for his incredible sweater choices!
Tests on concepts not taught before in class. Avoid!
Not at all helpful in office hours

This is the worst class I have ever taken. My workshop TA was pretty awful and Goodman's notes are too messy. His lectures never made sense and I always learned all of the material through the internet. Really annoying student body in this class too.

Worst professor in the history of professors ever period. Does teach anything in the lecture. Doesn't cover the basics in class. The exams are based on workshop. Bad workshop leader... you failed ... only get graded on class based on the 3 exam.. hope I'll never have to take him again.

His lectures are excellent. He takes the book notes and makes them much clearer and more easily understood. Take his old exams as practice because they will be very similar to the exam given. Workshop is also very important to go to and very helpful in learning the material. He's funny and the class is very good, although the final was brutal.

Dr. Goodman needs to retire and give someone else with more patience and passion the opportunity to teach. I was really looking forward to phys org, but this man made it out to be a complicated mess. He is a great guy, but not a very good professor. SKIP!

He's hard, but if you have a good workshop leader and pay attention in class it is passable. Grades are only based on a few tests, and they're incredibly hard, but if you try to answer every question the curve will save you, and you can drop a test. He can be funny, and though some students find him uncaring I just think he has high standards

To be honest, he likes his quest students more. He also does not like pre-meds as most chem professors do not, becuase of the general idea of not wanting to learn, but just needing the most points for med school. Organic Chemistry is tough and you either get it or have to really really work for it. He is very helpful, approachable, and practical.

Goodman teaches a very tough subject, but does an incredible job of explaining concepts in understandable ways. Sometimes he goes a little heavy on mechanisms, but his workshops and examples offer a lot of clarity. The best thing about Goodman is that he is EXTREMELY approachable and will help you understand to the best of his ability.
The lectures are not clear . The contents of exams are all from workshops instead of lectures.

Going in, I thought Prof. Goodman was going to be tough and intimidating. Never before have I been so relieved to find this was not the case. He is incredibly down to earth and, more than once, got the entire class to laugh at his jokes. He is very student-oriented, so as long as you try your best and show you care, you'll be fine. Great professor.

Orgo's a pretty rough class to begin with and he doesn't make it any better.  Has no problem yelling at and belittling students in office hrs. Lectures are somewhat helpful but often unclear.  Book is virtually useless except for some practice problems.  Get your hand on as many old exams as possible and go to all the workshops.

So, Goodman inspires strong opinions. You can tell from the other comments. Here's my take: his primary goal is to teach you to think and reason like a scientist. To that end, he did his job (at least for me) and I learned a ton. Homework and workshop really are key to an A. Don't be petty, and he's friendly enough. Hard class but nicely curved.

His class is hard, no doubt about that. He wants you to learn to think like a scientist so that may frustrate some people. He can be borderline mean if you rub him the wrong way, but can also be really nice and helpful if you show an interest. Book problems and workshops are KEY to success. Handwriting kinda sloppy, but all info needed is there.

Goodman's awesome! Witty, sarcastic, funny, and expert in his subject. Runs a difficult class, but if you work hard you should be able to get at least a B-. Friendly in office hours if you approach him correctly.

Great but challenging professor. Lectures are interesting in that he presents observations and real experimental data and then shows us how it all fits with the current topic. If you desire to learn (fake it if you have to!), he's helpful in office hours. If you just want more points on your test, prepare to be belittled. He can tell.
Good prof. A little intimidating, but helpful if he sees you're willing to learn. Exams are very similar to practice tests and workshop problems. He loves to make you think.

Like someone else said, he's all business and not warm and fuzzy like some other professors. But he really made me appreciate and enjoy organic chem, even though I disliked chemistry previously. He's got a witty, dry sense of humor, and his lectures make you think-they aren't just reams of information to memorize. Exams are very fair.

His class is conceptual and he loves to make you think, but his exams are very fair and reflect the practice tests and workshops. He covers all the material in lecture, and is very helpful in office hours. He's very approachable when students make a sincere effort to learn, but can be nasty if they act like they obviously dislike the subject.

One of the worst professors I have ever had.  I cannot understand why he is permitted to teach orgo to non-majors when he clearly resents it so much. His lectures are transcribing notes, handwaving theory and tend not to help with the exams.  Exam material is taught in workshop, which means you are entirely at the mercy of your TA.
Does not care about his graduate students, does not help in trying to understand graduate material. Rushes through lecture notes fast. Does not understand the material.

Goodman is alright teacher, sit up front and you will do fine. do all the practice exam so you get accustom to his type of question. His exams are challenging but worthwhile and fun. Don't expect to get clear answer from him, Read the text and go to workshop.

I got an A-. Lectures present impt info, but lectures are confusing because he includes lots of extra, not needed info. Exams are hard, but questions are VERY SIMILAR to practice exams AND workshops. Class is crazy curved so aim to get above average. Always understand and memorize practice exams cuz you never know what will be on the test.

Goodman is what you can expect of an Organic Chemistry professor. He doesn't joke around or give free points- he wants you to earn your grade. His tests are fair and you will learn everything that is on the test (even if its a small section of the notes). Just go to workshops, follow the notes, and memorize what he tells you too

He's got a sense of humor, so lecture is interesting. He presents the material by giving observations first and letting the class work out how it fits together. It's extremely useful. He's a nice enough guy, and answers questions clearly. But his handwriting is pretty bad. If you aren't listening when he writes something, abandon all hope.
ok professor. Tests are kind of tough. Not too bad though

He's a great teacher- to the point and very fair. If you study class notes, attend workshops and listen carefully to what he says you will do well. To me, his explanations were a lot better than the book's so I didn't really find the book helpful at all for the course.

This guy is all business, and because of this, he can come off as cold and abrasive. However, if you put the effort in, attend class and workshops, and study on your own, you should do fine. The tests are very fair and you get to drop one. Has bad handwriting and makes the final more difficult than the rest, but curves to a B. Recommended.

Least helpful person I have ever met.  He clearly is only interested in his research and only teches in order to be allowed to do this research.  Way harder than a professor needs to be in order to teach and orgo class.

Organic Chemistry is a hard class. You have to put work in it for sure. I felt that his lectures corresponded with the textbook except for the exceptions HE mentions. His tests are "fair" meaning if you go to class and workshop you will be fine. Also make sure your TA is smart. Goodluck to everyone about to take orgo...get that A!
He's friendly and has a good sense of humor, but not the best at actually teaching. It was tough to follow what was going on and he frequently disagreed with material from the book.

Goodman is a funny genius. People who complain about his class are those who fail to use all their resources to fully understand the material. Go to class because he has his own opinions about chemistry. He is what a professor should be: presents ideas and formulates material such that you must put it together into a logical percept. Just keep up.
He is just too smart. You learn a lot in class but most of the time I have no clue what is happening in class. Although reading the book before lectures can help sometimes

He is literally the Antichrist. Horrible handwriting, absolutely no explainations, and when I went to him for help he told me I was just stupid. Has made similar comments to friends, telling them they are wasting his time and they are idiots. Evil evil man with no teaching abilities and unwillingness to actually teach. Avoid at all costs.

The only problem with Dr Goodman is that he's too smart. His lectures are like a bad essay - no connections until the very end, but then everything falls together with some explanation. And some reading. On your own. Of the textbook.

I attended class for the sarcasm and amusing comments but should have stayed home in terms of learning. Class was lists of data and diagrams, all written messily with nearly no explanation. Tests were funny--because there was no way we could solve the problems.

Good Professor. First one to actually get me to appreciate a class. His exams were rather enjoyable. It wasn't stressful taking any of them. I would recommend that any student interested in organic chemistry should take this course with Doc Goodman!! Two thumbs up!!

One of the most likable professor I have ever had. He might seem like a sarcastic jerk in class but go to talk to him even once in office hours and you will see what an awesome professor he is. He is brilliant. He cares about the well being of the students and will not let you down. He is HILARIOUS! I had a LOT of fun taking his exams.GREAT prof.
This guy does not deserve to be a professor. He's dead weight and should be removed from the department.
Very intelligent and willing to help. Slightly disorganized but brought donuts to tests. Tests were not that bad.
Very thorough and clear in his teaching and notes.  Helpful in class or in office hours if you have questions.  Good sense of humor too, pretty sarcastic.
This guy will make you appreciate Dinnocenzo even more.
No one in the class does well, everyone just does lesser degrees of bad. We shouldn't have to say "Sweet! I got a 54 on my last test!"

At first you might think that he is not a very good teacher.  However, if you stay in the class you will start to understand the way he teaches and the material will seem easier to you.  He's actually nice to his students- just ask him questions and he'll answer them quite clearly.  A good prof.

I had him when he first started teaching second semester Orgo and he had no idea how to present the information. I'm assuming he's gotten better since then, but to his credit, he is very open to student opinions if the class as a whole doesn't like something.

I don't understand why so many people don't like him. Yes, in the beginning, when he goes through stuff that he expects you to know, he goes very quickly and is hard to understand. But once he gets to new stuff he is VERY thorough and very clear. He's even amusing. I think he's an excellent professor.

Everyone gives this guy a bad rep because he goes very fast, but he is very passionate about the subject and care a great deal about the students.  He is thorough with the material and while he does go fast sometimes, he makes sure everyone understands it before he moves on.
he is the wost teacher i have ever had.
He throws a bunch of crap at you without explaining it. I'd rather have a teacher who explains what the stuff we are reading is all about, and when it's helpful, rather than relying on luck.

He's not a bad professor, despite everyone's opinion. Once you get accustomed to his dry humor, sarcasm, and bluntness, he's actually pretty funny. He may come off indifferent at first, but he actually wants you to learn the material.

He actually isn't that bad of a professor, in my opinion.  He's pretty straightforward in what he wants.  Basically, go to lecture, go to workshop, make some notecards, and you'll be fine on the exam.  I have a B and I haven't even touched the book.  People may think he's rude, but in his review sessions he's very personable.
Pretty good

I have never been more disgusted with a teaching style. He actually had the nerve to use another professor's lecture notes (from a previous year) to teach the class. Aka he copied onto the board, at a superhuman pace, a ton of material that he himself couldn't explain or justify. Whatever institution gave him his PhD should be ashamed.
Among the worst at Rochester
One of the worst if not THE WORST professors I have ever had. He is a horrible teacher and is extremely disorganized. Expect to learn nothing (as far as chemistry is concerned).
No comments for this guy yet? WOW

I took this course three years ago and the experience of her teaching is still haunting me. This professor could not explain her own slides well and also test random non-biological questions for exams. Think twice before registering

Dr. Uy clearly cared about her research more than students. Grading criteria was extremely harsh and she was not accessible outside of class (didn't show up to office hours etc.). She expected students to memorize random material from the slides and she didn't curve any exam, even when averages were low. Don't know if she's worse than Minkley.

I didn't realize it at the time, but this lady's a pretty good professor, especially when you compare her to some of the other people in the math department (cough, Segal, cough). She has the most annoying voice in the history of the world but if you can get through that she's not bad. She's damn annoying but a pretty good professor.
She is out of control for workload, and she has a tendency to lose turned in work...and exams, blaming it on the students.
Most intelligent person I've ever met.  Assigns lots of work.  Always willing to help her students.

depending on the subject she may be very clear or not so clear...but regardless she is ALWAYS willing to help her students.  to her, teaching comes before research.  i have never seen such dedication from a teacher to her students.  i'd even be willing to say that she places her students before her sanity.  great sense of humor too.

At first you might be a little thrown off by her and think she is not a good professor...but once you get used to her, she is always willing to help at any time.  She is probably the only professor who answers webwork by herself at 2:00am the night before it's due.  She's a great person outside of the class and will help anyone.

She tends to move quickly in class (yet slowly because she assumes the students aren't as smart as we really are).  I guarantee she will assign more homework than any other class you have ever taken, and she will give tests that could easily run 3+ hours (my last exam was about 18 pages).
brilliant
She's completely nuts.  Her lectures can be confusing, but she's pretty helpful when you ask her questions afterwards.  Tests are manageable, but the curve always helps.

Very enthusiastic, however, doesn't know how to teach.  Is an easy grader if you do your homework, but she gives insane amounts of work.  Her tests are insane, though curved generously.  The end result is a decent grade with nothing learned.
No Comments

Such an icon.
Bad professor ever!!!

Some reviews are harsh (she recently became a new mom), though the descriptions aren't wrong. Homework from mid-October was graded just days before final grades. Classes were not well thought out or prepared. Expectations were unclear and felt inconsistent, with high demands despite limited support. She taught as if we were grad students.

She gives terrible lectures. Although materials for this course are not hard, she explains it in a difficult and difficult to understand way. Her homework are related to the textbook materials but different from her lecture material sometimes, since her lecture usually teaches wrong things other than textbook.

Worst professor ever. She smiles at you with fakeness and she loves to see you suffer. One hw problem had us do 200+ by hand calculations. If you want to be dehumanized take this class with this awful monster. Also randomly slanders students saying they use chatgpt when they dont. That is actually harassment the school should fire her.

This was the most stressful and discouraging class i've taken. The grading criteria was always confusing, and the workload was extremely heavy. The course structure made the experience very frustrating.

One of the most boring and mundane classes I have taken and the way material is presented feels very mundane and dry. Please be careful with what you get into when taking this class. Be prepared for a lot of unnecessary work and forced attendance.

Dr. G is very knowledgeable. She teaches almost solely based on formulas, which is excellent for some but not others. Exams are only 50% of the grade, so getting high marks is achievable.  All exams also have formula sheets. Labs and homework require effort but are graded generously. She also gives a lot of partial credit, so show all your work.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Nice teacher. You get a lot of partial credit back and the practice homework is always super helpful to do before homework because they're pretty similar. Homework takes a while but you use it to study for exams, so it makes the exams much easier.

Dr. G really cares about your education and seeing you do well. Her class is designed for you to do well if you do the homework and go to lab (each is worth 25%). There are even multiple opportunities to earn extra credit or bonus points. I scored a 70 on my first exam and still managed to get an A.

Dr. G is the MOST organized prof I've seen in U of R. Her lectures were very clear and thorough and it was clear that she was willing to help her students. Although she was a bit nitpicky at some point (especially in exams) and there were lots of HWs, there were lots of extra credits and chances to learn from your mistakes without much penalty.

I felt she didn't do a good job helping students understand why a solution was the answer to the problem, and her slides and information were very uninformative. I am not the best mathematics person, and I really did struggle to grasp concepts. Thank goodness homework and lab are 50% of grades; I wouldn't have survived otherwise...

Dr. G is one of the best professors I have had at this school. She explains R in a way that is clear and easy to follow along with. Lectures are mandatory and for good reason, they are key for following along in the class. Hard homework, but the assignments teach you a lot about R. I really highly recommend taking 275 with her.

Only halfway through and already the worst professor I have had in my 3 years here. Most boring lectures I have ever sat through, with a horrible style of teaching to top it off. She treats this introduction to statistics class like it is the most important class we will ever take, but I am so serious when I say it is common sense. VERY dramatic.

Amazing professor, probably my favorite. If you are a math based person she is easy to follow. Lectures had a lot of order and structure; she explains all concepts throughly. Class was hard, there is homework and R lab (coding language), content heavy, but she makes it enjoyable. Loved her!

Large lectures, the class was held in Hubbell. Weekly lab was very easy and rarely took more than 30 minutes. Content can be a little tricky at first, but all the later units are VERY similar, with slightly different procedures, and so the class for sure gets easier as it goes on - do no give up hope. She did lots of examples, and explained well.

this was the one class this semester I was not excited to go to and really struggled to remain focused. I felt like she overcomplicated incredibly simple concepts and had a very slow paced class when you would normally expect math/stats to be fast paced. Content itself and exams are easy and u could honestly self study this whole class

Dr. G is very helpful and patient, especially during office hours. There may be a lot of homework and the class may seem slow at times, but doing the homework is extremely beneficial as it gives you an understanding of concepts you may not understand just from lecture. I highly recommend taking this class as it is easy but it just takes effort.

Dr. G is very helpful and patient especially when you come in with questions to her office hours. Though the class may be a bit slow and there are many homework assignments, I believe these homework assignments truly did help my understanding so I would recommend spending your time on them as they also contribute to your grade.

Though the class may be a bit slow sometimes, Dr. G is an incredibly kind and helpful professor who is very patient when you come into office hours with questions. She gives a lot of homework but the homework truly helps with your overall understanding of the class.

The class was so boring (as someone who really likes Stat & Applied Math). There are so many opportunities to use statistics to actually research something you're passionate about & gain a deeper understanding for whatever that material is. The labs don't do that at all. She's a good lecturer, with good slides, but needs to change the curriculum.

Homework assignments are overly simplistic and require detailed work on basic problems, which feels like unnecessary busywork. The lack of challenge makes it hard to stay engaged or develop new skills. It makes everything worse when attendance is also required. If you want a class that pushes you, I'd suggest reconsidering this one.

Dr. G has a lot of patience when working with students. I was always the only one in her office hours and she would always be more than happy to clarify confusion. This course is R studio heavy so be prepared to memorize codes for exams.

Dr.G is an amazing professor. Her lectures were super easy to understand, although a bit slow. The homeworks were really helpful in understanding the material and if you do the practice questions first, you'll do well on the homework. She's also super organized and the extra credit from the practice homework problems help your grade a lot.

219 is one of the easier stats classes I have taken- would recommend. Some of the material can get complicated, but Dr. G acknowledges that and doesn't expect you to perfectly grasp all the theory. She teaches it in an accessible way. Heavy on the group work, most hw is done with your group but isn't bad. only 1 midterm exam and final project

Tough and hard professor. She won't let student do anything easy. The most mean professor I have ever seen in UOR. Though lectures are not bad, lots of rubrics and standards make it hard for students.

her lectures are incredibly clear and everything's super easy to understand. honestly i didn't go to a single class and i just watched the recorded lectures and got an A. the projects can be tough at times but you get to work with people so it's not as bad. homework was easy and based entirely on the lectures. dr g was also really nice.. love her

276 isn't an easy class if you have no coding background (if you do it will be easier). Tests are HARD, def study, and homeworks are really time consuming so start early. However, Dr G still makes it possible to get a good grade if you put in effort, so show up to class and ask for help if you need it. Overall, difficult but learned a lot.
She is so nice!! She uses a lot of her own time to help students and sets extra office hours! She gives lecture recordings so you could study at your own pace! She explains concepts very clearly.

Dr. Grzesik values the learning the process in her classes. You get out what you put into her course. She offers plenty of office hours and is very responsive to her email chains. Those who don't spend the extra effort to learn the material that they struggle with are just lazy... 5/5 Stars
Dr.G is so kind and amiable! if you have any question and email her, she would definitely reply very fast!!love her!!!

Professor Grzesik is really nice and you could actually learn a lot from her. However, she grades homework and exams extremely strictly. It is really nice of her to give out extra credit but unfortunately not really help to boost your total grade. Be prepared or you might freak out every single Sunday night.

While Prof. Grzesik is nice, she focuses too much on the conceptual calculus part of statistics, which is not in the homework or the exams. She covers so many equations that by the point she says something that's actually relevant, I'm not paying attention. I got much more useful information from lab, but I don't recommend taking a class with her.
Very strict in grading and do not accept any mistake caused by third party factors.hard to understand during the class

She was really nice and I really liked her as a person, but I just don't think I learned too much in her class. I'd recommend one of the other professors. She often brought up concepts in lecture that we didn't need to know, which just confused me and distracted me from what I did need to know. The only topics I did well on was what I learned in HS

Wow this class was tough. Really interesting class to take and you learn a lot from her. She grades ridiculously strict on homeworks, but gives good feedback. Start them early in the week. A lot of all nighters pulled on Sundays... Midterm and Final are closed book coding exams. Very hard, but she was understanding when it came to grading.

Good teacher. If you're interested in statistical analysis take her, she knows what she's talking about. However if you're just in it for the credit, take a different prof, it's easier. She gives you everything you need to succeed on her tests, but you have to work. Graded the group project tough. Is a stickler about being on time and office hours
I would rather try the course offered by some other instructor instead. She is an elementary school grammar teacher.
Very clear explanations of very useful information to know. 100% worth taking if you have an interest in statistical analysis

I lost interest for stat after her 276. She is nice, but her grading is cruel. She always takes off points for tidy mistakes. Heavy workload, however, exams are way harder than hw (basically close book coding exam). If you care about your grade, consider it before taking it.

Dr. G is generally nice and straightforward with her grading. Sometimes the course can be frustrating in that it is super focused on formulas rather than critical thinking and understanding. I recommend doing at least some of the practice problems (especially before the homework and exams). Workshop was also quite helpful, but it depends on your TA

I took Statistical Coding in R with Dr. G (I couldn't select this option in the rating for some reason), and she is extremely knowledgeable and helpful. It's not an easy class, but it's the kind of class that will actually help you get a job after college. I highly recommend. Also, she's a wonderful person.

comment: Professor Grzesik is an okay professor overall. She's straightforward with the grading and what is expected of you, but boring. Homework every week gets harder as the class goes on, but even if it's time consuming it's not too bad. Prepares you well for tests, but some are harder than others. There is one basically semester-long group project.
The professor is great if you don't have any disabilities, medical issues, sickness, or anything relating to being late or needing to change when complete the course.

Dr. G is an amazing professor and will go the distance to help you maximize your learning. I was intimidated at first because of all of the negative reviews, but they seem to all be from when this course was taught online or lazy students. Sometimes the HW is a bit long but exams are very fair if you did the HW and the practice questions.
If you do the homework and discussion, then it's easy to get an A for this class.

Very time consuming. Students are expected to watch pre-recorded lectures, attend workshop, write discussion posts, and complete homework WEEKLY. Aside from the heavy workload, Dr. G is very accessible. She answers emails very quickly and clarifies problems during her non-mandatory Zoom meetings.

I think that something Professor G forgets is that this is an introductory course, which means that a large number of the people taking it have to as a major requirement. So they aren't going to have a lot of background knowledge that she assumes we all do. It's tough, especially if you aren't very talented when it comes to math.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: It is a LOT of work. Especially for an introductory course. I spend about 10 hours a week on this course, which is twice what I spend on any other. You have to watch lectures, watch videos for notes, attend workshops and then do homework (which can take hours) and then do your discussion. Which is outside of revision needed for the multiple exams.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: Dr. G is a really good teacher and she puts effort into her lectures. The recent poor reviews are probably lazy first years who wanted an easy A. The biggest con is that it's too much work. She is a bit nitpicky with tests. Homework is a bit annoying, but this is a math class after all. Yellowdig participation was a complete waste of time though.

You're just going to spend every week listening to hours of videos that she filmed years ago. 50% of the test material was never taught in class so you better have done outside-of-class research on top of the weekly videos, lectures, workshop, homework and discussion requirements. And you're going to lose dozens of marks for nit-picky remarks.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: A really difficult class. It's called Applied Statistics but there isn't a single opportunity to practice application within class-time. If you want to take notes on the (re-used) videos, attend class, practice tests, attend the workshop AND do the assignments you'll need AT LEAST 7 or 8 hours a week. And the tests are covered in un-taught material

I've only had her online, but I've had no problem with her recorded lectures and the discussions so far. Many of her exam problems have been straight out of her notes or similar to practice and video problems. She's given more work than I expected, but she's approachable and responds to emails quickly if you have questions. Def possible to do well
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Assigns more work that the allotted credits, used lecture time as a discussion so all lectures had to be watched on your own time. Does not care about the students and acts as if her class is the only one you have. Tough grader, but gives partial credit for the work she deems fit (which is not much). Not taking her again if I can help it.
She don't really care about student. She just want to finish her own work of teaching.
Lot of work and you should prepare yourself to work a lot outside the class.

Dr. G was fine. She will tell you how to do well in her course throughout the semester. Follow her advice. She can be nitpicky and wants you to solve problems in certain ways she mentioned in class but she makes this clear. Besides that, discussions and workshops were 30% of our grade and are a giveaway, and she gives EC opportunities.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: could really do without her passive aggressive emails to the class. her lectures themselves are fine, but she's a pretty strict grader, so just be mindful of that. i really hate her attitude and her personality is the most discouraging factor for me.. may just be because we're online, acts like her class is top priority
She gives a lot of work and the class is not completely helpful.

Her lecture is very organized and clear, and so are her lecture notes. She takes off points on even tiny mistakes for both homework and project (often not necessary). Attendance in discussion required. Tests are relatively easy, and it doesn't cover all stuff in lecture and homework.
A solid choice if you are looking to take a stats class. Speaks clearly, very organized, helpful during office hours. A very fair professor.

Stricter in terms of grading than other professors in the statistics department. As a math major having taken classes with Dr. Mueller, McDermott, Nick, Joe, and Heckler, I can say that Dr. G is very nitpicky and takes off points for tiny details, although most people understood the bigger picture. A lot of people lost motivation because of this.
Always open to help (especially during office hours), lectures are slide-based (accessible outside class), weekly homework and recitations, no textbook, and take notes!

Prof. Grzesik really cares about her class and students. She is a good teacher and tries to help people out as much as possible. I would always get an email back within 12 hours or less. I found her explanation of concepts quite clear and she has a good balance between theory and demonstrating problems. Would definitely recommend

Dr G.'s lectures are clear and easy to follow, w/ tons of example problems. Her assignments reflect exactly what she expects you to know - no surprises. Everything is very straightforward. Office hours are helpful & she makes herself accessible to students to really make sure everyone is understanding the content. So glad I took this class!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Dr. G is the best, she's super organized, so much so that I still use my stats notebook as a reference. Exams are fair and office hours are super helpful. I definitely learned a lot!

Incredibly organized and straight-forward lectures. Material is super accessible outside of class and the homework is very manageable. She cares about the students' success and is has very helpful office hours.

Professor Grzesik is a great lecturer. Lectures are always organized and she does a good job of making sure the material is clear. Easy to get to outside of lecture and helps in every way. Exams can be really long for a short time frame and if you miss lecture youll be lost in homeworks and coding can be difficult.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: I've had Dr. Peck for 200 and 203. Very nice and helpful guy, but very disorganized. On the plus side, he's really lax with deadlines, but he also tends to revise the syllabus often, which can be confusing. He's very passionate about German literature and culture, and you'll get a lot out of his classes if you put in the work.

Dr. Peck is a great teacher, though at first I believed his teaching methods were a little weird, I eventually got used to it and I find myself understanding german texts after about 2 months of classes, his exams are fair, work-load is light and he is very friendly and cares about teaching German.
He is a very good Ger101 teacher. His tests are very fair and the grading is decent. He is a nice guy and cares alot about German.

Very difficult high level German course. Grading was harsh and only vaguely explained. This was listed as a 200 level class but seemed more like a gradate course. Two ten page papers in german in addition to 100 pages a week and two exams. Do not take course unless COMPLETELY fluent in german or you will flounder.
Salty banana.

i freaking love this guy. He's great, his lectures are good, he knows what he's talking about. Super friendly and nice and also unintentionally goofy at times. Lots of memorization, but I had a lot of fun in 110! Know the brain diagram super well! For studying, I found blurting/active recall and feynman technique useful.

Great lecturer, the course is difficult because of the sheer amount of things you need to memorize but you can tell he wants students to succeed. If I took this course with any other professor I would've definitely failed.

Professor Davis is the absolute GOATTT!! you can tell that he is very passionate about what he teaches and wants students in his class to succeed. He is very understanding and caring. Although the course may be heavy material, he makes it easy to understand.

Great lectures and a great professor. The course is notoriously challenging in the BME department, but my friends and I concluded that we cannot deny that it is indeed fun. He gave a proper amount of mathematical deductions to nearly everything. Homework and exams are hard though.

Very difficult but interesting material. Dr. Davis is super engaging to listen to, and makes coming to lecture that much more worth it. He curves exams because the class average is usually around a 50 but he is the nicest guy and this class is hard to fail.

Love him as a professor, but the way he structures his grading system is just flawed and brutal. The only grades being 4 exam grades and an optional final. Although they're curved, the amount of content for each unit and how intricate the memorization is, makes the exams feel impossible. Especially with how the exams, themselves, are structured.
As long as you study throughout the unit and not the last minute you will be fine.

I would 100% take his class again if he gives doable exams and makes it less exam heavy. His lecture is the BEST among all classes, but his exams are really difficult. Curve helps, but you will have to study A LOT for good grade. Go to class, do what he tells you to do (tablesss!!), memorize brain diagram, and please, go to his office hours.

Dr. Davis was kind and understanding but is very content heavy. The grade is based on 4 exams and an optional final and that's it. The exams are curved but they're still really hard. I will say the course said some inaccuracies (i.e. he said you could sleep for 1.5 hours every night and probably be fine, he said coke has no negative impacts).
Oh Prof. Davis. What a legend. 11/10 would recommend despite the lack of sleep I got the week leading up to one of his exams.

Loved this class and Dr Davis is hands down my favorite professor here. The best advice to do well in this class is just REALLY familiarize yourself with the paper structure because it's always going to be the same.

The material is interesting but in order to get an A, be prepared to spend every day looking at notes. You'll have to study your butt off if you don't memorize things quickly. Expect to study ~14 hours a week (at least) to memorize everything well. This class made me emotionally numb and I burnt out quickly. Don't take it if you don't need it

the nicest professor ever. his exams are really difficult though. you need to understand his questions and try to predict them. lecture heavy. highly recommend going and/or watching the old recordings he provides

Having him for a year in 110/201, I say he is very passionate about the material, caring and accessible, and an all-around respected professor. My suggestion for studying would be drawing on a whiteboard, writing down notes of recitation concepts, understanding his testing style, active studying, and getting OH with either TAs/Davis. All the best.

Dr. Davis has so much passion for what he teaches, and his lecture style really did help me grasp super hard concepts. Extremely effective professor. I looked forward to his lecture every M/W/F. Probably the most difficult exams I've taken in my life (you do have to get used to his question style) but otherwise a great time.
His fits and tests could use some work but he's chilling fr. Very content-dense lectures.
K dawg is the man. Best professor at UR hands down no questions asked.
really difficult tests given by one of my favorite professors on campus. don't take it if you don't have to, unless you want to. in that case, enjoy it!
Kevin is the best teacher I've ever taken in U of R. He's fun and really excited about his teaching. However, be ready to fail his class since he's the worst grader.

Its hard to enjoy a class with such hard exams and content but Kevin Davis really did a great job. I really enjoyed his class and the content but you really cannot get through this with a good grade unless you study. He is also extremely understanding and accommodating! I highly recommend his classes but do beware that it might hit your gpa.
tags: ['Amazing lectures', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Graded by few things']

comment: He did a great job, his lectures were clear and posted in case you need to rewatch them, and he was very clear about what you would be tested on. Generally a great teacher. However, the class is incredibly difficult because of the sheer amount of material within it. It sets up a great basis for the rest of the major but it is so damn hard.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Test heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Loved the material of the class and the professor. Didn't love the tests. Probably spent 15-20 hours a week studying, and even with the curve averaged out an 88. Study a LOT for the exams and review the material the day you get it. There is tons of content loaded into his lectures, but it's generally easy to understand if you go to lecture and rec.

Dr. Davis is a great professor. His lectures are well-organized, entertaining, and super informative. That being said, this was the hardest class I have taken at U of R. If you haven't taken BCS 110 before hand, prepare to learn a lot of material and feel way behind. That being said, he is super accessible out of class and cares about students.
Professor Davis is truly one of the most caring professors on campus. He actually wants you to succeed. There was also a lot of generous curves given on the exams.

Dr. Davis gives high-quality lectures and the slides are of the most organized among all courses in the university. He is caring and accessible after class and gives extra office hours before exams. His exams are truly tricky, but if you organize your notes and try to think a step forward and predict what will be on the exam, you will be fine.
He is one of the best professors I met at UR. He is caring and he explains concepts clearly. The course is interesting but really time-consuming. There is too much content to remember and understand.
Lectures are fun & enjoyable, however there are only 4 tests & an optional final so beware... Pls go to lectures he talk about what he'll test on in lectures only, and you need to study a lot. A LOT.
Super hard to get an A. As someone who cram a lot, I feel my brain is about to  explode every time before the exam. The course is informative and interesting, except that it may destroy your gpa!

I love Professor Davis, he was so amazingly helpful in office hours and he has a really big curve. I took BCS 110 as a transfer student who was not familiar at all with how harsh the U of R education system was going to be, and he made it a really welcoming experience for me personally .I think his lectures are fair and you need to study though!

Very engaging and interesting professor who has great lectures, just a very difficult and lecture/test-heavy class with lots and lots of studying outside of lectures. Despite all, he grades pretty fairly and passing is very feasible. It's just getting an A that is extremely difficult.

BCSC 110 is my second course with Dr. Davis, and I have grown to like him and his classes a lot more because I am prepared for the workload (which is a lot). Go to class and record the lectures yourself (the older recordings are less relevant). Pay attention and write down every word, reorganize the content later, and ask him questions to survive.

Dr. Davis has the most organized, detailed, and understandable lecture slides of all my professors. You could ask him anything you want during his office hours. You can't give him a low rating just because you didn't put in enough effort. The content is challenging, but not impossible, given the generous curves that he gives on every exam.

Prof Davis is such an amazing prof and person. You can tell he is super engaged in his material. BSC 110 is just an extremely hard course, but he makes it his best to make it engaging. He is very animated.The curve in the class is insane, the tests are like no other. The entire class is pure memorization. Be prepared to study and study for the exam

Amazing professor who actually knows a lot about his area of study and is genuinely focused on teaching. However content are hard and exams are harder. Curves helps but each lecture and exam results just leaves me so strained and hopeless. If you are a very sciency person who wants to learn lots about bioscience go ahead

Super great lecturer but tests were no joke. The curve works in your favor so most people don't do worse than a B- but you definitely have to put a lot of effort in to do well and understand the concepts.
Nice as a person and lecturer but he made this class so much harder than it has to be and will not recommend if 110 is not mandatory in your major

Dr. Davis is a hilarious and engaging lecturer, however I found his lectures very confusing. His tests are notoriously nuanced, specific, and difficult. He will re-do lectures for you in office hours which is great. If you want to do well in this class, expect to study A LOT. I also hope you like memorizing tables and diagrams...

Dr. Davis is a hilarious and engaging speaker. I felt more alert in his class than in any others I took this semester, and he definitely put his heart and soul into lecturing. That said, the recitations are mediocre at best and the tests are unnecessarily arcane. Dr. Davis and BCS 110 demand a lot for you, don't underestimate the low course number.

His lectures are quite engaging, but there is so much content to learn that the exams are really difficult. The wording of his exams can really trip you up so asking clarification questions on the exam is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED. I recommend going to office hours too. You need to think like Davis thinks, and not just know the content...
Great lectures. Tests are super nuanced and difficult, great curves though. Tests are on his lectures, you don't need to get a textbook. You need to study hard if you want to do well.

Professor Davis is a really funny and great lecturer but really does not care about his students' success. His exams are hard and he usually writes them the night before so you do not know what he could be adding to them. To do well in this class you really need a good TA.

He's a really engaging and thoughtful professor. He puts everything in a way you will understand and he's accessible outside lecture if you need help. As long as you study really really hard, you'll be okay. If you put the effort into the class, you'll get a good grade since his curves are really good.

He is an interesting lecturer and this class got me interested in cognitive science, but he makes his test unnecessarily hard. He curves every exam average to an 83 so if you study hard you'll be fine, but there is absolutely a way to teach the same material without such difficult exams, and that is the only thing your grade is based on.

DR.Davis is my favourate prof of university. He is so nice and helpful, give clear and good lectures. And he is Always delighted to help us on Office hours. I also took BCS110 and would like to take more of his lectures. His tests are hard.

If you're someone who crams, you will fail. I can personally tell you that you should be scared if you always cram lol. I do mean this is the best way possible. I did take the class online and so he made it more difficult so others wouldn't cheat, but even then, please go to lectures. The exams were multiple choice (online) and he made it so hard.
Loved the class! By far my favorite class and I took it online. Professor Davis is a great lecturer and explains complex topics in way that is interesting and makes the class fun! :)
Dr.Davis is super nice and experienced. Give good lectures and explains everything very clearly. But his course isn't easy, get ready!

My absolute favorite professor this semester. Funny, clearly cares and wants you to succeed, and his lectures are well organized and clear. Extremely difficult topics so you’ll need to study a lot but exams are generously curved. Go to his office hours too; he’s super nice and always willing to help!

In order to do well, you will have to memorize every single detail of what he says and puts in the lectures. No getting around it because most test questions include multiple concepts stacked on each other. But, his info is organized nicely on the slides and if you study A LOT, you can do well .

Professor Davis is definitely one of my favorite professors. He is very organized during lectures, and often uses understandable analogies when teaching a complicated concept. If you go to lectures, work hard, and make sure you understand everything, the exams shouldn't be that hard.

Going to lectures was pretty much useless, I was able to gain a better understanding through internet resources. Be ready to teach yourself a lot of the material. Pretty generous grading scale though, and most exams are curved.

Zhupa, what to say. He comes off as a tough guy at first, but towards the end of the semester he lightens up and even starts making jokes in his own horizontally-striped-sweater-way. comment:
Brilliant professor, but you should be aware of a few things:
1. There are surprise quizzes almost every other class. They are usually in groups and weighted lightly though.
2. The material for this course is EXTREMELY difficult even for both grads and undergraduates so attend class.
3. Attendance is mandatory. 1 class session = 1 quiz grade.

He's an interesting guy and very knowledgeable about the topic. I didn't like the structure of the class (entirely group work, everything done in class except for a term project, in-class group quiz almost every day), so I wouldn't take a class with him again, but if groupwork helps you learn, you would probably enjoy the class.

If you're into theoretical CS stuff, CSC 280 is the place for you. You'll be learning and solving many interesting problems from complexity theory. The small class size definitely helps with the in-class discussions and group activities. One of the best class formats I've seen in a course.
Genuine, caring, attentive, passionate, enthusiastic, loves to share stories (often over-shares random (but subjectively fun) stories), accessible, interesting course content and materials.

He is a nice person, and what he says in class makes sense, but I had to rewatch recordings to understand.  If you want to do well:  ALWAYS show up for attendance credit, and study the examples he does in class.  His exams are very fair.  If you understand the in-class examples you should be fine on the tests.  Work hard and you will do good, good.

Most people would complain about mandatory attendance when you can easily get 36% just based on attendance! Lane makes us do tons of practice that makes it impossible not to do well on the exams! He's caring, an expert in his field, and one of a kind! This is a theory class, so if you don't like proofs, DEAL with it and DON'T blame Lane for it!

Very smart man, cares deeply about his student's success. Lectures can be a little abstract if you aren't interested in the topic, but he delivers topics with great energy. Both the quirkiest and smartest man I've ever met. Get to know him outside of class; it'll be worth your while.
