Undoubtedly knowledgeable and well-intentioned, but a quirky mess. Assigns insanely excessive amounts of work and enjoys giving zeros to more than half the class for any given assignment.
Worst professor EVER~!!!  Rambles and talks too damn fast  :(

Mottley's an amazing professor. I thoroughly enjoyed most of his lectures though, he sometimes came off as boring. The tests were easy but became progressively harder, not too hard though. The grading criteria are clear as day, the labs were fun too!
Just be thorough with the Study Guides posted before exams and all will be good!
He's a chill, nice professor and it's easy to do well. However, some of the concepts covered in this class can be kind of confusing and requires reviewing outside of class to understand them better.
Jack Mottley is a pillar, the leading light, and one-man bastion of the ECE department.

ECE101 is an easy course, and Mottley especially designs it so that it isn't jarring or difficult if you have no prior knowledge of calculus or physics. Lectures are optional and although I recommend attending, they can be off-track pretty often. Homeworks are sometimes graded incorrectly based on the TAs, but labs and workshops are also not bad.
What a nice guy. He sets every student up for success and is always there to answer questions.

Mottley is so kind, so caring, really wants his students to succeed. All lectures are recorded, but go to class anyway so you can ask questions. Recitations and labs are mandatory, but the labs are actually really fun. Mottley also cancels labs on exam weeks to have an extended Q&A. Great professor.
Very nice man, very easy class. Even though a good portion of the final grade is the exams, they are straight forward and everyone should be well prepared for it. The practice exams really help!
He went through lots of examples in class, and he posted all the notes online which was very helpful. The exam questions were very similar to the homework and examples in class.
He went through lots of examples in class, and the exam questions were very similar to the homework and examples in class.

Professor Mottley is a cool dude. I only got to take a 101 class with him so far, so I didn't get much of a chance to get to know him, and it was very clear that he is much more talented in teaching upper level classes than beginner classes. He will answer all of your questions no matter how stupid. Can't wait to take ECE113 with him next year!

I took this class from 3:15-4:05, and I fell asleep nearly every class. He has a very relaxing way of speaking that almost instantly puts me to sleep. Not a bad thing but it made it very hard to learn, but luckily all of the lectures are recorded ane when I can stay awake, the lectures are very informative and the information is valuable.

If you pay attention in lectures and put in effort in lab this class is an easy A. The homework and tests(do the study guides) all go along with lectures and nothing comes as a surprise or is too challenging. He is very quick to respond to emails and help students with any problems. The labs are simple & fun and for most of them you get out early.
Chill teacher, but he speaks quietly and isn't to engaging. Class is relatively boring but easy, as long as you generally know what's going on you should get the A.

A real stand up guy. Very accommodating towards all needs. Class can get a little bit on the boring side, but as long as you focus and do homework, you should be all set to go for tests/final. He breaks down a lot of the content which makes things very easy to grasp. You will be more than prepared with Jack!

This professor is not motivated in teaching, his class very boring. Exams and homework too easy. Before the exam, he gives all previous years' handouts. Questions are almost the same. I feel that I almost spend no time learning this course and learned very little. Compared with my friends from other top universities, I feel I learned a fake course.
It's just a harder ECE111. Mottley is still a very good professor and the lectures are still a bit dull. The labs for this course are pretty useless.
Class drags on sometimes, but he does his best to keep intro topics interesting.

Professor Mottley is a great teacher who really cares about his students. His lectures aren't super entertaining but he explains all the topics very well. The labs, workshops, homework, and exams all fit together nicely, so it is easy to learn all of the material even though there is a lot of it. Overall great professor.
Jack is genuinely a very good teacher and a very nice person. His lectures can get a bit dull, but you will always understand the material after them.

I like professor Mottley a lot. He's super friendly and easy to talk to, always willing to help. His lectures can get a little messy but he'll go above and beyond to make sure you understand. I recommend attending to recitations where you can ask any questions and you can get more one on one.
Attend class and its easy to do well.

Mottley taught my 111 class in a "flipped-classroom" style at times, but most of the year was just him lecturing. If you put in a decent effort you're likely to do very well! Mottley says he likes to challenge students with hw assignments, so he made the tests very straight forward.

Professor Mottley (as monotonous as he is) is very helpful and clear. He knows and loves what he's doing with circuits so he's always willing to help. The homeworks, labs, workshops and tests all match up to complete one another but they are very difficult so study hard and you'll be fine.

Mottley taught ECE 111 very well. It's a fundamentals class, and Mottley gave students a strong foundation to build more ECE knowledge on. Students were well prepared for exams, which had material on them consistent with the homeworks, labs, and lectures -- something which is rare and underappreciated by students often. Well done, Jack.

Lectures are boring and don't provide enough examples for you to even start the homework problems.  Workshops are somewhat beneficial at best and the labs are pointless.  I barely learned anything in this class.  Mottley is a nice enough guy, but he lacks teaching skills.  After taking this class I still have little idea about how a circuit works.

ECE 101 is a simple class that's just following directions from a provided book or packet and building robots while programming with VHDL.  It's a really fun class that'll get you into ECE.  Sometimes Mottley teaches the class basics, and it's always very clear. He grades very kindly and helps you readily.  He's also fairly likeable to chat with.

This was my least attended class in my history.  He is a terrible teacher, no organization, no enthusiasm, terrible TA's, confusing labs.  This class should be extremely easy, but it becomes difficult because of the lack of support of material (hw doesn't support lecture, labs are confusing, lectures are pointless)

The tests are nearly exactly the same as previous years. Labs suck but they are easy. You will leave the class thinking that you learned very little but will find that you learned more than you thought.

Really nice guy, but not a good teacher.  Lectures don't help with homework, and labs are hard to follow.  Get a good workshop leader and you'll do fine.  Tests are really easy- very similar to previous years.  The book is useless.

Homeworks didnt really help.  Tests were easy because they are the same as previous years.  Spends to much time in lectures deriving.  Don't expect him to respond to emails or to even know what grade to expect.
HW are sometimes pointless, and lectures are fairly boring, expect to take 40 mins writing notes to have him tell you you only need to remember one small equation at the end. Nice guy to talk to.

pointless homework that didn't match tests, awful labs, poorly chosen TAs, boring guy.  stresses professionalism when he doesn't even follow half of what the syllabus says, and in general holds a really boring, difficult course.
very consistant. within 5 minutes, i was asleep.

CANT TEACH!!!!

prof quillen was always super reachable and incredibly kind. when i was struggling my freshman year she let me submit all of my missing lab reports a week before grades were due- and graded them herself. the sweetest lady ever. be aware though the lab reports are awful plz j take 121 instead

Professor Quillen is the nicest human being I've ever seen. She is intelligent and knows how to teach students. She is very accessible outside class and likes to talk to students. Very inspirational and encourage me to pursue physics and astronomy.
She has really good notes and lectures are fun to attend because of how passionate she is about what she's teaching. Homeworks can be challenging but she is accessible outside of class.

Quillen is the best. She no longer does tests, but you'll still learn a lot in her class. The way she weaves in modern physics in her lectures is incredibly helpful without being overwhelming to first years. Even without tests, 141 is a ton of work, but it's worth it in the long run.

Collaborate on the problem sets (took me many hours) and do the labs well (multiple days worth of work). She is caring and will help you a lot in office hrs

Pros: Very good lecture notes, very easy to reach, and cared about students and tried to make the class fair. Cons: all-over-the-place lecturer; I took honors physics 1, which required having taken high school physics - had it not been similar material to high school, I wouldnt have learned. Lecture notes taught me better than lecture.

She is very kind. Lab reports can be a bit intense.

She should not teach freshmen.  Although high school calculus is recommended for AST 111, the calculus in her presentations involves multivariable calculus.  Additionally, her lectures are hard to follow, due in part to her poor ability to teach AST 111.

She hates teaching freshmen and it shows. She teaches things that juniors who took the class never learned in AST 111 and either learned them in higher level Astro classes or not at all. She is great.

Real chill and smart. She knows her stuff well. It helps to be genuinely interested in physics and astronomy otherwise you'll find yourself getting a little bored because she's extremely passionate about that stuff.

Such a nice person and really enthusiastic and smart. It's sometimes hard to follow what she's saying if she gets carried away by her excitement and wanders from topic to topic, but she's always willing to back up and explain things if you don't understand.
Awesomest teacher ever.  Plain and simple.
Brilliant. Hillarious. Great boss.

Lectures are great, readings are chosen very carefully, she gives clear and helpful feedback and there are plenty of class discussions.
Great professor all around
Amazing professor. Super good at explaining concepts.
Dr. clatterbuck leads good discussions and is very nice. Homeworks are problem sets and tests are short-answer

Dr. Clatterbuck is a rock star. Engages class in meaningful discussion, very respectful of opinions, and always available to discuss topics. Class consists of small writing assignments, two essays, and two exams. If you do the reading you will be fine.
Professor Clatterbuck is great and Philosophy of Mind is a really useful class. As a CS major with an interest in AI, I found this class particularly useful and interesting.
Professor Clatterbuck is very smart and an awesome professor. She is chill but also knows her stuff. The class is very manageable if you just attend lecture and do your work.

Professor Ashby is an amazing teacher of economics. She is my favorite Professor and I encourage everyone taking economics to take her classes. She speaks to you like a friend and when you walk away, you feel like a better person. Her teaching abilities are out of this world and she is a top notch Professor.

My English is not that good and I have troubles listening to most Professors. Professor Ashby teaches her lectures in a way that is easy for me to understand. Professor Ashby takes time and will speak to you outside of class.

Attendance is not graded but you need it to have decent notes. The course is suspiciously easy and the tests are exactly like the homework and problem sets. If you do your work, you are pretty much guaranteed a good grade in the course. The lectures can be extremely boring and Ashby tends to spend a crazy amount of time on trivial things.
Ashby has clear powerpoint for students to review the material. But her grade really depends on exams. And the A grade needs a pretty high exam scores.

Professor Ashby teaching ability is top-notch and is willing to help you succeed in her class. Everyone has their strengths and economics is not mine. I recommend Professor Ashby to everyone who struggles in economics. She is very organized and easy to follow.
ECON 207. Too easy for a intermediate course.

Took both Econ108 and Econ207 with Prof Ashby and she is a great lecturer and person. I recommend her to anyone that wants to get into Econ. Lectures are not recorded so it's important to go to class, exams are based off of HWs and Recitation Questions from the unit, recitations are not required, exams are not cumulative and there is no final exam.
Loved the class and the Professor. I recommend taking her class.

Prof. Ashby is a nice person and is very approachable. Tests are easy and often draw straight from the practice sheets, but her lectures are disorganized. 
Lectures are mainly example based and Prof.Ashby overexplains a lot. Highly suggest reading the textbook, it simplifies most of the concepts so you can understand them.
I do not like Economics, but Professor Ashby is a wonderful teacher. I would recommend other students to take her class.
Great Professor.
Great class and a talented Professor. Professor Ashby really helped with problems I had in economics and directed me in the right direction going forward in the economics world.

Professor Ashby is a very caring professor, I enjoyed taking her class. Homework assignments are manageable, and tests are fair. Pay attention in lecture and ask for help, exams are difficult. Make sure to comprehend the material taught in class and not only memorize the content. Make sure not to fall behind, a lot of content goes into the exam!
Enjoyed Professor Ashby's lectures and she was very helpful whenever I approached her. If you attend class you will have no problem passing.

Took ECON 263. Not a difficult class, lectures were kinda dull. She also never/rarely was able to get through all the slides. Exams weren't difficult, she provides practice problems and goes through examples in class.
Professor Ashby was very helpful when I needed the help. Her classes were clear and easy to understand. I met  with her after class multiple times and she answered all my questions.
Very happy that Professor Ashby came to Rochester. I was advised by a fellow student to take her class and I am glad I listened to her. She is such a nice person and a great teacher of economics.

comment: My friend went to Syracuse University where Professor Ashby previously worked and recommended me to take her courses. I have taken two of her classes now and Professor Ashby is a amazing instructor. I am very excited that I listened to my friend.
Was scared to take economics and after taking her class I am not scared anymore.

Love her teaching style. Professor Ashby breaks things down and makes it easy to learn the material. She is refreshing and has a peaceful presence about her. Glad she made the move to Rochester. I have always struggled in this area and she made it easy for me.

Her teachings make it very easy to learn the material. Do the work and go to class and you will have no problems scoring high in her class. Professor Ashby will always help you if you reach out to her. Great addition to University of Rochester. If you are serious in Economics take her class.

Very nice Professor who is down to earth. Professor Ashby took the time to help me when I really needed the help.  Economics is not the most exciting class to take, but she does her best job to get you through  it. Just a good person.
Lectures are organized. Is willing to help if you ask. You will do well in class if you put your time in. If you have to take econ take her class.

comment: Do you work and study for the tests. Economics is really never exciting to learn, but Professor Ashby does a great job. If you go to all the lectures you will have no problem.

Seems like a nice person but teaches like a high school teacher that doesn't care about their job. Has "other important things to do." If you want to pass her class you shouldn't come to lectures because you will fall behind. Instead, read the text book and practice with the website you spent $130 on! WARNING (Don't take pictures of her slides!!)

Dr. Ashby is an amazing Professor. She is very organized and conveys her material with ease. She is willing to help you if you are having troubles and cares about making you a better student. I love her class and hope she stays at Rochester.
Good class and did a sufficient job explaining and covering course content. Projects were fun and not too much work. Hard subject, but overall good class.

He is a very funny professor! He is very chill and the essays are easy, however, the reading is kind of difficult. But I would definitely recommend anyone wanting to take an ENG course it would be with him. Again, very chill professor.

He is hilarious, makes lectures fun, and I've found myself looking forward to the class. There are lots of readings, but put in the time and you should easily pass. There technically are textbooks, but they won't cost you anything unless you want a physical copy as I did. He is extremely understanding and it was a joy to have him. Highly recommend.
Professor Zawacki is very chill. Be sure to participate in class or he'll ghost you on your grades though! He is a chill chost.

He's awesome! Makes lecture incredibly entertaining - you learn without realizing. He's really helpful with any assignments, and understanding of any circumstances you may have regarding needing extensions, etc. 11/10 I recommend.

Overall good and very caring professor, but her out of the book method isn't really optimal for a coding class. That makes this class difficult for 2 credits especially for people who don't have prior coding experience.

Prof. Carney is the goat. She is so nice and knows everyone by name. Her office hours are so helpful she even helped me on other MATLAB stuff. It's not an easy 2 credit course tho. Quizzes every class, but if you read the textbook you'll be fine.

I am glad to have met her at a relatively early stage of my BME study. Her class has truly inspired my passion for this major.
The only thing you need to be aware of is the Bode plot part. She teaches using the mathematical concept of limits. I would say the "poles and zeros" method, as described in the textbook, is more foolproof and efficient.
Best teacher here.
She's a gem! If you're sincere, she'll help you as much as she can!

Professor Carney teaches in a manner that provides students with a legitimate and constructive challenge. This class is certainly not easy, but has left most students engaged in the material. Along with being a clear lecturer, homeworks, tests, and hands-on labs help in fostering a true understanding of the material.
Really tries to get to know her students. Good professor. She is very helpful. Be prepared to get called on in class.
Very clear, honest with students.  Not afraid to fail you if you don't show you can handle the class. But vast majority pass. Class consistently improving year-over-year.

She puts in an effort to get to know students. She is very helpful if you show that you are putting forth an effort. Do the homework and the tests should be easy. The final is designed to rip you a new one so dont take it personally

This class is not that hard, (the midterms are pretty easy), but the final is very, very hard so do well going into it.  Professor is really nice once you get to know her and she tries to make a connection with students.. if you try hard you will do well.

This was Dr. Patterson's first time teaching a college course and, though it took some time for her to get used to running a course, she was a good teacher. As a clinical neuropsychologist, she effectively communicated many important aspects of the field, factually and practically. She cared a lot about her students and checked in with us.

Demina is a great teacher, and a good professor. She excels at teaching and explaining material in a simple and intuitive way, and she engages the class well. However, she is not super accessible, and can be difficult to contact out of class. Overall, she is very good, and hilarious too. Tests were very straightforward. Would definitely recommend!

Demina is probably my favorite lecturer at UR. She delivers the material clearly and is especially clear about what she's going to cover in lecture on the day. It's a hard class with really hard material but if you go in expecting to work and do painful problem sets, you're good. The accent is Russian and so is the humor. She is Legend.

comment: Her heavy Russian accent and ugly handwriting aside, her lecture can barely be followed. There is clearly no organization or logical structure in her lecture. You will find it more effective to study the subject on your own than from her. Also, the textbooks she used for my class is very dated. If possible, by all means, avoid taking her classes.
She's overall a pretty good professor. I mean she's got a thick Russian accent, but if she didn't have it, she definitely would be rated way higher. Her tests are seemingly easy... but very tricky.

Terrible professor. Demina's English is barely understandable,and she is rude and unhelpful at office hours. Her exams are very long and there is no grading curve. I got an A in the class,but that's because I taught myself everything from the book and got a 95% on the final exam. She ought to be fired.

Her physics is very good, her english not so good.  Nice power point slides, spends enough time on them and still takes time to work out problems on the board.  Always had a review class before tests.  She made it interesting.  She is defiantly recommended.

Very hard to understand russian accent, strange humor also. Her tests are way to long, not written or proctored by her either! Lectures drag on and don't cover more than whats already on the lectures. Good lecture but horrible tests that have lengty problems.

Demina has a very heavy russian accent that is difficult to understand. She goes through the powerpoints extremely fast and covers almost a chapter a lecture. The test questions come from the homework problems,so the exams are manageable but very long
No Comments
Does a thorough job of explaining material, boring lectures, straight forward tests and fair grading policy.
Really clarifies the information she's teaching, sometimes even too much. A great sense of humor and very straightforward tests.

Regina is cool, lecture gets boring but what hour and 20 minute lecture doesnt? be warned: her tests are only one hour long!  (wish i knew that before there were only 5 minutes left and i still had a whole page to go...)

She repeats everything at least 3 times, sometimes spending 40 minutes to explain a single PP slide. It's more than nessacery, and so really feels like she's wasting half the period when she could be covering a lot more material.
I really enjoyed this course, Morris Pierce is one of the kindest souls at u of r
HIST 186- he's a kind soul.
HIST 186- kind soul

Professor Pierce is a great guy. Any class you take with him will be relatively easy, but you still need to put in the work. He has great lecture slides with lots of information. Complete your assignments ahead of time and stay ahead of the game. Attendance isn't mandatory but very much appreciated. Great class!

Honestly the easiest/most chill class I've ever taken in U of R. Only graded by 4 papers that are very generously graded. Attendance is not mandatory, and as long as you follow instruction & submit your work on time, you should be all good.
Genuinely the easiest professor you can get at UofR. If you want an easy A and don't mind writing 4 more 4-6 page papers in the semester, you'll get an A.

I took Hist 186 with him. Extremely easy course. Take him if you want a free A. The grading was all based on three papers that are guaranteed A's. The lectures are not mandatory and he posts slides. You can write about whatever you want, it does not have to be related to lecture.

Easily the best professor and kindest professor you will ever have at this school. His papers can be longer at times, but they aren't hard to write and he will give you feedback to improve in future papers. For sure respect and suggest a Morris Pierce class.

Take this course if you are interested in military history. He is easygoing and friendly. He only restricts your essay topics to broad time periods so you can write about anything you find interesting in that time period. You will do well in the course if you know how to write at a college level (formatted, cited, and professional tone).

Never gives fair grades. He would only refer you to writing center which proved thousands of time useless. No grading materials and if you treat his paper as academic research you will get low grade. And if you use some new historiography you will get low grade.
Really nice Prof! He is super responsive and helpful, I passed his class with full marks on each paper and never went to class (reviewed PowerPoints in my own time). Honestly a gem!
5 papers in class... honestly I think it's just a completion grade. Didn't go to any of his lectures but still got an A. Very easy class, professor is kind and responsive.

If you have to take a history class Professor Pierce is your guy. Attendance isn't mandatory and the workload is minimal.  Showing up somewhat regularly and asking a few questions during class goes a long way. No textbooks either is a definite plus.
Interesting class and stories. Amazingly friendly professor who is easy to work with and provides students with plenty of academic freedom. Highly recommended.

Amazing class!!! You do not have any reading or exams. You do not need to attend class. The homework is just four essays which are easy to get high scores. You do not need to do anything and you can get an A.

Professor Pierce is low maintenance, easy going professor. You know exactly what he wants on tests and quizzes, and sometimes even says in lecture "you might want to remember this for the quiz" which he then hands out. Also he is a veteran of the Vietnam War and roomed with David Petraeus at West Point.
Go to class and pay attention.  This man has the most interesting stories.

This truly was the easiest class I've ever taken at UR.  He would plop in a video, turn the lights down, and then sit at the back of the class reading.  All assignments were papers and were generally easy to write if you paid attention to the movies and you read the assignments.  I think he spoke less than 100 words to our class the whole semester.
Easiest class I've taken here-no homework, really easy assignments, entertaining lectures.
Really boring professor. Does not know how to keep class interested. Also has no feeling for the whole class is lost and asleep

Professor Black is an amazing teacher, I learned so much in her intro to climate change class. As someone who has never taken any science classes she made the technical aspects of climate change very easy to understand without oversimplifying. She was always happy and enthusiastic to answer any question I had.

Professor Black is undoubtably the best professor I've had at UofR. She shows a genuine respect and care for her students, and is wonderfully accommodating. She's very passionate about environmental science, a fact which is evident in every one of her lectures. The first third of the semester was difficult, the rest was pretty easy. 10/10 reccomend

Where do I start... The kindest, most understanding professor I've had in my 4 years at the UR.  She's professional and fun at the same time.  She always values students' feedback and continuously tries to improve the learning experience. Do yourself a favor and sign up for her class; whether its grad, under-grad, or W, all options are manageable.
The only big assignments are problem sets and the final presentation (An extra paper for writing students). Not a hard class and would like to recommend people to take it.

Prof. Black is a great professor. Everything asked on the exam is thoroughly reviewed in class and she genuinely cares about each student's performance and wellbeing. Not too much work, but you should attend lectures as they are better than the book.

Loved this class! Great intro to climate science/environmental science in general. I'm an env. sci. major so obvious bias, but Professor Black is really clear on what you need to know, so all you need to have to get an A in this class is determination. Take thorough notes, review all the content before midterm/final, and you'll be in great shape!
Lectures can drag on but Professor Duro is extremely nice and helpful. He encourages discussion and the class is interesting

If you enjoy art history, this class will be enjoyable. However, if you aren't so passionate about art (as a cluster class in my case), lectures can get a bit boring. The class is graded on 4 essays spread through the semester and a participation grade. Professor Duro is very kind and he gives a lot of good feedback on the essays!

Definitely a class to take! The lectures can feel a bit long at times and seem to drag on but the material is very intetestinf, especially if you're into art history yet never had the time to delve into the theory on your own. The readings should read carefully when they apply to the essays, otherwise you can skim and be ready for class
Very helpful professor. He is very clear on getting the information across during lecture. Love his corny jokes too xD

Bailey is an awesome professor. He's hilarious and does a wonderful job explaining concepts in class. The homework is definitely highly suggested, his tests really are based off of them. Sad thing he's leaving next semester because he's a visiting professor but I'm definitely glad I took his class. Curves nicely.

Overall, he's a good teacher. Funny and personable. The exams are usually fine if you've done the recommended problems in the book and he curves so the average is a B. If you have to take multidimensional calc, take it with Bailey.
Hilarious, and a great treacher.
Good teacher, but another teacher makes math tests. He did not cover what other teacher wanted us to know for test well.
Easy class. Tests were a lot harder than you'd expect from the homework though, but the curve was sufficient. and homework was 50% of the grade.
Witty, funny, intelligent, a skilled conversationalist. Passionate about the subject and excellent at explaining.
Very nice and funny!!! Love him!!! Love his Curve on the final!!!!! mmmmm~

Very good professor. Grades with significant curve (makes average 80%). Tests are very reasonable, provides the ridiculous formulas. Only gripe was that he did not provide practice exams, only suggested homework which often comprised of 100-150 problems. Would recommend, however. Very difficult course but he made it possible

Professor Bailey is amazing.  He is an excellent teacher and does a great job at explaining difficult concepts in a clear way.  He makes himself very available for questions, and he is excellent at balancing scary material and yet making it relatable.  Very fair guy, excellent character.
Awesome professor!! Friendly, interesting, helpful, and makes things manageable!

Bailey is a really great professor.  He has a hilarious sense of nerdy humor and he's always ready to explain things.  He's very fair, and friendly, answers emails, and his catchphrase is 'I love cookies'.

Prof Kumar was so good to me. This was the easiest class I have ever taken. Get to know him, I went to his office hours every week and we would just talk math. It is so worth it because on my midterms, I knew I missed some points at, but he graded me very easily and therefore it ended in me getting 100s. Answer his questing in lecture!

No work done by himself. He did literally nothing except for reading textbook. Can never make a point clear. Class is useless, RUN if you can, GO ATTEND OTHER SECTIONS IF YOU CAN. Indeed one of the worst professor you can ever have in this school.
Grading are unclear and harsh, final grades are posted but without telling how you did.
He just simply recited the textbook in class. The assignments were too much and difficult, with little relevance to his lectures. The exams also had little to do with past exams.

Worst ever professor in the math dept. Lectures are useless and boring, basically just reading textbooks. Emails are responded but always not up-to-date. If he said in class he will get back to you on Wednesday, and you will receive his email at earliest Friday. basically all other work except for the lecture are done by other sections' professor.
Great professor overall. Lectures could be a little bit more engaging but he's a very nice professor and always takes time to answer student questions. Very patient and accessible!

Had interesting lectures but made them bearable to follow and pay attention. The course itself is hard and test make up most of the grading. But the professor was very helpful if one had a question and was always willing to help. Reading the textbook from the start makes the class much easier to follow.
His lecture style was a little disorganized and boring, and he mostly teaches to the textbook. Very understanding with missed due dates. Posts lecture notes online which is extremely useful.

comment: He is very respected and knowledgable in math, but his lectures are pretty monotone, he just reads right off of the textbook. In class he isn't great, but in office hours, he is super help
The syllabus with 8-9 chapters of content, comes with 13 chapters, tests involved in derivation, and proofs.

Professor Mueller had an uncanny style of teaching. His hand-writing ability was fine, but, he often explained what he was writing poorly. I found that it was sometimes extremely hard to understand the lecture he was lecturing. For exams, I had to watch "The Organic Chemistry Tutor" a lot. I tended to use his notes as a backup option for studying.

comment: His lecture is kind of fast, and I think reading the textbook is more helpful. His exam is extremely tough.

Definitely a brilliant guy, but not good at explaining things. Sometimes I just want the formulas, in which that's all his lectures are good for. Beats around the bush a lot trying to explain stuff, and gets time for 2 examples per lecture that don't help with the homework. Class is slow at times.

Professor Carl is def a good guy, patient, approachable. HOWEVER, homework wouldn't help at all tbh. they are completely different from exams. his exams can be really hard, and i personally found it more helpful to read the book to prep.
I took mth 201 this semester and he was pretty easy to reach out to. His exams can be hard, but he has a good curve. This course contains a lot of statistics contents.

Written HWs and Exams are not remotely similar in level of difficulty to anything covered in class (or in previous sections of the same class by different profs...). He's a good guy who's available, but if the class is going to be this hard, there needs to be better preparation.

He discussed EXTREMLY easy examples in class, but give us EXTREMLY HARD exams and written homework assignments. It is rediculous. MTH201 is not actually hard, but the prof is making the course extremly difficult. For class just reading books and rewrite examples in book and lectures are not perfectly structural. Massive and hard. I regret to take.
He's an amazing professor who is truly smart and dedicated. You'll learn a lot from him. Also, he'll make sure you work to understand every smallest detail, which I find really helpful in long terms.
Such an amazing professor. AMAZING

Awful professor, brilliant mathematician. Genuinely sucks at explaining concepts, mostly because he spends his time proving hand-wavey theorems and corollaries that will never be of any use to people who are taking this class as a requirement. Hell, even math majors get scared off from his teaching style. Nice guy, but that's about all I can say.

comment: Terrible professor. Does too many proofs and not enough examples. Over complicates everything.

Dry lecturer. He ends up proving random things on the board without really giving a good explanation as to why he's doing it. The only times I've followed an entire lecture without getting lost are when I read the chapter beforehand. The best way to get ready for the exams is to do the practice exams. Read the textbook for conceptual understanding.

Carl Mueller is a nice guy however a poor lecturer. Organization of notes on a blackboard can me mediocre at best. His voice will put you to sleep and his examples for theorems are poorly explained. I suggest not taking this professor if you striving to get an A in what is considered a hard class.

The class is what it is, but Prof. Mueller is a very poor lecturer. He mostly just rewrote the examples in the book. I felt uncomfortable in his class, and by the end of the semester most students had either stopped attending or had switched sections.  MTH201 is not easy and gets hard fast. Find a TA.

Hated this class--made me change my major. He jumps around teaching different concepts without spending much time on them/introducing them. Many times we wouldn't even know what he was talking about until someone asked why it would be useful. Expect weekly proofs and webworks. Go to office hours EARLY ON. If you ask for help, he will help.

Lectures can be a little confusing as he just writes in little corners where there is some free space so definitely confusing to follow him. Depends on your learning style but I found it wasn't worth my time to go to class. Really nice guy, and wants students to succeed. However, homeworks, WebWorks, and tests all seemed unrelated.

Honestly his class was awful and I had to drop it because I didn't understand anything, and I got an A in 141. He is so unclear with his explanations that I had to attempt to teach myself everything outside of class. Avoid him if possible.
Genuinely nice guy who has an interest in teaching to the best of his ability. Very knowledgable
Can get confusing at times, but has an interest in helping his students understand the material
so annoying as a professor. cleans board weird
Super friendly and helpful. Lectures were slightly dry but thorough. His subtle and lighthearted sense of humor and his calling on people at random made class enjoyable.
He looks like the Green Goblin from Spiderman! A nice guy but not extremely clear when explaining things. Gets very excited for his special problem things. Could have been better.
Excellent teacher- one of the best math profs.
Very nice and helpful, but class is dull and drags on. He calls on people without warning, which I hate. He also has a habit of not bothering to do harder problems saying "they're too much trouble."
One of the most clever profs I've had.  But subtle. Jokes only caught up to me 3 or 4 days later.  But this material I learned more thoroughly than in any other class.
Doesn't explain challenging problems in class which is harmful especially when tests and homeworks are harder.
He wears the same sweater everyday! His class is boring and confusing, but he is a nice guy, and wants to help his students.

REALLY likes math. Bores me to death but he insists on everyone participating, even if no one knows the answers. Class seems to drag on and on, but he is really nice & wants everyone to do well. Has a math sense-of-humor; very dorky. And Birkenstocks..

Boring and confusing lecturer.  Unorganized and frantic, always talking about her cats. The theories were hard to understand and her explanations could have been better.  Understanding the material is difficult but getting an A in the class is easy as she gives you exactly what will be on the exams.  Also seems to be quite lenient in grading

She was always all over the place and relied on the TA's to do things for her. She was very full of herself and never was prepared. She would show up late to class and got mad at the students when they didnt show up. Tests were somewhat easy and she often went over what would be on them. just very unorganized and kind of spacey.
Often unprepared for lectures. I had hoped to learn more in this class.

Professor Kroeger is very nice and seems to genuinely be interested in the material she teaches. You can tell she cares about her students. This class was easy and fun, mostly discussion based with a few small papers.
One of the nicest professors I've ever met. Lectures can sometimes get a bit boring, but it's an easy A and she really cares about the students.

Two things are graded: participation and a final 10-20 page paper. You must read a lot of articles, and if you are a STEM major, do not overload this class. I did and it was exceptionally hard to keep. It is interesting, but if you have no experience with analyzing and critiquing papers, its difficult to understand him. Mainly discussion

Miron doesn't teach students how to think critically about scientific papers and expects students to already know how to critique studies. 50% of the class grade was participation, 50% was a final paper, so you won't be graded until the very end and by that point, you can't do anything to change it. Grading criteria were unclear. Wouldn't recommend

comment: As a STEM major, Dr. Sbriglia was AMAZING. All the books he assigned were interesting and he read over my drafts and gave me great feedback that really improved my writing. I had to miss a few classes for med school interviews and he was so supportive and accomodating. I never felt like I was behind the curve bc I wasn't an english major.

comment: Prof Sbriglia is a great guy and always willing to help.

Took an American Studies class with him at St. John Fisher college and absolutely loved it. Great teacher, gave help whenever needed, and pushed me to find new pieces of literature to help better understand concepts in American history.

Prof. Sbriglia is the best guy on the face of the planet. As a chemistry major, I never was very good at English, but Prof. Sbriglia made it very easy to do well in his class. Extraordinarily entertaining, nicest guy at this school. Lectures were interesting because he made them fun and informative. I would take any of his classes in a heartbeat!

Professor Alio is really nice and definitely cares about her students. The class is mostly lecture based with some pop quizzes so make sure you go to class. If you attend class you don't need to read the textbook and there is not much other work. Interesting topics, mostly common sense, and overall an easy A.

Great professor, talks about relevant topics, not only in the US but globally. Discussion-based class, new interesting topics, funny, engages class well, receives constructive feedback. Class is easy A if you complete work and is proactive.
A nice teacher! Definitely an easy A if you do all your work.

She was a great professor! Her humor and knowledge makes you want to come to class. She's also published various research papers and has simple slides for lectures. The only thing I would suggest is to look out for pop-up assignments in class ( which are so easy). Take her for a nice grade and to learn new things!

I love Paula!!!! I think people on here are just sensitive. She was super funny and knowledgeable. I don't think you guys realize how accomplished and smart she is! I loved this class and loved the group discussions. There were pop quizzes but one missed one is excused. This class is a very easy A if you do everything you need to.

If you want an easy A, take it with her - no exams or papers, only 1 group project that is graded very leniently. However - I agree with other students that she is a terrible professor and not that great of a person either. Did not care a single bit about the class and made several offensive remarks.

I had Prof. Alio for P.H. 101 and really enjoyed it. Lectures were fairly interesting but sometimes boring. There are no tests (this may have just been a covid thing), just homework assignments, in-class workshops, and projects so it's super easy to get a good grade.
