Great professor, teaches writing in a very accessible & managable way. Gives amazing feedback, is extremely understanding and works with students to help reach their full potential. Take her class if you are interested in gsws or social science. She's very supportive and easy to talk to. Readings are interesting, very managable.

She's a great professor, very caring and kind and easy to talk to. She works hard to get everyone engaged in the work and gives great feedback on papers. I love how she structured that class and made a writing class interesting to the best of her abilities. We have similar academic interests, so I'm planning to take another one of her classes.

Reachable, kind, patient. She gave helpful supports and suggestions during office hour. I took contemporary social movement with her. If you work hard in this class you will get an A and feel more confident about writing.

She's one of the best professors I've had during my time at Rochester! There are some students who believe that they can get away by doing the bare minimum, but as long as you put in your effort, the class will not seem as intensive. As like any other class, if you want an A, be proactive, and you'll see your results.

I was recommended Professor ODonnell by multiple other students prior to taking one of her classes. She encourages creative thought and discussion, while also enhancing students learning on each topic presented. Shes extremely supportive and easy to talk to. Shes enthusiastic, knowledgeable, and one of my favorite professors Ive had.

She seems like a nice person but I feel like she takes this class way too seriously. It's basic required writing 105, not advanced 400 level English major specific writing. Also, she is not a very warm person, she acts like she is very funny and friendly but her comments on our papers and work make her seem harsh and cold.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'So many papers']

comment: I met at least five other students who took her classes and everyone shared the same feeling about professor O'Donnell: thought-provoking, funny, caring, clear. I took her Modern Social Movements class, the assignments were challenging, but her guidance was excellent. The readings and discussions: absolutely engaging. Very supportive professor.

Professor Welte's passion for science and teaching really made this an enjoyable class. I really appreciated that he took the time to get to know his students, and offer help. The assignments were challenging, but very applicable to a career in biology research. I thought this was the best course I've taken at UR.

It's obvious that he is excited about his art and wants you to share his passion as well. I guess the best way to make a person swim is to throw him in the water. This is exactly what Prof. Welte does. He would make you read loads of papers and come up with project proposals and give presentations and actively participae in class discussions.

What an EXCELLENT professor!  He answers any questions you have and encourages discussions toward which he contributes very clear and concise information.  He has a passion for the material, and his German accent is awesome.  Oh, and I think he's gay which would explain his apparent fabulous-ness :D

Genuinely, very smart, you can tell she knows what she's talking about. But so unpleasant and hateful to students that it made me dread every single class with her. Her entire demeanor is punitive and though I'll have to take other classes with her to graduate, I will be loathing her the entire time.

I was trying to give her the benefit of the doubt w how condescending her demeanor can be sometimes, but the way she graded and left feedback on assignments.. It just felt like she assumes too much out of intro level students, and doesn't make things accessible enough for us to understand. Then acts like its our fault.

Dr. Miller can seem harsh sometimes, but she does care. Lectures are dense, but you can record her to listen to later. Make sure you stay on track because it is very hard to catch up if you fall behind. As long as you study with enough time before exams, this is definitely a manageable class. Just be ready for it to take up a lot of time.

I honestly really liked Dr Miller but did not like this class. Unfortunately, this class made me switch my major (not because it was too hard, it's manageable). this class is unavoidable for any student pursing neuro so be prepared! The content itself was rather interesting but I thought we would have done more with this class.
Most condescending teacher i've met; reason why I'm not a neuro major.
my number one op. went to all lectures and OH in this class and she never learned my name. content was interesting, but she was very demeaning.

NSCI201 lab is graded by too few things. If you did terrible in one assignment or quiz, no matter how hard you try in other assignments, you will still be screwed. It is not a "graded on completion/effort" course, but it should have been, because many questions in assignments, even in quiz, are open ended.

She explains well and is available for extra help. However, she is a tough *very tough* grader and the class grades always stay the same. Her way of asking questions in exams is very "her" so write what she would answer and not how the book might answer it

I respect her and she is very knowledgable. I struggled with the content and had to rewatch every lecture to understand (self recorded), but if you have more bio/research background it may be easier. My ability to read research papers has improved, and if you demonstrate interest, she is really nice and understanding (including with grade bonuses)

201Lab was tough, since there were few assignments we were graded by. Listen to her instructions and copy them EXACTLY (take crazy notes or record her) and you will do well enough. She really likes when students demonstrate interest - go to her OH or chat with her and she might grade more nicely...I liked her overall and found her very knowledgable

She is such an intellectual and knowledgeable person inspiring her students to think critically. 301 is made up of discussions and presentations covering interesting topics that bridge science and society, like neuro ethics, scientific integrity, neuroeconomics etc. Do the readings, show up, and talk and talk. then you will get a A in this class.

Dr. Miller is such an amazing professor. I was told by peers to avoid her, so that's what I tried to do, but it's near impossible as a neuro major. I took two classes with her and I don't know what my peers were talking about. She was incredibly caring and kind to me, and explained everything so well, and was more than happy to answer my questions.

Professor Miller is one of the least understanding professors I have had at the university. She quizzes you on small details, grades really hard, and is not clear about the expectations for her assignments. She is the reason I switched my major, and I have heard similar experiences from others.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']

comment: I took her neurochemistry course in summer online. The content was dense but hard. A lot of paper discussions and write-ups & presentations. You have to attend the lectures and discussions as well as prepare for lecture quizzes and exams, but none of them was too difficult. Definitely learned a lot of things in depth and she is very helpful.

Dr. Miller is very knowledgable on the topics that she teaches and is clearly passionate in the field of neuro. Her class is tough and she definitely makes you work for it, but it's a class worth taking. She is also very helpful and caring during office hours, which I recommend going to.
A tough instructor, but a very intelligent and caring woman. Always prepared and likes to make you think. Class participation is very important.
Her class was overall very easy to succeed in however the book assigned was completely useless the only way to get a good grade was to go to class and memorize her slides.

She is my favorite professor at this school. Yes, her tests are hard, and she makes you actually learn and apply the material, but she is very willing to help you if you go to her office hours. Once I went to go over a test and she ended up giving me 5 points back.
She is very difficult to follow. Avoid taking a class with her if possible. Literally just throws jargon at you and is extremely rude.
Extremely helpful. Best professor at the school.
Had her as a lab professor. She was very nice and I thought she was approachable.
She seemed very nice to me and approachable. I only had her as a lab professor though.

Steven York is not a professor, rather, he is a TA for this class. The professor Mark Povich is a very good professor, but this TA ruined our interest towards this course. He deducted 10 points in midterm for using sth. instead of something???

Was more like an anthro class. She is definitely well-read and experienced but if you disagreed with her she could be rude. SO many rules in the classroom and felt like being back in middle school/being babied. Would grade super harsh then blame the class for our low average even though there were only 16 people in my class.

Was VERY political, and if you didn't agree then you were wrong. She only focused on female archaeologists and she always bashed the male archaeologists. Was more like a history class tbh. There is 2 exams (no final) and there are 2 long papers and presentations. Attendance is graded and she has a lot of classroom rules. Felt like I was 10 again...

Felt like sitting in a middle school class. I thought the class would be based on Archaeology, but it was more like Anthropology and she was very political. Not the best grader and she only considered "one correct answer" in many cases. Also could be rude and had very harsh in classroom rules, I felt babied often.

I had her for ATHS381, She is very passionate about the study, and it's obvious she cares a lot about the subject matter at hand. She did end up canceling a lot of classes, and since the class was only once week, I feel like I missed a lot, but outside of that, when we did have class it was very insightful and I feel like I learned a lot.

Did not teach archaeology as a science based course, but rather as a history class, based on the struggles and social issues faced by archaeologists across history. Not what I was looking for, felt like taking a high school class all over again: long syllabus, harsh class rules, etc.

"Inkas & Their Ancestors" class crosslisted as Anthro and History, but it obviously is an Archaeology class. Her lectures are VERY information heavy and definitely focus on Peru's prehistory (briefly discuss the Inkas for 2 weeks). Time consuming projects (make a khipu, study a site via Google Earth) but she's nice and passionate about her field

Bautista is a sweetheart, very knowledgeable, and incredibly caring. Class was almost entirely discussion-based with a few scattered lectures so participation is important. There's a lot of reading but it's difficult (though not impossible) to participate without the readings so at least skim them. Bautista expects a lot but she's a fair grader.
The class was difficult but it was helpful that Professor Bautista was very passionate about the topic.
Dr. Goldschmidt grades essays leniently and will give review sheets right before the exams covering everything you need to know. Funny guy, great class. Exactly what I'm looking for in a phil course

Funny Professor but can also explain harder concepts (e.g. Metaethics) very competently. His class is super chill: there are three midterms all of which are very manageable, plus an essay which he provides clear guidelines along with an example essay for. PHL102 is a great class to start a PHL cluster, especially if you have never done PHL before.

Only four assignments, three tests and one essay. The tests are pretty straightforward and you can learn everything straight from the book or internet, you really don't need the class. The facilitation of discussion is quite boring, frankly. The professor usually complains about his salary and that gets old after awhile. Wouldn't take again.
tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Funny professor. Cares for students that show up to lecture. Tests are straightforward. Makes lots of jokes that make more complex topics easier to understand and remember. Overall good professor.

I've taken 2 classes with Lacina and they're not bad. However, for this class, your whole grade is based on 3 essays so make sure you are good at writing and studying the content throughout the semester. My only complaint is that her grading criteria varied for each of my essays so it was hard to understand what she was looking for.

Professor Lacina is kind but not the most engaging professor. This class is incredibly reading-heavy, so make sure you can dedicate enough time to read a book a week (or at least skim it thoroughly). Her feedback sometimes varies, I wish she was a little more specific at times, but overall not a bad course!

Professor Lacina is a skilled political scientist and kind person, but sometimes not the most engaging as a professor. My biggest issue was that the amount of reading assigned was completely unrealistic, and this is coming from someone who has taken quite reading-heavy courses in the past. Feedback is useful and grading is not harsh.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Would not recommend Prof Lacina. She came across as very awkward,unclear, and not very confident with the material. The assigned readings for the class were interesting, but Prof Lacina was boring as an instructor and killed all interest I had in the class.

The course itself was an easy A, but the instructor was frequently confused and not very knowledgeable. Professor Lacina was also just socially awkward and not good at interacting with students, which made class meetings uncomfortable.

I love her.  She seemed kinda dry in the beginning, but by the end of the class she was my favorite.  She is not a pushover, she is organized and expects something from you, she is really smart and you will learn a lot.  She is an excellent lecturer and very inspiring, she treats you like an adult, in a good way. She's just really great.

Prof is helpful, approachable, passionate about the subject, but poor lecturer.  Frequently pauses in mid-sentence as if confused. An overall interesting class and not too difficult, but lectures are not inspiring and usually lackluster.  Take the course if you are interested in the subject. Lacina probably won't inspire.

Professor Lacina is awesome. This class was very interesting, and she managed the discussion in a way that kept it quite engaging. I would call her neither difficult nor easy, but students should expect to at least skim the reading. Her knowledge is vast, but she's still very friendly and funny. Acts more like a grad student than a professor.

one of the best econ instructors I ever had. No slides in class, so you truly have to attend class to follow the material. He encourages discussion during lectures. Assignments are challenging, and there are no completely “standard” answers. You can only perform well if you read the  materials and fully understand the concepts he explains in class.
You need to understand economics in his logic because his logics are logical and correct. Tests are awesome! Love this course
You have to understand economics through his own logic or else you won't pass. Grades are solely based on the two midterms and the final exam. Tests are hard.

Respected and well-known professor who is truly knowledgeable about economics. Might be a little controversial on his published books. Materials he teach is very clear and concise. Follows a nice logic and time line. Very well-structured lecture and information.

Landsburg is really smart, and the course content is quite fun. The course is 100% homeworks, so take it if for the low stress environment. The homeworks are a little challenging, but nothing absurd, and the grading is fairly generous. You have to do well in 207 in order to get into the course (you apply for it), but don't let that scare you away

Very hard course, but he is good at explaining concepts. Lectures are enlightening, but homework is hard. This course is only open to those who have got an A/A+ in Landsburg's 207 course. So, you will meet the top students there. Students are amazing!
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Fantastic genius! A true legend in Economics. If you study hard, put effort, and are good at math. You will definitely get an A. He is good at separating the hard-working and non-hard-working students. Grades will tell.

Prof responded to "no partial credit" myth with some stats. Unfortunately, the data is likely to be biased. Even getting 1% credit falls into the "partial credit" category. It would be more convincing if the actual distribution of the grades is shown. His course might still be good, but I hope people correctly understand what to expect.

He is a nice person and very approachable outside of class. However, his grading criteria is vague, and he has his unique way of solving problems and understanding economics. Highly recommend to do all the homework, but tests are much harder than that. His lecture is inspiring, but you do not need to attend if you just want to have a good grade.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: Professor Landsburg is definitely one of my favorite professors. His lectures are always fun, and he makes a boring economic concept very interesting. You will learn a whole new approach to microeconomics. Make sure to do your homework because those questions are very similar to exam questions.
Final was nearly impossible! Econ is not just about understanding econ! You have to understand his logic, the way how he want you to do it. If you don't, good luck!

Not very accommodating when it came to COVID and quarantine. Also, 90% of lecture were very boring (even for someone who loves econ). Tests were very difficult but the curve was fair. Don't look into his background bc he has said some controversial things that you prob don't want to know about.

His logic makes such little sense, and exam grading is actual crap, you either understand Econ HIS way or he fails you. But my biggest problem with him is that he doesnt post solutions for any previous exams he shares, nor does he tell his TAs about anything, so if they solve a question wrong and teach that, youll never know.

Final grades are available. Again, this is one of my favorite class at UR. It has been my pleasure to take both 108 and 207 with professor Landsburg. I am not sure if he is still teaching ECO108 and ECO207, but if he does, you should definitely take economics classes with him.
I am still waiting for my final grade for this class. But still, this is one of my favorite class and favorite professor. I like economics because of him.

He's not as bad as people said, but you really need to hit the point to get a good grade. For his class, either you are an A student or a C student, and there are NO in between. Sometimes even F... There are no partial credit even if you demonstrate you understand some of the materials.

This professor only gives a grade based on 2 midterms and a final. In these papers, he doesn't give any partial credit so it's very easy to mess up in one small area and get a 0 on that question. The concepts he teaches are not that hard but his explanation sometimes confuses me. I've understood more from TAs than him.

Homework does not count towards grades. If you get a question wrong on exam, means that you did not pay attention in class or did not completely understand the questions you got wrong on your homework. I can tell that midterms are fair, and the grading is not that harsh as what you said. So it is surely your problem for not doing well on the exam.
Lecture is good, but homework and exams are really tough... Insanely harsh grader on exam. Either you get the full credit for a question on exam or no credit at all.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']

comment: He is a really good economics professor! His explanation and the logic of his lecture is extremely clear! I like economics because of him, and I need his rating to go up!
good teaching skills

Professor Landsburg shares a lot of inspirational stories in this course. He introduces several useful and also interesting topics which might change the way you think about economics and business. Definitely should take this course if you are interested in economics.

Professor Landsburg is one of the best and smartest professors here at U of R. His lecture is well-organized and inspirational. His logic is clear and easy to follow. Spend times on reviewing lecture notes and HW problems, then you will get a good grade.
He knows what he is doing.

He is a great lecturer and you do not need to use the textbook after watching the lecture he really covers everything there. The only concern for this course is that exams counts for 85% for your grade and they are pretty difficult. Still, the curve is good 85.1% is an A in this semester so I think overall thee course is great!
A different vibe comparing to Rizzo
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']

comment: I like this class because we only get a few webwork problems each week, and as long as you pay attention to the lectures, these problems are easy to finish. Exams, two midterms and a final, are fair. You do need to spend time review the course materials and do practice problems if you want to do well on these exams.
tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Amazing class, amazing professor. I learned so much and his lectures really stick in your memory. Class is homework based entirely; the work is very difficult but rewarding and doable. Anyone who wants a true in-depth understanding of micro-economics should take this class

Ridiculously tough exams. I attended every lecture, understood every concept and did every homework and still got a B+ because I messed up one long question in one exam. The margin of error is razor thin. The class is very interesting, great intro to econ. Highly quantitative teaching style.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']

comment: His logic is extremely unique yet clear. This class is mainly graph-based and is easy for some people yet hard for others. Study hard makes an A easy. This course definitely gives a great introduction to microeconomics and some macro at the end of the semester. Worth the time to take this class with one of the most respected economists out there.

As long as you understand his unique logic (may take some time), you will see that his logic is extremely clear and simple. It is very important to follow all of his lectures and logics, and this makes an A relatively easy. People who tend to fail are usually people who do not go to lectures or people who don't seek help when they don't understand.

Professor Landsburg is excellent at presenting topics clearly, and answers all questions with as much explanation as is necessary. Tests are challenging but very fair, everything you need to learn is extensively covered in class.
People who got a bad grade come here to complain. Yes, I am, and trust me, u will be no exception. Ridiculous exam and grading. Ready to fail.
Only two midterms and one final in his class count toward your final grade. It is and he always makes the test hard as hell. Not recommended to take his class.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy', 'Tough grader']

comment: He is one of the smartest professors around. He will make you question simple things around you in a good way. His classes are more organized and structured which allows you to do well if you go to all the classes and review your notes. I was told his classes were math heavy but I would say they are more logic heavy than mathematical

Take landsburg if you hate yourself. Just kidding, take landsburg if you love math and are majoring in econ and suffering. Take Rizzo if you prefer a more abstract and accessible approach to economics. This class taught me some hard lessons. I burned out because I hated it. He and his style are not my preference. Be self-aware and save yourself
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Graded by few things', 'Test heavy']

comment: The class and professor will truly change your outlook on how the world works. If you want to know what Econ is all about, take this class. The material is easy to understand if you pay attention in lecture and make an effort to learn. There is not much homework but it is vital to continue to think about what was discussed in class.

ECO208W is the most challenging but also the most rewarding course in the economics department. It is the class where you see the Armchair Economist at his finest, and you really learn how to think like one of the best economists out there. The topics in the class are relatable and make you see the world around you differently.

Professor Landsburg's ECO207 gives strong foundation to more advanced topics in the field of economics through easy-to-follow lectures. Although many found his exams tricky, the key to succeeding is being able to apply key facts that are repeated clearly in every lecture and when reviewing HW in class.

Professor Landsburg's class is the better choice for ECO108 at U of R. He provides both a quantitative and theoretical foundation in economics, so you will be prepared for all other courses in the economics department. His lectures are very clear and easy to follow. If you learn and apply the basic rules he presents, you will succeed in the exams.
tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: The content covered is pretty much the same as ECO108, but the homework and exams are much much harder. He only covers very basic examples in class, and you have to really practice to get much harder questions right on exams. The final is mad tough, and you're probably gonna get at least one impossible question on it.
Easy course material, doable exam, great lecture.

Going to class was actually fun. The lectures are very clear, with lots of interesting real-world examples. Also, he always hangs around after class to take questions, which is really helpful. Tests are pretty easy if you study, impossible if you don't.

After I blew an exam problem, he sent me a long email, with diagrams, explaining exactly where I'd gone wrong. He also told me the rest of my exam was great and I shouldn't be discouraged by this one mistake. I really appreciated this. Lectures are clear and sometimes fascinating. Best course at UR so far.

I dropped this class because almost everything in this class is a nightmare Not very respectful to students in his office hours and gave out exams testing stuff that makes no sense. For the sake of my time and gpa, I dropped his course.

For Gives 0 partial credit on exams. Must read book, copy correct HW answers shown in class(Completing all these correctly can bump grade by .5 to 1.0 letter grade) & all he writes on board, do prac exams and go to review sessions. Get either A or F, but all based on you. Prac exams q's/HWK directly correlate to the topics you need to Ace class.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'Tough grader']

comment: Professor Landsburg is an expert in economics and teaches the material well. He efficiently and effectively translates difficult concepts to allow students to perform well on very straight-forward exams. The class really is not too difficult if you apply yourself and try to understand the concepts. I really enjoyed taking ECO108 from Landsburg.

He is a really good professor, and I highly recommend taking a class with him! I think I learned the most in his introductory courses and I really enjoyed his graph-based explanationsthey definitely helped to clarify and elucidate concepts. Most students Ive talked to enjoyed his class, but you do have to put in effort to get a good grade.
If you have the opportunity to take this class, do so.
Now that I am about to graduate, I can say that Eco 207 was the best course I took at the University of Rochester, and Professor Landsburg is the best teacher I've had anywhere, ever.
He was an extremely tough grader and really unfair. Barely gave partial credit and wasn't very approachable after class. He also seemed to really enjoy roasting students.
Difficult class but worth it if youre willing to put in the effort. Make sure to do lots of practice problems before exams. The exams are difficult but doable.

Just go take Rizzos. I love everything about this professor but not the final test. You either get it or none. I almost failed the course because of my test performance even though I understand all his concepts. Now Im retaking micro with rizzo and I feel so much relief.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: His class tests your critical thinking rather than the concepts that you learn. You can do all the problems on the etxtbook but it will be useless if you dont reflect on what you did.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Just avoid and take Rizzo's 207. It's that simple.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Ok Landsburg is not a bad lecturer. But his exams are HARD.. I know 3 people who failed ECO207 last semester and we went to every lecture and did all the homeworks. My point is no matter how well you know Microeconomics, you may fail the exams (100% of your course grade) and the class. Beware if you have to take this awful course.. otherwise avoid!
AVOID. Period.
Spent time, got nearly 100% on midterms and received a B-. Hmmm.
Trust me, you are more likely to get an A in the honored course than Landsburg's 207.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: I feel sorry for all students who have taken or are planning to take Landsburg's ECO207. You basically wastes a whole semester of valuable time and get yur life ruined. His grading criteria is more like a lottery and god please stop all this nonsense. Good luck to you all, you are all talented students and will succeed in yur future career.

Professor Landsburg may be a well known economist, but his class is unbearable. I did okay in 108 with him and took 207 and devoted lots of time and still didnt pass. Exams are impossible as he tests you on your critical thinking skills, and not the course material. Dont recommend if you need Landsburg unless you have to take the class with him.

Good lecturer and economist, but the exams (3 extremely difficult exams determine your grade) are crazy hard and this course will ruin your GPA. I'd avoid this course unless you have to take it or are very passionate about economics.

For students taking as cluster course, I strongly suggest you to think twice before adding this course. This course is nothing different from ECO108, i.e. learning repeated knowledge but A LOT harder exams. If you do not plan to invest excess amount of time in Economics, expect to have 50% grade or less in your exams and be prepared to retake.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS']

comment: ECO207 with Landsburg will not be easy. He is a fantastic lecturer with decades of experience to share. You will learn so much about economics in class. Now his exams (100% of your grade) arent easy since they dont necessarily test if you just know the material or not. You need to do a fair amount of critical thinking to do well. Practice lots!
Simply the best professor I have met at UR so far. His lecture is great because he explains things clearly, and he is super nice when you turn to him for help after class.

Great lecturer! Very inspirational, gives lots of real world examples to tie to microeconomic concepts. However, his tests can be improved where there's not too much ambiguity on how pts are awarded. His class is basically graded on 3 exams.. too much pressure on the student
His lecture is so great! I literally expect to take his class every Monday and Wednesday! Lots of inspiring cases introduced in class.
His class is really inspirational! Best lectures of this semester.

Amazing lectures but exams are way harder than the homework and very confusing. I advise that you do not take this class unless you absolutely have to and if you have to, work very hard to get good grades in your other classes so that this class doesn't do too much harm to your GPA because your grade in this class is very unpredictable.
Amazing lectures. So interesting, easily the best class I've taken at this school.

If you are interested in real Economics, only taking his lecture is not enough. What economic textbooks and theories tell you are often contradictory to what really happened in the world. But overall, Landsburg has done a good job in classes
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Exams basically determines your grade, specially the final. But if u understand each question in the weekly homework which will not count in your final grade, you will be able to solve them on the exams and get an A.

The lectures are fantastically clear and usually interesting. There is a lot of homework, but Prof Landsburg goes over every problem in class and explains exactly how to solve it. The exams cover exactly the same ideas and methods as the homework, so if you pay attention in class, it's easy to do well.
The man is a fantastic economist, but unless you have Einsteins ability to overcome academic question papers! do not take his class!

One of the smartest guy have ever met, grading based on exams only, but will bounce if you do nice homework. The course isn't hard if you participate the lectures, and the lecture videos are also available.

He has a clear thought of what he is teaching. Some people might think his exams are challenged compare to what he taught. However, he did teach evey basic principle need to use in the exams. And his homework is also helpful. I have to admit that if you work hard and follow the pace you should not find it is hard on the exam.

A fantastic educator. Landsburg is able to deliver the material of this course in a very easy to understand way. He is well respected and will be able to answer nearly any question you have on the course or economics in general.
"Awesome" just about says it.  I thought I knew a lot of economics going in, but this class kept giving me new and better ways to understand things.  I learned a ton.
In my experience, has very little respect for students and likes to be controversial and offensive just for kicks, even though his students don't find it particularly funny.
This man has changed my life.
I actually loved the exams.   Each question was like a fun little puzzle that wasn't too hard if you knew the material.  Because of this class, I am changing my major to econ.
Great teacher. Great man. This course taught me how to think.

The truth is I was very excited to take this class but it was very disappointing. The exams are so impossible, nothing compared to what he teaches in class. This is a hard course, but not because of the professor.  He genuinely wants his students to learn the material and will help you as much as you want, but only if you ask him for it.  He's very funny in class, although that often leads to getting off-topic.

His class is very easy to follow because he makes sure you understand the concept with multiple examples that make you think outside of the box (ironically, he uses a box and other items instead of standard variables). Always sets office hours and review sessions that work for the entire class, and he runs the review.

AMAZING PROFESSOR! Iosevich doesn't get to teach many undergraduate classes, so if you have the good fortune of taking his class you are very lucky! He is dedicated to his class and will go out of his way to help you even after you complete his class. He is a funny guy and a great lecturer. He makes sure you understand the math beyond equations.
Fantastic!!!!

Very funny. He cares about his students, and often asks how they're doing before class. His lessons are usually crystal clear, which is impressive for such a difficult subject. He's always honest, and is a fair grader.

I graduated from U of R 4 years ago, if I had to basically say there was one professor who was not professional, it was Professor Chao.

I would basically say that she's in a cult. And you will get bad grades on your work if it does not justify Falun Gong. If you research using official narratives such as NYTimes you will be penalized. No fair 4 me

I mean, I really like her. Since this is my last semester, if I had the chance, I would take her class again. Very nice lady who is professional and caring for what she teaches. But please do the readings if you want to write good essays. Once you read, it won't be hard to get a good grade. Please take her class.

She is incredibly repetitive, makes tons of errors and still grades very harshly. Please do not take her class! The only regret is I didn't check her up on rate my professors before I signed up for her class.

Extremely tough grader, very repetitive and sometimes contradicts herself. She couldn't spell properly and make tons of grammatical mistakes in her materials but expects us to hand in papers with perfect writing. The only good thing I can say about this class is the interesting readings. Overall 10/10 do not recommend.
Not much good to say. She made the lessons hard to understand, was repetitive, and not very helpful even when the students reached out.

The other reviews here shocked me - I've had nothing but good experiences with Professor Chao. Her English is fine, her grading isn't that rough (I got a B+ on my midterm and actually thought she was quite generous with that), show up and do the readings. She's a little repetitive but I always left class understanding the important points.

Insanely hard grader. If you miss a keyword that she's looking for, but accurately describe the concept, she will count it completely wrong. She focuses on tiny details- be prepared to really memorize every little thing in the readings. I'm taking this class pass fail because I just don't know how to meet her standards and she is not helpful at all
Was condescending and not particularly helpful, can't recommend this class to anyone.

This professor is absolutely terrible. She does not speak English well enough to teach this class. She says contradictory things in her lecture, and when you write down what she said on exams, she counts them wrong. When you go ask her about why you got it wrong, she doesn't explain herself and is extremely condescending. Don not take her classes.

This guy is a GOAT. He is extremely helpful to those students who strive to stay on top of the class. As long as you read your articles, attend lectures, and ask questions, I guarantee your time will be spent wisely. For those interested in journalism, I highly recommend this course! 

Be warned that there are pop quizzes and long articles.

Professor Liu is an excellent teacher. He would give ample examples on techniques he wanted us to learn and have us try it out in class, and he is great with constructive criticism. He kept the class engaged and interactive by having us read really interesting journal articles and by having us work with each other on in-class work.
she keeps asking posibly can not think for herself
Great professor!

Dr. Jeannine Dingus is a great professor! She is HIGHLY intelligent and extremely helpful.  Most of my classmates were too immature to appreciate her because she is a no-nonsense type of person, but she is truly great.  She is the very best professor at the Warner School!
No Comments

Easy class, easy prof., but def. not open to others' opinions, and not a high quality prof. I just finished the UR's M.S. in Teach. prog. and I regret attending the U of R because of Profs. like Dingus, with little classroom teaching exp. She focuses on the negative and fails to prepare us for anything but teaching in urban schools.
No Comments

Assistant professor Dingus obviously thinks that she is a great assistant professor.  It is apparent in the way she teaches and speaks about herself.  However, it is also very telling.  Watch out my fellow students, assistant professor Dingus definately has some issues in the race department.  Buyer beware: her class is not free, but should be.

If you want a professor who is upfront and tells you how it is, Dr. Dingus is the one for you. She is an excellent professor who is fun and engaging. She is a critical professor, but who said that was a bad thing? She gets you to think outside of the box. If you want easy...go to MCC!
She isn't HARD, she is CRITICAL . . . welcome to grad school people. If you want easy, go somewhere else.
No Comments
Too hard, too much to read!
DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH DINGUS!!!  WORST TEACHER EVER, WHAT A WASTE OF MY TIME AND MY MONEY.  SHE SUCKS.  I HOPE SHE GETS FIRED!
No Comments
He teaches you to think like a mathematician and it way more important than any calculus topic

We were behind in the first two months. But then he made less errors and got ahead of the other classes. His class is the calmest & simplest. Pick him if you're good at Calc BC concepts, pick a diff prof. if you want to learn the most. Responds very fast to emails + sometimes does hard HW probs in class. Confused in lecture? Ask questions then lol

Doug was an alright professor when he taught integration. However, his class lectures on polar coordinates, parametric equations, and series were often confusing because he would skip some important information on those topics. He did go over many examples for those three topics, but never really explained his process clearly. Get a tutor for 162.

Nice guy and very smart, just one of those people who just cannot teach and should not teach math. His lectures are very confusing and rather than teaching how to work through problems he just does them with little to no coherent explanation. His lectures are similar. Do not take him if you are poor in math.

Awful. Bad lectures. Doesn't know what's going on. Learned everything on my own. Gave our class 20 mins less time on 1st midterm. Whole calc department awful. No one willing to give points back on exams. Graders are so tough. Go to rec and do all webwork to boost grade and you might survive. Never taking a math course at U of R again.

Doug's lectures range from pretty boring to very interesting. He uses a lot of real life examples which many math professors at this university don't seem to do. However, he is very constantly making computational errors which slows down the lectures a lot. Also, I'm often leaving lectures not really feeling confident I learned very much.

Doug is nice and starts lecture by showing famous mathematicians' contributions. He's not great at explaining concepts. He teaches by running through example problems which is only sometimes helpful. He's often out of touch with what's on homework, which tends to be harder than tests. Use previous tests to study as questions are recirculated.

comment: Doug isn't the greatest teacher and has a hard time explaining concepts, he just does a bunch of examples and hopes the students understand. However, he is a caring person who is very funny. For the tests, just use the practice tests, as the tests are very similar year to year. Don't procrastinate WebWork!!!

Doug tells math history stories before every lecture, the highlight of my day. Do the practice tests online; they basically mimic the actual tests and don't cheat your webwork since it's the only homework you get assigned. He's very approachable during office hours and loves to chat with students.

Not a big fan of his teaching. He tries to make class engaging by talking about a random math fact every class, but it got pretty boring. In fact I skipped his lectures altogether and simply just followed the textbook content to self-study. I would recommend choosing the other 162 profs such as Charles Wolf or Bogdan Krstic.

His way of teaching is working through example problems to show you the different techniques. This makes it hard to organise the content as you don't always know what technique he's covering. So, I had to use the textbook to know what exactly was being covered and make additional notes after lectures. He's not the best lecturer but you'll be fine.

Arguably the worst math lecturer I've ever had! He starts every lecture rambling about a non-math tangentially related topic, and then fails to cover relevant parts of the course. Teaches poorly, and though the exams are what I expected, the lack of proper teaching and his nonsense exam curve made the class overly frustrating. Take it with Wolf.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']

comment: Starts every lecture with an unrelated story and always connects himself at the end. Has a pretty big ego. Lectures make no sense and he jumps right into applications without explaining concepts. His favorite thing to do is start a very complex problem in class and make mistakes solving it, only to say "you can figure that out". DO NOT TAKE RAVENEL

In the first part of the course (integration). His lectures helped but afterwards you need to look at other resources to understand everything. He is a bit slow in my opinion and does not explain everything included in exams. His exams are extremely difficult, but they have great curves. You can get 80ish on every exam and still get an A.

Calc II sucks, he's useful until sequences and series. After that, just watch Khan academy and patrick jmt. Starts every lecture with a story relating to that day's topic, which I liked but others didn't. Other students were pretty noisy, and lectures aren't recorded. Notes are posted but good luck deciphering them. Hit or miss mostly, but fine.

comment: Worst ever professor. Not interested in teaching. Makes easy tests. I don't understand the purpose of his class.
