comment: This class is video based and you learn nothing. The professor requires you to do two midterms and an essay. He doesn't tell you, but there is hidden criteria. If you disagree even slightly with his political views he will grade you harshly. He can be very ignorant sometimes and refuse to concede even the slightest thing that he disagrees with.
The class is video-based. Little to no teaching.

He's really funny in a cheesy, quirky way. at first I was really intimated and shy to speak in front of the class but by the end I was doing it like a pro. He is really helpful and makes you feel comfortable with speaking in public.

The Presidential Rhetoric class he teaches should not be a class. All he does is talk for 5 or ten minutes about his views on current politics and then shows a biographical movie about a president that has nothing to do with their speaking ability. The class is a waste of my tuition money.

Prof. Smith is really laid back, but he knows his stuff.  Excellent speaker, very passionate.  Limited bias.  He has an extreme appreciation for public speaking, so when he talks down about a particular president, it's generally about their ability to present themselves in public.  Fair grader.
Amazing teacher and good info, not hard.
Lots of video, real laid back guy

I had presidential rhetoric with him. he knows his stuff, and i actually didn't see a bias, not too tough to do well with him, he shows relevant videos and points out things i wouldn't have otherwise noticed about the presidents we studied.
all we do is watch videos.  funny how i learned a whole bunch in this class.
easy class if you dont fear public peaking..however must of us do. Repetitive, but he knows what he's doin. P.S. He's a Red Sox fan, keep that in mind

Bash Clinton, Democrats, liberal Republicans, or praise Reagan/conservative Republicans = automatic A.  Praise liberal democrats = automatic non-A.  Incredibly (almost humorously) biased, along the lines of "Democrats hate God" but easy to get a
Corny at times, but cool and knows his stuff. Looks like Robert Redford.
No Comments
Speechwriter for Bush (41)...KNOWS public speaking!

Seluanov was a great lecturer and very funny guy. Personally, I found the content of this class extremely interesting, especially Gorbunova's lectures about Ozempic and dietary restriction in the last two classes. Presentations are really easy to do well in for workshop. The exams are kind of hard, but the class is curved very nicely at the end.

Dr. Seluanov was the best lecturer out of all of the ones we had for this class. The downside to that is that the others are not that good, making it hard to follow the concepts, especially in-person. The workshops are presentation based and don't cover any class material which I think is useless, but the bonus points are nice to help w hard exams

Two exams, one 35%, other 45%. Only extra credit you get is through workshops (add up to 10-15% extra) and the class is curved in the end as well. A bit hard to understand due to the accident but you get adjusted quickly. Very understanding and interesting topic, but how exams are worded is why most people lost points, not content.

Seluanov has a heavy accent that's tough to get used to. He gives a disclaimer on the first day of the class that he's "a researcher before he's a professor." In other words, teaching is not his priority whatsoever. That being said, he's not the worst lecturer and he's really knowledgable. Quizzes in workshops. Tests are hard, but he curves a lot.

Nice guy and a generally good lecturer. His accent is sometimes confusing but you do get used to it. Material is difficult and there is a lot of it, but tests are fair (if sometimes worded vaguely). Take good notes in class!
Seluanov is a nice guy and a decent lecturer. His accent is difficult to understand at first but you get used to it. The material is hard but he's more than happy to help. I really enjoyed his class.
I was going to go on his field school next summer but I heard horrible stories about them from previous students.  I think these precious  reviews were written by Jarvis, they're not real!

I had for Archaeology in Early America and he is well versed in the subject. His lectures were clear and interesting and his grading was fair, but from what I could tell his grading varies depending on what he expects from a particular student.

Best professor at UR.  Funny, fair, amazing lecturer.  Makes you work for your grade, but this is easy to do if you follow the syllabus, which he sticks to.  Very professional and interested.  This is my second class with him and I can't wait for a third.  I enjoyed learning.

Prof. Jarvis is a great professor. He really knows what he is talking about and loves what he teaches. The course can be difficult but staying up with the reading, attending class, and taking good notes will keep you up with the class.

Prof. Jarvis is very passionate about his subject. If you like history, you will like Jarvis. Downside: the syllabus says there are no papers, but each test (4 total) involves a "take-home essay section" a.k.a. a paper. Don't be fooled!

Introduced himself as Snape the first day, but he's the farthest from Snape you could imagine. Great prof, super interesting, very clear about what he wants from you on exams/papers.  Only drawback is mandatory attendance.
I only had Jarvis for Maritime Atlantic 301W, but he was great. A little hard at first with all the reaction papers, but his class was lots of fun. Very helpful and enthusiastic.

Professor Jarvis picked the best kind of history to specialize in: early American colonies in the Caribbean/ Bermuda colonies. So whenever he has to go "study in the field" he goes somewhere with great weather and a beach! Pirates, arrrrrr!
He oversees my internship and is very helpful and willing to spend time to help.

Probably my favorite professor thus far. Very helpful, clear, and engaging. I've taken both 100 and 300 level courses and found him to be a tough but fair grader. He makes himself available to students and appears genuinely interested in their enjoyment and progress in the courses he teaches. I'd recommend any class taught by him.

He's a pretty chill dude. Did well at first and must have fallen asleep during the Final which is the only reason i didn't get an A.  Whatever, he's pretty nice and fair...he makes US history easy to swallow even for the most reluctant.  Also, go on the field trip @ the end of the year.

History can sometimes be a boring topic, but Jarvis made it pretty interesting.  His use of multimedia within lectures was a nice touch and helped make the class much more visual.  Jarvis knows basically everything there is to know about US history, which is a great asset.  If you have to take a history course, take it with Jarvis.
Jarvis is the man.  Really smart and knowledgable about the topic.  For sure, one of the best classes I've had at UR.  He turned me into a history major.  He also has some pretty funny little quips.
I am in love with this man. He is so nice and so funny. He's just so incredibly awkward-he cracks me up. You need to take a class with him-you definitly won't regret it!
madler is awesome
Prof. Jarvis is a really nice guy.  This class was awesome.  I want to retake it, but they won't let me.  You watch cool movies, you take fair exams, and you learn a lot about our country.
Definitly worth taking a class by him. He's a great teacher and very organized! You know what you have to study and his tests are very fair.

He spent about 3 days talking about Haiti, because he had pictures of his trip there, and about half a day talking about the Consititution in an Early American history class. Class was reading, memorizing, taking a test. Do the work = get a good grade. I got a D+. My bad
Great teacher, very hands on, and sticks to readings and assignments.
very helpful and knowledgable professor.  doesn't skimp of reading or writing, but topics are generally interesting and he leads disscussion well.
My AP American class was harder and more involved than this one. I think my IQ dropped by taking this class.
Very Interesting, engaging, only drawback is mandatory attendance...
Favorite Prof. ever!  Go Jarvis!

The content of the class was easy but he graded us as if we were all psci majors (when most everyone was taking this class for a cluster). At the end of the semester he didn't give us our grades for the paper, presentation, or final exam he just gave a letter grade. Basically everyone got a B+. Wouldn't take again.

comment: He is the best professor I have had. His lectures are so interesting and he cares so much about the subject he teaches I can't wait to get him again next year. He is great.

An especially engaging lecturer. Passionate on the subject, funny, full of energy, knows a ton. The reading is intensive, but as long as you go to class and skim the key articles, you'll do fine. Exams are in essay format, some in class and some take home. Very accessible for people with no PSC background or for environmentalist types.
Best professor I've had so far. Really interesting and cares about the subject. Easy as long as you take good notes.
No Comments
He's approachable and genuinely interested in teaching students. You definitely need to go to class but his lectures were occasionally a bit dry.
just don't
Condescending, rude, and illegible. He definitely knows the material, but it does not help nobody

Very good and clear professor who has thoroughly prepared the class ahead of time. You'll need some comfort with regards to mathematics to do very well in the class, but it's not very hard, just rigorous, and you need to be consistent. It's essentially problem-solving. Very good slides that I could follow even if I ever missed class and good TAs.

comment: He knows what he is doing. Kind of condescending if you do not understand the material right away. His slides are almost impossible to understand unless you have full understanding of what is going on and keys never give the process.
Great Professor! The material is quite tough. But the teaching assistants (especially Sergio Ascencio) is extremely helpful! Definitely go to histheirs office hours for help! (if you need any)

He is a nice professor, clear, and will go out of his way to help you, but the material is brutal if you fall behind.  Not too many tricks, just a lot of work.  Make sure you ask your questions in class because the T.A.'s could be useless.

Solid teacher, doesn't run the most interesting class, but engaging and very approachable. Surprisingly responsive to feedback and even constructive criticism. Also very good in a one to one setting when he has the opportunity to explain in greater detail than in class.
Prepares lectures throughly, cares, very sharp guy.

Very easy class, and would recommend using it to fulfill the upper level writing requirement. Lectures weren't that engaging, but I think it's just the subject and not his fault. Grading criteria are clear.
Professor Loporcaro's 299W course remains a GPA lifeline and a motivator of good thought around computer science and its advancements.

The professor was quite understanding and accessible during office hours. The lectures weren't the most engaging, but it was a writing-focused course anyways. Would recommend taking his course for the CS ULW requirement.
Fantastic! Highly recommended.
He is really cool
Very friendly and extremely nice. You just need to show up and speak every once in a while and basically you're guaranteed an A.
Super chill
He's such a great professor! Super nice guy! The content is also really interesting. Definitely worth taking!
If you enjoy playing video games then I highly recommend his VG classes! He is very passionate and very friendly and loves to talk about games with you. Really nice and helpful professor
This class is easy. If you need a ULW credit, this is a great option.

Really nice professor. Workload is manageable and he is flexible with due dates. His writing criteria for each assignment are detailed and clear. If you follow it to a T you will get an A. Highly recommend this course for the upper-level writing requirement for CS majors.
Very chill but also clearly very knowledgeable. Some of the class does feel a little like busy work though. Not really on him as ULWs have to meet a page requirement.
One of the most caring and nice professor out there. It was a great class. Nothing bad to say

Prof Loporcaro is the best! I would highly recommend taking any class with him. He is genuinely one of the most caring and understanding professors I've ever had and he makes class fun in a way that it doesn't even feel like work. Absolutely take a class with him if you can!
I will give 10 stars if possible. Kindest professor in U of R ever. The world needs more Professors like Professor Loporcaro.
Great guy! Very chill and friendly. You don't see him as a professor, you see him as a neighborhood friend. Love him.
Reviewed for half an hour before taking the 1hr 20 min midterm and finished in 20 min. Straight A. Inarguably the easiest professor at UR. I took literally every course he taught.

Overall a very chill class. This class isn't related to my major and I just took it for fun. The class is very group project based and you are able to work at your own pace. He gives good feedback and is usually very accommodating when it comes to deadlines. Very recommended.

Joe is my favorite professor at UR. His lectures are interesting, and he's a really nice dude. Attendance and participation is mandatory, but it's not hard to get full credit on this end, just say something during class and you're good. As long as you do the work, you'll get an A.
Very chill teacher and class. I highly recommend his class.
Chill class; professors great at lecturing.

Very generous and caring regarding students. Adapted very well to the online format. Allows you to revise your essays for full credit if you email him. Basic CSC273W stuff, lots of boring essays, but easy A.
Loporcaro is the best. Take a class with him even if you don't need to. The nicest, most genuine professor I have had.

He's chill. Sometimes it can feel like a lot of work, especially if you're a CS major and don't write/read a lot, but he breaks the work down easily. If you follow his criteria, you'll get an A. He is also very accessible out of class and willing to help you.
A great professor.

Prof Singh is the BEST professor I ever had. He made learning so much engaging and fun. I wish more professors could teach like him. The content I learned in this class helped me ace a job interview -- I got that job. Thank You Prof. Singh!

I really enjoyed the ME 450 lectures. Even though I was new to the field, I learned a lot of interesting and useful stuff throughout the course. I also liked that the class was challenging in a good way without being super stressful, unlike some other courses. Final project was fun, and it will be quite useful for my future research!

Professor Singh is VERY nice and funny but his lectures are unbearable. Good professor if you're there for the vibes, not if you want to deeply understand. Everything is on slides and he rambles/gets off topic often. Examples are rarely worked out on the blackboard. Plus, if you are against AI, he once used it to write a poem and read it to us.
Good professor

Prof Singh might be the most caring of all the ME professors. He just wants you to learn in be interested in the material. He told me class if he could he would give us all As for just showing up to lecture. The labs can get long but they are guaranteed 100s. Taking a course as part of a cluster and with no context or experience for engineering otherwise. Professor Ronald's lectures are clear and easy to understand, and he takes the time for all the students to understand the content and catch up.

great!! loved his lectures, learned a lot. very easy to understand.

Best lecture slides I've seen thus far. He is really enthusiastic about the material and explains things so well. Take his class in the summer if u can. My class had 11 students this summer, going to class was fun and the material was soo interesting. I'd be surprised if anyone got less than a B

Clark's class was unbelievably interesting. He tries so hard to apply what he teaches into life and medicine. I loved going to class, and he is adorable. His exams are pretty tough though. Memorize anything and everything he tells you in lecture - and believe me that's a LOT. The curve is nice, I expected a B but got an A-!

There is a TON of material that must be MEMORIZED to succeed in this class. Covers majority of it in lecture slides, but some random terms and definitions are only in the book. Good lecturer, can be unclear or assume concepts are simpler than they are at time.  Midterms are doable if you study, but tough.  The 300 pt cummulative final is BRUTAL.

Dr. Clark is a great professor. His lectures are interesting yet concise. The material that he teaches can be difficult to understand but after reading through his powerpoint again is manageable. His tests are definetly hard. And one of his downsides is that you never really know what grade you have in his class until the end of the semeseter.

Clark is a quirky and charming professor who is often nicknamed "Sheldon" (from The Big Bang Theory) across dinner tables. His lectures are evenly spaced and difficult concepts well-explained, but his lectures also tend to be long, dry, and occasionally coma-inducing. Exams are very difficult - lecture and workshop attendance is a must.

I have mixed feelings about Clark. On one hand he is a great lecturer and makes the topics interesting. On the other hand, even though he claims his tests are not all memorization, they are. Definitely a challenging course.

Clark pops into the lab occassionally, which is pretty great considering most lab instructors could care less about checking on their students.  The lab manuals are pretty well written and the techniques you learn/use are actually relevant to modern research. Two big write-ups are long and tedious. Practical and other assignments are easy.

Clark is very full of himself and only accepts the answers he has in his head. The tests are extremely hard and it seemed like all the points on multiple part questions went to the most minor detail. He does not know how to curve, and has a preset class average prior to even administering the exams. If you're thinking of taking BIO 112, just don't.

Definitely one of my favorite professors this term. Incredibly passionate and knowledgeable about the subject. He is also very helpful in office hours. His tests are challenging, but they really encourage you to think critically apply the concepts taught in class experimentally. For me, it was helpful to review his lecture notes right after class.

Genetics lab was incredibly educational. His labs teach you useful, real techniques and the class is designed so that you aren't mindlessly following a procedure, but so that you understand what you're doing. Lab manuals are occasionally poorly written, but the TA knows what's up no it's not a big deal. Curves the class to a B.

Clark is quirky and funny, and lectures are clear and for the most part, interesting. But his exams were extremely difficult, long, and to some extent unfair. The exams are difficult, and you really do have to work hard to get a good grade. Do not take this class lightly and make it one of your top priorities.

Dr. Clark is a solid professor and I would definitely recommend him. Although his lectures are a little long, they are fairly easy to understand. Tests are tough but fair, keep up with lecture notes and readings and you should be fine
He's a rather mediocre professor. He tries to be helpful with office hours but is unclear and confusing. His tests aren't bad. I just didn't like his style of teaching.

Dr.Clark is a very smart and nice professor. Biochem is not easy! Definitely attend his class cuz he mentions all the important points which will all in the exams. I didn't do really well in this class but it's my own problem not Dr.Clark's. I really enjoy this class and learn a ton! Office hour really helps and he is very approachable! Best ever!

Professor is a little awkward, but he's actually really funny and nice.  Lectures are dense but all the slides are online.   Biggest advice is keep up with material, it's impossible to learn it all right before the test. I've never gotten below an A- in any class ever, but I got a B- because I didn't keep up with lectures.  My fault, not Clarks.

He's a pretty good professor. Lectures are long and dense, but this basically means there's never something on the test that wasn't mentioned. Take good notes, don't just study slides. Tests are hard, but he knows it's a tough class and the curve is nice at the end. Overall, a great class. You learn a TON. He's a nice guy too.

He is a pretty good professor. His lectures are clear, if a little dense, and cover everything on the tests. Tests can be tricky, though. He is also very helpful in office hours. Don't worry too much about the bad reviews from earlier - he was still a new prof. He has clearly gotten the hang of how to organize good lectures and teach well.

He is very clear about what will be on the exam, but make sure you take note of questions asked orally in class or questions on lecture slides. Lectures are long but are good study tools. Office hours are also very beneficial because questions asked during office hours might come up on exams.

He is a good professor. Not amazing, but good. The class is tough with a ton of material to learn, but it's all in his lectures and he's helpful at office hours. I came in thinking I could breeze it because I did well it a tough AP Bio class and got a 5 w/out much work. WRONG. So for you smarties, put in some effort. But really, study and you're ok

It's a tough class and you really have to know your stuff for the tests, but everything is in his lectures. He lectures from power points and sometimes doesn't finish them, but posts all of his lectures online and will finish the material at the next class. Take detailed notes. He curves at the end so you'll probably do better than you think.

Clark is crazy smart, but he is not a great lecturer. He's awkward, but very approachable.  Lectures are way too long, and the slides tend to have so much on them that they're overwhelming. Pretty rough for an intro class, a lot of hardcore biochem.  Exams are NOT easy, you will have to study A TON to do well.

Lectures are awful. Each topic is rushed through in 4 or 5 slides, and Clark never finishes his absurdly long powerpoints. Exams cover only powerpoint materials, but the slides are poor to the point of indecipherability. Your only chance of getting a respectable grade is to review in workshops and in office hours.

He has a lot to improve but I'm sure he'll do better with a few years of lecturing under his belt. Memorize EVERYTHING because he will put anything and everything on a test. He looks like Sheldon from the Big Bang Theory

Clark is a new professor so he's still learning how to present material efficiently and clearly. He isn't bad but he needs a bit of experience with his lectures. His PowerPoints tend to be a little too long, so he usually has to rush through the last 15 slides or so. Biochem is really tough; he's apparently helpful at office hours though.

He can be a bit awkward, but he's a nice guy. His tests are very hard, but the answers are always in the lectures - missing a lecture WILL hurt as making sense out of the slides isn't that easy. He's certainly approachable, but it may take a little bit to get the answer you need. Office hours are helpful, but crowded.

The key to succeeding in this class is memorizing powerpoint slides. Also, piecing them together into an understanding of the bigger picture. Clark is awkward and not very helpful. He is new though, and he has to live up to the name of the great Terry Platt. Exams are hard, and the fact that he doesn't give enough time makes them harder. Work hard.
He is mostly good.   Tests are hard, but only covered lecture material. Office hours help simplify things.

Exams come from slides- Memorize them. MUST go to office hours to do well on exams. Very helpful during office hours - ask questions! Lectures are often long and tedious but he is smart. He's so awkward that it's funny. You have to put in lots of time to make sure you understand concepts - Loves it when you "appreciate" the "big picture".

He's a new professor. It's apparent that he does need more time to improve, but everyone does. His review sessions are extremely helpful. You will not complain about him if you don't keep facebooking and texting in the class. Good person and good professor.
It's obvious that he's never taught before.  There is no cohesion in the material and he over-complicates things.  Office hours do help somewhat, but he's often too busy helping other students.

(For Contemporary African Poilitics) Professor Harding isn't a super easy A, but he has clear, organized lectures that build on concepts each week. The readings and lectures go together really well, but even if you read you really should go to class. He is very knowledgeable about the ideas and clearly interested in them which shines through.

Professor Smith is very kind and passionate about the material. The way she lectures is not the most engaging but the material is not very challenging and there are plenty of opportunities for extra credit. She is always happy to help and answer questions.
straight forward lectures, very available, class content is simple enough, but she makes it easier. very understanding. good calm and "easy" engineering course

This class was pretty easy. A basic understanding of math is needed. Dr Smith herself is obviously passionate about the material but isn't the best lecturer. She is also not the most consistent with posting assignments on time, something that became prevalent in AME 141 (the next class in the 140's series). Labs are pretty good, and TA's are great.
TOO EASY LMAO

This class was really easy for me, Sarah Smith is very very nice and made the lectures really clear with her pre-class notes. Explained everything from the basic math and physics principles for people who haven't had much experience with it, and overall very helpful in both the lectures and labs (when she comes).

literally the most caring professor ever. he makes an effort to get to know you and will help you out with anything you need. he works around your schedule in order and helps you out whenever you need it.
Really nice Prof, he read drafts of my papers before each submit and if he did not get around to it he would extend the deadline which was really nice of him.

Jimbo is my absolute favourite. I adored every single class with him he is so fun and kind and his classes are super lightweight and not very work-heavy. He gives great feedback on assignments that if you just follow, you'll get an A and the assignments are very lenient. You get given a style of article and you choose what you write about.

I <3 Memmott SO MUCH. Lil Jimbo is my life. He is so kind and caring, he's happy to give you extra time on assignments and all the help you need. His classes are super light-hearted and not content-heavy AT ALL. He's amazing, I really adore him and his class so much.
one of the most amazing professors I've ever had. Makes journalism digestible for everyone, even pure engineering students.
Took 3 of his classes. Such a great man. Might be an Easy Class but you can learn a lot from this man.
So little work. Smart man. Kind teacher.
I <3 Memmott
Best Professor and overall genuinely great person. Take his classes if you want an easy-going class that is also fun. They are few and far between at the U of R.
Any class with Memmott is a treat.  132 is, by far, the best the class I've taken in 3 years at UR.  If you have the opportunity, take a Memmott class.  You won't be disappointed.
Who loves Memmott? WE LOVE MEMMOTT!!!
Jim Memmott is arguably the greatest man in update new york. this is not a joke, best ever. Memmott should be a major within the Eng. dpt.
Memmott's the MAN!!
Awsome guy, awsome class. Really down to earth.
Jim is awesome!  Funny, honest and wonderful.  Highly recommended!
An awesome guy! Fun class, easy assignments and grading. Laidback and helpful. I'd recommend him to anyone for any class!

I love Memmott.  I could never say it enough.  Not only does he look like Larry David, but he has a wonderful personality.  He befriends people so easily and takes an interest in getting to know you, even if all you do is read the CT in his class!
great guy, always a joy in class and very helpful
easy easy easy!  a little flakey perhaps, he lets you turn in your assignments basically anytime before he records the final grades, but no complaints here. he knows everyone.

One of the best lecturers I've taken a course with; he's extremely knowledgeable, engaging, and willing to help you work through any issues you have or anything related to the course that you're interested in outside of lecture. Highly recommend this class; it's so much fun.

Heyworth is incredibly intelligent and is more than happy to share his knowledge at all times. In class, he's always focusing on how students think and look into nuance. He has high standards but is committed to helping his students reach those standards, ultimately for the better. He cares a lot about his students and has a high degree of respect!

It's obvious that Heyworth knows his stuff, but sometimes during our lectures, he would focus on small points and we would end up losing class time because of it. He's very passionate, but it would've been nice to have a more structured class and paper set up. He grades fine but he really nitpicks sometimes on things that aren't that important.

Professor Heyworth is very smart, but it tends to show in his lectures that he makes a good amount of the stuff on the spot, although it sounds good. This makes his classes sometimes feel like it's all over the place. He also occasionally concerns himself with little lines that sometimes cause a drag to the class. Not bad, but he is a tough grader.

Really enjoyed Ravi's classes. It's a LOT of work, but very rewarding and with so many resources provided for out-of-classroom self study. Need a solid MS Excel foundation & willingness to play with code & tools. Genuinely get the impression he wants you to succeed. Homework and tests are well documented and fairly graded.
Great class.

5 homeworks, no exams, 1 Group Project
But that does not mean the course is easy.
If you do bad on some of the homework you may not have a good grade.
The lectures are carefully arranged and the slides are easy to follow, but the pace in class is very quick so you have to focus.
But after all this course is fruitful.

Took Writing 105: Argumentative Detectives. Interesting class, lots of papers but it's a writing course so it should be expected. I had a hard time staying on top of work this year but she was really understanding and really helped me out. If you're swamped you can get an extension. Great professor. Grades fairly and sincerely cares about students.

This was one of my fav classes at this school. Prof Grimm is so well prepared and really knows her stuff. She assigns A LOT to read but is okay with you not understanding it all as long as your bring your questions to class.

Professor Grimm was somewhat tough. Lectures did not always follow the reading that was assigned prior to class. Also, took a while to get back to me on emails and assignments. Not a lot of help on assignments before due dates even though there was not a clear rubric for some assignments.

The class is like 3 courses in 1. It's lang doc./ling readings, tech stuff, and cult. anth stuff. Her feedback half time is critical w/o any substance and other times it simply makes no sense. Take when you have time to read a lot and only take it if you want to do linguistic-oriented fieldwork.

comment: I took Ling104 randomly my first semester and this is the class that convinced me to become a Linguistics major! Nadine is a great professor and very understanding of her students' personal problems. This course was also very interesting and a pretty easy A as long as you do the readings (usually around 30 pages every class) and try on the essays.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Prof Grimm is kind and sweet, but she is very vague with her assignments. She takes a long time to give grades back and is a slightly tough grader. Very nice and understanding person, but not the best with feedback.
Takes forever to give back assignments and is very vague on assignment instructions. And when asked for clarification is kind of flaky. I would not recommend this professor under any circumstance.

Dima is a great professor, although he is a tough grader. He fingerspells too fast during exams, even for ASL 101. I wouldn't  have pushed myself this hard in this introductory class without him, yet I think this is still a bit too harsh given this intro-level course. Overall a very enjoyable experience despite the grade.

He's great! I love him.  He's really helped me understand more about Deaf Culture, and there's so much learned from him despite the lack of speaking, which I was a little hesitant about at first but now realize was a silly worry.  He's very caring and will help you with something over and over again until you get it right.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Very friendly, approachable, helpful and humorous, I've taken two of his classes and he's always a pleasure. Does have a tendency to pair strong and experienced signers with less skilled ones, which can be awkward for both. Don't listen to the MCC students-he's a good teacher, he just doesn't tolerate rude behavior  like speaking or texting.

If you're looking for a good way to fasttrack your ASL education, then Dima is the way to go! He is a hard grader, but that is because he really wants you to learn.  However, if you put in some effort outside of class an A shouldn't be too difficult to obtain.  Just realize that you MUST put in that effort. Otherwise, he is super funny and nice!

Dima is an excellent teacher.  be forewarned, however, he expects you to take the subject matter seriously.  That should be obvious, but in my experience, it apparently isn't.  Dima is a great teacher for people who genuinely want to learn ASL.  Those looking for an easy credit should look elsewhere. For serious students, there is none

DO NOT take his class if you're looking for the easy way out.  Also, show up on day one knowing ASL alphabet and numbers, at the very least, otherwise you WILL be confused.  I like a challenging class, but the challenge should not be based on inability to understand what the professor wants you to do.  Other than that, great teacher all around.

I love Dima! He is definitely my favorite teacher in the whole school. Because of him, I was inspired to change my major to ASL. Like said previously, he does seem cold but once you get to know him he is so much fun. And even though he is the toughest grader, it totally pays off!

I took 101, 102, 105 with Dima. He is the best professor I've had at this school. At first he may seem a bit cold, but he is the friendliest person ever. He is known to be harder the hardest grader, but it is so worth it. In 101 I was able to communicate comfortably with people in 105. I wish he taught more classes so I could always have him!
He was funny but the same thing happened to me as the previous commenter, I got a B in 102 even though I worked hard and seemed to get good grades throughout the semester. I still like him though.

I enjoyed having Dima as a teacher until I received a B in his 105 class last semester.  I put much more effort into his class than what was expected.  His grading policy is unfairly vague and subjective, and it has made me dislike him.
Love Him!
He's hilarious.
Love Dima! He helped inspire such an interest in ASL and he is so helpful!

I cannot express how upset I am that he's no longer teaching 105.  I was seriously going to plan my whole schedule around his class.  I took his evening class in Fall '05, with only 10 other kids (small classes are the best esp for ASL).  Best class ever.
Amazing teacher.
dima is awesome!!

he was an awesome, fun, and helpful teacher. i took 101 and 102 with him and he was always incredibly helpful and had great activities to practice your vocab and the projects and tests weren't hard at all. a great guy.
No Comments

Dr. K. is a great professor that teaches content meaningfully and spares no effort in making the class accessible regardless of whether you've taken MUSC101 or 110. Homework was over half of the grade, and was distributed on a weekly basis (usually no re-dos). More than enough time is given to complete the exams, and they match the practice.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lots of homework']

comment: I absolutely loved her MUSC 111 class. She isn't harsh at all on grading but still gives great feedback on homework assignments. Her lectures are more hands-on so you'll interact with the material a lot more in class. Plus, she's incredibly sweet and cares deeply about her students. She even brought us cookies for our final which was super nice.

Professor Zeng isn't the best but he really tries to make sure everybody understands each topic. He covers a handful of examples for very topic and for the most part tries his best to be very clear and direct. Probably the most interesting math class of the 160 series and he definitely was a solid professor.

I won't say he is an amazing professor. But he is just about average. His lectures are clear. He is also very nice and would try his best to answer your questions. He got accent, which might be sometimes not that easy to understand. But he is very helpful if you go to his office hour. very patient.

Taught a section in virology. Very good lecturer, but make sure to take notes on his slides since he doesn't have anything but the main point down written down, which is why I say attendance is mandatory for more details on his slides. Definitely has a sense of humor. Super nice professor and answered any and all questions I had :)

One of the worst professors I've had. Makes his TA do all of the work and grades notes subjectively. Slides are not helpful and lectures are lackluster. Tough grader with little empathy for students. Used to consider going to grad school for Art History but reconsidered because of classes/professors like this.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Quiz and test material is only from the lectures. The slides barely have any words, so you have to go to the lectures and take good notes to figure out what's going on. People record the lectures on their phones so that if you miss anything you can go back. A lot of hw reading, but it's a history class so it's what you sign up for.

This class requires 40-100 pages of reading after every class. Almost the entire grade of this class is based on notes taken from these readings, with no guidelines, arbitrary grading and no feedback. Lectures consist of him rambling off trivia facts on the lecture's topic, with no class discussion (which was promised in the syllabus).
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: He makes his TA do most of the grading. The requirements for notes are not immediately clear and you are graded mostly on your notes. He directly refused to record lectures as required by the school. He does not care about the students. Do not expect any flexibility or kindness.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: He's a decent professor and explains math concepts quite well. Also open to answering questions in class and helping students understand. The only con is his handwriting can a little hard to read.

This man explained chain rule in the most diabolical way possible. I honestly ended up just teaching myself most of it. The lectures weren't very engaging. The tests can be pretty hard especially if you're underprepared. This is not like calc I in high school.
Math 161 should not be this hard. Does not explain well, lectures boring. But, need photography advice… GO to Pham!
Great professor, very accessible outside class. Attended all his lectures, had fun all the way through. Handwriting could be sometimes hard to read, otherwise good at explaining concepts.

He writes *really* quickly on the board, which can be incredibly hard to follow (especially when he's doing proofs that are completely irrelevant to you). One on one he's really helpful and a nice guy to talk to.

Fili is a really nice guy and extremely helpful when you go to his office hours. 164 is a tough course and with his help it isn't as bad. He does a lot of proof based work towards the end of the year but going to office hours will definitely help you get some good examples and explanations.

Fili is a smart guy and a great professor. He moves along at a reasonable pace and is probably the most helpful professor outside of class I've ever had: responds quickly to emails and is always helpful during office hours. 164 is tough, but he makes it manageable. And to top it all off, he's super friendly. Really top-notch.

He's super nice and helpful, but I often got the feeling he was too smart for our class. His lectures are very proof/theory based and unlike the tests. I found it helpful to search lessons on YouTube. This was his first year teaching discrete math, though, so I'd cut him some slack. The class isn't too hard.

He is a nice guy. However, I cannot follow him at all! He is very smart and maybe too smart to me. I don't know. The good thing is that he IS the textbook. If I don't understand him, I will check my textbook.
Fantastic Professor! He really cares about his students and is passionate about the material. Take his classes!

Lectures move very fast and are sometimes less than clear, so stay on top of your note-taking. Fortunately he's patient and helpful in lecture and especially in office hours. HW is a lot harder than tests. Overall a great professor who's passionate about his subject. Decided to add a math major after taking his class.
Really nice guy, but tends to rush and skip steps which leaves you puzzled trying to figure out what your notes mean after class
Great professor. He gives a lot of work (at least at the beginning of the course, it dies down after a while), but he is both very accessible and willing to help.

Stella is such a nice lady but her class is very homework heavy and unless you do extra work you will automatically receive a B grade. The class isn't very difficult and she is very understanding but expect a lot of tedious work.

Professor Stella is wonderful! Both inside and outside the classroom, she is a student advocate who takes mental and physical health very seriously. She's very accessible outside of the classroom because she would stay until 10pm to provide support. Just a person who has a great spirit! I definitely recommend her classes.

Ms.Stella is an AMAZING professor. She is very caring and understanding which is a trait you hardly find in most professors. She has experience in different writing styles and techniques and has helped me to find a citing style that would benefit me for my major. She's just the sweetest professor ever. I recommend her class a ton.

Professor Wang genuinely cares about your growth as a writer or a student. She is always available for meetings outside of class. The course has a heavy workload but everything is graded based on completion. If you do everything you need to do it's an easy A. You will get as much as you put into the class.
Easy to get good grades but don't expect to become a great writer after taking this class.

Please do yourself a favor and never take a class with this women. She never gives feedback, she wont teach you about writing and she will constantly remind you to breathe. I have no clue what i am doing in her class. She just randomly comes up and tell me that she doesnt like my paper and thatI should resubmit it 3 weeks after submission.

Stella is about the nicest, most caring person you can imagine. She has a "labor based grading contract", which means your grade depends on how much work you do (basically just participation, if you do the work, you get an A). Expect homework almost daily. She doesn't really give feedback, so don't expect to improve too much as a writer.

Stella is such a caring and understanding person and shows that love to each of her students. Her grading is pretty much just participation and just getting your work in on time. Her only downside is almost daily homework (though it's not too intense most of the time, just tedious) and she doesn't really give feedback on your writing.

The grading criteria is clear. You submit the tasks you get A. As long as you do everything, the grade is under control. However, you will not get any benefit of the class, she gives no useful feedback no writing materials. You never expect to be a better writer after taking the course. In short, wanna easy A without learning, take this class!

Professor Wang is super supportive under this special circumstance. She replies emails very fast, she always come prepared to class, and she is genuinely concerned about students' health condition. Put effort into this class and a good grade will definitely ensue. She is just so so kind! Wish I could take her other classes
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: She is a very caring and accommodating professor, unfortunately I never felt like she actually made us better writers. She often gives criticisms in order to make you conform to her perspective instead of finding ways to help you argue your point more effectively. Overall having her as a teacher was not a great experience.

Stella is very caring and gives very thorough feedback. Nothing is graded until the very end of the year, so it is a low stress class. Not a lot of homework and she is very flexible with due dates (if you have a test on the same day, just reach out to her and she will change the due date). Always accessible outside of class! Very sweet teacher.
You think you can go to her class and get an easy A? Go find another professor to get an A

She is a wonderful person. Very engaged with her work. Truly and positively motivating. If you have an ambition you can create a wonderful project thanks to her amazing supervising, feedback and inspirations. She's truly openminded and let students explore their ideas.
She is one of the nicest professors at UR. Always so passionate in class discussions and is very accomodating to students. I would definitely recommend her for WRT 105!

I don't mean to take this class in the beginning, but I really love it and learn a lot from Stella! She is very nice and gives helpful feedback during office hour. She talks a lot in class and expects class discussion. And she will try her best to help everyone to enjoy writing. I love her WRT 105E!!!

Stella was an amazing teacher. I went into this class ready to hate it but she made me enjoy it. We didn't have to write as many papers as the other WRT 105 classes (only wrote 2). She gives amazing feedback, too!
One of the nicest professors I've had. She will do anything to help you, and puts 100% into the class, helping students, and making the class engaging. Very fair in grading as well.
she is nice but i find it is not helpful to take this writing class at all

Nicest professor I've ever met. I love this woman and have great respect for her. Well informed, helpful and very nice. She has a tendency to talk a lot, but she tries her best to make the class interesting.
I took Cosmology with her, and she was absolutely hilarious.  She graded tough, but fair, and her assignments were never too onerous.  One of the best writing classes I've ever taken!
by far the worst teacher I've had. expects you to already have the writing skills of a grad student and grades very harshly.
One of the best professors I've ever had. He looks out for his students, explains things well, and assigns actually engaging material. Really recommend his class!!

Professor Chitrakar gave great feedback for each paper and it was clear he cared for his students. He was very easy to reach outside of class and would respond quickly. There were few homework assignments during the semester. Overall it was a manageable course and I without a doubt became a stronger writer.
a lot of work but great professor
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: i love Professor Rogers. Best professor I've had a Rochester. His intelligence and ability to teach in an understandable way is outstanding. I would recommend taking anything with him!
Simply the Best
Very interesting guy and great at explaining. The constant presence of examples makes the class feel tangible and reduces the abstractness.
Hes the best at everything he does.
I loved having a rogers as a teachers, he's a big goof ball who is insanely good at math and teaching

This is the Best professor you can ever have for a Japanese for film class. She is knowledgeable and passionate, and she's still trying to learn from her students. Don't be daunted by the seemingly overwhelming syllabus of her class, workload is actually not that much.
Amazing. Passionate. Kind. Thoughtful. Interesting.

She's a rockstar. Organized, knowledgeable, and humble. I had no background in Japanese culture but she introduced it so fascinatingly. One of my favorite college professors. Her grading criteria and assignments are simple and well organized. Gives ample time to complete tasks - you'll have to watch 1 film/week + 90 mins of other work.
Had prof bernardi a couple of years ago and her classes were the only ones i truly enjoyed.  Very caring teacher.  And yes she deserves a chili pepper.

Boring class. There are no discussions. He almost seems offended if you ask a question or show up to office hours. You also have to show upto every class and note down everything he says to get a good grade because there is no other material to study (like slides). Earl isnt particularly great. His lectures are turbo BORING and can be hard to understand at times. Dr. Dwyer is the best! Overall, his lectures are really interesting and CLST 172 examines a lot of very interesting films and readings. He does a great job making the class manageable in terms of weekly work. 10/10 would recommend taking a class with him.

HOT!! He has an adorable accent! Also a great professor! Takes the time to explain everything in detail everytime and doesn't assume that you should know things. Is very helpful in office hours and wants students to succeed. Tests are fair and mirror class notes.

Excellent teacher.  Makes everything perfectly clear.  Has tons of office hours and will help you however he can.
Awesome teacher, very nice and willing to work with the students.

"Heap is a god!" Heap one of the most clear speaking and devoted teachers I have met at this school. Professor Jarrell is perhaps the best finance professor in Simon school, I still apply what he taught me 6 years ago in my job on a daily basis.

Professor Bridy really knows his stuff. He always explains topics clearly and if you follow through the course and do the work you definitely should come out doing great. If you get stuck or confused, he does an awesome job of explaining in office hours.

Really great guy. Loves math and is really good at explaining concepts and answering questions. For MTH 150, don't focus too hard on the proofs he gives since they aren't in the exams. All examples he gives are useful and matter the most.

She is a great professor. And contrary to a prior post, she does not hate men, she just probably despised that student because he seems close-minded. Such anamazing prof, she is so interested in what she teaches and loves to discuss, as long as you pay attn in class you will get an A, on the test and paper as long as you put in a lot of effort you will get an A. she is amazing, favorite prof of all four years..VERY FAIR

never took an anthro class before and I loved this class, the books are really interesting, she keeps the discussions going and is just an overall awesome professor, gives you general questions to study before the exams that are really helpful

Formal logic sounds like a dry subject, but Sherman is genuinely hilarious.

Really, there should not be a doubt, if you like the subject matter go for it.  Also he is very helpful, a really cool and super approachable guy, math oriented though.
He is the coolest teacher at rochester. You can get an A if you try.  This guy freaking rocks though.  Really a fun class and a great prof.
