comment: Highly recommend everyone at UR to take Orisa's writing course! He is not strict with deadlines and cares about his students. As long as you do all the informal and formal assignments, you will be okay with this course.

One of the best professors I've had at Rochester. Takes the time to listen to his students, gives great feedback and suggestions, and is accessible even at night on a weekend. Also a very lenient grader!!!

I personally found the class more boring than what I went in expecting. However, I don't regret taking it. I'm probably in the minority, but I did not enjoy the readings and didn't feel super interested in the material. However, I did enjoy the environment of the class. Santiago is very caring, understanding, and just an overall amazing human!
One of the best professors I've had here. Truly a gem in the Rochester community!

Amazing instructor and person - he cares for his students and frequently takes time to hear out (and apply) our opinions/suggestions in class. Course content is very engaging if you are interested in his writing course topic. The course schedule is structured so that all writing assignments are doable on time without unnecessary stress.

Professor Morrice is a very caring, thoughtful, and human professor. The readings he selects are very insightful and the discussions that follow are very well mediated and enjoyable to participate in. He also gives lots of freedom in his writing prompts which means that you can almost always find something fun you would enjoy writing about.

He is AMAZING! You will have the best reading discussion ever in his class! He also gives you fair grades, and they are usually pretty good as long as you follow his suggestions. Don't be afraid to catch him up after class and ask him anything you don't understand! He'll explain every comment he gave to your paper and help you to write better :)

What a legendary professor! He became a professor in the writing department of Rochester last year, but he has already become one of the highly recommended professors! His lectures are inspirational! Take him!
Professor Morrice holds AMAZING discussions in classes. I really enjoyed attending his writing classes and he gives you both fair grades and constructive feedbacks.

You can really tell Prof. Renninger cares about teaching. He explains the material so well, and he always gauges student comprehension in class. Go to class and workshop, and the homework and exams, while not being a walk in the park, should have no surprises. If you are considering graduate school in physics or optics, this class is so valuable.

Prof. Renninger is clearly an expert in the material and his homework and exams are very fair.  The course material is easy to follow, and closely follows the textbook, which is a good resource if you need additional explanation.  If you listen to his advice and go over material on your own you'll save yourself a lot of time and frustration.
Prof. Renninger teaches a hard class, but he is very well-organized and makes the content seem easy. Homework is well-written and useful, exams are extremely fair and easy. Great class overall.
He was a great professor, but really hard class. Super grateful he let me pass.
Midterm is easy, but the final, wow.

Professor Renninger is amazing. He is clear with his lecture content and you can tell he wants you to succeed. He is always open to answering questions you have about the course content. He will involve students in his lectures by asking questions. I highly recommend you take his class if you are pursuing physics.

His teaching style is easy to follow and you will learn a lot of helpful concepts that you will use outside of this class in other classes! Homework assignments can be difficult but office hours and workshops set up help a lot!

Know that I took this class in spring 2022. A lot of people who took this class last year rated it very low, but you can clearly tell he took feedback and seriously improved. His lectures are some of the best I have seen, and he clearly cares about students and is always willing to take quesitons. He has seriously improved.

Prof. Renninger is great. He is so passionate about his job, and you can tell he really cares about his students and wants them to do well. His lectures are clear and go hand in hand with the hw assignments. He is always willing to help and he actually listens to his students when we give him feedback about the course.

This was hands down the hardest math I've taken. Not because the material itself was extremely difficult, but because his handwriting is near impossible to decipher, and the things he teaches are only a light skimming of what he asks for on the 12-hour homework assignments. The TAs are going to be how you get through this class.

He was not helpful in learning what is likely some of the hardest math people will attempt to learn. He can be unforgiving and when asked to do explicit things by students he would often not do them. All the learning is done through the TA's and workshop so attend those and be prepared to take a graduate level course.

This man was such a lazy professor and all your learning is through the TAs. His handwriting is impossible to read and he never responds to emails. It is apparent he does not care for students and does not care about actually teaching us anything.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Taught the Undergraduate class as a Graduate class and was one of the most confusing math classes I have ever taken. The professor seldom cares about the students and doesn't really respond to emails. It's possible that it may be better taught in person, but this semester was especially difficult.

Professor Lee is excellent for MTH 162. Going into the course I was very scared, but he presents the material in an extremely clear, straightforward, and organized way. He frequently pauses and asks the class if they have questions. He has clear answers to these as well. Super nice, very helpful if you speak to him one on one. A great Prof!

Best calc teacher I have had so far. During class, he gives examples of the concepts and uses student participation to answer them. Constantly asks if anyone has questions. Tests are very straightforward but the calc deparment expects you to memorize everything & work hard. Don't fall behind!
Lectures are boring and he just throws everything to you. There is no connection between chapters, or at least he failed to find them.
I barely understood what went on during lecture, I basically taught everything to myself
hard, but very understanding teacher and personable too.

he's a really nice guy but the lectures are not very engaging and content is gone through very quickly. exams in my opinion were also pretty difficult, having a good calc background would be beneficial. if you have to take 209, take it with a diff professor.

The instructor relies heavily on slides, but the slides did not include concepts in very detail, many concepts were not organized, and he was only reading them. He needs more practice in teaching. He focuses heavily on math when discussing intertemporal models and utility maximization problems, although he was unable to explain the math clearly.
Not very experienced with teaching. Lectures were complicated and unorganized. In-class time was just him reading off the notes.
He does't know what he is talking about.
Classes aren't worth going to.

Prof. Seiferas is very helpful, inviting students to his office anytime. Main problem is many students are forced to take class without having the prerequisite, for them the class obscenely hard and the lectures cryptic. I wish he would stick more closely to a textbook- papers he gives for us to read require reading many other papers to comprehend.

The guy is ferociously talented. I have got to give him that and due to that nature, he is far beyond comprehend-able. It is impossible to follow him in class. Just terrifying difficult in the beginning but it gets better. Still teaching could be a lot better. he is dedicated though but too brilliant to understand student are not as fluent as him!!

Really cares about his students and welcomes feedback.  Not a very good lecturer though, especially when he uses Powerpoint slides.  Tests were surprisingly hard.  Expect to do a LOT of extra studying outside of class.

Great prof, and exams are very true to the course material (clear format; she tells you some things she will ask beforehand). The final project (which you can do either individually or in a group) is very interesting and fun, and you can pick any topic you want. Also very relevant to actuarial roles if that interests you.

Prof Polak is incredibly nice and flexible. She is receptive to feedback from students and TAs and ensures that grading is completed quickly and accurately. Her lectures are easy to follow and reflect the content on homework and exams.

I really enjoyed her lectures and the fact that she takes time to answer questions. Recitation are very helpful if you have a good TA. I wish she wouldn't use textbook officialy because university adds it to course costs. The book is free on line.
She is engaging in class, and makes an effort to try and interact with students.

Assignments every week which aren't lengthy, but they're so horribly worded that you it's hard to understand what she wants you to do. There's no curve in the class. Also her teaching made me upset because she doesn't really know what she's doing, as she's new to Java. This made it harder to learn because she was also learning

CSC 161 was fairly easy for beginners in programming. Polak did a pretty good job of lecturing and demonstrating coding while she was teaching. The hws and midterms were not hard, though the final is a bit tough. Overall, she was pretty nice and approachable. I like her.

Polak does care about students, but she cares more about Cryptography than this class. Outside of the boring lectures, she uses AI to generate labs/projects (said so herself). The only project she made herself was given over Spring break, was difficult for no reason, had unclear instructions, and wasn't relevant at all to the the class material.
She gives curves and practice exams and plays video about dancing.

Would never take her again, It was a mistake. She is understanding but her teaching is so egregious and she is unapproachable. Her office hours are so short and she does not respond to emails. It seems as though she is new to teaching.

Polak struggled at the beginning because the official language of the class was JAVA, but she is used to coding in Python. As the semester progressed, she became better at it. To me, the class was easy because I learned everything but graphs in high school. The lectures were okay and I liked her project because I am a cryptography enthusiast.

Polak was lit. She explains hard topics in a way that's easy to understand and makes sure the class is following along with the info. Also very thorough with lectures and explains stuff step by step. Hw was kinda hard tho but the exams were light.
Interesting lectures

Never before have I seen a professor who cares so little about his course. He claims that attendance is mandatory and that you will lose points if you do not attend, and yet he himself seems to not bother showing up half the time. You only find out that he wont be there when the TA tells you since he doesn't bother sending an email.

Is a super careless professor. He rarely shows up for class and makes his TAs teach whatever he doesn't feel like doing that day. Attendance is mandatory, but it's a joke because he doesn't care if you don't show up. Assignments are easy once the TA tells you what they are.

This was a pretty ridiculous class. No one showed up on time and people just stopped trying, and the prof just didn't seem to want to do anything about it. He'd tell us each day, 'it'd be nice if you showed up on time' but there weren't any repercussions if people didn't. I would have actually liked to get a lot of out this class, but alas.

If you do your work and ask the TAs for help, you will come out with an A without using too much brain power. However, Brady is incredibly negligent in showing up to teach the class or the students. The entire class is disorganized, and your grade is determined by one assignment that he won't teach you how to do.  It is a miracle he has a job here.

Don't take a class with this professor. Last semester I took his intro to debate class, and he would skip every other class leaving his overworked TAs to teach the class. He just wants to stack the debate team with people. 
His absences though did make the class easy because he gave up teaching after a few slideshow monologues.

He doesn't really teach much about debate, he just reads off long slideshows about the structure of debates. The class isn't as much about critical thinking and argument as how to win at a debate tournament. He's pretty much impossible to get ahold of outside of class and can be extremely unorganized sometimes

he does not teach at all, he reads off of long slideshows. he is also extremely unorganized, he tends to forget what he put on the syllabus. not once did he ever explain how to do projects/group assignments. he doesn't even introduce debate, all just trying to get you to join the debate team.

Two reasons I didn't like this class: 1. This isn't "how to construct a dynamic, thought provoking arguments". This class is "how to win at the sport that is college debate", unless you love high school policy debate, you will hate this class as I do. 2. For a debate class. Fletcher is incredibly disorganized and extremely frustrating to work for.

Four total debates (midterm, two finals and one SPAR/spontaneous debate) and one group presentation. Great and accessible professor! Even though this was an intro class, more experienced peers made debates more challenging and fun

He saw that I was really struggling with a major depressive episode and worked with me outside of the classroom to get the help I needed. It's a demanding class and the first difficult CHE course in the curriculum. I loved it so much I'm taking it again (definitely not because I need to fix my gpa) next year!

His lectures are great; he writes out the notes with you and adds extra details, but read the textbook to supplement the material. Sometimes, the sample problems in the textbook are similar, or at least they give you a better idea of how to approach HWs and tests. Recitations — he does a good job of going through problems. Slack him with questions!

Foster was really funny in lectures, most of the time he just writes things on his ipad the entire lecture, but lab is really fun and if you get to know him and talk to him hes going to be very chill and really down to earth. Once we made him seat every single student to where we sit usually and he did it easily so that was impressive.

His lectures are great and he is easy to understand. He makes things pretty entertaining but the exams tend to be really hard. However, he gives a ton of partial credit and the curve is pretty heavy. He's very clear about what is gonna be on exams but sometimes throws in questions that no one can do, but it all works out in the curve.

The exams take a large amount of your final grade, and they are usually pretty difficult. Average will be like 50% 60%, but he will decide final grade wisely. His lecture is perfect. The problem comes from the course material that is not difficult to be taught in general, understandable language

Very full of himself. He claims he's accommodating at the beginning of the year but is not. If you are struggling in his class talk to the TAs they will be more helpful than him. Go to office hours as frequently as you can.
Foster makes Separations a class you want to go to. Legendary stories and immaculate lecture notes every time. Homework and Exams are a breath of fresh air compared to CHE 243
This legend sips on luxurious beers.  Very positive guy, nothing but respect for him.

Foster is so chill in CHE250.  He beat us up in 243 but he's an angel in 250.  Lectures are laid back with fun stories told by him, hw is not long, exams are short, and he is a much nicer grader.  You'll still learn a lot as he still keeps things professional once he gets his "acting gear" together.

Foster is very full of himself, and hard to reach out to. Very "my way or the highway" mentality, which, when you reach out to him when you're struggling, is very unhelpful. Also your grade is almost all based on your exams, with no way to earn points if you have a bad day. Homeworks are also often long, confusing, and very difficult. Prepare.
The workload is a lot but this is one of the more interesting courses that I took from the CHE department
Great at explaining concepts. I hate his exams and the way he grades them. Way too long, difficult, and a tough grader.
Great teacher, but the grade is test-heavy (75% is test-based). Labs were fun, but make sure you do everything that is "suggested." Take his advice about getting ahead on the work (esp labs).
He is kinda like the big brother that likes messing and tormenting his little siblings only to say "gotcha!" at the end. Very big ego but overall not that bad.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: Test Heavy is the best way to describe this class, although its not outlined in the grading criteria you're grade will be decided entirely by your tests. The final isn't as bad as it seems, but do not have a bad day on a midterm as it will cost you your final grade. Very clear and direct professor, definitely full of himself but you'll get over it.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Professor Foster a high opinion of himself, and a lot of his decisions and actions are guided by his own ego. He tries too hard to appear intelligent, often brags about how he likes to solve equations in his free time, and purposely obfuscates questions and material. He also acts like a brofessor, maybe so students will like him more.  I dunno.

Great professor. Clearly intelligent and well-read, but also expects a certain level of effort on your part. Homework isn't a large portion of the grade, but is critical to understanding the problems on exams.
tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: This class is k, but the final was quite challenging. It also requires a lot of time doing HW. A lot of people think Prof. Foster is a good guy but I can definitely feel that he is kinda biased against students whose English are not their first language.

I came into this class thinking I was going to hate it.  Instead, it turned into my favorite class thanks to Foster.  His lectures are incredibly detailed and engaging, and seriously help you learn.  He spends time after every class just answering students' questions.  Incredibly helpful and friendly.  Best prof I've had in my two years here.

Foster is an amazing lecturer! Very clear and organized, but if you don't go to class you don't get his notes. Gives lots of homework that if you do yourself and actually understand the tests aren't bad. Always willing to answer questions or go more in depth. Gives real world applications to make it more interesting. Best professor I've ever had.

Learned a lot in Fluids. He's very passionate about the subject and does a good job explaining tough material. Tests are tough but if you do the homework, go to office hours, and study you'll be fine.

Great teacher and knows his stuff for sure. This is a really difficult class but necessarily difficult given the subject manner (Transport is really hard everywhere according to friends I have taking it at other universities). Foster is approachable and his lectures are fast paced and give you what you need to understand the material.

This professor might have good verbal communication skills, but that is it. He tries to make himself seem like an expert, who is really into it. His answers, to questions are brief and lack any depth. He assigns the same homeworks and solutions are typed over from other sources. He simply copies the book over onto the board. Too superficial.
Fantastic, brilliant, helpful, and the lessons stuck with me.
He is a very interesting man. I love the way he teaches the course, but honestly he's a monster. I call him Captain Kodak. He puts on a quality act.
Possibly the best professor I have had at the University of Rochester. He will make you work, but he is definitely helpful and extremely enthusiastic about the material.

Also had him for CHE/BME 259. Great teacher.  He works in this field, so he really loves what he does. Helpful, clear, and organized. I actually LEARNED from his class. One of the Best professors I've had.
Enthusiastic about the material and always available for extra help.  Really loves teaching and wants students to succeed.

He really cares about what he is teaching and goes the extra mile for it. The class is hard, but he's fair and wants everyone tp succeed. Be prepared to work your ass off but your actually going to be learning a lot
Foster is the man. Fluids isn't an easy course but he endlessly facilitates help. He even goes to the recitations! This man knows and loves what he's teaching. One of my favorite professors at UR.
Be prepared to work. Look over your notes after class and ask questions about stuff you don't get.

Professor really cares about students, and does his best to keep you up to date and make you feel good about yourself... Sometimes he doesn't answer questions clearly and bypasses them... but overall a good professor
Great professor; really likes teaching.  Hard class but as long as you go to lecture and keep up with the homework you will do fine.  He really wants his students to do well.

One of the best engineering professors in this university. Lectures are fast paced but informative. Exams and homework are difficult but supportive of the course material. Very approachable and a great guy.
good
Great Prof, yep VERY HOT....I love his class.

Excellent Prof.Expert on material, cares about students, I learned allot.I wish he taught every course I took.  No doubt the best prof in the university. Yea, he's hot, but the great thing is that he doesn't know he's hot, or at least I don't think he does. Very approachable, cares about students.
um.. yeah, good prof, I like his class but... come on girls...he could be our dad...do we get distracted by our dads?, I think not...lets rate the class not the looks.
Well known at the UofR for two things:  1. an excellent prof who really knows what he's doin and a great teacher who cares about students, 2. total hottie, distractingly good looking.
Excellent Prof, really knows the subject, and distractingly good looking. Brilliant and HOT.
Excellent Prof, knows his stuff
Excellent Professor- communicates well

I don't think he teaches well, not only because he's not an AI expert, but also due to unclear slides and assignments. There are no hints for homework in the slides, and his exams have too many questions to finish. The midterm average was 79/100. His slides are fixed by Berkeley's CS188, but it's better to watch the videos than take Kang's course.
Professor Moon is funny and seems like a great guy. However, beware that he takes a long time to respond to emails and grade papers. Overall, good class.
No clear grading guidelines and harsh essay grader

Amazing prof! Very reading intensive, but if you pace yourself and are strategic it's fine. He does take a long time to grade, but his feedback is thorough. Attendance not mandatory, but go to lectures because they really help and he gives important updates about assignments. Also go to his office hours-he's really hilarious and great to talk to!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: He grades extremely late (papers weren't graded for around 2 months, while in the meantime he would give more papers), he was very vague with assignments, and would have papers listed on the syllabus for a date that was nowhere near the date he gave them and gave no warning about assigning papers or finals, and his lectures are very involved.

Professor moon is overall okay but there is definitely room for improvement. Homework can be a lot of reading but you can definitely get away with not reading everything; it's more tedious than difficult. Grading can be a bit subjective but not horrible. He takes ages to grade your papers and assignments.
this is the worst class I have taken in my four years as a mechanical engineering student

Prof. Borrelli's lectures are really in depth and a bit technical, but this is not always the information that we are expected to know. It takes a bit to figure out what you are expected to take away from each class. But it's a super interesting class that crosses over a lot of disciplines!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: Not very suitable for non-environmental majors. I didn't feel like learning anything from this class, and the test was graded very harshly. Although Professor Borrelli is really nice, the materials are heavy to study. I received all As in other courses but received a B+ in this 100-level class. You have to get 95 to earn an A so it's tough.

Professor Borelli is knowledgeable but very unapproachable. She does have lots of extra credit opportunities but the class material is too heavy for an intro class or anybody looking to take an elective. The TA in charge has an attitude and the exams are fair but it is a lot of material to memorize. Would not waste the time in this.

Didn't really care for her class. Borrelli was very dry and just reads off her slides for lectures, making it very difficult to pay attention. She has extra credit which is nice, but there is no curve. Tests are kinda hard, but if you study you'll be fine. She grades strict on homework and tests. Class is hit and miss.

Professor Borelli is a real sweetheart. Even though this was her first time teaching over zoom she made sure to be well-prepared for classes and made a lot of effort to make sure we all knew what was happening. She also provided a lot of optional extra credit to studnts and even allowed assignments to be attempted again after initial submission.
Not too interesting in class. Speaks real slow, but is a fair grader and organizes awesome specially curated trips into the archives of George Eastman House.
Good professor. Explains things well, likes discussion.
Boring lecture with awkward questions (followed by awkward silences); unclear syllabus/assignments.

Lectures can be kind of boring and important material kind of hard to pick out. Field trips to George Eastman House can be interesting, though. She is flattered when students take interest and asks questions during her lectures. Sometimes she pulls material out of no where for the test though. You really do get a good base knowledge. Lenient grader
excellent teacher
interesting subject, knowledgeable teacher--looking at slides in the dark makes you want to sleep every time though.

She's nice but the class is rather boring. The material could be interesting but she talks from the second you walk in until class is over. She expects you to already know a lot even though it was an INTRO class.

Only saw the guy once the entire semester. The worksheets seem to have been in use for like 20 years and are kind of cluttered and disorganized. The course website is a total mess. Seems to just be completion graded.

I never had any contact with him, all of my learning was done independently or with TAs. It's clear that he's tired of teaching this course given that he has no part in it whatsoever, and he gives out Incompletes like candy to those who procrastinate. It is a hard course but if you start early and pace yourself its not too bad. I, however, did not.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Lots of homework']

comment: I never even exchanged an email with this guy, never saw him in person. The TAs were great though! Just make sure you start the workload before the last few weeks of class.

If you're here because you are considering self paced physics, DO NOT DO IT. 
First of all, he has no clue how to use Blackboard. Assignments are nearly impossible to find, somethings are listed in multiple places, or nowhere at all, and he never updates his assignments ever. Not to mention the TAs will yell at you in front of the entire class.

This class is not worth it if you can't pace yourself. There are weekly homeworks and quizzes(13), 4 midterms, and a final. It is a lot of work. Ask the TAs for help and attend workshops. I learned most of the material through Crash Course, Prof Dave Explains, & Khan Academy. The homeworks & answer keys are from 3 years ago and haven't been updated

Honestly, Dr. Rich's lectures are not engaging at all, he just reads off of outdated slides I don't think he even made himself. Tests (only 2) are pretty easy if you just memorize info from the slides. Pop quizzes are graded on completion, so show up to lecture. Didn't really learn anything long-term, but if you just do your work it isn't a hard A.
tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: PHLT 103 was a snoozefest. Rich mainly reads off his slides or speaker notes. I felt as though I learned nothing of importance in epidemiology. Adding on, I wish the grading criteria were more lenient. If you lose 1 point on your homework, your overall grade goes down by 1%. My TA graded my homeworkers harshly, so be aware of the grading system!!!

Boring lectures (made me hate epidemiology even tho it's my major). Lots of pop quizzes. HWs took really long and TAs grade so harshly. Tests are just the slides so just memorize those (if you can memorize 60 slides for every lecture lol). He barely shows up to class; the entirety of December was just guest lecturers/recorded lectures.
tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Dr. Rich was near impossible to reach outside of classroom hours. He would take days, if not weeks, to respond to my emails, and even then was very difficult to schedule with. To be honest, he made me disinterested in epidemiology.

Dr. Rich's lectures can be somewhat boring, but some of the guest lecturers are pretty interesting. Although there was a textbook, all the test material is from information from the slides so you don't really need the textbook. Know the definitions of different terms for the exams.

Dr. Rich is a good person, but his lectures were somewhat boring. I think this might just be because epidemiology as a whole isn't the most exciting. Try and memorize the slides he presents in lecture, since the exams mimic these slides. I purchased a textbook for this class but never used it and did fine, so I would recommend going without one.

If you do not have interest in epidemiology, you will find this class very boring. Dr. Rich just reads exactly what are on the lecture slides and adds nothing else. The guest lectures are interesting. One midterm and final which are multiple choice and are easy if you memorize the important concepts. Homework isn't hard, but tedious.

Professor Rich speaks in a monotone voice and his lectures are very boring. The course is difficult because we are given no study material except for the slides and pop quizzes. 60% of your grade is from two exams so you must do well. If you are good at memorizing and teaching yourself concepts, you'll be fine. Otherwise, this course will be hard.

Professor Rich does not care about his students and reads off the slides which is not helpful. He does not try to make the class easier and the exams are difficult. Every class consists of around 60 slides that need to be memorized for the exams. He holds his office hours off campus which is not useful for students.

I thought I was gonna like Public Health but I was wrong. This man is boring as hell, I don't pay 80k for a slide reader. His guest lecturers he hires while he is on vacation in Europe are somewhat better than him. There are only a midterm and final which determine your grade. If you are actually interested sure take this, otherwise don't bother.

This class may be easy if you have an interest for epidemiology, however I would not recommend taking this class if it is your first time doing public health.Professor Rich constantly reads off his power point slides during classtime, and his voice is rather monotonous, which may make it hard to pay attention. He only gives one midterm, so do well!
tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: good lecturer, not too boring that youd fall asleep in and stays on track. Always willing to help students and answer questions/emails. Class is pretty basic, not very hard content, but there is a lot to memorize. Textbook is nice but not necessary, 99% of the exam is covered in lecture slides. Stay on top of hw and pop quizzes, will be a breeze
Honestly the reason I am going to study Epidemiology. A really kind, down-to-Earth professor. Just go to lecture and take notes and you will be good to go!
Very nice and accessible professor who really knows his stuff. You do need to study for his class (he gives pop quizzes) and homework grades are somewhat dependent on your TA.

The class itself was fun for me personally as it actually involved getting out and doing activities. What ruined the class for me was the very harsh grading of the final which to me seemed like was on track to do well based off of his comments but ended up getting a bad grade which tanked my GPA.

You have to spend 1.5 hours outdoors every week on top of homework. Also, he grades based on what he thinks and if he does not agree with you, you will get points off. He will set up meetings with you which almost automatically gets you a better grade. The class was not difficult itself, I just did not enjoy it at all.

Gave surface level feedback, often it seemed that he skimmed the paper at best, sometimes giving feedback that was resolved in the next paragraph. Often seemed to not take students opinions in class discussion seriously until someone said his opinion. Grades arbitrarily. Grading and email replies take a long time.

didn't feel that the class was hard but i never felt like he took my perspective seriously in class discussions and he rarely gave insightful feedback. readings have to be finished before lectures and some of them are strange. interest in the outdoors is almost a requirement

He will probably be harsh on your initial drafts, but just follow his notes and revise accordingly, and you will receive a satisfactory grade for the final draft.
If you are not very passionate about outdoor activities, he might not be the best choice for WRTG 105.

Grades randomly. Many times he would leave feedback that clearly showed he did not read the entire paper and that he was unwilling to see things from a different perspective. Also, for an outdoor-based writing class, he brought up issues like class and race a lot. Cool guy, bad professor.

If you are an incoming freshman AVOID THIS PROFESSOR at all costs. He is the most unfair and illogical grader ever. He grades without a rubric, and deducts vast amounts of points for small errors in papers. I came into this class as an experienced writer writing for my high school newspaper for 3 years, with over 50 published articles.
best professor I have ever had.
He will tear your GPA apart for ambiguous reasons. No mercy!
I really liked him but he grades his papers hard. Class was discussions based and mandatory attendance. Daily assignments are light but the 3 papers hits hard.

Justin was an extremely helpful professor and always gave useful feedback. The lessons were interesting a discussion-based. The assignments were difficult, but he is helpful with them and is allows for an extension if it means it will improve your work!
Hes nice enough, but somehow he made an interesting course boring. Extremely tough grader, I got a D+ even though I took AP English in high school. Use the writing center, not him.

Professor Coyne is patient to answer students' questions, and he gives specific and helpful suggestions to students' essays. He is always prepared for course so don't forget to read the reading materials before classes!

He managed to make a class on inequality boring. The professor doesnt know how to teach, doesnt know how to facilitate a discussion, and grades harshly based on a super niche criteria of his work. I managed to get an A-, but there was a lot of work, and only a few things actually mattered for my grade.
tags: ['Graded by few things', 'Group projects', 'So many papers']

comment: He is an extremely friendly professor who wants you to become a better writer. He gives very specific and good feedback but you have to be willing to talk to him either outside of class or during. He helps you analyze all the texts we read (and there are a lot of them!) and really wants his students to understand the topics.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Tough grader']

comment: - Three papers over the semester - Readings for every week - Mandatory attendance - Tough grader
tags: ['Accessible outside class', 'Graded by few things', 'Tough grader']

comment: Seem like as long as you do spend your time and effort on the papers, you will get a decent grade. The workload is not heavy and the prof is really nice and willing to help anytime

He is a pretty nice guy, quite accessible outside of class. You do need to go to class. He gives good feedback sometimes. He seems to lack the motivation to fully read/understand what you write, almost like he skims. It seems that he reads but not fully like he should, for a wrt teacher. He picks uninteresting topics.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: Pretty hard grader but gives good feedback so you're able to learn from your mistakes and improve over time. Attendance super important, but if there are extenuating circumstances he's pretty understanding. He's pretty much always open to talking about concerns or ideas outside of class, so just reach out if you want to talk about your work.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: Yes, he is a tough grader. But he is super approachable and friendly in and out of class.

Very strict grader and will take off a significant amount participation points form your final grade even if you arrive a few minutes late to class or don't participate. Is ready to read and provide feedback for several drafts of your assignment given that they are sent at least a day prior to the deadline
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read']

comment: The professor is nice, but beware his class is not well organized. The first half of 448 will be your easiest class. But in the second half you will be thrown into tons of difficult coding assignments. The notes are half pictures so studying for paper exams is impossible.

There is no exam, no homework, only (six) projects that will make you put your hands on and get to learn parallel programming using some initial samples from lectures' codes. The TAs and the professor do answer your questions but it is your code so don't expect them to find your errors, they will tell you maybe what to look for.

He is great at teaching programming and you will learn a lot from him. BUT the quizzes were quite tricky. The exams and projects were fair game except the TA's made mistakes in grading them VERY OFTEN.
A really good introduction to quantum formalism, and very organized lectures and notes!

I really like how he structured the class. Cheat sheets, drop lowest exam score, AND each exam was curved. I do think he genuinely taught the content well in a way that non-physics majors could understand. Physics II is a lot of your own understanding and practice regardless of the professor, but I think he still did a great job.

Prof. Blok's Quantum Theory course was easily the most interesting rendition of quantum mechanics I've ever taken. Because he's a quantum computing researcher, he had lots of interesting examples to connect to in class, and he was very clear about what were still "open questions" in the field. I struggled with the math in the course, but LOVED it!

During the first day of PHYS 114 lecture, Professor Blok said he was here to guide us through the material, not teach us. This was highly discouraging to hear. I also did not like how homework was only 10% of your grade and some of the exam questions were worded weirdly.

One of the best professors in Black/African-American literature. Very kind and understanding. Great lectures. Clear grading as well - class structure is a few reading responses, and 2-3 essays, participation, and lesson plan questions.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Prof. Tucker is so clearly a master of the subjects which he lectures on. If you're willing to participate in class (which you totally should), you will grow so much more. He's kind, responsive to emails and questions, and all-around is a professor I've learned a lot from. I look forward to continuing to take his classes.

Always respectful, super happy to help, wonderful prof. My class was almost entirely discussion based and he always found a way to keep it going and get people engaged even on a Monday morning. Very light workload, technically all readings are required but you can do well only reading the ones that you have to respond to (trust me). Great guy.
Excellent Professor who gives great lectures and detailed feedback on your assignments. Also gives extremely clear grading criteria which I found to be extremely helpful. Would definitely recommend!

EXCELLENT PROFESSOR. I absolutely loved his teaching style, and you can tell he genuinely loves what he does. He speaks softly, but you hang on to every word. He facilitates a classroom where you walk away having a better understanding of the course and why you study what you love.
Professor Tucker has an amazing ability to keep everyone in his classes involved and interested. He has a genuine ability to make students feel as though they and their opinion truly matter.
One of my favorite professors.  Genuinely interested in his students and cultivating their intellectual pursuits.

GREAT professor.  Taught a very intresting class and attempted to get to know everyone in a large class.  Assigns a fair amount of work and you will do well in the class if you keep up.  Plus, he gave NO tests!!

Jeff Tucker is a kind, patient, helpful, reliable teacher with a genuine concern for education and a strong desire to foster intellectual interests in his students.  I couldn't possibly say enough nice things about him.
Anyone you can make Poe boring is a terrible professor.  Staying awake during his class was the only challenge I faced.
He's awesome, really helpful and a professional sweetheart --make sense?e

Prof Korn is an excellent professor. He would always make sure that his students are learning the Italian language and that they practice their writing and conversational skills. As a matter of grading, he can be a tough grader sometimes but he would always give good feedback. Because of COVID we did not have quizzes, instead, we had papers.

Although he was not bad last semester in IT101 he has made a 180 in his teaching and his grading. He is a strict professor and does not listen well to student feedback, as he finds ways to justify his harshness. You need to go to class, but even if you participate don't expect 100%. Exams- he will take points off even if your answer is right.

Andrew is passionate about Italian language and culture and has vast experience inside and outside the classroom.  I was afraid to start learning a new language and he gave me the confidence to not only try but persist, which is critical in language acquisition.  When Andrew tells me, bravissima!, it is worth all the work.

He is charismatic and dedicated to being a good teacher. Told a funny story about eating raw chicken in Japan. Did a final showing of the class' final project of sound design though it's not necessary. Since there are few jobs in sound design, I don't recommend taking more classes. Definitely read the book on sound design to prepare for quiz.

Prof. Lavaque is so passionate about what he teaches, he makes the class so fun. He is quite hands-off in his approach and mostly leaves you to figure things out by yourself, but he or the TAs will always help if you get stuck. The projects take a lot of time, but they're not brain-rackingly difficult.

Esteemed professor with loads of industry experience. Projects are structured with real-world-clients in mind. Genuinely cares for his students' success and is understanding when life get tough. Don't slack off or you can easily get behind. 

*another rating said he expects you to know certain software, but it's literally listed in the pre-reqs

He is known for being irresponsible, not only been ignoring the students questions via Zoom, but also been a procrastinator in terms of giving grades and assignments. The class is frankly boring and irrelevant to the topic. He would talk about softwares which we should be already familiar with. Therefore, I don't suggest to take this course.

If you're planning to take this class, think again. Previously, I expected the class to be super fun and interesting. Yet, it turns out to be unpleasant and unsatisfying. He's known for his unpunctuality of getting the class started, his irresponsibility, ungenerous, and his irrelevant teaching. Thus, I won't recommend students to take this class.
Easy and fun class, just do the work and for the most part you will be fine.

Professor Lavaque is a great guy.  He's heavily decorated and really knows what he's talking about when it comes to sound production.  He's always quick to give good feedback, and won't hesitate to help if anything isn't clear.  His classes aren't easy per se, but it's the kind of hard work you have fun with.

Very fun and worthwile class! Class is mostly project-based, and it really gets you familiar with the tools that professionals in the field use (of which he is one - an Emmy-winner). His demos can be rushed somewhat unclear at times, but he takes a "learn by doing" approach to teaching the class.

Professor Caie is undoubtedly brilliant. He completed his Doctorate in 2011, and already has 2 papers published in the Philosophical Review. Many of the best tenured philosophers have only achieved just 1 publication in the Review throughout their careers. However, he has struggles as a lecturer in presenting ideas clearly and stimulating a class.

Michael Caie is a professor that means well, but ultimately fails at teaching. He is a nice enough person, but isn't the sort of person you want teaching you. This becomes particularly important when his specialties are logic and philosophy of language--two areas that are easy to become confused in. Ultimately, I would have to say to pass on Caie.

In case he hasn't retired by next summer, don't take this course. His grading criteria is based on regurgitation of definitions, not demonstrated comprehension and ability. He's rude and condescending to students. Don't make the mistake of ruining your summer by taking this course- you won't enjoy it, and  you won't get the scores you want.

Taking this class in the summer might be the worst decision you ever make.  Unless you have previously taken the course or AP Chem in high school I would not recommend taking it.He does not teach during the year and there's a reason why.  Don't be a fool in thinking it will be easier over the summer.  It's not and you won't get the grade you want.

15 weeks of gen chem in a 6 week session is difficult.  Dr. Hickey paces the course as well as can be expected, but without any time to let the material sink in, it can be tough to keep up.  The fact that Dr. Hickey demands a level of mastery in excess of other faculty at the U or R translates into brutal exams on a very compressed schedule.

Tests really don't reflect what he teaches. He asks you to fully interpret things that he gives you a rudimentary description of. He does know his subject material quite well, though. But most importantly, he might be the slowest teacher ever.
He is a very good teacher but his tests are extremely hard he wants you to be a master at the topic and talk about it as though you have been studying it for years for a general chemistry course.

You won't learn economics directly in this professor's class; he shares trivial details from his own life and leaves it to you to reflect on what.if anything—you've actually learned. he assigns bizarre CK. If you're the type of student who expects knowledge to be delivered straight to you in the classroom, dont take his course it will be a disaster

Super entertaining lectures that you can learn a lot from if your open minded. But homework is very time consuming and mostly busy work. Tests are also very rough, they are hard to study for and unnecessarily off topic.
I passed, but did I learn anything? Not really. Did I enjoy it, not really.

Long and diffcult Exams/HWS. Lectures are interesting, but can be confusing and rushed. If you want a straightfoward class, not for you. Very manageable if you do all HW/EC, exam grades can be forgiving if you do those. Outside of class, hes a awesome guy and very knowledgable, just nuts. He teaches how to think economically. !!Read the syllabus!!

I think he's an exceptional intro economics professor, and I always enjoy discussing intellectual questions with him. IMO, try to speak to him one on one, and brush off his lecture persona. There's a lot you can learn from him. However, be aware that he lacks professional boundaries—I had to learn to not take *anything* he said to heart.
confusing lectures, really long weekly homeworks, bad attitude. just don't do it bro

He often goes off on tangents and jumps around / skips more than half of his slides. He comes up with unnecessary references and takes hours to explain logical things that could have been easily explained through a few beginner-level terms. No textbook. You'll also be forced to dedicate hours every week to assignments (TA said 8 hours on average).

Ends up being more confusing/frustrating than helpful. Homework's extremely wordy, long, and dense. Expect tons of unnecessary stress for an intro-level course. His teaching's also very unstructured and disorganized. Exams and grading criteria don't make any sense and are often arbitrary.

comment: rizzo is so silly and i love him dearly! he's very accessible, go to office hours, you have to care about the class to do well in it! the homework assignments for 108 were a bit on the denser side, but they're rewarding!

Professor Rizzo is a character but I think he is a professor you need to take at some point at the U of R. His homework do get long but they are not graded hard and every project is a guaranteed A as long as you do it. His lectures are all over the place and it seems like he is on acid but he's just super enthusiastic.

this course is about thinking about the way the world works. There's no use of textbooks, and lecture is not required, but homework is quite tedious. The exam questions can be confusing sometimes and not related to things you learned in class. Extremely engaged professor and his lectures are fun to attend. Has a very unique teaching style.

8+ hrs of hw weekly! Lectures are fun but are more ranty than econ/mathy. You'll learn about understanding human motivation...feels like glorified psych with some budget analysis. Tests are brutal and feedback is non-existent. You either get it or you don't. He cares about you though. Want a sample? -> can we conserve species by eating them?

His lectures are super interesting and definitely changed the way I viewed some things. However, if you're looking for an easy grade, don't take this class. The homework takes a lot of time, and the exams are hard. The lectures are fast-paced and it's important you actively listen in class.

Great Professor, engaging during lecture, very accessible outside of class.  Show up early to his class because he frequently will give insider knowledge to his exams, homework and extra credit during this time.  He remembers faces very well.  Assigns lots of Homework.
I understand the frustration with him, his assignments take forever and can frankly be quite mindless. However, he's a treat to talk to and genuinely cares about his students. Great guy, hard class

Participation isn't necessary but you should go to lectures and recitations if you want a good grade. Office hours aren't very helpful academically but definitely helps with learning to integrate EWOT. Homework took 10+ hours a week for me. HW/Test grading is TA-dependent and not very consistent. However, a course revamp is coming next year.

A lot of people don't like Rizzo and he isn't for everyone but if he's for you it will be your favorite class. I think it's worth giving it a shot. Even if he isn't for you if you do the work and actually pay attention to what he's saying you can still do really well.

More of a writing class than an econ class, if you wanna rip your brains out throughout the semester, then sure, take him. If not, I'd recommend someone else. Also has the most corrupt TA's of all time. Countless TA's would give answers to the exams during review sessions. He rants about his personal life.

Don't take him, he might be the worse professor i've ever had. Overcomplicates things by telling us stories from his personal life, talks about his kids, ex wife, and his gf MJ, overly long rants about random bs. I could've taught my myself the whole course.

***Read all of the reviews on RMP***

I personally loved Rizzo's class. However, a few notes on ECON-108:

-The syllabus is 31+ pages. Read it.
-There are two homework assignments each week, but we got skips.
-Lectures are not mandatory. Show up.
-Supply and Demand curves don't show up until the last week
-Go to office hours
-AI use was encouraged

Run

One exam question:

How much do you think you should write for this question?

Definitely not economics.

He struggles with teaching. If you are expecting to learn economics, do not take this god-forsaken course. You will be learning rizzonomics instead of basic textbook econ. You will be confused when he goes on various tangents, assigns random readings that are barely relevant to the course, and asks the most pecuilar questions on exams. Good luck

comment: Horrible. Should quit to be honest. I didn't learn a single thing when I took this class. Save your time.

comment: If you have the opportunity to take a different professor for this course... TAKE THE OTHER PROF. IF you're not on his wave length, you will fail.
my fav class my freshman yr fall, gen one of the most interesting courses I have ever taken and the mindset you learn in this class is applicable to so many different aspects of life.

I wouldn't recommend taking any course with Rizzo. His lectures frequently go off-topic and lack a clear structure, making it hard to grasp the core material. More importantly, the content covered in class often doesn't match what appears on the exams, which is frustrating if you're trying to genuinely learn and succeed in higher level classes.
Professor Rizzo is one of the greatest teachers there is and fundamentally changed by life in a positive way. I truly cannot thank Professor Rizzo enough.

Exams were very lengthy and the rubric for them was pretty wanky. A lot of times the response he was expecting was so exact it was hard to get full credit. He sometimes curves the grade at the end but just a little. Go to all the lectures; it'll help you understand his mind a bit better. 207 is a lot easier than 108, but you still have to study.

Best lecturer I've ever taken a class with. Super engaging and entertaining to listen to. Genuinely cares about the material and helping you understand. That said, he is horrible at writing exams, and grading criteria often feel arbitrary (e.g., no one gets full credit because no one guessed what he was thinking). Gives a lot of extra credit.

I think Rizzo's great. If you don't vibe with his style in the first couple of weeks, drop the class and take it with a different professor. Don't get to the point in the semester where you hate the class and can't switch out. That said, he teaches a very good class and tries hard to make the Econ topics engaging and interesting to learn for y'all.

comment:
His classes are hard, have a fairly heavy workload, but you learn a lot!
Don't take if you an easy A, But you will do well if you work hard in his class and engage with the material. 
Do take if you want to learn Economics.

Writing this before I get final grades, but I am doing fine rn. Not suitable for everyone, but ime, i have gotten so much out of taking Rizzo's class. 

3% EC, super caring (helped me with internships), and respectful/engaging (even though I disagree w/ him a lot). 

Make sure to pay close attention (and record if you can) to his lectures though.

Rizzo's teaching style is definitely not for everyone. It's non-traditional, emphasizing some philosophical/psychological ways of thinking and viewing economics. You should attend every lecture as his stories are what's in his exams. TAs are amazing and will help you through the class, def go see them and regularly attend office hours. I loved it.
Too much homework if you're taking this class outside of your major. Lectures are interesting but not well structured.

comment: Weekly homework that is writing heavy. The class teaches a mindset, which you will take with you, and truly embracing this mindset makes the completion of the exams and homework significantly easier. The recitations, while optional, are very enjoyable. Very open during office hours where very enjoyable conversations can be had.

Rizzo is a cool guy. Fun lectures and is truly interested in making you love learning. Be curious and attend lectures or else this class will be a living nightmare. Some of the homeworks are kinda redundant but overall a great class to take.

Everyone says that Rizzo is a nutcase, and they're probably right, but his class was fun and although there was a lot of complaining, the workload wasn't that bad. TAs grade all your assignments and you can use ChatGPT on everything, even tests, but don't let that fool you into thinking its an easy A. Overall pretty good class would take again.

Took this class out of pure curiosity. It's definitely a hard class, and the way to a good understanding of the material is murky at best (hence the low rating, this class should be made more accessible), but it's fun if you appreciate learning that's more than rote memorization.

Worst unorganized lectures I have ever attended. A 5 year old with a lisp could teach economics better. The tests seem to consist of his diary entries and are graded harshly. First two were open note probably because he knows none of his teachings make any sense. Very subjective questions, none of the tests are multiple choice. So much homework.

Only take this class if ALL of the following is true:

1. You're a good test taker. Tests are nightmarish: ten short essays with convoluted prompts. NO NOTES OR CHATGPT.

2. A philosophical approach works for you, and you can teach yourself math. 

3. An interesting class is more important to you than your final grade.

One of the best professors I have ever had. Would definitely take a class with him again if I had the opportunity to do so. His style of teaching a little different, but if you get used to it, there's no class more fun and interesting than Econ 108 with Rizzo
Good man good lecture

never ever take this professor, his lecture makes no sense, and never teach you what is economic, instead he just be yapping about why his wife left him and other nonsense. The test is useless,  three hour long, and ten short essays, what people do is just copy from chatgpt

He's big on yapping and you'll never know what he's trying to teach you. It's obvious he knows a lot about economics but he's bad at teaching the concepts without talking about his ex wife or kids (specifically his daughter). No one scores well on the tests and they are not curved. I have to take him again but would prefer not to.

Honestly one of the most fun classes you can take at this school. There are no exams, simply two projects during the semester, with at least one being a group project, and some weekly homework. It's a chill class where you can just come to listen about sports economics or you can choose to engage in the discussion. Would recommend it to anyone.

I received a higher grade in 207 but I enjoyed 108 more. Rizzo's 207 is not math-based and sometimes the exam rubrics can be controversial. He is less organized than other instructors. Besides the class, he is a great friend and we had serval in-depth conversations.

The approach of his ECON 108 is a little bit different and more towards humanity, which can create good insights. It is a lecture-oriented class so understanding his stories in class is important. It is easy for me to see the connections between his homework and lectures but I understand that others might not feel this way.
Rizzo's class can be challenging, but it's worth the effort. The lectures are engaging, and you'll learn a lot about economic principles. Unstuckstudy AI and the free textbook are great study aids.
There is a lot of homework, and the lessons are not related to the homework.

I had no idea what he was talking about in his class, it felt like he was giving assignments that didn't have a single thing to do with the content of the class, that you had to write a lot every week in order to complete the assignments, and that you weren't going to get a good grade, even if you had the finances to do so
I love Prof. Rizzo! I chose to major in  Economics because of him. I'm a huge fan.

I enjoyed Rizzo a lot for 108. He goes downhill for 207. It does not feel like a real micro class at all. A lot of the things he chooses to cover in the course are based on what he likes to teach, NOT what is important for us to know. He stays away from the math which makes future classes difficult. Definitely not meant to teach a complex econ.

Rizzo is an extremely misunderstood professor by students. I know a lot of the other reviews say to not listen to the reviews like mine, but I think that his class was great. Somewhat difficult but great. You learn a lot in his class. Overall, it teaches you how to be a better student. The microeconomic topics are explained well and in a fun format

Rizzo is def one of the professors that you either love or hate. I personally enjoyed his lectures a lot, as they are more casual and conversational. He is also VERY knowledgable. However, his homework are extremely stressful, so be prepared to spend 5 hours each week for this weekly research writings. He also yaps too much on HW/exam questions.

Professor Rizzo is a amazing lecturer. He can make something as boring as CPI interesting. He truly cares for his students and only has the best intentions. He is a professor you will not regret taking. Just make sure to ask for help. This is what your TAs and office hours are for! It is an extremely rewarding class if you try. Thank you Rizzo!

Rizzo gets so much hate for his storytelling lecture style and his grading scale, but he is one of the best professor's at the University of Rochester. He is caring, knowledgeable, and always willing to help his students. Please get to know him! I took 108 and 207 with Rizzo and I have learned so much. Don't listen to others, take the class!
tough grader!

comment: Very stressful.

Probably the most fun class I have taken so far. It is hard, but you really learn a lot and lectures are super entertaining. It is a lot of work but 100% worth taking the class over the other 108 option.

Love the guy. He's definitely better and more interesting when it comes to elective courses (sports econ, environmental) so take those with him for sure. I always learn something new and worthwhile during class.

Ignore all positive reviews, they are written by sycophants. Lots of homework(4-6 hours a week) and tests with unclear questions that are also a large percentage of your grade. I'm taking 207 with him and have noticed a large drop in quality recently(talks about taking his own life constantly!). Can't recommend him to anyone majoring in economics.

Guys. Do not look at the rate, it is not accurate. I just calculated the weighted average. The result is 789/216 which is approximately 3.65. NOT 5.0. Again, !!!!! HIS SCORE IS 3.65 NOT 5.0!!!! Do NOT take this class with him!!!

comment: Theory of econ rather than an intro econ course. More about the principle of econ, applying it to different scenarios and learning how to think like an economist. 2 hws a week and can be difficult if you don't understand how Rizzo works. If you like straightforward classes with textbook-based information and tests then this is not the class for you

He is a great professor, very engaging and never a dull moment. But, tests were confusing and graded weirdly imo. Homework heavy, around 5-7 hours of homework every week. But I really learned a lot from his class and would like to take another course with him. He is genuinely one of the only professors that I learned life long lessons from.

Could not tell the difference between his rambles vs actual course material, he lectures in a very strange way and is all over the place. Exam questions are hard to nail, reviewing the answers afterward was very frustrating bc you would never have guessed that's what he wanted out of it.
N/A

Lectures are entertaining, he mostly tells stories. But the stories are confusing and it is hard to extract the intended meaning from them. Lots of homework, usually unrelated to lecture material. His tests are totally bizarre. Grading feels unfair. Rizzo is a great guy, but I can't recommend his class.

It is not like AP econ. You will see supply & demand curves 2.5 weeks before the final. This class is a grade wrecker. He grades in a very specific manner and makes it extremely hard to get anything above an A-, yet complains that many students are dropping his classes due to the harsh grading scale. Take 108 with another professor.

This is a very bizarre class. He is concerned with teaching how to "think economically" but what you get is very vague and bizarre examples and anecdotes that try to make a point, but they are difficult to understand and don't work well. In the end, I didn't end up knowing much about priniciples of economics or "economical thinking".

Rizzo is a great lecturer and a really nice guy, but if you want to get an A I wouldn't take him. The ideas of the class are vague sometimes and TA grading can be extremely frustrating. There is also a lot of homework. Basically if you are fine with not getting an A and doing a lot of homework, econ 108 with Rizzo is very enjoyable.

biggest yapper i have ever met. obviously misses his ex wife based on the number of times he brought her up. just a dude who loves yappin and yappin. All the info you need is in the slides during his lectures but he forgets to go through them because he gets carried away talking about his ex wife.

comment: He does not teach economics, he teaches what I like to call "Rizzonomics" which is basically his views of the world. He's clearly hardcore libertarian. Exam questions make no sense, he just wants you to write down his views for the answers. 2 writing papers a week for HW! He talks a lot about his divorce. He's Unhinged. I'm taking 207 with Ashby

You either love him or hate him. Rizzo's such a unique character, his lectures are something you will never get to experience anywhere else. Be sure to attend his lectures, everything on the test will be from lecture or somewhat related to them (there are recordings but they're from fall 2022). No slides, just take good detailed notes. great prof.

Amazing professor and wonderful lectures! I learned so much from his class and would seriously recommend. Go to study groups and office hours. Attendance is not mandatory, but you will not do well if you do not go to lectures. Try and start weekly assignments early in the week as they are long and tedious. Tests are open note and internet.

Truly one of the best professors I have had. The lectures are engaging and completely changed how I see the world. Class is lots of work (I would often be writing 15-20 pages weekly), but if you put in the effort, I promise that you will leave a better student and person. Strongly believe that everyone should take at least one class with Rizzo.

Very tough class, but so rewarding if done right aka put in the work! The way he asks questions is VERY similar to a certain liberal arts interdisciplinary competition which is particularly popular among intl HS students (not going to specify, but iykyk). Its helpful to have prior econ knowledge. In exams, think like him. Go to study groups!!

Lectures hardly cover economics and are mainly him venting his opinions. Same thing with his exams. The only good thing about this course is that the homework is actually doable assignments and can save your grade from his terrible exams.

Rizzo's class has way too much homework for no reason. Also, he grades extremely precisely. If you get an 89.999999%, it doesn't get rounded up. It would be a B+. His exams aren't economic based it's basically just what he thinks. The tests are also graded on "vibes" -an actual quote from a TA.

Professor Rizzo is by far the most approachable professor on campus and has the most passion for economics I have ever seen by someone else. His exams are difficult, but possible to do well on as long as you go to lecture and make use of office hours/TAs. Overall, I'd be excited to take another course by him and hope more people do.

Everyone loves or hates him. I personally hate him. He does not teach, people will literally show up to class because its entertaining. I think he talks about him divorce more than he does economics. The tests also make no sense don't take this class.
Take Ashby's class if you care about your GPA, not GPB, GPC, or even GPD.
Take Ashby's Class if you care about your GPA
I wish I could understand half of what he spews.
GPA Destroyer

As a freshman, I found his class to be very intimidating and dropped out of it immediately. Professor Rizzo is very passionate about economics and is a funny and eccentric lecturer, but the downside is that his class is very disorganized, which is terrifying when there are so many readings and assignments. His ECON 108 could destroy your GPA.

Go to class if you want to do well in Rizzo's class. You either love him or you hate him, but he grades very fair and most of the tests are open book and you are allowed to use the internet. Personally, I love rizzo and the style of the lectures but it's not for everyone.
Will give extra credit and drops lowest exam grade as well as adds 8 points to overall exam grades. Must go to lectures to understand material. Open note tests

Most entertaining yet informative professor I've ever had. Course consisted of weekly assignments that took 1-3 hours each (best to work as a group) and 4 exams that made 60% of your grade. You HAVE to show up to lectures otherwise the class won't be easy at all. He dropped an exam plus 8% grade boost so it's pretty easy to get an A.

His lectures got me interested in Econ. He puts all the concepts behind a story so it may be hard to decipher at first but once I did, I felt like I had a stronger understanding than if he just delivered dry lectures. Super funny, and watch out for the money he gives away on the first lecture...

It is a harder class as it's very non-traditional, but I think it's best to try and pick out the economics behind his stories. He talks super fast so it's kinda hard so just literally write down everything, then after class look it over.

The Econ concepts in this class are easy, but he like to teach them in a tough way. Tons of information in the lecture and the workload for homework is heavy, and he seldom give study guide for exams. The lecture is fun though.
Really fun class
Money wasted if you don't take his class

there is tons of hw, research assignments every week. if you want to pass go to lectures. alot of extra credit opportunities. he teaches through stories which can be nice but i don't learn that way. it is hard to tell if he is telling a story or if hes teaching econ. exam questions are weird too. ta grade everything. workshops are not mandatory
Be ready to listen in lectures and be entertained while understanding the principals of Econ 108.

Amazing lecturer, but tons of work. Lectures are extremely entertaining and easy to follow. They made me excited for economics. Weekly homework can take up 5-8 hours, writing intensive (1-2k words), and disconnected from class material imo. Can't really study for the exams, final was open book, mostly test on your thinking skills.

Professor Rizzo is a nice guy and his lectures are entertaining however I would strongly recommend against taking this class with him. There is a ton of HW each week and the grading is arbitrary. Also, nothing you learn in this class will help you with future econ classes. Take another professor for 108.

If you want direct, clear lectures, don't take Rizzo. Classes are more of an econ approach to philosophy. I learned a lot, but it's not your traditional econ class.
