comment: Professor Novy-Marx is wonderful. She really cares about her students and tries to involve everyone in group discussions. Make sure to come to class ready to participate. Tests are what you would expect, she does not try to trick you. Strongly recommend taking a class with her!!

You need to know what the reading talks about since a lot of the class is group discussion. She basically tells you what is on the midterm and final so it's not hard to study for. Most of your grade is from your final group projects and she's very lenient with grading. She really cares about her students and wants them to all succeed! Love her <3
Skip is the bomb. Nobody can understand how spellbinding, hilarious, and soul-deep his classes are without being in them. TAKE HIS CLASS.

You think you know all about theater until you meet this man. This is perhaps one of the best classes I've ever taken, and I'm really sad that this is the only course he teaches. He makes it fun and enjoyable, but you really learn a lot. But get what you want out of this class, don't just sit there and expect to be lectured all day.
Amazing professor with very clear notes. She prepares you well with her lectures and past exams. A good amount of memorizing but nothing super difficult.

Hands down the best prof I've had at this University-- cares about students, remains engaging through the semester, and hosts helpful office hours. 3rd and 4th exams are tough and graded harshly, but success is ACTUALLY possible... this time (sorry). Don't expect it to be a breeze just because she's nice-- biochem is challenging but rewarding.

Funny and caring person and overall a pretty good lecturer. Last two weeks of lectures are A LOT of content and could benefit from more in-class review. Wish she put less emphasis on memorizing names and minute details, but a lot of that is just the nature of biochem I guess. The content is hard but there's lots of other ways to bring your grade up
She has an attitude and every time students asked her for help she would blame them for her own shortcomings as a professor. Another superiority complex. An insult to the institute.

very kind and wonderful professor I could tell she really cared about her students and their success and she is a great and engaging lecturer her class is almost entirely exam based for grades so very little homework the exams are not to bad if you study and prepare ahead of time, but are often graded harshly with very detail answers expected

Loved her class. She truly cares and listens to students. If you struggle, tell her and she will help you find solutions. Lectures are dense because it is biology, but she explains clearly and wants you to succeed. Stay on top of notes, and you will do great.

Very chill person and wants everyone to succeed. Biochem is just a really hard class, and metabolism is 100% memorization based, so you can't fault her for that. Plenty of ways to pick up a grade in addition to exams, and she is very open during office hours. Curves to the average.

Stein is a kind soul, a good person who wants you to succeed. However, exams were graded incredibly harshly; they take off so many points for not mentioning super specific details even if your answer conveys a solid understanding of the content. If you did not specifically mention certain key words/phrases, you will get little credit.

Dr. Stein was OK as a lecturer and seems chill personality-wise, but I wouldn't recommend this class. You could know the important details and gist of the concepts but constantly get docked off on exams for not having some trivial factoids you wouldn't even think of no matter how hard you studied - she doesn't always include them in lecture slides!

Would recommend taking her class if you can, probably the best prof in the bio department. Grading can be harsh but most of the time if you submit a *reasonable* regrade she'll give points back. Plenty of points to get an A (4 exams, 3 PSets, 1 Project, points for recitation). Curves the class to wherever the average is. Very engaging lectures.

You could know everything about metabolism and more and still not do well in this class. Gotten unnecessary points off everywhere for not hitting key words that couldn't have been more obviously implied from what i wrote. Explained it perfectly but didn't explicitly state “x” is obviously a protein? -2 points
Harsh grader. Unless you can remember every minute detail, do not expect partial credit.
Did god's work to curve the class.
very difficult but FAIR exams

Dr. Stein is a good prof and really cares about her students. She is fair on exams even though content is difficult. I would start memorizing metabolism ASAP. Grading is fair and there is credit for recitations, projects, and exams. Sometimes she was unclear about exam content, but overall she is a good professor.

This was a great class, and Dr. Stein explains things great, but do NOT do what I did and get behind for the final exam on metabolism!!! I do not love that she saved so much content for the last exam, as this exam brought me down to a B+.

Amazing lecturer, so funny, makes class fun. This class has a lot of tedious content but she makes it learnable. 2 exams + 1 exam (not cumulative) during finals week - last exam has a lot of info to memorize. Recitations are helpful + boost your grade. Mostly depends on your midterm grades tho. Possible to curve exams/class, 1 EC opportunity.

Prof Stein is one of the best profs I had in the U of R. Despite biochem being new to her, she was so good in explaining concepts despite having Dr. Fu's slides. Her office hours one on one were pretty good. She's funny and gives good explanations. If you keep up with the material and problem sets, you will be fine. Labs are long tho.

I really enjoyed learning the material Stein teaches and I think she's a very knowledgeable person. I just don't think the exams are well written, and it's hard to earn partial credit points. It sucks that she doesn't give any practice exams, and the third exam was information overload nearly impossible to memorize it all.

In office hours she is funny, cool, fun to listen to, and just a nice down to earth person. Even though I absolutely love her as a person, as a professor she just isn't good. Across Genetics and Biochem the lectures usually felt disorgnaized in the way information was presented. She is a tough grader and not very understanding despite her niceness.
I loved Dr. Stein! Super accessible outside class and was a great lecturer. She made genetics fun!

Dr. Stein is a very reasonable professor. The content itself is difficult, but she is very approachable in office hours. The practice exam and practice questions she gives are very good at testing your understanding of the material. The same goes for the homework and recitation content. The course is curved, so it is a difficult but doable class.

Very difficult class but Professor Stein is a great professor. She is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the subject which makes her class interesting. She is also very kind and willing to help students understand difficult material. If you have the option to take one of her classes, highly recommend doing so.

198 is very dense and she moves too quickly during lecture. It's difficult, but doable. Memorize the slides, go to workshop, know that it is not a point system and partial credit is skimpy. Overall, Stein is a great, caring professor and an even better role model, especially for all the women entering stem. Professors like her are hard to come by.

She goes into depth on all topics and expects a lot of details on exams and doesn't give partial credit easily. Her lectures are easy to follow and she offers good explanations although she does move quickly. She is very approachable during office hours but is hard to reach via email.

Professor Stein is one of my favorite professors so far. Her lectures are easy to follow and she has good slides. You definitely have to put in the work for an A (use the lecture outline questions on the first slide), but she makes it doable.

Dr. Stein is very caring about her students. Her lectures are dense, but she makes herself accessible and breaks down content more if you ask. There is a lot of hard material, but if you go to lecture and understand key concepts you can pull through. The big group paper at the end of the semester is also really helpful for your grade.

The key to doing well in her class is to memorize the slides. If you can remember everything you'll get an A. Class isn't a point system so if you don't realize that early it's hard to reach an A after messing up an exam.

There is a lot of material to know, so it's important to connect the concepts. Dr. Stein is super accessible outside of class for questions. She explains concepts clearly and makes genetics very interesting!

Professor stein thoroughly explains topics and homework is helpful to understand. She gives learning objectives and practice problems that are helpful. This class is a lot of information but she is lenient and willing to help. I would recommend her even though this is a tough class. If you work hard outside of class and come to lectures it is easy

Stein is awesome. She's exceptionally knowledgeable about the material and judges nobody for any questions, and is willing to help not just with course material but study habits and other topics as well. Explanations can be confusing but again, she's willing to clarify anything. Very transparent with grading and expectations.

Professor Stein seems like a good person but she should stick to 50 minute lectures. She sped through way too much material every lecture and expects you to know minor details in her ppt slides. Study the slides hard, go to recitation and get outside help if needed. Exams are difficult but manageable with the curve.
Great teacher, passionate about the class and the content she teaches. Exams are very fair if you study and do the practice exams. Definitely go to recitation if you want to do well!

Dr. Stein is horrible at explaining difficult topics. She speeds through challenging units in lecture and expects you to know intricate details for exams. If you are not specific enough during exams expect to lose nearly all points on questions. Dr. Stein should also never teach an 75 minute lecture because the lectures are often dry and boring.
Dr. Stein is great. She's an engaging lecturer and very respectful towards students. Tests are easy, and she's funny. Regularly talks about the genetics of her cats.

I had Dr. Stein for this past summer term, and she was amazing! Lectures were pretty info-dense, but she explained concepts extremely well. She wants her students to succeed and enjoys students actively engaging with the material. Grades were mostly based on exams and a paper. I highly recommend taking a class with Dr. Stein!!

I really liked Dr. Stein. Her lectures were info-dense but they clearly outline what she wants you to know on exams. Assigned hw that wasn't thaaaat helpful, so focus on her lectures when studying. Her exams were tough but she made them open-note and gave us 2x time than normal. She does make you work for an A, but it's definitely doable.
tags: ['Accessible outside class', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Test heavy']

comment: Always helpful at office hours

The material for this class can be hard sometimes, but Stein is a great lecturer who really cares about teaching. Plus there are many other resources to help understand the material outside of class such as workshops, TAs, office hours, discussion boards, and the textbook. If you put in the time, this class is rewarding and not that difficult.

Dr. Stein's lectures (virtual now) are very info-heavy, but the exams are open note/-book. She has office hours twice a week with thought-provoking conversation (and occasional visits from her cat, Monkey!), and she patiently reexplains hard concepts. She cares about us and once moved a test because it coincided with orgo. Kind & easy to talk to!

Love Dr. Stein! If you study the lectures you'll be fine - textbook could be helpful to understand concepts she explains but typically her material is already overlapping with the book and you don't need to actually get it (even if you are a book person). Material may be tough, but Stein is incredible!

I 100% do not recommend anyone to take this course. She gave us 7 difficult 3-hour midterms every other week. HW was so long and tedious. Promised short videos but posted 5-8 20-30 min videos in each chapter for each 7 modules. Too much content and not enough time to review. Don't make this mistake of taking this class now during a pandemic!!!!!!!!

Dr. Stein changed the format of her class for COVID and I much prefer this new way. Instead of 3 closed note, memorization heavy midterms, it is 7 open book conceptual module tests. She is an amazing lecturer who cares about the material and her students, and is flexible when she needs to be while still delivering the required amount of content.

Dr. Stein is a decent lecturer; I learned a lot from her class. However, as much as she makes it seem like she's doing us a favor amidst the pandemic, she's not. She gave us 7 exams, each being 3 hours long. The class was split into online modules, where the lecture videos add up to more than in-person lectures. The exams were also graded harshly.

AVOID! This class was the worst class I've ever taken in my academic life. We took 7 3-hour exams every other week + she teaches way too much content in 3 1/2 months! Awful exams! I am exhausted and the hw is longer than the exams! If you leave out a slight word that she was looking for in the exam, you get points off! BEWARE. It is not worth it!!

Where do I even begin. Taking BIOL198 this semester was the worst decision I've made of my entire college career. This semester, amongst a global pandemic, Dr. Stein felt the need to give 7 full-length midterms every other week. Although I believe she is a great lecturer and I understood her content well, the structure of the class was not it.

Rather than in person 3 exam schedule, she gives 7 exams harder and longer than the typical exam. No practice exam, even if you follow what she teaches, you still get points taken off. She looks for extremely specific things in exam that no one would never expect. You dont get answer key for the workshop. She doesnt show up to her Office Hours.
Really fun class. A LOT of memorization, but the teacher is great and the tests are fair with a curve.

One of my favorite professors at UR thus far. She made genetics easy to understand and very enjoyable. Not to mention she has a wonderful personality and her passion for genetics shines through. Wish I had attended more of her office hours.

Dr. Stein gives really fun lectures for BIO 198: Genetics. Clear-minded, intellectual, humorous and explains everything clearly. Homework and exams are neither too dense nor too hard. Accessible outside classroom and very patient at answering questions.

I took genetics with Dr. Stein over the summer term. It was online due to COVID, but nevertheless I learned a ton and would take it with her again. She's fantastic at what she does, is super passionate, and gives great feedback on tests. There were 6 tests and lots of homeworks. The textbook didn't help much, just pay close attention to the lecture
Very helpful professor.
Heidi is so nice and a very sweet person. She is extremely helpful..made my CAS class seem so simple...and passed with a good grade :)
No Comments

In terms of grading, there is no clear rubric, so you have little idea how your work differs from an “A.” Evaluation feels subjective. In discussions, he often interprets comments in exaggerated ways and uses extreme examples, making meaningful conversation difficult.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Just don't take the meaning of life with him. He will literally try to tell you the sky isn't blue if you say it is. His feedback is ok, but if you don't have the same view as him, just be quiet and sit through the lecture. Easy class, ROUGH prof.

I mean he wasnt a bad professor but he definitely played devil's advocate for a lot of the conversations discussed in class. It felt as if he wanted to argue but not in an easygoing manner. Idk i just felt that it was weird how he disapproves all the students' povs. There is a lot of reading and writing required so be weary of the deadlines.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']

comment: I took his "What is Human Nature?" writing class, and Professor Stauffer is insightful. He gives you great feedback after every submitted paper and is easily accessible outside of class. There are readings and summaries, but it's not a bad class as long as you show up and do what you're supposed to. Not the hardest class, but effort is needed.

Dr. Stauffer gives very good and detailed feedback on all the papers you submit, which helps a lot. Attendance is part of the grade, but as long as you attend, it is relatively easy. There were readings and summaries due before almost every class, which could be long sometimes, but otherwise, the class was relatively easy and helpful.
He was a great prof. He gave helpful feedback, and the lectures gave a good perspective on what is expected of job application materials. Highly recommend taking this class with him.

Definitely one of my favorite professors. Very kind and respectful. Attendance is important, so if you show up, you're all set. Always willing to meet or discuss during the week if you need help on anything. Overall, I'd highly recommend his class if you want to have fun in-class discussions and want a great professor.

He's really nice, I liked him a lot. The only thing is the 8-10 page paper at the end of the semester is 40% of your grade. He's a pretty light grader though. He also cares a lot about attendance, so make sure to go to every class. He doesn't ask much, there are just short readings for each class.

Stauffer is an incredible instructor! Always accessible outside of class, they offer valuable guidance and are highly knowledgeable in their field and writing. Their passion for the subject makes learning engaging and enjoyable. I would take their class again!"
Perfectly good teacher for the WRTG105 class. Teaches you what you need to know, and doesn't make it painful. Has students email assignments instead of using blackboard, which I found annoying.
While not the hardest teacher, he definitely makes sure you learn in his class. Definitely take his class for the WRTG105 credit if you get a chance.

Took his "The Meaning of Life" course and the readings & discussions were very insightful and makes you think. Super nice guy and always is able to add on to your comments in a discussion. Very clear grading, as long as you follow the criteria you'll get a good grade. Great prof for 105!
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: he was very nice, and quiet. but, i feel like the class is hard to do well in if you are not the best writer. I feel like it is hard to get the grade you want. I think he has clear expectations on what to do for your papers. I tried REALLY hard on my final paper and went to so many resources for help and still didn't get the grade i wanted.

This class was definitely not an ez A. However I do believe that this class is a great seminar style class with weekly discussion and interesting readings instead of a dry writing class like other classes. I think Dr Stauffer did a great job by making the topics interesting and always available to help his students with their writings.

I always enjoyed Stauffers' class. Interesting (and long) readings that led to great discussions, always asked us interesting questions and created a good atmosphere in the classroom. Amazing at giving feedback on essays, and a very fair grader. Answered emails very quickly and I felt that he cared about all his students. Great teacher for 105!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Even though I typically don't like writing, I really enjoyed Dr. Stauffer's class. The one I took was about life in the digital age so the content actually was pretty interesting and the essays weren't bad at all. Show up, participate, and put a decent amount of effort into the essays and you'll do well.

Definitely take him!! I took his life in a digital age this semester, which is always very intriguing. He really like to bring up critical thinking question and statistics to drive the class discussion further. For his essay, make sure your organization and logics flow well then you should be fine.

He is THE BEST writing teacher. I took his human nature class. We basically had to show up to class, participate in the discussions and do the papers by the deadline. Easy to satisy requirements for A and the teacher is very kind, accesible and gives very good feedback. Take him!

I LOVE his class. The grading is extremely clear and as long as you follow the instructions, you will get good grades. We had lots of terrific discussions in class. I put effort and I also like the content of this class. The final paper (8-10 pages) is the college policy, but he helps me a lot through developing ideas on this final papers. THE BEST
I love his class. We had lots of interesting discussions in class, and the professor gives plenty of good feedbacks on your writing. I hope that he can be my upper level writing professor!!!!
Very friendly and accessible out of class. Interesting topic. Participation is highly recommended. Will recommend his course to peers.
The best professor ever!
Great professor, I had him for WRT 105 Posthumanism. I saw that he's teaching one of my other writing course, so I'm definitely taking it with him again!
A really good professor talking about American's society and politics.
Great professor!
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: Making of Trump's America is pretty much your typical WRT 105 class. It is not just a Trump roast-fest, more of an examination of the state of modern america. It won't blow your mind, but Stauffer is fair, and the assigned readings are quite easy. He does not put grades online quickly, (or at all so far), but I can't imagine getting less than an A-

BLST156/ENGL116: Intro to African American Lit is an inspiring course that enables students to explore myriad literary works dealing with a wide range of topics from the 20th century to the present- from DuBois's book to Octavia Butler's short story. Professor Omelsky is also caring, kind, and supportive! Regardless of your major, you'll enjoy it!!

Took Black Speculative Fiction in Fall 2024- learnt a lot from it. The course examines a wide variety of literature, short stories, and films...etc produced by Black authors worldwide. The material is very interesting. Professor Omelsky is one of the best instructors I've had. Highly recommended!!

Amazing professor. Would 100% recommend this class to anyone looking to explore great authors from all over the world. Truly changed the way I view literature, his class was the highlight of my freshman year!!

He's such an amazing professor who actually genuinely cares about his students and what they're going through. He assigns really good reading material - I also took his Black Speculative Fiction course, and to this day, it's one of my favorite courses. His class discussions are so insightful and engaging; he really tries to pull his students in
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Professor Omelsky does a great job facilitating class discussion and helping students become passionate about the material. The workload for my class was fairly light, and he was always very willing to help students outside of class.

Good guy and easy to get a good grade, but not a good professor. Way too reliant on TA's and recitations (sucks if you have a bad TA), teaches overtime, hasn't changed the course in 20 years, projects are incredibly redundant, condescending when you ask a question, unorganized, poor use of lecture time (whole class used to hand draw excel sheet).
Prof. Perucchio is absolutely amazing to me his class was a really fun intro to engineering. The projects were interesting and his lectures were not at all ambiguous.
Great guy but often goes over time for lectures and content is very repetitive

Professor Perucchio is passionate about his 'Engineering of Bridges' class but was harsh when grading the group presentations for my final project. His TAs were very helpful though for the homeworks!!!
Perruchio is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable; however, he often doesn't express exactly what he wanted in projects and his “time management” is poor.
Teaches things very clearly and makes it easy to understand. He will 100% go 5-10 minutes over time though after lectures.
Do not schedule something right after class, he will always go over the time allotted for lecture.
He is very passionate about what he teaches and the energy is contagious. Great professor. "Very fundamental!"

Perucchio was one of the most passionate professors I had as a first-year. He was relatively understanding and wanted his students to succeed. GO TO RECITATION. I learned most of the class through recitation and found that lectures were easier to follow after going to recitation. Be prepared to do important group projects. Utilize office hours.

Very good professor that makes the material fun and interesting to learn. Material is hard to understand at first because it is new and unique but can be learned quickly will little practice. Recitation are very helpful if payed attention to and the homework are only long because the material has to be taught first. The projects are kinda hard.

He teaches forces, vectors, and equilibrium stuff from the ground up. If you've taken physics before, the class should be pretty easy. Homework is relatively light for most of the semester, but the last two weeks are a GRIND. We had a homework, a project, a presentation, and an exam all within five days.

A bit overrated. His homework dates are very generous. Lectures can be insightful but often boring, there was once a lecture when he spent time drawing out an entire excel table. Practice exams are old and didn't feel representative of what the actual exams were. Recitations and TAs are the MVPs of this course. And he's a good and patient person.

He seems nice, but the grading scale is not forgiving at all and he is very harsh and blunt if you dont know something. Most of the time he won't criticize you for not knowing things directly, but he will ask you many question that you cannot answer to make yourself look stupid. He gives no extra credit either and is very harsh when you appeal him

Amazing professor. You can tell that Perucchio has a passion for mechanical engineering. The lectures were boring, but applying the concepts from his class was fun in workshops, homework, and group projects. Beware that Perucchio gets scary during the third project.
Interesting guy. Lecture can be a bit boring but overall good.

Great intro to ME. Lectures can feel slow, but only because he explains everything in great detail and will take as long as it takes to answer a question fully. He's a great personality and really cares about each student. Workload is totally manageable and there are plenty of resources to get help if you need. Don't buy the textbook (ME104).

Professor Perucchio is a great lecturer and fully applies the lectures. As Chair of the ME Department, Perucchio's class is a great base for entering the ME track. His class is a decent and fair amount of work but the projects and group work is fun and knowledgeable. A must take for ME.

Professor Perucchio is a very caring teacher and is willing to answer questions if you have them. He is very passionate about engineering as a whole and architecture as well (including bridges). His lectures are a bit dry, but going to office hours with the TA is very enlightening. As long as you know the process, the class won't be too difficult.

I don't have the space to say everything I want to, but, for context, I received a 4 on the AP Physics C: Mechanics exam. Now, listen carefully: for the love of god, don't take this class if you have had *any* physics experience; you will be punished for it. The grading method for this class is beyond asinine and I can't understate my hatred for it

Very passionate about his work and what he is teaching in class. Kind yet straightforward when talking one-on-one. While he is fairly good at explaining concepts, his greatest strength is attracting and finding the most competent, knowledgeable, and helpful TAs who show you how solve problems on homework and exams. Taking ME104 helps with ME120.
Great introduction to mechanical engineering

Dude's great. Be prepared to get blindsided by the amount of work the first project is, but from there it's an easy A as long as you do your work and go to lectures. The lectures are sometimes confusing because of their fast pace but overall Perucchio is engaging and helpful and I would recommend taking his class if possible.

"Are you with me on this guys?" - Professor Perucchio can give in depth lectures in engineering, and paying attention is a must, because if you are not "with him," you lose track of variables and ideas. Not so good at explaining when asked a question. You may have more questions afterward. All in all, he is a solid choice, TAs are helpful, etc.
DONT BUY THE TEXTBOOK. Amazing professor, very very passionate. Make sure you find a group of four students asap because you dont want to be stuck working with someone who doesnt care.

Professor Perucchio was extremely helpful as he would explain any question you had with as much effort. He does sometimes get lost in what he does as he is very passionate about it but he definitely teaches all the material that is needed.

Great professor. Lectures can sometimes get boring because he drones on and on, but I still found the material very interesting. His TA's are fantastic and are great resources for help. He's more than willing to explain concepts and help if you go to his office hours. One of the most passionate professors. Very tough on the final project

Do some preview before you go to class. Answer his questions and go to lectures. Although his homework and projects will cover almost everything you need for the exam, his lecture will give you some very very interesting and helpful info. Enjoy.

Be warned: although this man looks like an adorable old Italian man with a strange obsession with strange hats, this cat's got claws. The homework was really hard, but he picks good TA's for the class, so you can usually just do it during office hours with their help. Also, he gets scary during the final project.
Awesome professor, great class. Really sparked my interest in Mech E.

He's a really great guy, with a deep passion for the subject. Really comes through for each student (more so than any other I had this term); as an example, he attended a play in which one of his students was acting. Office hours are very helpful. Don't be afraid to go to them. Highly suggest anything he teaches.

He's really passionate about whate he teaches and really wants every1 to do well. he tries to make ppl pass with higher grades when possible.  unfortunately for him, he's teaching a boring subject. the lectures tend to put atleast 5 students to sleep.

Perucchio and his stereotypical Italian accent are great.  He was always excited about the class and did his best to make it interesting.  Unfortunately, many times his lectures would put half the class to sleep.  Other than the occasional boring lecture, Perucchio did a good job teaching the basics of ME.

Perucchio is a complex professor. For several lectures, he is interesting and the the point. For several others, he repeats the same information over and over and over. This accent is a HUGE plus, and his trademark slogans ('Is everyone witth me on this?') almost put you to sleep. Good TA selection and the course is a blast...you'll remember him!

Prof. Perucchio is very passionate about the topics in class.  He knows what he's talking about and makes sure to ask if everyone is clear on new concepts.  There are 4 group projects throughout the semester that can be a little hectic to complete, but none of the homework or tests are unfair.  You get to play with "KiNex!"
Great teacher! Spends extra time to make sure everyone understands and presents the material in a clear, concise manner. 104Q was my favorite course at college so far, mostly because he taught it.
No Comments
such a cool guy. so interested in what he does and making you understand it. all around great teacher.

Cares immensely about student wellbeing and understanding of material. Fair and thoughtful. Interesting guy, too (and his Italian accent will keep you at least mildly interested no matter the lecture topic). I've TAed for him, so I speak from experience.
condescending

Very nice person, cares for students, and gives LOTS of extra credit. I had over a 101% in the class before the final project. Final project is difficult, focus on something simple, but do it according to the process. He did seem very overwhelmed though and it hurt the class, since he was disorganized, probably cause he didn't have much time.
He defines awesomeness.

I loved the way Prof. Hoque was able to relate the materials to real-world scenarios. The guests lectures were very helpful to make the connection. Cranking up the prerequisite so that students with solid programming and research focus could only take this class will help. Otherwise, you are bound to see a bi-modal distribution in the feedback.
Prof. Hoque is a great teacher and genuinely cares for the students. Anyone who gives you him a bad review clearly did not enjoy being put on the spot in the class or was just hoping for an easy A.

HCI class has historically been a very easy class. A lot of students including myself took this class with that pretense and it backfired. On the bright side, I appreciated the way Prof. Hoque always responded to the anonymous feedback. He likes to  randomly check on people in the class; so you gotta always pay attention.

He is probably the worst professor I've ever had from the CS department. He is extremely condescending and has ridiculous expectations. He basically never taught anything in lecture-just talked about his research or brought in guests. The projects also took over my life, and I wasn't even rewarded for it.

Hoque was a new professor and he taught this course for the first time here. He pushed the TAs and the students to work really hard. He graded based on his personal preference on your projects, no matter how hard you worked. Plus, you need to warm up yourself with the skills to be used in the projects. Watch out!

The course was interesting at the first glance, but I quickly got bored after two weeks. Prof. Hoque taught superficial stuff in class, and simply by asking students a question and asking another to repeat what the previous one's answer was insufficient to draw the audience attention back from facebook, youtube, and games to the class.

This class ended up being lot more work than what I had anticipated. But the final project was a lot of fun, and Prof. Hoque is an entertaining lecturer. I personally loved the guest lecturers as our final project was inspired by one of them. If you know how to code/build, you would love this class.

I took his HCI class which is the first he's taught. Prof. Hoque is a great professor and will be great to have in the university. He really cares about his students
Prof. Hoque is new at the UofR, and very obsessed about his new class. I think he put a lot of effort in teaching HCI, CSC212.
The class was very unorganized and the processor is extremely condescending. I do not recommend taking courses with this Prof Hoque.
Great teacher, really personable and fun!

Great Teacher, hard workshop problems. He has a good TA as well
Really good teacher. Very clear, students in his class get very high scores.

Wei is hard to understand... I almost walked out the first day due to his accent.  However, he is the best math professor ever!  He will answer questions over and over again until it all makes sense, and he responds to emails very quickly (roughly 10 minutes, at most hours).  I learned more with him than with the "better" ones.
smart guy, helpful, easy grading

Almost impossible to understand in class. Very unorganized as well. Probably the worst math teacher I've ever had. It'd be a lot better use of time to read the text book to go to class. Also the quest workshop has nothing to do with class and is pointless and the TAs are less than useful.

He's a really nice guy, but it's a little confusing when he teaches. If you ask him for help, he's very nice and will show you how to do the problem. Great one on one. I'd recommend having taken calculus before, though.
I like his lectures. As he warned it, MATH 285 is a tough course and putting 9 hours after class each week is not an exaggeration.
He's the best professor in the math department, take his class
Best professor in the math courses I've taken
Geba is very respected and you could do a lot worse, but to be honest I didn't think he was a great lecturer. He's  a nice guy though.

Prof Geba really made me love math again. Clear and thorough lectures, he did one example from the practice problems and there was one worked out in the book for every topic. He is a super harsh grader, no curve, and is very rude when you go to him because he graded someone differently that you  when you had the same thing. Overall rude when one-on-one and his notes are terrible.
His lecture is clear and understandable. You can learn a lot from his lecture.
For those who love mathematics, especially proof-based mathematics, you cannot miss Geba's classes!

Great Professor. Friendly and approachable in office hours. Early content is pretty easy, but get ready to read the book for the second midterm. Tests are tough, but reasonable. Do your work, and you won't have to worry about your grade.

MTH190 is only 1 credit, but Geba's very available in office hours. Problems are very difficult, but he helps a lot. The first time I went to office hours he made sure I knew that his door was always open for any questions/concerns I had about my future math studies. My favorite professor this semester, can't wait to take more of his classes.a
Best teacher I ever had. Got me really interested in the material. Especially helpful in office hours- take advantage of these.
Great professor. Prob the smartest guy I've ever seen. Take his class(tho I dropped because I had to take another class...)!
Great professor. Very funny!

Prof. Geba is awesome! He is so smart that he doesn't need to read or copy any of his notes. And he really teaches you what math really means. He talked a lot about motivations. He is also the funniest person on the planet. Love him!
Geba is awesome. Tests were straightforward for this class IF you knew your stuff. Would have done better if I had taken the time to really understand the concepts.
great professor, really cared about the students and made sure you understood the material
i never actually went to him for help outside of class (even tho i really needed it), because he scared me. and i almost never skipped class, and always had no clue what was going on
Professor Geba is the smartest man I have ever met. I love him.

Hands down the best professor I've ever had. She's taught me everything I know about reading ethnography and how to write well. Incredibly knowledgeable and interesting

I think I learned more about how to write well in this class than I did in my WRTG 105. Overall, I loved this class and had a great time.

Professor Doughty is overall a great professor. I actually feel that I learned a lot over the course of the class, although it was very reading intensive. She talks fast, but her lectures are interesting. She prepares you well for tests and grades pretty easily. Also, she was very flexible and understanding in terms of attendance and due dates.
Amazing professor in every way. Grading criteria is clear, she cares about her students, and provides great reading material and discussion. One of my favorite classes I've taken.

The best professor in the whole university. She taught me how to write and think for myself. She takes the time to scrupulously comment on your papers so you can improve your writing and arguments. The topics covered are tough, but the class discussions mixed with her beloved rants humanizes our detached univ. Highly rec for every major!
Just pure awesomeness. She even helped me with an outside project.
Very amazing professor. Definitely recommend anyone who can to take her courses!
Professor Doughty had amazing lectures. I admire that she tries to fit so much material in a 101 class, which shows that she cares about students actually getting something from the class.
The most passionate professor I've ever had. Knows her subject well. Has changed my college career. Highly recommend!

She is tough, but fair. She expects you to engage with the material, but is understanding of the fact you are a college student. She is really helpful, despite the fact she might ramble a bit. But, her ramblings are always helpful! Even if they sometimes cause you to think more deeply about the issue. She is really great. Be prepared to work hard.

She is very passionate about what she is teaching but does tend to speak very fast. Readings are mixed with some very interesting ones and some you just have to get through. Exams were pretty difficult but if you take good notes and know the structure of the readings then you will should do fine.

Speaks really fast, but you get used to it. She was nice and helpful when you go to office hours or as a question after class. Doesn't lecture often, sit in a circle and had group discussions of the reading. interesting topics, hard exam essay questions, easy weekly journals. MANDATORY attendance-she will notice if you arent there and email you.
She is very nice but she talks really fast and there is often no information provided to you except the readings.
Did not enjoy his lecture style did not feel like it was meant to be accessible language for undergrads and often pretentious. No grades were submitted in Gradescope throughout the semester.

comment: Burges is the best professor I've had at U of R. He is warm and funny in class and most class periods were devoted purely to discussions, which were almost always effective and insightful. He was accessible and helpful outside of class. Midterm and final assignments were hefty, but he gives ample feedback for both. Would give 6 stars if I could.

Professor Burges was born to be a professor. He seems to truly care about what his students have to say. Discussion in his class can be lively and invigorating. On top of that, he is incredibly kind and accommodating. As long as you clearly communicate with him, he will ensure that the class will never be too much for you. He is great at his job.

Professor Burges is a great teacher who really cares about his students. The class is tough, be prepared to put in effort into writing papers but if you're interested in the material, you'll find it really engaging. Be warned - attendance is mandatory and they are strict on it. If you're someone who skips class, this is not for you.

Joel really likes his essays. I ended up with 5 for the rest of the semester which was really rough. He taught a class on television which was a flop because of his constant replanning of the course syllabus. He's a smart guy who can lecture well, but this class was not run well (which he is aware of).
Ridiculous amount of workload for a non-W course. Your grade largely depends on the group project, and he picks your groupmates for you. Allow two absences, takes attendance every class.

comment: Took his class as a first-semester freshman. A three pages paper each week. But you can surely learn things and inspired by his class! One of the best teachers I had at UR

His lectures are very fun but solid. Every lecture was prepared and delivered well. Definitely an inspirational course to learn about all kinds of media and how to analyze them. Very heavy load of homework though. Lots of papers and readings to do. The good thing is that the topics and times are relatively flexible. Take attendance every time.

I love Professor Burges! Took me some time to adjust to his class because there was a lot of papers to write and a semester-long group project but he was very flexible and cared about his students. He took individual concerns seriously and was determined to let everyone learn. He's very intelligent and his lectures are amazing. I'll miss his laugh

comment: It's as if the light of God is reflecting off his bald head. Great teacher, good guy, would definitely recommend. He's so pretty! And smart. The end.
He's absolutely brilliant, and Intro to Media Studies was one of the best classes I've taken so far.

Took me a while to get used to his type of teaching (no technology). He uses his extensive vocab and flaunts his aluma maters quite often however i learned a ton in his class, even though it was the hardest class i've taken at UR thus far.
Took me a while to warm up to him, but he's a brilliant professor. He knows his stuff. Classes can sometimes be boring, but that was more the subject matter than the professor.
Amazing.

Interesting material presented in a fresh and intriguing way. Burges is an incredibly passionate and intelligent professor but teaches at an elevated level. If you're not willing to do the reading and participate, this is not your class. I learned a great deal and felt positively challenged. Highly recommend.

His lectures are so boring that nobody cares or listens. He takes attendance at random times. He asked why there were so many of us in the first lesson, and he added a midterm because of that. The exam was challenging. The slides were very poor, and the assignments were AI-generated and unclear. It's not an easy A anymore. Don't take this course.

Prof. Xu is really knowledgeable and engaged in research. Lectures were inspirational but involved little coding, so be prepared to learn PyTorch on your own. Easy A. comment: A terrible professor with poor character, a bad attitude in class, and no respect for students.

Actually CSC 298:

Abysmal communication. Slides intentionally hide info (you cannot learn / review after class). Lectures are poorly structured and delivered: always derailed by simple student questions that he spends 10min answering at *extreme* length. Project instructions self-contradictory and intentionally incomplete.

He is the professor who spent the least effort in teaching. He's lecture PowerPoint was borrowed from another school. You could feel that he had never prepared his lecture before class. He had 1 hour/per week oh and he didn't reply to the email. His TAs put the minimum effort too, when you asked someone he would let you find the other TA and so on.
Prof. Xu is great!
CV is hard but Prof. Xu can explain everything in a clearer and easier way.

The whole operation is tightly run. The class is such a struggle, but it leaves you with the feeling that you can only blame Xu last. So that's good learnin'. The assignments are where it really all connects. Wouldn't recommend this class for credit if you are just casually interested in the material.
Professor Xu is a very nice guy. His slides and teaching are very clear and you can tell he loves what he does.
I like the paper discussion.

This professor is not very responsible. She usually posts review question & solutions or homework solutions like only 2 days ahead of the midterm day. I am not very sure what other students feel, but for me it's very overwhelmed. Imagine when you looked at some weird review questions and there were only 2 days left.
If you did the homeworks, the midterm will not be any trouble. Im not trying to trick you *Class average is a 50% on the midterm...
Her tests are almost not related to what she taught. Read the textbooks! Dont trust her slides.

Her lecture slides are very vague and given the material is quite dry and difficult to comprehend, it's hard to follow her lecture. Once you're lost in lecture, you ain't finding your way back. Go to TA office hours for help! And read the textbook. It's much more detailed than her slides. Study hard. Not an easy class!
Write out the definition of Competition Equilibrium. That worth 10 points on the midterm

Lu's first time teaching ECO 209. Nice, a little quiet, and approachable in office hours. It's important to go to class lectures,  the recitation when offered by the TA, and to read the textbook. Her class goes really quick. GO TO HER OFFICE HOURS!
The exams were a little bit challenging, but I found them to be reasonable, and it covered essential materials.

Worst Econ class I've taken. No textbook. Doesn't explain things during lecture. Isn't clear about what we need to know or don't need to know for tests. Puts way too much material in each class and assumes from her barebones lectures outlines she puts up online prior that we have a complete understanding.

Professor Brown's Optics 101 course was an exercise in arrogance. He consistently dismissed student questions, openly acted superior, and seemed far more interested in showcasing his ego than teaching optics. Lectures were condescending and unhelpful, making the entire experience miserable. Avoid at all costs.

Overall Thomas Brown's class was an amazing overview of optics, from basic thin lens to holography  The test were very fair and resemble the practice tests very closely. Definitely not impossible to do poorly on but if you know your stuff you'll be fine. Lectures made me a bit sleepy at times, but the professor is still very passionate about optics
lectures can be a bit boring sometimes but prof is very caring and kind
He is such a sweetheart and clearly passionate about what he is teaching. If you pay attention and go to workshops you'll be fine. Take the time to talk to him one on one! He is a great guy

Professor Brown is one of those teachers who cares about his students and ensures everyone's success. While he does care about his students, his lectures are extremely boring. He took lasers, LASERS!, and made them not interesting to me. I learned a lot more from the workshops and practice tests than from the lectures, but that's just personal.

Everybody loves Prof. Brown. It is clear that he is very passionate about what he's teaching. There is graded homework and the tests are relatively easy if you simply listen in class. That being said, because optics is not widely studied and we don't use a textbook, his lectures are the only place you find what you're learning.

TGB is the real deal; he knows his stuff inside and out, but he explains it in ways that anyone can understand. He mixes up the lectures, homework, and tests with jokes and fun stories, and really cares about each individual student. Amazing person and professor!!

He is such an amazing professor, but this is a difficult class. If you do not go to the lectures or watch his videos you will be lost in the class. Also the homework is difficult so don't procrastinate, and go to his office hour for extra help.

very nice guy, very personable. his class is all matlab which is very dry but he does a pretty good job with it. little tip; if nothing else put lots of time into the take home midterm and final, its the easiest way to get a good grade...heinsight

His lectures are enjoyable. He teaches at slow pace, willing to answer and explain questions. He has quite a sense of humour and is friendly and approachable.

He's a great lecturer, but can move through the material pretty quickly at times. He's always willing to help. Since most of the grade is based on tests and they can be challenging, it's best to start studying at least a week ahead.

I don't consider myself to be a math-oriented person, but Prof. Davis' class was super great and helped me understand a lot. He obviously cares about your retention and learning of the material and is very helpful in supporting your understanding. He is also an engaging lecturer which helps.
Great at explaining concepts, and has great lectures with many example problems. If you take 141, definitely consider taking it with him.
Maybe a good practitioner, but does not know how to teach. She blames students for not asking questions during the lecture. Maybe she needs to learn teaching in graduate class 101.
Bad instructor, doesn't care about student's needs.

For being in grad school and teaching, she is doing very well. She was always more than willing to help at her office hours, and she would answer questions at midnight sometimes. Very knowledgeable for being so young. I wish the course had less math.. that was one thing I think the course could do without. Great person!
seems smart in topic, yet has difficulty conveying information to other people

Absolutely terrible professor. She is extremely boring and hard to follow along with. She also is very unclear and doesnt explain things even when asked for clarification. I loved this class. Only class I looked forward to going to. Depressing topic, but really informs you about Refugee and Immigrant situations in America. Class discussion based, sit in a circle, several films shown. She does a great job of engaging and encouraging students to talk in class.
Bickel doesn't seem to care about his students success at all, and is very unwilling to answer questions about material, and is also very unwelcoming and unacommodating.

3. There is a lot of paper reading, and if you don't like ecology or macro biology, it's very painful.

Thought lectures were interesting and engaging, but topics often felt kinda disorganized. He apparently hadn't taught BIO113 in over a decade, and it shows

Really really caring and understanding. However, I felt like I understood the material well and still didn't do great on tests. No extra credit allowed in the class, and it is hard to do well if you slip up on any exam.
This is a lecture heavy class, but they are all recorded and he is available for help outside of class
He's a nice guy I guess but the worst biology professor I've ever had. Boring class too
He is great! Very clear, very helpful. His accent is a little hard to understand at first but in time it gets cute. Overall he's a very kind, well-qualified teacher of calculus.

One of the best professors I have had at the U of R. He is very organized and clear. He also always explains the reasoning behind calculus concepts. I knew several people who were registered for this class with other professors but would attend his lectures instead because he was so good.
He is soooooo cute! Very intelligent!

Lai was very soft spoken but if you sit close to the front, you should be fine. He was very clear with presenting material and covered revalent examples. All test questions were more than fair and he often went over complex webwork problems. Overall a great teacher
Great professor for differential geometry, knows his stuff.

A nice and funny person, a brilliant researcher, but a very bad lecturer. He just goes through slides and bases classes purely on mathematical equations. The lectures are not engaging and difficult to follow. Exams were very easy - he's a lean grader.
brilliant researcher but not suitable for teaching

For Intro Physics II, it was miserable.  Like the last post said, lectures were so pointless less than a 1/4 of the class would attend lectures.  Without the book, students would be doomed.

Rajeev is woeful. Students stopped attending lecture because he goes on tangents unrelated to class material. He has a sense of humor, but beyond that no redeeming qualities that merit him teaching a class of UR's caliber

Rajeev is an advanced theorist, but his courses are well-paced and enlightening. I recommend him very strongly.
The professor seems nice, but the lecture was pretty average and lacked depth.
I love her

Searle is a gem of the University of Rochester anthropology department. As a class discussion heavy class, doing the readings helps you get the most out of this class. comment: I have come away from each of her courses with the feeling that not a second of my time was wasted and that the experience was truly valuable. She is always available outside of class, super helpful, and really fun to talk to! Her classes do require serious participation (and a good amount of reading), but doing so is incredibly rewarding :)

Llerena Searle is a phenomenal professor. She is one of the most intelligent and well spoken individuals I have ever encountered. She genuinely cares for her students. She is a tough grader but in a fair way, if you put effort into the class you will be fine. She is the reason I want to major in Anthropology.
It's really easy for you to get A even you scored 80 percent or less in your exam, not just because of the extra credit but also the fair workloads and student hours, and workshops, etc.

The course moved very quickly because it was an accelerated summer class, she made the material feel much more manageable. You could tell she cared about her students actually understanding the material and doing well, rather than just making the class unnecessarily difficult. She created such a positive and encouraging environment.

Taking Orgo 1 in the summer is a lot, but if prof Tichy is teaching it, TAKE IT!! It is so worth it; she genuinely cares about her students doing well and is super understanding of the summer intensive schedule. Numerous extra credit opportunities and take home assignments that help boost your grade. It is worth it to take Orgo 1 summer with her
She's great, clears up any doubts, understanding and fun! She's very passionate and always looking for constructive feedback. Great experience

I had her for the lab lecture and lab of CHEM 131, you work in random groups, she does not really answer questions when you email her, and makes labs more confusing than they actually are. Also, be prepared to code :(

Dr.Tichy genuinely want her students to do well, and is great at teaching/explaining concepts. Summer orgo is intense, but if you show up consistently, it's doable. Class size is small, which is nice, She gave multiple extra credit opportunities . Her own set of lecture notes template and workbook problems are helpful for exams. RECOMMEND!

FMS 131 was the worst college course I've taken. Big lecture-style class but attendance was mandatory and for some reason they tried to make it discussion-based? I had Haidu for Hist of Photo, and she made the class very interesting. The exams were a little tricky as you had to remember lots of photo ID's and there is alot of emphasis on participation in class but she knows her stuff and her lectures are very interesting :) I recommend taking her classes
Engaging lecturer.  A very fair, but tough grader.  The readings are difficult.  Helpful outside of class.

comment: I loved Professor Michael. He was kind and knowledgeable and respected every student's input. Great Professor! Deeply cares about his students and will go out of his way to gte to know you/help you. Very articulate and enthusiastic. Tough grader but willing to work with you on papers and often gives opportunities for rewrites. One of the best professors at UR!

Nice guy/decent professor. Is very good at leading discussions, but values certain students comments over others. He basically calls on the same four people all class and it can get pretty boring. Easy to approach and very clear on objectives. Pretty tough grader. Overall, pretty good teacher.
Very Nice Guy, but classes are very boring when he lectures. When they are discussions they are better. Fair grader!
Really smart guy, which can help and hurt. He is clear on what he wants, doesn't waste your time with busy work and treats you like adults.
only real problem was he jumped around a lot in class, switching subjects than going back, etc.
Very enthusiastic about the course, lots of reading, but the book choices were decent.  Papers weren't graded too strictly, if you write well you won't have a problem.

I took this course for my public health major. It is an interesting class that shows your a different side of health and gender studies. Super chill professor, very passionate about what he's teaching.
He's great.

(WRTG 273) Wayy too much work for a 2-credit class. Assignments are almost all written and mostly talking about yourself. (easy?-ish) Stay on top of everything or you will fall behind. She is nice and will work with you if you reach out. She obviously knows a lot about English, so if you have questions about that, her feedback is valuable.

Ashley is undoubtedly one of the kindest professors I've had at the UofR. Provided excellent writing feedback and truly cared about our growth as writers and students. Karl seems like a nice guy but he cares more about the writing than the student. If something comes up it'll be hard to get him to be understanding. He's kind of strict, but he does try to make lectures interesting.

Very caring and understanding prof. You can tell he wants you to succeed and gives really good feedback. I went into WRTG 273 thinking my LinkedIn and resume were already fire but he helped make them so much better.

Nice professor willing to answer and help with your questions.

A lot of work

comment: He cares about the students. He understands that students have things that are more important than life design notebook entries. If there's conflicts between actual interview/opportunity and class time he is open to communicating how to work that issue around. He is fine with you turning a LDN late by a couple days, as long as it's not over a week.

Amazing professor. His office hours are also very helpful as he gives a lot of specific instructions to edit the essays. One downside is that he is a REALLY TOUGH GRADER. With that being said, the educational process is the most important, and he is one of the only professors at the university who knows how to teach.
He gives the grade not very well although I did a huge effort on the paper.

This class is not an easy A class, but getting an A is worth the effort. As long as you participate in class discussions about the reading and put decent effort into your papers you will do just fine. Karl gave me great advice when it came to my papers, and I definitely improved thanks to it. I'm glad I chose to take this class, it was fun!

Karl is strict with his class structure and grading criteria, but he is also flexible and understanding of his students. He gives amazing feedback and I feel like my writing really improved because of him. My interest in writing increased after taking this class. You have to work for your A, but it feels deserved and not given to you.

Professor Mohn was fantastic. My writing really improved throughout the semester and he always brought a great attitude to class. His office hours were incredibly useful he is very good at giving one on one advice on how to improve your writing. You do need to put some effort in for his class, but I would recommend taking it.

The best writing professor I ever had. Talk to him if you do not have a clear idea about your paper. He gives amazing advice on your paper. If you work hard and willing to talk and discuss with him during his office hours, you will at least get an A-. If you just hurry in the last hour and imagine getting an A, this class is not for you.

Not much homework which was nice but also this means 75% of your grade comes from the three papers that you will write. However, he gives good feedback and you have peer review days which are very helpful. It was easy to pay attention in his class as everything was interesting. I would definitely take again.

I took this course online. Karl is really an interesting person, and his class is overall joyful. I myself did a lot research for the final paper, but I do like the result. His comments on the drafts are useful, you can learn a lot if you want to.

During my freshman year, I took this class, and I have to say Professor Mohn's lecture is one of the best lectures I ever had. He is a harsh grader, but he is usually easy to reach out to and gives you a lot of useful feedback.

Professor Mohn is definitely one of the hardest graders out there. I would suggest not taking his class for a grade because frankly you wouldn't get an A unless you are really good. However, he is really nice person to talk to and get your writings cross checked from. A really nice person to be around

comment: A good indtructor over all. Not so much reading. Not that tough on greading papers. Try hard and you'll at least get a B.

If you want easy A's, don't take Karl. If you sincerely want to learn, please do. He is a tough grader, but he lets you know exactly where you are at and makes you work hard to better your writing skills. I find reading materials and some of his feedback immensely useful for future use.

I would recommend every comics/anime fan to take Professor Mohns class. Professor Mohn is always willing to assist with papers and is ready to meet outside office hours. His feedback really helps in revising drafts and with his cooperation getting an A is not hard if you are will8ng to put in effort. Going to his office hours helps a lot.

This professor is vague in his feedback and assignment guidelines, and yet he has high expectations from the students. Although a 2 credit course, for some weeks there are about 5 assignments due. Each week there is 1-2 work intensive assignments due.

comment: OH MY GOD. He only teaches freshman writing class, and I got a grade lower than the ones from upper level ENG/ HIS courses that I later took. HOW COME? HE EXPECTED BEYOND THE COURSE'S SUPPOSED LEVEL OF DIFFICULTY, and he DID NOT PRPEPARE US FOR HIS STANDARDS!!! MY FONTS CANNOT BE BOLDER, MY RAGE CANNOT BE HOTTER.

Professor Karl is a good professor. He is passionate about his class and respects all his students. However, the work for his class is heavy and he is kind of a tough grader. It's not easy to get an A range score in his class unless you work really hard.
Professor is nice, classes are fun, but grading is some kind of hard. If you like comics, take this course, you will definitely love it! There are trips to the art gallery and a comic-con.
classes are fun. readings take time. participation matters. be genuinely interested in the content and getting a good grade will be much easier

A lenient grader, but she's good at promoting discussion of topics. She is well prepared for classes - providing lots of handouts and extracurriculars like contemporary artwork, statistics, primary sources, etc.
great professor! plenty of opportunities in class to ask questions and she makes herself available to meet with you outside office hours when necessary. she wants to see everybody succeed.

Prof. Nasra is very kind and understanding. She does not make the class easy and the workload is fairly constant. It seems as though she has high standards of her students, particularly with writing, but she wants to help and prepare you.

good prof, manageable work, grades tough but you can do regrades. idk who wrote that she takes down bad reviews because while i love her, she can barely use blackboard so i highly doubt she knows how to report these reviews. just show up and do the work and you're fine

Prof. Nasra moves quickly and assigns a lot of homework, but her lecturing style is focused and easy to understand, and if you take the work seriously (which I didn't always, hence the B), it's exactly what you need to absorb all the material and score well on tests. She genuinely cares about her students, and I really recommend taking this class.

She's a really good professor and she actually cares about her students. While she does give a lot of homework, and the class can be hard, French is hard in general. It's a college-level class and lessons do go by fast which is why there is a lot of homework so you don't forget. She's one of my favorite.
DONT TRUST THE REVIEW THEY ARE FAKE. THE PROFESSOR ACTIVELY REPORTS NEGATIVE REVIEWS AND GET THEM TAKEN DOWN AND INTIMIDATE STUDENTS. WTH

While this class did involve lots of homework I found it to be useful and helped me prepare for tests and really learn the language. She is really caring and wants you to succeed and is willing to help in any way she can

She is a great teacher and will go out of her way to help you understand the material. You can tell that she really loves teaching and cares about her students. There is quite a bit of homework and class participation is expected but I felt that I learned so much from her.

You'll def have to put in effort to do well in this class. Not an insane amount, but at least a couple hours of review per week. Prof. Nasra is a good teacher, but if you're not on top of stuff outside of class, good luck Charlie. She is very sweet but doesn't have time for bs.

I think that Nasra was a great intro professor. Although she has a tendency to come off as harsh and strict, as long as you put in effort both in the class as well as getting to know her, you'll become friendly in class. The work load was very manageable, so if you're willing to put in effort, you'll be fine.

His lectures are always clear, and his PPTs are very organized and helpful for reviewing before exams. He's very approachable and always holds review sessions, which are helpful! Exams are very fair and based closely on what's taught in class — if you study the materials carefully, you'll do well. Highly recommend taking his class!
He is currently a terrible teacher, but in a few years he won't be. He will be slightly better than terrible.

Honestly, he is a terrible teacher. He does not know how to teach at all and his homework assignments are weekly. In general, you will most likely use outside sources to understand the material. Which, isn't difficult in the first place.

He's a new professor, so he doesn't seem too confident or loud when he's lecturing.  It's actually pretty hard to hear him, even when sitting towards the front.  He is knowledgeable on the subject and a compassionate and understanding professor, but he could be a much better lecturer.

ECE 101 is not an introduction course even though it is presented as one. As a first time coder, this was not a good class to take and, although I learned some things, I would not recommend taking this course. It isn't required for the major, and it isn't a good class for beginners.

The guy on his own is a nice guy but GOD, his lectures are so boring. The course itself is pretty fast-paced and if you fall behind, it might be hard to get back on track. The programming portion of the course was horrendous, one had to learn the syntax and stuff all on his own. He wants you to succeed but his way of doing it gets you to do work.
