comment: Professor himself gives decent lectures. Lot's of opportunities to participate and be engaged but you don't have to. Office hours are very helpful for specific problems or extra help. Actually listens to student feedback.
Just great professor.
You should see him at his office hours more, he really wants to make sure you get the idea and he helps you out a lot in those hours more.

ECE101 Fall '14. Huang is an extremely intelligent professor and truly wants you to learn. He encourages questions and doesnt rely on tests to evaluate you. He is more concerned that you understand the material. He is ALWAYS there to help. At times he isnt 100% clear in lecture, but makes up for it in office hours and by encouraging learning.
For the first time ECE101 was a course Huang was great at adapting to what the class was capable of. He's extremely smart and wants you to understand the material.
Absolutely the best professor I've had in ECE. Nicest guy and best class. Pay attention in lecture and your labs are easy. VERY ORGANIZED
mean as hell about late homework

Huang is very prepared for lecture and makes them as comprehensible as possible. If you don't understand something he spends the time to answer questions thoroughly. He's also very organized and accommodates to the pace of the class. ECE 114 itself was largely lab based. Grading was generous. Overall, one of my favorite professors.
No Comments

Huang is a great professor all around.  He puts a lot of work into his lectures and if you pay attention in class its easy to understand whats going on.  Extremely helpful and very easy to find/contact.  Make sure you keep up with the labs.  Huang is very lenient about late work but if you don't get labs in on time you fall behind VERY quickly.

This teacher truly knows his C++ and does a great job teaching it.  He understands that in an intro course in C++ he has to at least introduce data structures by the end. This by nature creates an intensive course. He makes up for this by having extrememly easy grading that anyone can get an A with. Lab intensive, most points are from labs. Niceman
Professor Bilgic wasn't even teaching this class. He just posted other Professor's lectures and added added a recitation component that replaced his second lecture of the week.
Not recommended to take his class. If you are a data science major, try to take other Stats classes to fulfill the requirement.

The class is poorly structured. We are required to read the slides or watch *another faculty* talking through his slides && take a quiz before class. The professor always say he is going to do R demo during lecture but always end up talking through the slides again. His ambiguous written English in slides, hw, and exams is rather frustrating.
Bad lectures. Study the PowerPoint and do the homework, then everything will be ok.

He is a very disorganized Professor. Planned many quizzes and tests but forgot about them occasionally. Final exam was somehow delayed for 3 hrs because he forgot. The lectures were confusing at most of the times. The questions on the exams were confusing with grammatical errors. The grading was not too harsh because the TAs were overwhelmed too.

The most frustrating and disorganized class you will ever take. Professor's poor English makes lectures, assignment instructions, and test questions impossible to understand. Incredibly vague instructions. Extremely rigorous assignments take upwards of 10 hours a week. Consistently forgets to open quizzes and post assignments; very unreliable.

I hated this class. Please don't take Mitsu, take literally any other professor for CSC 120. His lectures are of absolutely no use, especially if you don't have prior coding experience. He uses autograder for the exams, which is pretty much useless. I got a really bad grade, and my only mistakes were adding space or not adding space in the exam.

It's true that Professor is great and he will curve the first two exams. However, It is hard for me to learn it especially if u haven't learned it before. I will not recommend u to choose this course.

Lectures are pretty much optional because he puts all of the lecture materials on blackboard. If you go to his lectures you probably won't learn anything anyway because he's hard to understand and his slides are confusing. Test wise, there's only a midterm and a final. There are lab assignments every week, but the TA's are really helpful.

I loved Dr. Ogihara! Yes, his lectures sometimes got confusing, but the quizzes he gave actually helped me understand the material so much more (the labs helped as well). Don't worry too much about quizzes though. They are only 5% of the grade, so they don't hurt you that much. He curves A LOT, too. Very enthusiastic and overall a respectful prof.

If you have not taken computer science, you will have to spend a good deal of time reading and programming outside of his class since his lectures aren't very clear or engaging. Do all the labs and go to his office hours for help. Make friends with someone who has programming experience.

I'm sorry. Seriously if you're stuck with this guy like I am either A) kill yourself or B) find a tutor ASAP. He is very enthusiastic about the subject just does a terrible job teaching or relating subject  matter to students. You can bearly understand a word he's saying so it matters worse. Nice guy though. DO NOT TAKE! Vaya con Dios

Enthusiastic and tries (and fails) to keep students interested. Is extremely helpful and available for his students. His accent can be difficult to understand, but wears well over time (I loved it after a month).
He tries hard to keep students interested and works hard to help them, that too, for very boring subject matter. Props to him for that.

Kostin cares a lot about the material, and is very accessible for help. Web dev is fake CS, so the material is all very easy. He focused more on front end/UX as opposed to more theory. MS not a PhD, but if you get a PhD in web dev you have bigger problems.

As a student with no knowledge of Cs, the professor makes this class worth a while. He is always available to respond to students in the class group chat whenever you text him-even if it is 1 am. This class has weekly lab work, and 3 projects. If you attend class and listen to all of the lectures you will be fine. In fact, he explained the labs.

I believe this was Kostin's first semester teaching this class so need to mostly rely on the textbook and self teaching. However, Kostin is willing to improvise and change things to make it easier on the students. He provides a lot of help outside of class and all assignment criteria is always very straight forward.

The WORST professor in DMS you can ever find. Academically, lame lectures, boring topics, and disrupting people ALL THE TIME. If there is ever going to be a discussion or, he will never let the students finish any sentence, for real! Personally, a man with NO MANNERs at all. Communicating with him is like arguing with a jerk on the street.

Professor Kostin is a chill guy. First day of class he said if you pay attention, it's an easy A, and I found that to be true. Even though I've never taken a computer science class before, his lectures and labs were straightforward and informative, so I was able to easily follow and learn the material.

By far the WORST professor I've had in my time here as a computer science student. Lectures are not mandatory to attend but he "takes attendance." Double jeopardy is HUGE on the labs, don't understand one concept but understand all the others? You won't get an A, or a B, or a C, because he will take off every lab you ever have from then on out.

This is the kind of guy who will, for the second day of class, assign a strictly time-limited three minute powerpoint presentation, including the setup time on a screen you've never used before, but then when you're too slow and the alarm goes off, it's "When the Bell Tolls" by Metallica because he thinks he's cool, funny, and relatable.

Professor Kostin is a fun guy. Although he doesn't really teach you what to do, everything is in the textbook. As long as you read the textbook you got an A. The group project is tough only when your members don't do anything (half of my team members pretty much did nothing). As long as you do your parts, you get your points.
He's really good about explaining stuff during the lectures. As long as you do all your labs and projects, you'll get an A.
Good intro course--labs and project instructions are clear and easy to understand. Kostin is funny and understanding, which is a plus.

Though he is a nice and funny guy, he basically does the homework for you and tells you the answers on the exams. I don't mind, but I wish the homeworks and projects were a bit more ambitious so I could learn more and he spoonfed us how to do them less b/c I want to learn more web development!

Cool Guy. I personally never went to class and only saw him once and he made a bunch of jokes during the final exam. Class is an easy A. No due dates and redos for some assignments. This class is more of a Computer Science 101 for those that haven't taken computer science. If your looking to actually learn how to code I recommend you look elsewhere

Most of your help will be on the TAs, who are always willing to help in lab and through email. Labs are optional attendance, I only used them if I had trouble with the assignment/uploading. Grades are based on the weekly labs and projects (dont fall behind!). Easy A. Lab instructions are easy tutorials. Attend if you like to get a walkthrough.

Kostin just got more classes here at the u of r - but he doesn't really know what he's talking about. we essentially had to do the class , he just sat and gave feedback. don't take this class unless you need it ... everything i learned i got from the book.

Kostin has no experience in the field of design - he has said himself that he doesn't know why he's teaching the course. You'll get an A but you will not learn anything. The professor can have weird attitudes towards students.

Kostin is the bomb. Loved his "no due date" policy. Very friendly. He's an adjunct prof so he really knows his front-end web development. Don't bother buying the book we never used it, it'll be outdated in 6 months anyway. CONS: No mandatory attendance, but online daily quizzes which were password protected (the password was given in class)

Prof Kostin really knows his stuff and you learn a lot from his course, but he's such an easy teacher. You don't have to hand the labs in on time, and he literally gave us the answers to our final before we took it. Definitely take this class - it's fun and an easy A and you still learn a lot about web design.
He is a nice guy, but he can't explain himself clearly. A simple idea could become an extremely hard concept by listening to his explanation.

Petridis was an excellent teacher; he was very enthusiastic about the material and truly wanted students to learn the information covered.  Tests and homeworks were fair, and he was always willing to help students.

Petridis is a good teacher, not great.  He often just teaches in such a frenzy that he's difficult to follow.  It's obvious he's extremely intelligent and knowledgeable, but sometimes he has a little problem explaining himself.  Great guy though, he's extremely kind and helpful.
He is a terrible teacher. Going to his lectures is a waste of time.

Bioorganic is much more relaxed than orgo so take prior reviews with a grain of salt. It's an exploratory course built for you to learn, not a weed-out.

Grading is lenient if you show understanding & effort. He's friendly, approachable, and goes on tons of tangential stories. A good background in orgo is vital and can carry you through the course.
The subject sucked, and his lectures were just like reading a textbook off a whiteboard. Hard class, but very passable with a curve.

Not a great lecturer as he assumed we knew most concepts that most students were actually unfamiliar with. However, gave lots of practice exams and was accessible outside of class for extra help. Might be easier to just read the textbook to understand some concepts.
Dr. Nilsson explains every concept clearly. He is passionate about orgo and he is more than willing to help people to understand orgo. Love him and respect!
His exam involved a lot about the problem sets and workshop related question, if you put enough effort on those things , it's easy to ace the course.

His teaching could be a bit unclear sometimes, he gets flustered and makes mistakes but usually is corrected by a student. If you go to workshop, do the practice problems, and go through examples, the tests are fair. There is not much partial credit, but there weren't as many questions that were super difficult as compared to CHM 203. Big curve!

Nilsson is extremely unclear in his teachings. He often makes mistakes. This class is hard, and made it clear that he thinks anyone who doesn't get the material is incompetent in his view. He grades very unfairly and inconsistently. I found him to be very rude and one of my least favorite professors.

Much like orgo 1 this class is really tough. Better prof than goodman (tho thats not saying much) but his TESTS ARE VERY HARD & partial credit is slim. Lectures are decent, sometimes mechanisms are unclear. REDO PRACTICE PROBLEM SETS & WORKSHOPS. Sapling online HW not that helpful. Must MEMORIZE BASIC RXNS & LEARN MECHANISM PATTERNS to do well.

Super friendly and very willing to meet with students who ask for help. Tests are difficult but not insane, though he doesn't give a lot of partial credit on mechanistic questions. Occasionally drops hilarious lines during class - he once said (describing hydronium) "it's just a dirty little proton getting shared around by all the water molecules."
Very good professor. Difficult tests, but fair. His workshops and optional problem sets are great preparation. Happy to meet with students and is helpful in office hours.
Very nice guy, but his tests were super hard. Get prepared to work hard.

A whole lot of fun and open to being helpful and improving himself (which is especially important when his H's and N's start looking the same on the board).  Tests were difficult but not generally out-of-left-field, with a fine curve when they were. I found it easiest to learn from lectures over the book, but many of my friends studied from it.
Very Good Professor, and the exams are just like the practice exams making it easy to do well. Only issue is that his homework can often be long and tedious.

Professor Titus is a very lenient professor—flexible due dates, resubmission of homework—and is very clear on what he expects on exams. He does a review session prior to each test, as well as providing study materials. I took MUSC 110 and then continued to MUSC 111, but his lectures are just plain boring and I will not be taking 112 with him.

Titus as a guy is amazing. He's great to talk to, lenient on due dates, and accessible outside of class. His lectures, however, are plain boring. It's very hard for me to be engaged throughout the entire lecture. Homework was pretty easy, and he does a review session the lecture before a test.
Best Professor. Take his classes and you will not regret. He is

Prof. Titus is super attentive, understanding & accessible outside of class. Hands down the best Prof I've had so far. I would suggest you go to his lectures, his piano demos are really fun and he goes out of his way to make sure we do well in his class! He's the reason I decided on Music as a minor & I am taking his classes (MUR111&112) next year!
Great professor overall. Grading rubric is clear, exams and homework are reasonable and straightforward.
Really nice guy! He was so patient. He will give us sufficient exam materials. I will definitely take his course again!

Class content isn't very hard, but he can explain it weirdly. Spends a lot of time on things you don't need to know, sometimes glosses over important things. Gives test study guides; understand them and you'll do very well. weekly online quizzes, 3 points each- not very hard. Lets you resubmit homework. Very kind professor, very funny.

Professor Titus is a very kind professor that allow makeup tests and always there to answer question, but his lectures are a little dry. He does know a lot about music but it's hard for us to engaged. Many people stopped attending lectures a few weeks later, but you can still managed to get A by just practicing and watch his videos. It was an ez A.

Awesome guy overall. Explained topis very clearly and thoroughly which could be boring, but was nonetheless super helpful. Super nice on extensions for HWs or quizzes (both of which were take-home), I was late on a few but he still gave me full credit.  Class was very well organized and he provided a lot of extra material to study.

Professor Titus is a very understanding and helpful professor, but unfortunately, his lectures are quite dry. I stopped attending lectures after the first few weeks but was still able to secure an easy A by reading the textbook and watching instruction videos, though I don't find the class to be very interesting.
Dr.Titus is super nice, he replies to emails very frequently. Love his lectures, gives out everything clearly. Lots of quizes and 3 tests, get ready!
Caring professor! He replies to emails quickly and answers questions precisely. His lectures are well-organized and logical. His sense of humor makes insipid knowledge of music theory less boring.
You won't regret taking him. He really knows the stuff. Well-structured learning modules.

As long as you pay attention in class and complete the weekly (relatively easy and don't take a ton of time), I'd say the class is an easy A. Probably helpful to have a good music background, but it definitely doesn't have to be strong. Titus' lectures were also very well structured.
The class is easy to get high grades!
Always know what to cover in exams and hws.
Exams covered all we learned in class, never out of bound.

Jason is a good professor, but the only thing I advise people is to make sure you have some music experience before taking the course. I've been around music for 8 years and I had some trouble with a couple things; I couldn't imagine what it would be like if you didn't know how to read music or basic elements of musicality and take this course

He just rambles on and on and on and on about utter nonsense. If you know anything about music theory, override their decision and go straight into MUR111. This class is such a waste of time, and he assigns so much unnecessary dumb work to do.
Easily one of the best profs I've had. His knowledge is astonishing and is humor is top notch. I love it when he plays demos on the piano. An absolute gem of a professor.

Titus is a solid prof for 111. He explains the material very clearly-you don't really need the textbook if you go to class and take good notes. If you do the work required (do the homework carefully, and go to class) it's pretty easy to get an A. His tests come directly from the homework exercises and his practice tests are similar to the real ones

Attendance counted but also if you missed a class, you missed the assignment given. All the assignments are posted online but without either taking a music theory class prior or going to class, it's really hard to understand how to do the work. The assignments are short but usually take a little time. The class before tests he goes over everything.

Titus is a fairly good teacher. He deducts points for things that some may not even consider errors depending on school of thought. His class can be a little boring and dry at times. Overall, good teacher, but if you have the option, get BaileyShea. He's truly an expert in the field and teaches at Eastman too. He also doesn't use the expensive book

Great professor. Very clear about teaching music theory and has an obvious passion for music. Coming from AP theory, this was a very easy class but he still offers a nice perspective on stuff. Attendance is recorded. Very funny guy though, worth sitting in lecture for.

Titus is a great professor! He loves what he teaches and teaches well. You don't need the textbook if you go to class. Grading can be harsh, but the material is easy, so as long as you understand it, you won't have problems. He can no longer factor attendance into your grade b/c of issues last semester with swine flu. Oh yeah, corny jokes galore...

Titus was a very great professor! His grading harshness on homework really makes you watch everything you do and not rush. He goes over test topics the lecture before the test so that is nice. The only thing I didn't like is that he didn't follow the syllabus schedule- we are often way behind it. Other than that I would definitely suggest him!

As previously stated, Titus is THE man. My only complaint is that he seems a little poorly organized. I'd like to see more syllabus adherence. That said, he's HILARIOUS, and somehow manages to make music theory not only funny, but really quite interesting. His music theory dorkyness really shines through and makes you care about the material. A+!

Mr. Titus is my favorite professor at  UR. He's really funny and he teaches the material well. Like others stated, he'll deduct points for all errors, but since he reviews every type of test question before hand, it compensates for tough grading. He also puts 50% weight into homework, but he'll accept late homework without deduction, always do it!
Titus is a great prof. I can really appreciate his humor and better yet, he's super nice. watch out though, homework takes up half of your semester grade and attendence counts towards 10%!

He's really nice, and he teaches well, but the thing is, he grades REALLY hard. One mistake is like -3, and the mistakes add up. So watch out for the extremely hard grading, because the WHOLE class depends on your performance on the homework (even though it doesn't feel like it) since hw is worth 50% of the grade, and each mistake is so crucial.
Titus is awesome - witty, fun, interesting, really knows music theory, I loved him

Not only is Titus the man, but he is an increadible music professor.  You can tell that he has taken a deep interest in music and pursued it.  There is no greater professor than one that truly loves what they teach and this is true of Titus.

Ok, so here's the deal.  Titus is the master of all that is music theory.  I mean, yo Titus, you are the bomb!  He's funny, witty, clear, and awesome.  In all seriousness, Titus is an incredible teacher and has won the respect of this student fully.
Titus is the master of being cool, despite the fact that all signs would tell you he isnt.  What a great professor.  I only wish I could take all my music theory with him
No Comments
Titus is a nice guy and tries really hard to be funny.  He assigns very little work compared to other professors of the same course.  A pretty easy class overall.
HORRIBLE PROFESSOR!!!!

I had difficulty with exams, but it's clear she wants everyone to do well. Her lectures are really helpful - she is really good at breaking down problems. They become harder to follow if you fall behind so it's really important to keep up.
To be honest, I'm not a big fan of her lecture, but it is not hard to prepare for her exams. Read the book/notes, do her practice exam and additional problems, and you'll do fine.

Her lectures are dull and full of mistakes. She makes hard exams. She loves to test thermodynamic cycle but do not teach how to solve a question on it. She expects that students already know so much in chemistry, so she does not do enough efforts to teach in class. She is quite arrogant and rude. You learn most in workshops and through self-study.

Best teacher ever!! Some of these reviews dont do her justice at all. Shes the most inspirational professor Ive ever had the privilege of meeting, and she is also a great person. You will DEFINITELY do well if you do homework and attend workshops!

CHM 132 with Bren was not that bad. The tests are easy if you do the practice problems (which she made sure to provide a lot) and she genuinely cares about her students. She adjusted the difficulty of her tests after she noticed we all did poorly on the first exam and made sure to provide us with plenty of resources for the next tests.

Horrible Professor. Makes so many mistakes. Even on exam questions she make so many mistakes. She confuses her students and keeps telling them "I know you find this too easy" "I am assuming you have done this before". Her class is for people who have done AP or IB and yet those people don't do well either. I will never recommend her to anyone.

Professor Bren clearly knows her stuff and fits a lot of information into lectures. The textbook chapters align well with her teaching and are very helpful. She provides plenty of resources to get the chemistry practice you need. Exams can be tough, but if you know what you're doing and fit in some practice, they're not bad.

Not at all helpful. When I asked her to explain a part of the question again in class. She says you can refer back on your notes, I am done explaining the problem. She makes so many mistakes on blackboard and is very confusing.
tags: ['Tough Grader', 'Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: Professor Bren lectures are really good and she is available outside. Her tests are sometimes difficult but are fair.

Prof. Bren is the best professor I have ever had not only because she is one of the most knowledgeable and modest professors on this University, but also because she truly cares about her students' success. Chemistry requires individual work, but if you follow her lectures carefully, you will never have to do anything except practice problems.

This is the worst class I have ever taken. My workshop TA was prettty awful and Bren notes were messy and full of mistakes. Her lectures never made sense and I had to rely on internet to learn chem. Really annoying, avoid!

Hope she teaches CHM 132 for the first and last time. Not at all clear on blackboard. Cannot solve a problem without an error in it. When students ask her to design challenging workshops to prepare for the hard exams, she simply told class making such workshops would take a lot of time which she does not have. Very uncaring professor
Confusing professor. Makes lot of errors on blackboard.

For the first time teaching CHM 132, it's evident she has put a ton of time into developing the curriculum. Very open to suggestion and really listens to what students have to say. First exam was extremely difficult with workshops that did not reflect material, but second exam was extremely similar to homeworks/workshops. Good lecturer

Her class is so awful that I couldn't pay any attention to the texture and can't help looking at phones. There are so many errors on the practice exams solutions and doesn't reflect the true difficulty of the real exams. I found no useness to do these practice.
tags: ['Tough Grader', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Lectures are great for learning and really understanding the material. Go to her office hours if you can! One of the nicer profs around.

Is not at all helpful in her office hours? Make a lot of errors on blackboard. Her workshops don't represent the difficult level in exams. if her exam average goes down to 60%, she blames students for poor study skills and do not take any responsibility for weak workshops and her poor teaching skills.

Workshops and textbook don't prepare you for what's being tested on exams. Beware exam questions can be page long and you won't be able to finish the entire exam. Her class is best for students with ap chem background.
She is an awesome researcher. Hope she does not leave class at the mercy of other professors and workshop leaders.
Clear, interesting, fun class
Hard class.  Kara covered so much but she was very clear and explanations were very clear so it was manageable.  Glad I took this class and learned more than i expected.
Prof. Becker is very warm, dynamic and really cares about her students. Classes are structured and easy to follow with many interactive elements.
Professor Becker is so nice, and her tests are pretty easy as long as you pay attention in class.

Genuinely one of the best art professors at this school. Passionate, talented, and a great listener, Heather will ALWAYS want what's best for you and help you try to achieve your creative goals the best she can. If you are taking any art classes at UofR, take a Heather Layton one.

I love Heather so much. If you can, TAKE A CLASS WITH HER!!!! She cares so much about you outside of class and takes the time to get to know you, your interests, and your well-being. I wish I can take every class with her.

Heather Layton is one of the best professors in this entire school, she teaches painting in a way that gives you so much freedom, it was your vision not hers and she loved seeing everyone we came up with. She really enjoyed out of the box thinking, but no matter what was supportive of every students piece.

Professor Layton was one of my favorite professors I have ever taken. She is so incredibly kind and so beyond understanding. I was having a really difficult time in my life, and she would constantly take time out of her day to talk with me and support me. She is so inspirational and really amazing at dealing with all levels of skill. 11/10 Amazing!

What a great teacher. Very involved when you want her to be, very hands-off when you just want to work on your own. Also, incredibly smart and well experienced whether that has to do with art, science, or travel. Rated a 3 difficulty because once she sees what your capable of, there's no slacking.
She is really a great professor, even a great friend of student!
One of the best classes I've ever taken. Heather helps you grow as a person and as an artist in her class.
She's awesome.
So BRIGHT in every way. You will learn something about yourself in a class with Heather, guaranteed.

heather is a very inspiring teacher!  Down to earth, always enthusiastic, extremely helpful and fun spirited!  She is incredibly understanding and she brings out the very best in her students!  This class was a blast and I learned a ton about painting!  Love her to pieces!!!

Cares for students, lectures are organized and easy to understand, but the exams are so hard. I understood the content perfectly but could not understand her exams. Exams and class are normally not curved. HW is graded by correction. Not the easy A people say this class is. She's a great professor though, and she wants her students to do well.

The class is fair, although I did find it challenging. Make sure to fully understand material and practice it. The exams get harder with each year and material is seldom repeated. Sometimes, they aren't written the best so make sure you understand what the question is asking. Homeworks can be difficult but they are really helpful.

Dr. Brisson is knowledgable and very fair with her hw assignments and exams. She makes it clear what she will and will not test you on. Attendance is mandatory but going to class is extremely helpful for passing the class. Study well for the final because it's worth a lot of points. One of the easier bio courses and she is very nice

Dr. Brisson was a pleasure this semester. She explains concepts super clearly and has a fair grading system. I really liked that she only teaches information she knows students will use in the future. There is plenty of material to help you study for this class! Attend class for the attendance points and go to recitations, both are super helpful!

Professor Brisson was excellent in Genetics. Although I was not the best in science, she tries hard for us to understand. Her slides are clear and study the HW, workshop questions. As well as the past exam questions, they are fair but she does grade a bit strict. However, she wants you to succeed and is open for any questions in office hours!

Nice teacher. She wants students to really understand the material. Homeworks are easy and are good preparations for the exams. Recitation is mandatory and those also help with exams -- there are plenty of practice resources to get you ready for the midterms. She's always willing to answer questions.

Dr. Brisson is one of my favorite professors! She has a really reasonable expectations of students and always takes the time if things are confusing. She mentioned many times how it is literally her job to make sure that we learn and I always felt like that was the priority of the class.

If you have a chance to take a class with Dr. Brisson, do it. Shes an amazing professor who truly cares about her students well being. Takes feedback strongly into consideration to make the class accessible to everyone. The material was not difficult so if you do the work, you will do fine! Im not a biology major but wish I was because of her!

I took her class in the fall. She is very fair with grading. Her exams are heavily based on the lecture material, so go to class. Plus, she does attendance points so class is basically mandatory. She's very good at answering questions, and is helpful outside of class! Go to office hours if you have any questions!

Dr. Brisson is very fair. If you do the practice exams, actually do the homework, and go to lecture, her exams are extremely fair. She makes you work for it, but if you put the work in, you'll do well. Beware, class is really not curved. Homework is worth a nice chunk of the class grade.

Dr. Brisson gives very dry lectures and looks like she has no energy. She assumes that students already know many concepts of Biology therefore, she does not go into very much detail. I feel like learning is jeopardized like this. She teaches very basic but exams require you to have to solid understanding. exams are all application based.
Hard class but study and you'll be fine! Dr. Brisson is really passionate about genetics and is willing to help her students.

His lecture slides are a bit messy and he has in-class for participation quizzes, so it is best to attend in-person or study using the lecture videos and not slides alone. He doesn't provide practice problems which can make exams/grading criteria unpredictable, but otherwise Dr. Glastad an engaging and passionate teacher. (ask him abt ants too)

Dr. Glastad is clearly very passionate and knowledgable about Evolution, and is very easily accessible outside of lectures. His lectures are a bit hard to follow sometimes, but are overall engaging and funny. Exam questions tend to be a little vague, and you may end up losing lots of points for not mentioning specific things.

Pretty standard bio course load where you memorize the slides + lecture notes for exams and end up getting out what you put in. Does offer bonus questions and grading is pretty fair. Clearly likes the subject and wasn't actively praying on anyone's downfall. If you like evolution you will probably enjoy the course?

Prof Glastad was not very good. He voices little concern for students and does not adjust his exams. Exams are difficult and very unfair. Guidelines are unclear. No practice exams were given. Recitations are useless. Leaves exam review for the TA's and does not provide much support. Rambles too much. Lectures so dense and too much to study for

He's inherited the department's bizarre sense of humor, but he seems to understand the content and how to teach it (although he needs to tone down the meme content). The course begins very easily but gets significantly harder as it goes on.

I had him for Web Programming and he makes class very interesting and never boring. Notes are online but attendance is required for random quizzes (approximtely weekly). It's not particularly difficult but you'll learn a lot of programming languages by the end.

BEST PROFFESOR EVER!!!!!! Very caring and understanding if you need an extension. If I could I would DEFINITELY take this class again!!!! AMAZING lectures and a super compassionate professor. Be ready to read a lot and reflect on it in class. Readings are super fun tho!!!! I can't emphasize how SPECTACULAR this professor was.

Joan Saab is one of the reasons why I love humanities at the U of R. She is so knowledgeable and has a teaching style that most people respond best to. She genuinely cares about her students and wants her classes to be enjoyable and you can tell. She is everything you want in a professor, enthusiastic but chill, and just so understanding.
Nice and caring professor!!
One of the best. Approachable, encouraging and supportive. I loved this class! She will give you an A as long as you participate (as long as you try).
Professor Saab is one of the best professors around! She is super caring and is available outside of class. She always responds to emails and is a very clear grader.
No Comments
Extremely smart and passionate about the subjects. She uses variety in her teaching style. She can be a bit intimidating when attempting to approach her however.

She's really nice and always in a great mood.  Very passionate about the subject.  I learned A LOT about American architecture, she is usually very interesting.  one midterm and a couple of large papers but you have a lot of flexibility on the paper topics.  Saab is a great teacher.

The course structure felt outdated, as all assignments had to be submitted in print Blackboard was not used. I also found the classroom environment discouraging at times, particularly for newer poets. Feedback often came across as overly harsh rather than constructive, which several classmates found deeply discouraging.

comment: All assignments had to be submitted in print and Blackboard was not used. I also found the classroom environment discouraging at times, particularly for newer poets and students still developing confidence in their writing. Feedback often came across as overly harsh rather than constructive, which several classmates found discouraging.

comment: She is highly respected in her field, and it becomes evident why that is as soon as you enter her classroom: she is knowledgeable, passionate, and committed to spreading the appreciation for poetry. This class is 100% manageable course load, and requires some reading and writing; but, nothing too formal aside from having to submit your own poems.
Professor Grotz is as great as her rating suggests. Take a class with her if you love poetry, or if you are considering getting into it—she is inspiring on either front.

Her workshops are productive, and not bogged down by the overly-intellectual or unnecessarily academicness of it. That's not to say we don't have intellectual discussions, because we do, but it's relaxed and low-stress while maintaining a degree of productive critique and improvement. She's very kind and eager to hear different viewpoints.

Very lovely person! Very passionate about poetry, would spend a week studying a poet and analyzing their poems. Discussion driven obviously, respectful and loves any/all input even if she interprets poem differently. Had 2 written assignments ("suggested" due dates but could turn them in the very last day of class) and presentation
Grotz really gives you the space to growas a writer! She consistently kept class engaging and really connested our readings to what she expected from us as writers.

Grotz is hilarious. She's quirky and swears like a sailor, which is surprising since she has such a sweet demeanor. I loved this class. We read some great poets and she always had stimulating things to say. She grades fairly. I'm really excited to take another course with her next semester.

I took 2 poetry courses with Prof. Grotz.  Granted, I like poetry, but I really enjoyed these and felt like I learned a lot. She made the classroom feel like a safe place to share personal writings, and experiment with new styles.  She has a good sense of humor, but expected everyone to keep up with assignments too - which was fairly easy to do.
I've taken two poetry classes with Prof. Grotz, and loved both of them; she leads the workshop format excellently, with a lot of in depth discussion of both the text readings and the student work.

Kim is very funny and kind like much of the ASL department here is. This class was my first experience with ASL, and the conversational approach she took for the class definitely helped me retain the language. Many classes involved us learning the vocab and then walking around and using it to talk to our classmates. All around great intro course.
exams are 17% of grade
One of the easiest courses. Exams are take home, but grades are emphasized on in class and out of class discussion, allowing 4 skips out of 12.

This isn't the Niemiec I loved from Psych101. This course is really boring and repetitive. Every lecture seems to have the same exact takeaway, just a different application (i.e., at work v.s. home). For example, you learn that feeling competent is good for you in every lecture- who knew! Grading is very easy, but if you don't like writing, avoid.
Niemic is a good professor overall, passionate and well spoken. His class isn't necessarily hard, but he's not understanding with health situations or anything like that.

I did enjoy 181 overall, although I feel the grading criteria weren't really the best. I felt this class was a downgrade to my time in 101 cause he barely showed up to in class discussion, and I feel it would be better if he had taught in person, but I doubt it will change. He also wasn't available to help outside class  :(, this class is ok ig....

Goat professor. Very straightforward exams, very crammable if thats your thing. Has extra credit which can boost your grade (ex. B+ -> A-). You don't need to do any of the readings and you will be fine. But if you mess up on one exam you're kind of cooked because most of the grade is 4x50 point exams, with 50 points from TA lead "mini courses".
Not accessible outside of class, can be successful in class if you memorize EVERYTHING, goes on a rampage about his two daughters, offers some extra credit.

Chris was such a nice and caring professor, with the course material being super interesting too! I wish we had more in person lectures with Chris though, as most of the course was a mix of online modules and in-class discussions with TAs. The grading criteria, and how the attendance would factor into the grade wasn't made very clear either.

Unclear of grading criteria for students and may change it without informing students beforehand. Unreachable outside of a class that is almost entirely asynchronous and pretty much only taught by TAs. Nice and funny guy, but almost impossible to get an A for bogus reasons.

The professor only had two lectures and the rest were asynchronous videos. Grading criteria was not clear on how participation impacts your grade. The out of class discussions can feel forced, most of the time no one has anything to add. Nearly impossible to get a hold of the professor or the grad TAs over email.

I wish I were able to give a more detailed review but I saw the professor twice the whole semester. The class is basically taught be TAs and some videos. The professor only teaches two classes in person. The TA sessions are required and sometimes they feel very forced and the TA just wants everyone to speak even if there is nothing to be said.

Great professor, material is really basic and broad, he made psyc a little bit more interesting. Go to lecture and take notes, rewatch all lectures that will be tested on the exam. Overall just memorize to get A.

By far one of my favorite professors, and I loved that this was one of my very first college courses. Neimeic makes lectures hilarious, interesting, and light to learn, and tests weren't hard either. Mini workshops helped, and his reenacting of Freud's psychosexual theory still is one of my favorite memories. Love to take more of his courses!

Niemiec is a great professor. He explains the content clearly and is super funny! His style is also very passionate and doesn't bore you.  Not hard to get a good grade. 4 easy-medium difficulty tests and a ton of extra credit; like so much extra credit your grade can be raised by a full letter. Please take this course if you can.
Chris has great lectures and the tests are very straightforward if you study. Just know you will have to take mini courses run by the TAs- these don't take a lot of time.

Prof Niemiec keeps lectures light and interesting, stays on topic, and uses personal anecdotes to help students connect with lecture material. Class is easy and manageable if you take good notes and review them regularly.

Christopher is a great professor. Always go to the lectures they are very engaging. The exams are straight forward and easy to do well on if you study. Take lots of notes and go over the slides before exams. There is also an opportunity for extra credit with the mini courses provided.
Chris is so entertaining and his lectures are actually entertaining. Loved this class, made mre realize I want to minor in psych.
Records all lectures so you don't have to attend class if you don't want to., thus practicing what he preaches about self-determination theory and the importance of autonomy in intrinsic motivation.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: Chris was a great professor and really funny! It was nice being in a class of all freshmen with a chill professor. The tests aren't hard as long as you effectively study. I got a textbook but it's not necessary (he records all lectures and the test material is only from the lectures, not the textbook)

Great person and professor. Gives clear and organized lectures that prepare you well for the exams. His class was entertaining and a great introduction to psychology. Made me even more interested in the field. The mini courses were a bit stressful since it was outside of class, but it's not tough. You'll do great just by reviewing lecture slides

Chris is a great guy and his lectures are always entertaining. His tests are multiple choice and are only based on what he says in class, so I wouldn't bother reading the textbook. The mini courses were easier but just annoying to attend outside of class. The whole grade is based on four exams, and there is no final. Great introductory class.

For PSY181, Niemiec is essentially an abstentee, only sometimes popping up into the TA discussions (we all watch the same 5yr old lectures - don't like the lecturing tbh). Don't like the class set up. Exams aren't horrible, but all mc/T/F means a few wrong is a big hit to the grade. This course is a HISTORY of psych course. Title is misleading.

The class is alittle harder than expected. The tests are based half of T/F questions and its annoying. They are also only 25 questions so it is hard to do well. You meet with a TA once a week and discuss the lecture you watched instead of meeting with Niemic. The set up is odd and the class is a little boring, mainly memorization. Hes nice tho

Prof. Niemiec is very passionate and knowledgeable in what he teaches. Lectures are very engaging and informative. The materials in this class are useful and easy to understand, but expect at least 2 research papers to read and 1 essay to write per week. Overall, definitely a class that's worth to take.
He was a pretty awesome lecturer. He grades based off of tests (not cumulative) and mini courses led by TAs. The mini courses are super interesting. Easy class but also informational!

Take him, easy/funny - you dont have to show up to class to get A, he records all lectures. 4 multiple choice tests worth 50 points each. 2 mini courses offered by TAs (attendance and a small asaignments to do- you choose the course) worth 25 points each. 2 discussion/debate session worth 2 points each (for showing up) - can get extra credit

Chris is essentially everything you want for a professor, especially for an introductory class. He is well spoken, funny, and he makes the material as interesting and engaging as possible. The classes were lecture heavy but I think that's more a result of the psych 101 material itself.

I know that PSYC101 typically an easy course, but I guess the hard part about this one was the lack of grades being put in. Most exams happened to be when I had exams for engineering or papers for writing due, so it was hard to find time to study for an elective. I did pretty well with minimal studying and there is extra credit and mini courses.

For intro psych, the tests are multiple-choice which is a real blessing. His lectures are straight forward and he tells personal stories which helps keep students engaged. He's funny and laid back. I would recommend this to everyone, especially pre-meds.
Compassionate. Supportive. Compelling lecturer. Lots of theoretical knowledge. The readings and classes are 110% worth your time and effort. Manageable workload.
Amazing guy! Clearly passionate, and so will you be after you take his classes!

grading was super late and i had written half of the essays before one was graded. weekly in person recitations and zoom workshops. intensely boring lectures. i felt like i was just regurgitating information for a grade.

Chris is awesome, especially considering the online format because of COVID. Grade is based on a few 50 question multiple choice tests w/ explanation, open note. Tests are easy, if you watch the lectures. Also, you have attend some mini-courses taught by the TA. Overall a positive low-stress class to take with some interesting material.

Almost all of the grading is based on the exams which can contain very obscurely-formatted questions a lot of the time. All of the lectures are pre-recorded so you can watch them when you like but you must watch them if you want to pass the exams. You're gonna be talked at for 2.5 hours every week and you need to scribble down notes. Very boring.

taking notes for his recorded lectures were hard for me because he covers a lot, so attending in-person was a must for me. Plus, I liked going to his lectures because it's always a good time. Exams are straight memorization from the lectures because it's multiple choice. Great and easygoing guy. If you're going to take PSY 101, take him!

Chris is a really inspiring lecturer that'll change your life for the better. Learning about motivation is really important and interesting, even to a non-psychology student. The class is really easy if you do all the papers and attend the lectures (they're recorded too!). I would take Niemiec again in a heartbeat
Literally just show up for a good time, super great personality, and entertaining lectures.
He is a good professor who would record his own lecture and post after the class. The exams are always covered in the lectures. So be prepared for reviewing the videos before the exam.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria', 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Chris is a great professor and a cool person. He is very interactive with the students on class, and he always keeps the lecture exciting. The material is easy and all tests were multiple choice. Mini courses outside of lecture were also interesting and were easy points towards your grade.

The structure of this class was very different than any other psych class I had taken. It was nice to be able to watch the modules on your own time and I found my discussion group helpful. Chris is a great guy and his videos were very straight forward, but I think for this course in particular, you interact with the TAs way more.

Psych is a lot of common sense and especially in this intro class, so if you've got your head on straight you'll definitely pass and probably do well without too much effort. Don't bother getting the textbook, only his lectures matter. He is entertaining, posts lectures online, but going to class is worthwhile bc he's funny.
He may be fun but the lecture halls are too big for him to actually care about you and your struggles in his class

Had a really bad experience with the first essays in recitation, where everyone got a fifty percent or below because the grads and undergrads were saying different things about the grading criteria. Niemiec's response to this was saying that our grades don't matter as much compared to the material we learn in class.
Would definitely take this class again, Chris was an incredible Professor and the course was interesting.

He is really fun and makes the lectures entertaining, I didn't do amazingly in the class because I struggle with multiple choice and there was soooo much content but he is a really good professor and really good at explaining.
Very multiple choice test heavy, which can be a good thing. Lectures are amazing.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'GRADED BY FEW THINGS', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: If you study (which you should), you'll be just fine. He is a charismatic professor who cares about his students and makes lectures interesting, I would definitely take again!

Fun and interesting lectures, but not an easy A class. You'll do well if you're good at specific multiple choice questions. Class seems too big for him to care about his students. Not sure if he's too useful for specific/personal questions...
This man is the greatest teacher i have ever had. I love him so much. he makes the class fun, he's organized and he is just an amazing prof all over

He records his lecture so attendance is not mandatory. Overall, I thought the class was very easy. Exams are multiple choice. Make sure you study all your notes and memorize them. Even though I thought the class was easy, I did not do extremely well on all the exams so make sure to do the extra credit which will bump up your grade say from B+ to A-

Make sure you do the extra credit. I think a lot of people go in expecting an easy A. Well let me just tell you that the average exam grade was usually a low to mid B. Trust me, there are plenty of people getting below an A- in that class. Make sure you actually take notes and everything. It's not too difficult, but I wouldn't say an easy A

This was a very easy class. Tests were simple, mostly you just have to memorize vocabulary. However, his recorded lectures were impersonal, and they were incredibly boring. The discussion response papers were not graded efficiently. By the time I submitted the 6th, I had only received feedback on two. I will be avoiding Chris' classes in the future

He's my favorite prof that I've ever had. He wants you to want to learn, and doesn't force anything (he talks frequently about his hatred of exams). He talks a lot about his family and how the material applies to life, which is great. He makes you feel like a person, not just a student. All his lectures are put online as well.  10/10!

Professor Niemic was such a cool guy and showed a lot of passion in what he taught. The class topics were really interesting and there was not a lot of work. As long as you understood the main points of his lectures and show up to the mini-courses,  you should get an A.
Chris is the GOAT. As long as you take notes on everything he says in class and study off of that the night before the exam, you will get at least a B+.

This class was one my favorites throughout all of college. Niemiec makes his classes so that if you come to the required discussion sessions/recitations, do the required work, and study for his exams, you will get an A. His tests and assignments are super fair and the materials are interesting. He is also very relaxed and seems to love his job.
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'TEST HEAVY']

comment: Well the class was divided into an online module version and an out of class discussion session. The modules are watched at our own pace, but it's a ton of material and it took me three hours worth of time to note everything. The out of class discussion was useless, as it didn't really add to anything. The exams were very fair.

Very straightforward class. The exam questions come from all of his online lectures and are factual in nature. A lot of different personality theories in this course but most of them were covered briefly in his psy 101 class too.

Really great lecture, does a good job of making things interesting. The only grades are the 4 tests, but they are  all 50 multiple choice and fairly easy.  He does assign the textbook, but you really don't need it and you don't need to read it.
Easy class to pass. Just have to memorize and you're fine. The SONA extra credit is also helpful.
Easiest class ever.

Chris Niemiec is the man take his class it's very straight forward and not hard at all. He really cares about his students and the class is an interesting, easy class to make life easier first semester freshmen year. All his students love him.

The class is a joke, and I kind of hate it. Psych itself is really interesting though, but the class isn't about learning psych, it's about figuring out what's on the exam. The lectures are recorded, it's a walk in the park.

Tests are super easy, and you do not need to show up for classes to get an A. However, he recited the lecture and it's boring and rigid. The classes are good for non-psych majors with mere interests, but for people who wish a deeper career in the area, it's not as helpful.

If you want any easy A, take this class. You get out of it what you put in, but he presents it as a game to figure out what's on the exam, not about learning the concepts. It was interesting however, and it was a good first exposure to psychology.

He's a good professor overall, but lectures were SO FREAKING BORING. Sometimes he would say something hilarious and we would wake up, but overall he just read the slides. "turn now to another consideration" is burned into my brain. But the class was a typical intro course. Nothing too hard.

Chris' freshman psych class was one of my favorites. He gives you every opportunity to succeed (putting noteslecture recordings online, test review sessions, and make-up tests), but his lectures are also fun and engaging. Even though I could skip class I never wanted to because it was always fun.
Chris is a great lecturer. The points are clear and straightforward. The videos are posted on blackboard so you can choose to learn at dorm. I register his PSY262 for next semester.

Chris is a great, and in my opinion the best, professor in the psych department!  He leads all of his classes from an SDT perspective so you have a lot of choice regarding the class and he is extremely open to feedback.  You will not only love Chris, but also the class material!  He is also a very approachable professor
Niemiec is very passionate, though his lectures may drag and lack in organization sometimes. He is however a great lecturer and tests are easy if you pay attention during lecture.

Tons of philosophical theory in this class, which can be pretty dry.  Memorize absolutely everything for the exams and be ready to spit it back up verbatim in the short answer section.  MC is pretty easy.  Its sad because Niemiecs an awesome prof and the material in this class is just terrible so he'll probably get an undeserved bad rep.
He was a terrible teacher who never used the textbook. His test was just based on memorizing his lectures.

He does not use the text books. Tests are based on what he says in class. He records his lectures and has them (and his powerpoints) available online. I'm a STEM major who needed the writing credit and Kate was the best choice I could have made (yes we were allowed to call her Kate). She was open to any idea, opinion, or discussion imaginable and was super flexible with due dates. Don't get me wrong though, we still had very serious and respected assignments, but overall a great class!

Ms. Phillips is the epitome of the high school english teacher who grades essays based on how much they like the student (in this case, being liked depends on being a feminist, liking Ariana Grande. and raising your hand for every question in class). Also, fair warning, human happiness is NOT what this class is about.

Professor Phillips is a great person. She is very charismatic and passionate. However, the contents of the course have very little to do with the title. Although it is a required writing class, we have really only discussed making an argument and research, which is not the only kind of writing there is. Ultimately, I wish I chose something else.

Course was Post-Industrial America. Professor Westbrook is brilliant and clearly enjoys and cares about his students. I gained a ton of useful knowledge. Most of the reading was from two books. One was great, the other difficult to follow. We were always 1 or 2 lectures behind the reading. Discussions lasted too long, I learned more with lectures.

comment: Have him for Golden Age Movies. He should stick to history. Takes points off papers for not liking a choice of words - btw there are only 3 short papers (6-8 pages) and one long final paper (8-10). Speaks SO slow to the point of wanting to sleep/mind wanders. Adequate film history course, I guess. Liked the movies well enough. He's not engaging tho

He's really passionate about what he teaches, and if your looking to take a hard history class and are really interested in it, then go ahead and take it. If your not a history minor and also not looking to take a moderately hard elective, this class is not for you. Its hard even when you try hard. He takes off points for not agreeing with you.

Nice guy, very smart. Very to his own idea. If you disagree with them or write about something that he disagrees with you get penalized for it. Also, very tough grader. Always come prepared to class because he does randomly call on people. Makes the situation extremely awkward if you aren't prepared. was not one of my favorite professors.
Westbrook is as friendly and helpful as he is brilliant. One of the best professors I've taken a class with.

Westbrook is an amazing professor. He really respects his students and challenges them to think about what they are reading. He is a hard grader, but definitely fair. The course consisted of a lot of discussion- not too much lecture. When he did lecture, he was generally pretty interesting.

The reading work (all primary sources) necessary for class discussion is extensive; be prepared. But the actual number of graded assignments is few (4?). However, his grading is difficult and adequate knowledge on the subject is required for a good grade.
Very good prof, clear lecturer, nice guy, fair work load/grading. Interesting class that I enjoyed very much, would definitely recommend any class with Westbrook.

he is absolutely brilliant. really nice guy, very likeable. classi s interesting if you have an interest in history. he assigns a lot of reading but you can get buy with just skimming the stuff. be prepared for class though, he randomly calls on people all the time. don't bother to go if you haven't prepared-- you will sit there dodging bullets.
Professor Westbrook is marginal.  I credit him with demonstrating the irremediable shortcomings of historical analysis, effectively truncating my interest in the profession.
Nicest guy ever, also brilliant.  my problem was that this should have been a philosophy class, not a history one.  and i hate philosophy.  so willing to help though and always in a great mood.
Great Prof. Brilliant man. Difficult grader, lots of reading. worth taking his class recent american thought

I loved this class.  The material was interesting in itself, but Dr. Westbrook helped bring it all together in a very organized and enlightening way.  His lectures were very informative and interesting, and he ran the class discussions very well.  He is one of the best history profs I've had.

He is a great teacher who really cares about his students.  I was in a huge lecture and he still knew who I was 3 years later.  He uses a lot of electronic reserves which hurt my eyes and/or my flex account.  He loves Bruce Springsteen and will find some way to incorporate his music into every class he teaches.

the worst professor/lecturer ive had at rochester in 3 years.  Reads straight from a piece of paper and does not engage the class at all.  Hard grader too, ive taken 300 level classes and gotten much better grades than i did in this piece of crap class.
Good professor.  Direct teaching style, very helpful and open to questions.  Impressive, nuanced knowledge of the material.
Missy is caring and gentle, always encourage me to create! Definitely take her class!
She really opened my eyes to the area. I thought it was one of the best classes Ive had.

Boring teacher. This kind of stuff can be so interesting but she makes it difficult to sit through the class. White slides with black text. Reads what is written on the slides almost word for word. You could get away with not going to class except that there are in-class assignments, and even some that are not on the syllabus.
She literally reads from the slides. You don't need to show up to class.
HORRIBLE
horrible teacher. wait till the professor is there next year. she's a grad student and her teaching is not coherent at all
Memorize concepts and you're good TAs know nothing (they get confused and give bad examples)

This was the first time that this class was offered, she seemed excited by that. The lectures were informative and easy to understand. She posts her slides and makes sure to have a review day before each exam. Would recommend taking this class with her.

Professor Starr is one of the worst professors I have had so far. She is very disorganized and is a professor that just comes in because it is her job. I never felt she actually cared whether her students understood the material or not. Her class is very dependent on the exams so good luck.
Professor Starr is a very nice and caring professor but she looks like she dreads her job. She walks in and already looks bored. Her class is pretty easy.

The professor is nice but she can be clumsy or unprepared for class often. The class isn't really a lot of new information, mainly everything is read off the powerpoint. I wish there were more assignments in the class or opportunities for discussion. The class is alright, not too hard if you study. Sometimes the professor seems like shes rushing

I fleet Asia to avoid the "follow these steps" kind of education, but clearly she brought it here. As a math double major I have taken stats, ODE and numerical analysis, but she still forced me to take this course.  She will punish people for every single step that is not identical with the format she provided (which is full of redundant steps).

Difficult Class. Rigid guidelines. TAs aren't given rubrics so grading can be confusing and different for each person. Many co-curent deadlines, rarely gives extensions, late hw not accepted. Only two midterms (therefore weighted heavily). Requires writing an entire publishable paper. Lots of coding. Flipped classroom. 
Professor is a nice person.

comment: Online lectures are great.
She doesn't teach at all. Just give recorded lecture and you need to watch them before class. The lectures are useless

A lot of materials to be covered in one semester so the explanations are not as detailed as I would prefer. It appears to me that she's trying her best to make things clear and she gives amazingly organized notes. Very "Asian style "of teaching. Quite a lot of work indeed but I don't think it's too hard to get good grades in this.

Terrible professor. Having taken a statistics class already, I already knew much of the information in advance. She overcomplicates the concepts that are much easier than they seem to be. She unnecessarily makes the homework so long. This class is required and she clearly hates teaching it.

At first I did not like her but throughout the semester I learned she does care. She is not great at making things understandable and is quite unorganized during lectures but solids is a hard class and it is hard to teach. Read the textbook, pay attention in class, and be prepared test scores might not be great. The labs are terrible too.

Lectures are borderline useless with way too many mistakes and very poor explanations. Labs were poorly explained and had unclear grading. We would frequently have homework due the same day as she taught the concepts. Exams were brutal and not representative of the homework in both difficulty and content. Only helpful part of class was the textbook

Prof. Abdolrahim has good intentions, but the execution needs work. Grading was fair, but lectures had frequent errors, notes were hard to read, and homework was often due near the day material was taught. That said, I appreciated that student feedback was usually considered and applied. The textbook was really helpful too.

The textbook was the only helpful part of this class. Lectures had frequent misinformation, notes unreadable; TAs weren't equipped to help, especially with labs. Tests included barely covered material, and homework was due before topics were fully taught. Student requested example problems were poorly explained and full of errors.

She put so much effort into listening to feedback, thats why she earns a good rating. If you didnt like class at the end maybe you didnt give good feedback, I personally saw my feedback get implemented. She makes mistakes, yes, but forgetting a sign during math isnt the same as making conceptual errors. The work is gruesome. Hardest ME class so far

She does not explain things well and often will not revisit important ideas or equations. Her notes are mistake riddled, messy, and do not give a step by step walk-through(Including homework and test solutions, most of which are screenshots of the textbook) The tests dont cover the same stuff that we were taught and the review for them is unhelpful

Easy because nicely graded but the lectures are awful, just read the textbook. Never answered any of my emails, despite saying she's accessible outside of class and willing to meet the needs of students. Also test questions are poorly written and often have many mistakes or missing info. Was excited for solids but not anymore because of professor.
Nice to answer questions and provide help. The grading is very nice.

She gives incredibly hard homework and her lectures are not very well organized. The textbook is the saving grace of this course because without it you're done. TA's are helpful for the most part, but OH can be crowded as they are really the only time you can learn the content. Tough times in ME 226. Take it with the other Prof. if possible.

One of the worst teachers I've experienced in my entire life; her lectures cover tons of material yet seem all over the place. She consistently gets things wrong on the board, is hard to understand, and has 0 relationship with the class. If you read the textbook it is WAY more helpful which is embarrassing considering how expensive this school is.

her lectures were useless -- if you read the textbook and go to recitation you'll be fine. there is a huge curve on exams too
She is great in explaining materials. She really cares about her students. Highly recommend her.
Very dry lectures with LOTS of mistakes, homework and most textbook problems don't prepare you for the tests, and long homeworks.
