comment: Though she makes mistakes on the board, it does not take away from learning the concept. She really cares about the students. You can argue for extra points after receiving your test.

Her lectures are okay but she's really bad at math. Every time she does math in lecture there are lots of mistakes. She talks really quietly but is really nice, accessible, and good at explaining topics clearly outside of class.

Actually mind boggling that people like this professor. Mediocre lectures, unreasonable. Once used r as a constant without saying it was a constant for a test question IN OUR UNIT ON POLAR COORDINATES. Bald and deserved to be bald.

Love Professor Wolf! He explains things in a detailed manner which is easy to understand. He starts with the very basics to make sure the higher level concepts have a good foundation to them. His notes are very easy to follow and his office hours are extremely helpful as well. If he taught higher level math class, I would take those as well.

I hated Calculus, but I would go to office hours often, and Wolf does a great job of working through the problem and making sure that you fully understand the concepts. He also made sure to do extended office hours the days before the midterms and final if you needed any help. Definitely utilize CETL and recitations if you need help.

He explained things simply and efficiently. He's a solid choice for an intro math class and a friendly guy. Webwork (homework) is unlike the lecture examples and exams. When studying for exams, review notes/lectures and then work on old exams.

prof wolf seemed like nice little man until we got into the material. he rlly did try his best to teach us, was v accessible outside of class for help, but is one of those insanely smart guys that simply cannot impart knowledge. class was mostly just doing an example prob and then expecting us to pick up on concepts and letting us loose on the hw.

Nice guy! He is patient and gives us time to write and makes sure we dont have any questions. Theres just the weekly webwork homework, but I reccommend going to study group for help, much harder than examples in lectures. Dont do what I did and bs the homework. Spend time everyday on them. I failed most midterms because I wasnt serious about study

Herman is a great prof. He is very approachable and kind and explains stuff well. The class had some moderately difficult parts but overall it was pretty reasonable. I had him for 161 as well and had a similar experience. Would def recommend

Incredibly caring professor, and the best lecturer I have had in the math department so far. Expect endearingly bad jokes. The exams are intentionally difficult, typically at the level of the hardest problem set questions. But he writes them knowing he will curve the letter grades. My section had a 58 avg on the midterm, which he curved to a B.

Very caring and approachable understands he's teaching math.  He keeps the class engaging by going off topic but with only to break up monotony.  Very helpful if you ask for help. For calc 161 he is the course organizer so he writes your tests if your in calc 161.

Notes are super organized and he lectures very clearly. Definitely go to lectures if you want to do well in the course. Witty humor and although it may seem like he's harsh at first, he is an awesome professor who understands what it takes to do well in the course.
Great professor, notes are super

Amazing professor, can't recommend him enough. Explains calculus in a clear, simple way, and if you pay attention in class you won't fall behind. Lectures are engaging and funny, but not to the point of being distracting or off-topic. The class moves fast, and it's easy to lose momentum, but if you stay focused and do the work you'll be fine.

Great lecturer and provides well-motivated and clear but simple explanations of all the major topics. He's very enthusiastic which is great, the lectures are high-energy. Sometimes a little intimidating to contribute in class but great guy. Effectively references the textbook as a good supplement but not required to read.

Dr. Herman is a phenomenal lecturer; he's very engaging and passionate about the subject, and he goes about teaching in a very clear and concise manner. The course content wasn't the easiest (as somebody who isn't the best at math), but he breaks it down in a way that makes it a lot more manageable. Highly recommend!!

This dude is hilarious. He'll talk to himself making jokes, tell random stories from his life, advertise Pepsi, and on top of that he's a remarkable professor. Answers questions, explains things clearly & legibly. The class is tricky, but I wouldn't want anyone else teaching it to me. If you ever get the chance, take this guys class.
BEST MATH PROFESSOR!!

He is a really great guy and always more than happy to help with anything. The class isn't easy by any means, and the exams in particular were hard. Homeworks are not too bad if you ask for help when needed. He just wants you to put in the effort which is great to see. Also he makes funny jokes.

Diverting and amicable, as Mark always has been, Math 208's quizzical materials were broken down into palatable piecewise information that was fairly tested on. Had the assignments been easy, the class would not be a banger. Challenging as they are designed to be, they siphon out students' thoughts.
he is nice

I'm typically not the rate my professor guy that will write comment or rate the professor, but I signed up the account for him! His class is truly interesting and engaging. I really understand a lot of concepts that I didn't get before with his help, he's just amazing!

He was hilarious and knew how to teach so well. It was a morning class and the attendance wasn't mandatory, but I didn't miss a single lecture even though I did most of the material in high school. If you take cal 161, take it with Prof. Herman.
He is funny and nice! Explains concepts very clearly!

Prof Herman does an extremely well job in teaching math. One of the most brilliant math professors. He does however teach extremely fast and sometimes can be very direct and rude at times. He definitely cares for math and genuinely tries to teach students, but i found his teaching style to be sometimes difficult to grasp. Be ready to take notes.
He's very fast but he also teaches well. If you pay attention and do webworks you should be fine.

Hands down one of the best professors I have ever had. Professor Herman is incredibly helpful and genuinely wants his students to succeed. I have developed a greater interest for mathematics because of his excellent teaching. Great class!

Prof Herman is a great lecturer and gives many examples for each topic. He also explains why concepts in calculus exist instead of just giving you the formulas, which really helps with understanding. That being said, the pace is fast and it's almost impossible to cram for the tests, so it's important to stay on top of your homework and studying!

The best math teacher I've ever had, never got the chance to lean from him or talk personally, but his lectures were awesome. He connected so many dots for me that had been floating around from previous calc classes. There have been multiple times I've thought "Why didn't my teachers in HS just day that?". I wish I could take him for 162 :(
Great professor
word hard, then you will get an A

Professor H is a great math teacher and really funny. Showing up to lecture is very important. My advice is to really focus on the homework because that is what prepares you for the test and the practice quizzes.

Great professor, walks you from the eaiest ever examples to the hardest ones. detailed lectures and alway on point when it comes to what really matter for exams. I would recommend attending the lecture he gives pretty great examples in them.
Amazing 161 professor. He gives a lot of examples to help understant.

When talking about the Dijkstra algorithm, I am confused. Taking so many years of algorithm competitions, I am surprised he is teaching algorithms this way. I can feel if I am new to these things I might get confused. He gives me a feeling he wants examples to explain algorithms, but those examples may not be suitable and confuse you more.

I think this class is fine. I went to his office hour and he helped me a lot. Sometimes I just cannot follow this class or missed a class, and I can go over his notes. He basically includes everything in his notes.

This guy is the bomb. I have no idea what these other dudes are talking about. Maybe they are not attending class. He clearly pours his heart into teaching this class. Take it if you get the chance. He's smart and hilarious and super helpful if you go to office hours.

I have no idea why we are going to class. His lecture is sooo confusing, and I just couldn't follow. Notes are extremely confusing with lots of useless phrase though I have to review it to know how to do homework. Takes lot of time. Why am I taking this class??? If you want and easy class, take it, and get ready to study everything by yourself.
Notes are not clear. Lectures are not understandable. Homework is hard. We are struggling.

Amazing professor, would definitely take him again. Cares about his students and is very understanding. Funny and gives clear explanations, lectures are recorded with notes. Difficult tests, but they are the same regardless of the professor. HW load is reasonable. I'll never love calculus, but Professor Herman made me hate it a little less.
Very nice teacher and class. The pace is fast, and the exam is hard, so you should always review the notes and webwork assignments.

comment: Class moves pretty quickly but he's very helpful outside of class. One of the best math professors at UR.
Lectures were not recorded. He's very open to questions and good at explaining but will not stop moving forward (pretty quickly might I add). Overall one of the better math professors I've ever had.
He's such a fun, quirky guy! His lectures are extremely fast-paced and hard to follow but the perk of that is you get many helpful examples.
Such an odd and funny guy which makes class interesting. He gives good examples during class that will mimic those on Webwork so it's important to attend class.
He has a true passion for math. His interest in the subject during the lecture draws me into it a lot. Always answers your questions with enthusiasm.
THE WORST!!!!!!!! I DON'T EVEN UNDERSTAND WHY THE HECK IS HE TEACHING 150!!! I AM AN A STUDENT AND I HAD TO STUDY EVERYTHING ON MY OWN!!! WHY THE HECK ARE WE PAYING $5000 FOR THIS COURSE ALONE???
He just does not know how to teach probability or math in general. Lectures are boring. Reading textbook is better
Great professor, a little fast but honestly he is amazing. Take him.

soooo boring and assumes you'll know things that you don't when lecturing

comment: Great intro to discrete math. Very funny guy and explained things well. Always took the time to answer student questions clearly. You will need the textbook but you can find the pdf, and the questions from the book always translated very clearly to what he lectured in class.
Prof. Herman is very skilled in his expertise. His lecture are fun and organized. He is also very respectful to all the students. Overall, he is a great professor. Fully recommend to anyone.

I really love Prof. Herman. He is one of the few professors who listen carefully to the students. You can ask him question almost anytime and he would explain clearly and patiently. I would fully recommend him to any students. Go for it!

Herman is a great guy and answers questions well. That said, he just writes notes way too quickly on the board. I spent all class trying to keep up and get the notes down without being able to process anything.

Don't miss out! He has perf amount of humor in lectures. Office hours are worth going as he explains things well. He doesn't talk into the board! He responds quickly and is impressively patient despite how busy/knowledgeable he is. You can feel his effort to help students learn. He has  great comedic timing- I 'd definitely have him as prof again.

You'll be fine as long as you pay attention and take notes. He tends to move a little fast, but his office hours are helpful and he replies to emails pretty fast. Woe unto you if he's the one setting the exam, though. Otherwise, he's a pretty decent professor. Don't take too long to seek help for problematic areas, it's hard to play catch up

Herman is a really great guy and a wonderful professor. He gets really excited about the material, which keeps class entertaining. He explains everything clearly and gives examples of every concept. Highly recommended

Unnecessarily long and repetitive hw assignments, though they're pretty doable. Good intro to math logic without killing you on it. Lectures are better than the book for notes and understanding the material. Practice exams super helpful. Not a walk in the park, but if you put time into the course you'll ace it. C or below if you don't.

Herman is one of the better teachers in the math department. He is extremely knowledgeable and explains things clearly, but he moves very quickly through lectures. Always go to the lectures, you basically have to in order to do decently in the class.

Herman is a decent professor. I probably wouldn't have him as my first choice for a class, but he's a good back-up plan. He does write and talk fast, but you get used to it after a few lectures. The class itself is hard, especially when it gets to infinite series. Herman does help to explain the harder concepts, but it's not enough on its own.

MTH 162 is an awful class, and Herman didn't make it any better. Moves ridiculous fast in lecture, and his handwriting is terrible.  Can be condescending and rude if you ask a question he considers simple. Webwork is really hard, and doesn't help you prep for exams.  The book problems are a lot better. Midterms were tough. Final was BRUTAL

Out of all the MTH162 professors, Herman is the best. That, however, is not saying much. He speeds through lectures and uses exact examples from the textbook. I found it much more useful to just read the textbook and watch lectures online. The tests in 162 are pretty fair, aside from the final, which was ridiculous.

Herman is a great professor! He does tend to go fast, but this is because he is giving you more in depth coverage/examples than the other professors. Also, he is open for questions.  He goes deep into theory, but once you understand that you can understand anything that could possibly be on the exam. For the harder subjects do look a the book.
Excellent professor. I really enjoy be in his class though he speaks super fast and provide students lots of notes. He is willing to help students after class in his office hours or by appointments.

Excellent professor.  He is super helpful outside of class and makes himself very available to his students.  His lectures were almost comically speedy at first (but still clear), but he slowed down by October.  Must have been the weather... Also a good guy to know (Director of Undergraduate Studies)

He's young and has a sense of humor. He can be eccentric but he always seems happy to help out students who are making an effort. He writes & talks at supersonic speeds which makes note-taking a challenge but his lectures were good enough that I barely had to crack open the book all semester. I would definitely take him again if I had a chance.

Lectures are always very engaging and he throws in a nice bit of humor. He speaks really, really quickly in class, but you get used to it after a while. Really patient/helpful in office hours. He like to use the entire grading spectrum, so you might get a low test number, but he adjusts the curve accordingly.

Very helpful professor who is always willing to spend extra time with his students. His lectures move at the speed of sound and will burn through a dozen pages of notes in one day. His curves are helpful and generous but not obscenely large. He is gorgeous and I want to run my fingers through his receding hairline.
Very good teacher. Although he goes over stuff bit fast in class, he is very helpful afterclass. He explains the problems to you until you get bored. His test can be long and a bit hard

Great experience in CHEM 262 with Dr. Partridge. He cares about his students and communicates deadlines and expectations very clearly. He is sometimes slow to grade and post assignments, but he will adjust deadlines accordingly.

comment: his love of math is inspiring and sparked a deeper interest in mathematics. Very thoughtful professor, we need more professors like this.
I have been hate math in high school, but this lecture is inspiring and I think I have found some of my confidence in math now.

Pretty good at teaching, obviously really passionate about math. His notes were a little bit messy and he's kind of awkward, but if you asked him for help, he helps you. He wants the student to succeed. Just take practice exams to do well on the tests.
Enthusiastic and approachable. His passion for math is inspiring.
his love of math is infectious. genuinely wants students to succeed. explains anything you ask

His lectures were frustrating. He wrote on the board the whole time while teaching. I couldn't learn this way- where the professor doesn't teach but describes out loud what he's doing. Very poor instruction, guidance or interest in student's education. Do not waste time with this instructor. Do not be misled by her authorship of textbook.

It is doubtful the text written for the class is used anyplace else, it reads like a high school science book, and is very lite on science.  Tests are poorly written, and do not relate to the material covered in class.  Overall a bad instructor in a bad program.

Amy Karch's class is extremely poor quality.  Concepts are overly simplified in the textbook she has written.  As A graduate of a Top 10 university, Graduate classes taught by Karch are worthless.  Tests are not based on facts from an easy textbook, but on abstract NCLEX style questions, that do not correspond to the material covered in Lecture.

Brilliant teacher. Very knowledgeable. Breaks down complex information and makes it entertaining and easy to learn. Uses case scenarios as writing assignments, which forces students to use critical thinking skills to connect ideas.

Extremely difficult class. Tests are impossible to prepare for and there's no partial credit. A perfect score on all the projects and test scores at the median will get you a C. Take this with another professor if possible.

He told us straight up he doesn't like teaching and it shows, his lectures were hard to follow at times and he is intimidating. I recommend watching the old recordings from 2021 they helped a lot. Doesn't respond to emails and has extremely limited office hours. TAs were great tho, start projects early! Hopefully he gets happy again.
The course was hard but a lot of fun!

Great lectures and slides, tests are extremely difficult and make up a lot of the grade. Projects are also very challenging. I was a bit intimated by him at first, but he is quite nice in office hours. Project grading took a while but that is more so a TA thing.

He does not know how to teach at all.

AND THE TWO GRADUATE TA SUCK. I doubt they understand any of the material and grade your exams just by mood.
Horribly irresponsible! He tries to pretend that he cares about the students but actually doesn't at all and don't expect him to reply to your emails :( This whole class does not even make any sense.
He encourages you to reach out to him if you have any questions. However, he did not reply any of my email throughout the semester.

The class materials are so beneficial and he is good at teaching I enjoyed the class a lot. But grading is horrible. Exams are super hard. Assignments are so so hard and you need to study on your own to do them the class materials do not help a lot with assignments. And yet he does not curve the class. I hate his grading criteria but good teacher.
Got above average grades on both my midterm and final and an A average on my projects but got a c+ in the class because he didnt curve the class at all.

Professor Zhu is easily my favorite professor in the CS department. His lecture style is very detailed and manageable, the projects (homework) are difficult but well-designed as they are from the textbook. Does a good job of making computer architecture very accessible. Start projects early, go to class and you'll do great. A really nice guy, too.
Great prof. Class is hard but it's a hard topic. Lectures are dense but good. If you can pay attention through lectures and start the projects early, you'll be alright. Really nice guy too.
Prof Zhu is great! His lectures are clear even though he covers a lot of material, and he's very nice if you reach out. Definitely a hard class though. Start the projects early.

The course is very difficult. You will have to work hard to keep up. However, Zhu's lectures are extremely comprehensive. He makes extremely complex concepts easier to follow. Excellent professor all around. The class cirriculum is super fun, she cares about her students and makes the class engaging. On top of all that, she's an easy grader and gives good feedback. Probably the best professor I've ever had.
Solid 10/10 writing professor. Best Professor I met at this stupid school ever. She really nice and patient to listen all things you talking about:)
My favorite professor!!

Professor Tinelli is amazing, she is more than approachable and is always willing to help. Professor Tinelli is my favorite teacher and truly a gem. I really enjoyed her class; she put a lot of effort into revision feedback, and her assignments were very clear. I highly recommend any class she teaches.

Liz was one of the most fantastic professors I've ever had. If you have a chance, make sure to sign up for any of her classes. She's funny, understanding, and a very fair grader. One of, if not my favorite teacher ever.

An amazing professor. She is always wiling to help and gives fantastic feedback. Doing the assignments were genuinely beneficial to my writing. She also gives good grades as long as you out in some effort.

For a required course for Hajim students, she made it very fun and enjoyable. I loved Liz! Highly recommend taking 273 with her!!

Liz was amazing! The workload was so manageable, and she made an otherwise boring topic seem interesting. She was so understanding and kind, and an easy and clear grader. AMAZING PROF EVER MET if u have chance definitely take hers and enjoy your semester
Love her! She gives great feedback and is very helpful. Show up, participate, do your work, and you'll get an A. She makes writing less intimidating and teaches you very useful skills.
Really an excellent professor! She is very inspired to teach and will give you really useful comment on your paper. I would definitely take her class again in the future!

Goes above and beyond. Phenomenal professor. She is aware that WRT 273 is a mandatory course, but does her best for the students to get the best out of it. She actually cares about the course and the students. Highly recommend.

The only instructor who I would love for life. She helps you to always have hope. The A- during my first semester of this two-part course was a pity but it was largely my own fault. One of the best professors I've ever met! Really inspired me a lot!
This this the best professor since I enter college!

Dr. Holz was my favorite professor out of 4 years of undergrad. He is not only intelligent but also incredibly kind, caring, and witty. Highly recommend taking for all pre-med students especially. Great, engaging professor. Highly recommend Physiology if you are willing to put in the work!

Dr. Holz was very entertaining in his lectures, and he showed he really cared for students. Great class, great professor. Explains things very clearly, and tests are extremely fair (not easy, but your grade will be proportional to your effort). Probably my favorite class so far, and I'm excited to have him for BCS 246. Highly recommend him.

Excellent teacher

Loved his Arabian Nights class. Readings are very enjoyable and he is a fun guy. Very helpful too. I would definitely take another of his classes.

Fantastic lecturer and a cool guy. Lectures are very well organized and easy to understand. Useful office hours too. I think this is his last semester here, but highly recommend him if he sticks around.
Professor Snyder is the best math professor I've had at the uofr. He explains things in a really straightforward and clear way and is super accessible outside of class.

great professor, easy to talk to, relaxed, funny and helpful.
amazing, amazing man. my hero.

Professor Marshall's passion for teaching really stands out from other professors in the department. One of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures are engaging and clear. Syllabus and class organization are clear. Homeworks and tests are difficult but fair and lead to better understanding of the material. He is also very accessible outside of class, even when sick and at home.

Marshall is definitely one of the best lecturers in the physics department. He cares about how students understand course material and REALLY knows how to teach. Very fair homework and exams and idealized grading rubric. Business casual never gets old.

One of the best lecturers I have ever had at university. His homework and exams were incredibly fair, and he always went out of his way, even when sick, to be available and helpful. Made upper-level physics very approachable and understandable. Genuinely a great human and professor.
He clearly knows the material and how to teach it. His exams are not easy, so do not be fooled, but if you do the practice papers, homework and workshops you have will get an A, guaranteed!

I would go out of my way to write a review for very few professors at this school, but Professor Marshall is one of them. Hands down one of the best professors I have had. Provides students with every opportunity to succeed and sincerely cares about their success.
Best professor at the school. His exams are exactly what you expect them to be and he is super organized. Takes students feedback into account and changes course based on what everyone wants.

Professor Marshall at office hour: "I wanted to make this semester being online less suckish for you guys." I usually don't rate my professors, but I highly disagree with the earlier negative reviews. You only get a great guy like Prof. Marshall as a Professor a few times in your college career. He was VERY accommodating.

As a first-year professor, Marshall puts a lot of time and effort into running his course. He is a genuine guy who actually cares about his students and asked for feedback (that he actually listened to and implemented) multiple times throughout the semester. Exams were not ridiculously hard, and it's physics, so nobody should expect a cake walk.
marshall's a good professor. people who complain about him usually complain because they aren't doing well in the class. this is more of a reflection on them than the actual prof.

Professor Marshall seems like a stand-up guy, but he must enjoy his students failing. After literally the WHOLE class complained about the first midterm being too long and too difficult, he proceeded to make midterm 2 the same way. Everyone does so badly that a grade in the 60s is a B. I don't think he knows what the word "fair" means.

Chris is all over the place when teaching physics and skips steps. Makes really hard exams, and very long workshops. He teaches everything in terms of vectors and complicates concepts with derivations of formulas. This course is an intro level course for pre-meds however, definitely feels like a high level physics course. He is not accommodating.

Erin's awesome. By far one of my favorite professors that I've taken at Rochester. She gives great feedback on papers and does an awesome job integrating interesting topics during writing exercises. She's really understanding and wants to see you succeed, which is a rare trait for most teachers at this level. Take her class.

Erin has to be one of the best professors to have, especially as a first year. She clearly shows compassion and empathy for her students making sure they are able to balance their classes along with writing. I also loved the topic int his class and felt that the material was very intriguing and applicable to what I liked.
Like other said, he is disorganized but lectures and class discussions are really interesting!
The professor is great but maybe a little disorganized. The lectures are extremely interesting. The TA was not good and graded the midterm and final incorrectly.

comment: I took this class as a requirement for my breadth for my political science major. Let me say, professor Hein is a very kind professor, however he is very disorganized at times. This class is also only graded on the midterm and final so if you fail one you are practically screwed. There's also pop quizzes for 10% grade, TA is tough grader and rude.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Beware of pop quizzes', 'Test heavy']

comment: Great professor!  Even though he is disorganized, he knows what he teaches and is passionate about it.  Love his lectures and jokes! I don't understand the bad reviews he got on here, I recommend him.

He's disorganized, constantly rambling about unrelated topics, and rarely covers the material we're actually supposed to be learning. The readings and assignments barely get mentioned,  random tangents that have no relevance to the course. he's completely unreachable TAs are no help either the entire experience has been a waste of time and energy.

Professor Goemans would brighthen up my day whenever I went to his classes. He was understanding, compassionate. While he may be slightly disorganised, his lectures are always interesting and the TA's are always great help!

Prof. Goemans  is by far my favorite professor I have ever had. He is both passionate and knowledgeable about IR, and he truly cares for his students. Although his lecture style is slightly disorganized, and he rarely uses slideshows, he makes up for that in his ability to engage the class by telling crazy stories to explain the concepts.

Professor Goemans is the reason I switched my major from IR to Political Science. He is extremely disorganized, hardly responds to emails, and is rarely at office hours. He is quite rude to students and does not respect their personal circumstances. For example, he was very reluctant to let me move my exam for a family funeral. Would not recommend

Goemans is one of my favorite professors. He always turns students' bad days into good ones. He is thoughtful, jovial, and he brings a good sense of liveliness to the classroom. He expects a lot from his students like doing the reading and participating in class actively. You will not regret taking any of his classes!

he is super friendly and always up to chat during office hours. But he is NEVER at office hours. His lectures are interesting but he tends to ramble and after the theoretical parts its's better to just skip the lectures altogether. I honestly don't feel like I learned anything in this course. Very unclear about exam formats and just frustrating

He's generally rough around the edges. Although the class covered a wide range of topics in IR, he made each one not interesting. My ta truly thought me everything I know in our recitations. Hein is hit or miss whether he'll be on-topic or not during class. The class made me question if I wanted to be an IR major.

I would die for Hein. Lots of readings (a loooot) but it's more about getting a general idea than knowing every page. The most genuine, caring professor I've had- cried in his office before the midterm, he coached me through and reassured me with "you're smart, you know this". Lectures are full of ramblings but take what you can and you're fine!

The course definitely provides a good overview of a wide range of topics that are related to the major. The lectures mainly consist of a discussion in which the most important points from the readings are explained or discussed. I recommend using the main book assigned and attending recitations for getting a good grasp of all of these concepts.

comment: Hein seems like a fun guy, but not the type of person you want as a professor. He rambles and mumbles, and assigns way too much reading to keep up with and digest. Personally, this class put me off of IR, but some people in my class seem to enjoy him.

Lectures were entertaining because he's a great guy, but you could honestly not attend a single lecture if you did the reading and went to recitation, because most of the learning happened there. The class was stressful because there was no way you could keep up with the absurd amount of reading assigned, and that was absolutely essential to tests

Prof. Goemans' lectures are scattered, but that makes them entertaining. His humor is interesting and he's VERY  approachable and helpful. He cares about your future and has a lot of outside class advice to give.

Goemans is great. Apparently he was a DJ in Amsterdam in his youth. He's very approachable and helpful with academic life in general, not just his class. He's very passionate which is very inspirational. Make sure you do the readings though and see him during office hours.
A professor who is very involved and excited about what he teaches.  He gets excited for class and does his best to explain everything. Would highly recommend.

Absolutely brilliant, fits the "absent-minded professor" stereotype 110%. He leads great discussions and has interesting ideas as well as a lot of knowledge. He assigns a LOT of reading but is sympathetic if you don't get through 100% and tries adapt to student's tests in other classes. Only negative: Hard to reach outside of office hours.
Greatest Professor ever!!!! I love his class!!!!

Amazing class! I know it's a lot of reading but he's so much fun and he actually levels with you and makes you think think think!! I love it that if someone doesn't know the answer he just stays there until they figure it out, critical thinking! His tests are very easy too.
Taught a great seminar course and really knew how to encourage and maintain good discussion. Reading load was VERY heavy, but made the discussions very interesting. Very knowledgeable professor.

He's extremely difficult to understand. Has a slight accent, but mostly it's that he rambles and writes sloppily on the board. Comes in late to every class. TOO MUCH READING for an intro class (about 150 pages a week). Recitations are pointless.

Lectures are hard to follow, but he is a fun and interesting teacher. Had no idea what to expect for midterm and a lot of reading to do each week. Hard to keep up in the class since the material is not that interesting.

I had heard he would be quirky but I didn't know that he would be disorganized and scatterbrained. This professor does not teach well and while he may know the material his failure to impart it on his students is unacceptable. I would advise not taking this class and pursuing a different IR class that you truly enjoy

Very scattered, and has a difficult time getting to the point. Not clear on what he is teaching and honestly, the TA sessions are worth 5 classes, even though they arent all that great. Avoid this class.

Most people either love and hate him, he's funny and interesting and keeps lectures fairly entertaining; or you can find him scatterbrained, disorganized and hard to follow. I LOVE Goemans, I think he teaches what's relevant to IR, is extremely smart, and loves a good discussion.
Funny guy. Very interested in the material, and motivated teacher. Teaching a difficult class but makes it interesting. Great readings.
Knows and loves to tell almost unbelievable but useful historical anecdotes.

Nice, smart guy, forced to teach a class he really does not believe in (and he'll tell you so). If you really want to understand conflict, though, he gives plenty of hints and clues. Take him seriously, and you'll get more than you ever expected. One on one's are opportunities to really get the most.

Nice guy and pretty funny, but his lectures are all over the place and make no sense.  recitations with the TAs are useless and the final was complete **** that he pulled out of nowhere.  midterm we knew exactly what to expect though.   it was a fun intro class in some ways.

He is extremely knowledgeable but rambles and talking too fast.  Good luck figuring out what you need to do for the w section bc he won't really tell you.  He's really good to talk to one on one though
His intro class is fun and easy. He is knowledgable and very approachable.

Very interesting material and fair amount of reading for an intro class.  His lecture style can be all over the place at times, but he'll crack a joke about it.  Funny prof and a more than fair grader.  Also, he's a smoker which is a big plus!

Very knowledgeable, lectures are hard to follow, tests are fair (though he makes them sound harder than they are). He goes off on tangents but is very enthusiastic. He loves what he teaches. I suggest you go to office hours, he may give you hints on what will be on the test.
Tests do not cover what he teaches.

Hein is a very interesting and knowledgeable professor but his lectures are terrible.  I really didn't learn much from his class.  I think he would be a great professor in a small class setting (less than 30 students).
Nice and funny guy. Makes class entertaining and most importantly eager to teach
No Comments
So FUNNY:)
Extremely hot.I think I am in love.Oh and the class is fun.
Hot sweetie. Very smart. Funny, talks too fast
He does not require workshop attendance! This was awesome for me! I suppose it would be a problem if you sucked at chemistry, though.
I liked his jokes during class.  It wasn't such a bad class.

He was my lab lecturer. I'm sure he's a very intelligent man but all he does is talk about mastermind as a fundamental for learning and logic. Also he sounds really insecure when he talks and I didn't get much out of going to his lectures. Ppts posted online for his lectures.
What the hell is everyone talking about. Turner is quite possibly one of the coolest chem    prof. His exams are easy but tricky. Come on people, he's not that bad.

AVOID THIS TEACHER...FARRAR IS A MILLION TIMES BETTER!!!!This "professor" is an unreasonable person who unnecessarily teaches everything based on biology. I had received a raw score above 870 out of 1000 possible points, a score 100 points higher than another student who also received an A- and 20 points less than a student who received an A...

Turner needs to stop teaching.  He makes you think that you know the material, then throws an impossible exam at you.  He misleads you on the material included on the exam, saying it is from the book when it really isn't.  He is ruining chemistry for me, and only made me laugh (uncontrollably) a total of one time. AVOID AT ALL COST!
Worst professor I've ever had.

Terrible at teaching. He knows what he's talking about, but couldn't explain it for his life. Tests are ridiculous, and memorizing formulas was stupid. Doesn't go over enough examples in class to help with the tests at all. Waves his hands funny, and bobs up and down.
He is a horrible teacher luckily i knew all the information from AP chem

one of the worst classes I have ever taken. so incredibly boring and he doesn't even know what he's talking about. the tests are ridiculously hard (harder than the other chm132 class), but he does put a significant curve on it. all he does is wave his hard around in class with a piece of chalk in it. he doesnt answer questions clearly either
This smug professor might be research prodigy for all I know, but he is a HORRIBLE teaching professor. Unapproachable, poor teaching style, an absolute bigot.
Not very approachable.  A lot of lecture topics were about his research rather than test material. Overall, the class was okay, average amount of work.
No Comments
Tests were ridiculous! This class actually convinced me to stop pursuing chemistry

Class was hard (tests) but definitely doable, may seem boring but shows you if you really like chemistry or not.  Turner's tests are absurd in the fact that he makes you memorize all of the formulas.  Other than that the class was fine.
I disliked this class a lot. The classes were very boring and seemed to have nothing to do with the tests.

EXTREMELY DISORGANIZED! Will not grade anything the whole year. Trust me it is not worth doing the assigned readings for they don't have much to do with actual content. I feel like I wasted my money on this class.

he goes by Brady fletcher, check that for more reviews. he does not teach at all, he reads off of long slideshows. he is also extremely unorganized, he tends to forget what he put on the syllabus. not once did he ever explain how to do projects/group assignments. he doesn't even introduce debate, all just trying to get you to join the debate team.

The professor is quite nice and approachable. It's the last semester he teaches here. 
The weekly assignments and workshops are very helpful as well.

The assignments and projects for this course is the perfect balance between challenging and manageable. Rich is super nice and accessible outside of class through Slack (usually responds within 24hrs). The assignment/project instructions are very organized and easy to understand.

I don't really like computer science but overall Sarkis was funny, kind, and clear, and his assignments were doable, although I often needed assistance from a TA or tutor. My grade is low because I didn't do well on the tests, but the labs, quizzes, and projects were all super manageable.
easy A, but if you really wanna learn something, lol you won't

An autograder determines a large portion of your grade, and he is impossible to reach outside of class. His lectures don't really apply to many of the assignments and he is not good at explaining how to do things despite his clear knowledge in the area.

I had coded before but really enjoyed the class and the assignments. They made me think but I never couldn't figure out the answer. Get started on the project early that definitely makes it easier. He always answered my emails or Slack messages in a timely manner. Go to the last few lectures, he does EC quizzes during the last few lectures.

His CSC 161 course is my best class I have taken. Coming from a non coding background, it helped me a lot in future CS courses and inspire me to minor CS. He's also super fair with hiring TA with an interview process. 10/10

Actually a 3.5. He is a good professor and provides a good intro to programming for students who have not previously done it. As someone who hates coding, I found his class bearable although, the assignments were quite challenging for me. He is personally not that available but has a ton of TAs to help out with assignments.
If you just want your GPA and credits, go to his courses, his class is easy to get a high grade. But if you want to learn something, sorry, no way.

Though get a good grade, but I do not feel I really learned much from him. He really does not care about his students, not reachable. I once sent an email to him asking for how to solve the programming problems. He said he was too busy to help me???What????

NO a good professor. He do not care about student. Unreachable after classes, especially during the online version. He does not respond to your questions and there is no way for you schedule an office hour with him. He really sucks!!!

tough grader  autograder is hit or miss lots of homework  weekly workshops, lab assignments, quizzes, and The Project The workshops were good and helpful until mine kept getting cancelled. Professor lectured super quickly, was difficult to communicate with (ex. not giving space for questions in class), made coding not fun :-(

This class is fabulous. I have no CS background, and this is a very smooth introduction to CS. I also like the project we did. Professor Sarkis is very nice, and he tries to provide extra time to students due to the pandemic. Dont turn in things late, because he gives you plenty of time (If you get a 0, it is your problem.)
Grades Harsh and dont try to argue with him

Sarkis is very knowledgable about CS but isn't t the best teacher. He lectures quickly and sometimes assumes we have prior knowledge of coding. I had no prior knowledge in python or CS so this class was difficult but manageable.

He was terrible about the switch to online classes during the spring 2020 coronavirus outbreak. He ran the class as normal, but assigned more work, and made it harder to access help. He doesn't respect his students and his lack of compassion especially showed during this time. Hard grader and does not accept late work, even during a pandemic.
Highly disorganized and doesn't treat his students with the slightest bit of respect. I'm blown away by how easy this class was. I can tell that he never really thinks ahead. Such a disappointment.

If you are a business student who would like to take data science or computer science double major, I definitely recommend CIS 191for you rather than this course. It is a simple A but I think the only thing covered is really basic python skills and no useful project or modules are introduced. If you want to inject water into your GPA, then take it

Very approachable and cooperative. Spends plenty of time explaining concepts and tries to make sure that everyone is following along. Lectures can get a bit dull, but he tries to liven them up occasionally.

His lectures are really clear for a beginner. Also, he gives a lot of extra credits in the lab assignments and the project. Even when you are unsure about your exam score, you can finish extra credits in the weekly homework to approach A.

Professor Sarkis knows a lot about Python and tries to break the material into feasible content. Lectures are mostly straight-forward. The weekly lab assignments and project can take a while if you don't know what you are doing. Overall, I thought this class was a bit tough for an intro course.

Okay lecturer, didn't make things very exciting. There were a lot of homework assignments which were very difficult for people not used to coding. Towards the end there is a final project on top of the homework which can be a lot if you don't start early.

The lecture is great and he's pretty nice, however!!! The exams are difficult (much more difficult than questions from workshops and homework). There are weekly quizzes, HW, and workshop. Also, there're projects across the semester.

He is a very good teacher and knows a lot about computer science. He is very accessible out of class and is a good teacher. However, if you know nothing about computer science he goes by very fast. You have to take a quiz, attend a workshop and submit a lab each week. Homework and projects are hard for people who don't know how to program.

He's a nice guy but his business modelling course is difficult unless you are a robot. He dives into extremely tough VBA coding techniques before students even have the chance to master the simple ones. It's a useful course but if you don't like coding, it might be tough. HWs are really long. Though, he's understanding with extensions and stuff.

Avoid taking this course with this professor if you can. His lectures are not helpful in understanding the material at all, but attendance is graded. Exams are difficult and graded harshly, especially for an intro-level course. His overall demeanor is unhelpful, and he is not receptive to student feedback.

Worth taking this class a different semester if you can to avoid. Very very difficult and lectures are extremely complicated. Expected to be extremely good at calculus. Averages were incredibly low all semester, but he did curve at the end. Overall, you are better off waiting however long for a different professor or taking it self paced/online

TAKE SELF PACED! Somehow more difficult than organic chemistry or biochem. He asks a lot from his students, and is unhappy with them when they do not deliver. One of the exam averages was a 48%, so his class could not exist without a hefty curve. Definitely not the professor you want to be teaching level 100 physics.
Go through all workshop questions and you will be fine.
Very nice person and made the course a lot easier

E&M self-paced is rewarding IF you have the time for it, I can't imagine trying to learn this material through in-person lectures. The textbook is really good. I suggest going into the class with a friend group where you can discuss study guides and problems. Fair warning you will have to take 24 pre-tests and 12 quizzes AT LEAST to finish content

Phys 121 is a hard class, but Aran made it a little better. He's very clear in lectures and answers as many questions as he can. His demonstrations are helpful but only if you can see them. Some topics covered were not on homework or tests so I'm questioning why they were in lecture. Held test review sessions which were semi-helpful

This class is tough and usually required. Aran made was a good professor the class just simply is a lot of work. Get the text book and be delight and you will get a good grade. Tests are hard but class is curved. His lecture notes are good and he is easy to listen to so go to class but outside studying is needed.

TAKE SELF-PACED!! Lectures constantly felt like a waste of time. You might laugh sometimes, make new friends, and see physics demos, but that's about it. This is the only class where I can say the hw was more fun than attending lecture. Also, we get tested on things we don't discuss or barely discuss. A lot resources exist to help with hw, use them

One of the best science professors I have had. Very clear and extremely organized. Break down concepts and explains them so that students have a clear picture of the topic and can develop a deep understanding.  His workshops and homework adequately prepare you for the exam. Great with administrative stuff and adapting to best help students.

Lectures were presented in a relatively easy way to follow, and he explained the material very well. Posts lectures after class online, met with students who received below a 50 on any midterm exam to make sure they do better on the next few exams. Clicker was not necessary though, but he used it to gauge where in the class everyone was in lecture.

I hated the mandatory attendance. It filled the class with people who didn't really want to be there and sat there playing games on their laptops. As a lecturer the professor wasn't bad. I loved the demonstrations he did almost every class. The way he wrote out everything on his computer using the projector was great. Really helpful.

He's a pretty solid professor. He's a grad student so he doesn't have much experience teaching but he knows what he's doing. I really like the way he teaches. Calculus 2 is a hard course but the way he taught was pretty clear and effective for me. He's funny and a very nice person.

Really solid professor. I've found his explanations of calculus concepts and processes very clear and John Lin tells you everything you need to know to prepare for exams. His office hours are great too, especially for help on webworks. Overall the math department is tough at this school, and I wouldn't have gotten the grade I had without him!
very caring professor

Thrilled with Prof. Demirhan's course in Spring. Math 282 Initially seemed daunting, but it turned out to be enriching and beneficial. He is a very approachable professor, his office hours are conveniently scheduled before hw deadlines. You will learn a lot, so definitely go to his session. Possibly he's only prof in math dept doing review sessions
He was an excellent professor. He teaches everything in detail and would be happy to help you with any questions.

I took the writing version of MATH200 to fulfill my upper writing requirement. He was so nice that I got extra help for both of my papers. He was always available no matter after class or during his office hours to talk about homework problems as well as class contents. Highly recommended to take his class.
Breaking down and going through problems helped me a great deal. After office hours, I was normally able to have a better idea of how to solve problems.

I'm in discrete, he gets himself confused during lectures and has never ended class on time. He can be quite hard to understand at times but if you ask him to clarify he will and make sure you understand it more than you probably wanted to. His mannerisms are so adorable and he's unintentionally hilarious you can't help but love the guy.

He's not the best type of math professors, but definitely a good one. Easily understandable lectures and are always happy to help outside classroom. If you understand everything on your homework and sample exams, you will have no problems on the tests. Remember that practice makes perfect.

You can tell that he is a genuinely nice guy but he should not be a professor. The lectures are super disorganized and all he does is read directly from the textbook and write it on the board. Overall, if you don't read the textbook/teach yourself you're not going to know what's going on...
Lectures are incredibly hard to stay awake through.

Unintelligible. Unecessarily made things very complicated which should have been very simple. Grading did not account for people who dropped course due to its difficulty. Fortunately, she discovered that teaching is not her forte and is now working at the Federal Reserve.

Seems to overcomplicate things a lot, she could make everything a lot more straightforward if she wanted to.  Does not seem to communicate with the TAs, so everyone teaches a different method of doing problems, which really sucks when the material is confusing already.
Part of the problem is with the statistical economics course itself, but she really doesn't help much with her explanations of the material. A bit cold and distant.
Made economics "beautiful" if you know what I'm saying.
She is great! Very helpful and knows the material very well!

She makes mistakes on the board all the time, and had to be corrected by people in the class.  She wants you to do well, and is willing ot talk to you about it, but is not very clear or all that helpful in and outside class.
Thick accent.  Good luck.

The “full non-tenure-track professor” who is trying to prove himself to his superiors. He joins other professors' projects so that he can have publications to his name, but he seems unable to complete a project on his own.
this professor made sense and was kind
The so-called 'full professor' data scientist who doesn't have any data to do research.
I thought there were much better time series courses than the one he is teaching. I wish I had taken the other class I was considering: Ancient History of Belt Making in the Developing World.
This untenured professor claims that he is a tenured professor on his website - actually, he is not. University administration should prevent him from making false claims.
I can sense that he is jealous of many other real researchers in his department. (Ajay Anand is not a real researcher).
Low quality researcher. He can probably be a good elementary school teacher.
He writes his own comments.
A very bad teacher. He made only superficial comments about my final project.
Teaches clearly and easy to understand
He was a good and clear teacher
NEVER on campus. It is very difficult to find him if you want to ask him questions about the course material.
He writes his own 'positive' reviews, and whenever others point this out, he asks the admin to remove the comment.
I don't know why the university hired this guy. I don't understand UofR's policies. University education is a scam.
good professor
Professor Anand is an extremely approachable and knowledgeable professor. The assignments are relevant and stretch your learning. Would recommend any class that he is teaching
He is respectful to his students and his expectations are often clear. This course is a difficult course to teach and he does a good job.

Prof Anand was very knowledgeable and his lectures seemed well thought out. I enjoyed the course and although it was a little hard, Prof was available to answer any questions and help us understand the materials. I have since graduated and Prof Anand's course was helpful during interviews. I would highly recommend the course.

Prof. Anand explains the content clearly and the course is organized well. The course covers statistical and deep learning methods for time-series analysis which was very useful. The professor is very approachable and responds to emails promptly.
Great professor!
He just tries to complete the semester with minimum potential effort on his behalf.
From his interactions with the students I realized that Prof. Anand doesn't understand much about research.

Professor Anand appears indifferent to the fair distribution of work among group members in the capstone project. Whenever complaints arise, he tends to overlook them. Additionally, during his office hours, he is often unavailable.

This guy has been given a semi-important position at a university because of his experience at a Tier 2 company. UofRochester should hire better professors with a better research background. Having gray hair and an old belt shouldn't qualify you for a professorship at UofR.

His lectures are satisfactory, but he did not provide grading rubrics. Despite sending many emails throughout the semester, I received no responses. When I questioned the grading of my final project and attempted to schedule a meeting, my emails were ignored. He changed the group project to an individual one midway through the semester.
Completely inaccessible outside class, never responds to email. Many points were deducted from the final project without any feedback at all.
Not the best course I have every taken, and not the worst course I have ever taken. Slightly less than mediocre - you can take it, because there aren't too many options in the department anyway.
Fair course for data science, statistics, and other STEM major students and for those who want to go data data-related industries. Lots of extra credits for undergrads.

I have been a student in his capstone course, and he simply doesn't know most of the tools a modern data scientist needs to know. During our meetings, he wasn't able to make any productive comments about our project. He just comments on how 'nice' the visuals look and cannot say anything substantive about the content or the technical aspects.
Less than average.
OK.
Falling asleep is guaranteed.

I did learn a lot from his lectures, but I have to say that his exams are just terrible. Me and my friends spent hours studying the materials, understanding every formula on the lecture notes, but none of them showed up on the exam sheet. My double sided hand written cheat sheet looks like a joke to me.

Another professor with NO charisma at all. His usual way of teaching:

Anand: Oh, great. Where did you use it?

Whenever Prof. Anand is done with a lecture, he starts talking about useless stuff to fill up class time. He provides excellent lectures on how to bore students to death.
Prof. Anand is a somewhat good professor.

Very good class. Very fit professor. He can fight with two bears using his bare hands. He can lift two cars at once if he wants to. And he can whisper beautiful songs into the ears of lions to control them.
Fairly good course for Data Science majors
The course was offered for the first time when I took it and hence it lacked a bit of a course structure and timeline. But overall the course is great and the professor teaches it really well.

Far too much to memorize and you wind up feeling incompetent. Wasn't there half the time, with the substitute being useful if not as dry as the Gobi desert. When he's there he's a great guy and really knows what he's talking about. He obviously doesn't want to be teaching an intro class, though.
Smart guy, funny lecturer, but the class has so much stuff you have to memorize. Not very available as far as office hours and email contact goes

The content was hard, but it was a privilege to be in the presence of Pouget. He clearly knew what he was talking about, and he speaks well. He wasn't there all the time, but his co-Professor was just as qualified. Loved him.
There was a lot of material, but I'm so amazed by how much I learned.  Dr. Pouget was organized and really passionate about BCS.  He was a lot funnier than I expected.

This class is based on memorization, but if you start 2-3 weeks before the exam and cover a little every few days, you should do well.  I was closer to the B range, but he was nice enough to move me to a B+. (This might not work for everyone-special circumstances) The material's dense, but he does his best to liven up class with a few jokes

Challenging class. Lot's of informations to memorize. I found reading the book quite helpful for reviewing before taking midterms. Eventhough his lecture slides are online, attending to class is crucial to pass the class. I personally enjoyed this class and learned many informations. I would highly recommend this class.

This class is tough. The midterms are based entirely on  the lectures so reading the book was pointless. I found the notes he posted online to be very helpful when it came time to studying. The final exam was pretty brutal. Overall, I learned a ton in a very short amount of time and Pouget always tries to thrown in some jokes to keep us entertained

This is not an easy course, theres a LOT of material to be remembered...but Pouget somehow gets the information across and its not terribly hard to get an A if you spend a great amount of time studying. Tests are all multiplce choice, but r very detailed and tricky.

Knows his material, but his accent--he's french--sometimes prevents clear understanding.  And, as a lecture class in a large dark room with padded seats at 9:40 in the morning?  Zzzzzzz...  literally.
Good professor considering the amount of information given and class sizee.  Just wish he placed more priority on the class and used less guest lecturers.
He got me excited about BCS!   When I came into the class, I didn't even know what BCS really was.  Now, I want to major in it!

Alex is an expert in computational modeling. He expects a high level of performance. The syllabus claims the class is for all math skills but be prepared for lots of derivations and much more intensity than Robbie's 512 course.  CS446 Foundations of AI is a good complement to the course. You can learn quite a bit about modeling if you work hard.
YEA. pougets cool. amazone dote coame, axone, things of that nature. 110s better than 111
Pouget is awesome. He is really cool and funny (without trying to be). Kinda awkward and French. Lectures are interesting and clear. He does a great job. Tests are multiple choice and easy.
Material is great, he doesn't teach much... which is a shame because his lectures are easy to follow, but he seems to pick good guest lecturers

he taught less than half of our classes

Very nice and caring professor who wants you to succeed. His lectures were somewhat helpful, but he was often unclear and didn't highlight the main ideas. Workshop was extremely helpful and was truly where I learned the concepts. However, I found his tests to be extremely fair. (4 midterms with one drop and a final)

His lectures are well organized and build off each other. For me the information took a lot of time to digest. I rewrote my lecture notes, rewatched the lectures, and explained concepts to friends. Workshops were one of the best places to harness the information, but it requires engagement and not being afraid to try and get problems wrong.

his lectures are not very helpful. you understand the material from the workshops. I highly recommend going to all of them. his grading scheme is ambiguous.  his exams are hard you will have to learn the content elsewhere. go to the review sessions they are really helpful.

The lectures were not particularly helpful for tests, mostly learned the material on my own through other resources. Tests were very difficult but manageable if you studied a lot and workshops also helped a lot.

Overall, a decent professor. Lectures are strange in that you have to seek outside resources to really understand the material. Workshops are crucial. The same goes for practice exams. I found that grading is based on how closely it resembles the key, so make sure you memorize the wording used for the keys on past practice exams.

Dinnocenzo is an decent professor, and he clearly cares about his students. However, his lectures are really difficult to follow. In lecture, he assumes you have knowledge from the textbook, so if you don't read before the lecture it will likely not make sense. Review past exams and rote memorize and you will be fine, but it is not an easy class.

Dinno is a warm person who wants you to succeed and I suggest going to office hours where he's far more helpful. That being said, his lectures leave a lot of blanks so you have to do a lot of reading from other sources. He says the textbook but if you use orgo tutor vids and the masterochem site to make notes, you'll be fine. Do the practice tests!

Dr. Dinnocenzo is kind and knowledgeable, but is delusional and unorganized in the lectures. The lecture notes are not helpful tools to study for exams. Go to workshops and do all practice exams in advance, you will be fine. Also try to remember the reaction itself first before trying to understand the mechanism.

Dr.D's class notes are not very helpful for exam prep.Class is tough. Grades only based on 3 exams and final. There's a lot to learn and not enough time to learn it- make sure to keep to a strict study schedule. I think for OChem it's important to memorize first then TRY to understand material and then do practice.Exams get harder with every year.

Dr. Dino is great, but the class is challenging for everyone. You have to change your study style. He doesn't explain everything, more like key points. You must read the textbook to do well. Go to workshop, and take advantage of help sessions by TAs. You must heavily study past exams, use flashcards, and watch youtube. You will thank me later

Dr. D is a very kind and knowledgable professor. He obviously cares about his student's success and always makes himself available for questions. That being said, this course is very challenging and it is frustrating that your grade is only determined based on exams, which are graded harshly.He struggles with simplifying concepts that are difficult

This guy - although by nature very caring - is not merciful at all. You have to submit your test for regrade IMMEDIATELY after receiving them back, so forget about it if you are unwell and cannot make it to class. Even if you qualify for partial credit, you won't receive it because he is a tough grader as well.

He's a decent professor and really nice guy, but I can't stand the way he lectures. The notes he writes down are basically useless to study from and he skips over the most basic concepts expecting you to know them. Tests are also pretty hard but the curve is nice. Great guy, but not a great professor.
Womp womp. The man cannot teach.

He does not care about students at all. I missed exam 2 in his class, as one of the exams can be dropped so I wasn't worried about that. When it went on to exam 3, I had to request make-up due to medical reasons and he did not allow it, and it was just because  "he cannot give make-up to all students because it is too much work"

Dinnocenzo's lectures are great but they will not make sense if one just rote memorizes. They are taught in a way that requires thinking about how to organize notes in a logical way, but that helped me understand the material even more than with just memorization. Grading is extremely exam heavy, but all orgo courses are. Office Hours are great.

Professor Dinnocenzo is very knowledgable but an awful teacher. His lectures are disorganized and hard to follow. He skips over certain topics and explanations. He is very stingy with partial credit. getting regrades is necessary because of how many mistakes are made when exams are graded but requesting them is a complete mess.

comment: Honestly don't get all the positive ratings on here. He is a terrible professor who has terrible lecture recordings and you can't see the board at all in the recordings. He's also a harsh grader on exams and the entire class is graded solely based on exams. Do not recommend at all.

Dinnocenzo is a good professor. He knows what he's talking about, but is delusional when it comes to how he teaches. He considers this course a "liberal arts course", but if you have a different way of thinking about something you are marked wrong. He is the most unaccommodating professor I have met for numerous reasons I can't fit in this text box

He only grades on exams and nothing else, so you're screwed if you have test anxiety. He also only accepts 1 type of answer to a problem on the exams, so if your mechanism or explanation is right but isn't what is on the answer key, you get 0 points. The only times I did well on exams was when I memorized answers provided on practice exams.

Prof Dinnocenzo is an expert in orgo but not good at teaching it. His lectures are very unorganized and hard to follow. I spent most of the class teaching myself and learning through workshop. I cannot wait for this class to be over.

Genuinely the most uncaring professor I have ever had the displeasure of being taught by. His lectures have no direction, and since he barely holds office hours, most of lecture is spent by students asking questions that are for irrelevant material/prior exams. Met with him about an exam and he agreed I was correct but refused to give points back.

Refuses to hold office hours before regrades (regrade period is during 50 min class), meaning if you write a plausible mechanism that doesn't match the test key, you will get the entire problem wrong. Never responds to emails OR requests to meet if you cant make office hours (which are during an orgo lab time btw). Knows Orgo but a BAD professor.

This class is so traumatizing and prof dinnocenzo does not make it any easier. Lectures are so unclear and all over the place. The only grades are the tests, but you can drop your lowest midterm. The only reason I am passing is because the tests are very similar to the practice tests. Grading scheme and regrade policy is awful.

This is 100% a tough class, but if you put in the time outside of class you will be just fine. Lectures are a bit dense because there is a lot of information to get through. My best advice is to stay caught up with the class so you are not trying to learn a month's worth of information the night before the exam. Also, workshops are supper helpful.

I loved Dr. Dinnocenzo! His tests always have similar style questions so you sort of know what to expect on the tests. His lectures are relatively clear and he is really good about telling you exactly what you need to know for the tests. Be careful though because this class is only test based so they really matter, but you can drop the lowest one.

comment: Organic chemistry is dreaded by most students but Professor Dinnocenzo makes the subject accessible. He provides affirmation, grades fairly, and dispels myths students may have about o-chem. Reading the textbook is necessary and lectures can be a bit dry, but put in the effort and you'll find that you'll have learned a lot in the end.

Prof. Dinnocenzo developed the first-year orgo course and teaches it with great precision and efficiency. He genuinely cares about his students, and provides many great resources outside of class. Workshops are excellent preparation for the tests, but you will need to put in work. One of the most rewarding courses I've taken.

Dr. Dinnocenzo was a fantastic professor. Organic chemistry was certainly a difficult class, but if you worked hard it paid off. He would offer study advice during his lectures that was ultimately very useful and would oftentimes stay long after class ended to answer student questions. It was clear to see that he wanted students to succeed.

Organic chemistry is hard, but it's a lot easier with Professor Dinnocenzo. Straightforward class and had A's for nearly every prelim expect the final (a 7-10 pm exam). He gives out practice exams that are very similar to the exam you would get without surprise. Very kind, teaches very well and was a pleasure to have. 100%better than 2nd year orgo
He's really nice and very accessible outside of class. Email him for office hours, which are super helpful. The textbook problems aren't that helpful, but I recommend reading it.

Class is very one-directional, traditional lecture style, primarily based on examples and very hard to follow in my opinion. Grade is entirely made up of tests. Prof is very caring and does not believe in stupid students, only those who haven't found their right study method yet, which is nice.

Professor Dinnocenzo really cares about his students. He's extremely useful when you ask him questions during office hours so I highly recommend doing so (he doesn't make you feel stupid at all)! He always talks about test taking/studying strategies but teaches at a fairly fast pace so it's important to read the textbook for extra clarification.

comment: Professor Dinnocenzo's CHM171 is really hard----even for those who got 5 in AP CHM. Some students drop the class and go to 131. The reason is the pace in class is very fast and he supposed you to have finished textbook readings which are impossible to be finished before class. But he is very patient when answering your Qs. Wrk leaders & TA awesome

Lectures are somewhat boring, but the class is great overall. He is very kind if you talk to him in the right way and clearly wants his students to succeed. The TAs will help alot, and he always has great TAs.

As a lab lecture professor, he was decent. Lectures were uninteresting but not unbearable, and group work made lab understandable. He clearly wants students to succeed, although he is less forgiving than you might hope. Overall, he did a decent job

I started freshman orgo thinking I was going to fail (no really). I ended up with an A and became a TA for organic chemistry. I worked hard, but Professor Dinnocenzo definitely helped me ALOT. He was always available for questions and he never made me feel stupid. He is hands down, the best professor I have had at UR.

Orgo is impossible, but dinnocenzo is really good at explaining it.  expect a ton of work reading the textbook and doing extra problems.  class pace is really fast, but he tries to answer questions before moving on.

Organic Chemistry is hard, but Dinno loves it so much, and really wants his students to love it to. He really wants students to exceed. Exams were tricky because explanations got you all the credit for the question, and but if you do all the workshops, practice exams, reading, and homework, it'll pay off. Funny guy. Good class (for orgo).
Dinno is a great professor. He really cares about his students. Tends to weed out the weaklings in the beginning, but seems to lighten up a bit as the semester goes on. Just be sure not to give up.

I didn't do very well at the beginning of the semester, but managed to rock an A on the final. I think the class actually gets easier and easier because it comes full circle and all the concepts start to make sense and become applicable. Great professor.

hate chem, detest his exams, but can't say prof isn't good.  nice, a little uptight and intense but loves orgo and teaching thats for sure.  Wonder what he does in his spare time --- Props b/c u can tell he always prepares for each lecture thoroughly.

He's a good professor and dedicated to helping students (you won't find many professors who are willing to hold 3 hr review sessions on weekends). But his exams are difficult and he's a very strict grader. He's one those guys whose life outside of school/chemistry is hard to picture.
Lecture had a poor focus/direction.  Workshops were awful.  Book reading had nothing to do with exams.  Exams were impossible.

This guy must be from the gods...by far the best professor Ive ever has in my history at Rochester. His concern with students understanding of the material is incredible. He stays way after his office hours for his students and comes in on the weekends to reteach material that we didnt quite get. Outstanding listener, outstanding professor!!!

Calls students who ask for help "irresponsible," and spends more time talking about how he won't fill our heads than he spends teaching the concepts. A sign of a good teacher is not getting upset when people do poorly, but rather having a class where people are able to excel, which very few people do.

Amazing teacher; the best I've had in this school yet.  Incredibly passionate about Organic Chemistry and genuinely wants students to do well.  He gets upset when class averages are a little low because he feels he didn't get through to people; the sign of a great teacher.
Always available for help.
Good teacher, thorough.  Very informative
AWESOME: smart, nice, understanding. Student's are almost as important as chemistry is to him:). Cool research, lab full of fancy glassware and tools! Lets me play with the laser.

his handwriting is amazingly neat!  also, if you get bored in class, watch him use the chalk.  he only uses new pieces, so there's a massive pile of barely used chalk at the end of the board!  haha  he wants everyone to do well.  very nice and encouraging.
great teacher, nice handwriting...
He is very smart and a good lecturer.  However he talks down to his students and mocks them openly in class for proposing incorrect answers.
