Professor Barnett is a really great guy who sometimes makes funny comments in lectures. Inorganic chemistry with him is difficult, but he implements a generous curve and (at least my year) pretty lenient grading on exams. His exams can be tough, but are mostly fair. Make sure to study problem sets, lecture, and textbook. Again, an amazing person.

I love Barnett. His lectures are super clear, and he puts in the effort to make the class organized and functional. Even when his tests were difficult, he was very fair in regards to test material and his expectations. Overall, he was a fantastic professor. I would recommend getting help for the homework either through office hours or UCS.

Took this class in 2022, disappointed Barnett's rating was "low" (i.e.,3.8). This guy is chill af and I love him. I wish he was my dad. As for the class, it's tough. You must study everything for an A: lectures, textbook, workshops, office hours. Missing lecture is brutal cause it's not recorded. Go to as many office hours as possible.

Dr. Barrentt is super knowledgeable!  While not a chem major, I really enjoyed his class. His tests were reasonable and the homework helped me prepare for the exams. His lectures were nicely organized and difficult concepts were explained clearly. He provided many opportunities to get help and is an understanding and funny person overall.

Professor Barnett is very knowledgeable and passionate about the material. His exam questions are fair and test the material well, but sometimes the tests are too long. He records lectures but only makes them available near exam dates, so attending lectures is important. An understanding person and a funny professor. Overall a pretty good class.

Prepare for no notes or recorded lectures being available outside of class. Even if you have a doctor's note, he will not provide lecture material, so make friends in class you can get notes from. Also, homework must be turned in during lecture time as a hard copy. This class is brute memorization (no periodic table given on first exam)
The best econ professor ever.
Professor Bottan is one of the best professors I've had so far. Incredibly helpful.

Took Econ 180. Tests were all MC based on lecture. Very accessible out of class and very nice. Minor accent but understandable. The recitations were optional but helpful. Lecture slides were easy to read and study from. Good luck to those who are studying under her. She is moving to a different university.

Available and caring professor who does a really great job of explaining harder to comprehend topics. Has really solid lecture slides too. I do NOT recommend this professor if you do not plan on going to lecture, take this course with a different professor instead if you don't go to lecture. Has a minor accent, but she is usually understandable.

Dr. Bottan is a solid professor. She is so nice and caring. Definitely utilize her office hours as she is very good at giving 1 on 1 help. Her main flaw is that she tends to lecture quickly and often explains equations and graphs in an overcomplicated manner. Recitation, the text book, and office hours are great at clarifying the lecture.
Manageable tests. Put in effort, do well. Nice and helpful during office hours.
great professor

She is very caring and open to questions. Homework don't take a lot of time and the exams are pretty easy. My only criticism is that she sometimes goes too fast in the lectures and her explanation of graphs are too complicated, so be ready take notes on your own after class to catch up.

Great professor, very good explaining and her power point slides are great. During class she goes through the slides, solves problems along with the class, and makes participation engaging. 

Fair grading scale, lots of homework but they are useful for practice, exams are medium difficulty, and she records all lectures, which is very useful.

you can never go to recitation, hardly attend class & cram hours before exam and still get high 90s every time, because 
1. slides are through 
2. exams are exactly what's on the slides
despite all this i still wouldn't say she teaches at surface level, and she tries to make lectures engaging when i did go hence the rating

Her coursework load isn't heavy—three exams per semester plus one case study. But the exams are very strange. There's no grading curve for the midterm, and initially she told me I could replace a low midterm grade with a higher one, only to later say it wasn't possible. This made me feel deceived.

For ECON108 not 207. Prof. Bottan is very kind and knows her stuff. She was always supportive during office hours and overly generous to her students. Her exams are challenging mainly due to the material. Sometimes her lectures were a bit convoluted, but going to recitation was helpful. Her lectures are also very by the book and could get boring.

I took Bottan's ECON 207 as a freshman, she was very nice, caring, and approachable. Her lectures were engaging, the content was understandable. All hw were multiple choice, and each one had two attempts to try. The midterms were not hard, the final is a bit challenging. I asked her for a transfer recommendation, and I will miss her.
She gives tons of extra credits and the course is just not hard.

Contrary to other reviews, the exams were NOT difficult. In fact, they were almost 1:1 to the practice exams. Lecture notes are detailed, and there is a 1% final grade extra credit for answering questions in class. HW was 10 MC with two tries (lol). She is very attentive and will pour extra effort into answering questions in and out of class. 10/10

Good teacher who cares about students and listens to feedback. Lectures are engaging but sometimes lack clarity in connecting ideas, with vague examples and confusing edge cases. The grading is skewed, with 75% based on tests, including a difficult final worth 35%. Study consistently and attend recitations to do well.
Really nice professor, wants you to succeed. Midterms are very clear, final is quite a bit harder but nonetheless the class is doable. Professor is very approachable and open to listening.

She is in charge of the lab module of BME 210, not the whole course. She gives equivocal instructions in the lab and will deduct a lot of points for any minor "errors" in your report. I quote-unquote the word error because there is actually no rubric, and no one really knows what she wants us to put down.
Sadly, to BME students, she is unavoidable.

Genuinely the worst professor I've had. Extremely hard to get in contact with bc she changes her office hours without warning and neglects her emails. Gives quizzes with little explanation of their contents. Instructions for project were unclear and she neglected to give us needed material. Takes weeks or months to enter grades for each assignment.

Straight up horrible. Gave us an extremely hard project with confusing instructions and no rubric. Criticized us in front of our entire lab about not having things in our project, yet she didn't tell us we needed that in our project. Took 2 months for her to grade our midterm #1 because her computer got "hacked". Would make students cry.

Overall, she's absolutely dreadful. Every email she sends gives me unnecessary anxiety because it's something new we were supposed to know but didn't, and it's sent way too late. Her assignments and quizzes are stupid hard and is too much for a 2-credit class. Disappointment.

She assigns projects that are worth 20% of our grade as if they came up to her in a dream. She plans as she goes, which stresses us out even more because she will email new pieces of information that are critical to finishing the project less than a week before it's due, and then will take her frustration out on us with her attitude.

She's as unavailable as my dad, but will pretend that she isn't and will turn it around on us when we struggle. Everyone emails her with questions. She probably deletes them to complain that she gets no emails to play the victim. She also will hold office hours, but the majority of the time is spent trying to figure out why her door is locked.

She is genuinely the most uninformative and last-minute professor on the planet. She attempts to teach, but the slides she posts, if she posts, are empty, and we all end up learning a grand total of nothing. With this knowledge of nothing she has bestowed upon us, she gives out quizzes that expect us to read her mind or think like MATLAB. (1)

comment: for BME 201P: impossible to pass any quiz or exam unless you can read her mind to tell what she's grading on. does not take feedback. doesn't release assignment grades until months later so you have no clue how you're doing in the class. doesn't respond to emails or show up to class.

Dr. Ganeshan was okay when it came to explaining concepts when they were first introduced, but if you forgot something a week later, she would look at and talk to you like you were stupid. She treated the material as if it was common knowledge for everyone after we had just learned it for the first time.

Horrible teacher with an insane amount of course load. Following the instructions on the lab report gets you a 70. Lab reports are long and irrelevant. She prepares you to join her life mission to stay in a lab and replicate smarter people's discoveries and basing your entire career on it. Be prepared to hate BME to the guts after this class.

Hands down one of my least favorite professors. Labs are a ridiculous amount of work for no reason but have little to no purpose. Barely teaches you anything, and often expects for you to know exactly what you are doing. Instructions for labs are often unclear, so you do not know whether or not you are doing the correct thing.

Veena was my instructor in the Signals class. She was very approachable when I needed her help with the writing part which is the difficult part of the course. She was good about giving clear feedback on reports. My first graded report was hard to accept but after the second one I saw how much I improved as a writer.

Veena Ganeshan is a professor for the super hard Circuits class. It is always hard to understand the lab since it is so much ahead of the class. Veena helped me on so many occasions when I was having trouble and guided me through each step. We had a full class but she still gave me the time I needed for each question.
She doesn't help students and if you ask her a question she will berate you instead of actually helping. She also doesn't respect social distancing and gets within 6 feet of you.
Unclear grading. Get marked down for things she never asked for to begin with and were never in the assignment. Posts things late and then expects you to get them done in the same amount of time.

Veena is the lab administrator for a few BME courses and is just plainly a bad teacher. She offers very, very unclear instructions and if the equipment is faulty during lab, instead of helping you fix it, blames you for not knowing what to do (even if she also does not know how to fix it). Just the worst teacher I've ever had, avoid if possible.

Classes discussion-based, very effective, every student led 1-2, encouraging strong understanding of material. Makes sure everyone understands stuff b4 moving on, participation always felt encouraged, welcoming environment. Thorough feedback. Personally met with each student 2x during semester. Lots of freedom to pursue interests in final project.

MATH-171 was my introduction to higher math. I found the course incredibly difficult, but am very glad that I took it with this professor. He packed an insane amount of information into each lecture, which was at times overwhelming, but in the long run rewarding. The textbook, Calculus by Michael Spivak, will be your saving grace.
He writes faster than I can think omg. The only reason this class is somewhat doable is because of the workshops and the good TAs. still not easy tho
He ruined my life :)))))))))))))
There are many abstract examples in his class, but if you can understand them, you will find the exam pretty easy

just a heads up, while sevak is def one of the better math profs out there, 150 is seriously no joke. he is an amazing teacher but i found the material so ridiculously difficult that by a certain point even with the office hours (which were v helpful ALWAYS TAKE ADVANTAGE OF) i still had to google for so so much clarification by the end of semester

Excellent professor! If you need to take Math 150, definitely take it with Sevak. He explains things very thoroughly and clearly during class and is very accessible. The class itself can be challenging at times, but I barely needed to touch the textbook at all - his lectures were usually enough to understand the material.

Take MATH 150 with no one but professor Sevak! He creates a laid-back classroom atmosphere and does a great job at explaining concepts and distinctions. He also tries to answer every question raised in the classroom and makes sure students understand his responses.

Sevak is my favorite professor during the freshman year. I barely did anything for the course rather than his lectures and they were more than enough. Although the topic are difficult sevak made them easy so that I got an A without studying much. If you are going to take Math150 then take it with no one but Sevak! He gives it only in fall though

He is my best professor so far! Clear and helpful lecture and notes. I recommend skim the important or complicate sections of the textbook. Go to every office hours of him even without questions! In addition, if you know how to solve every problem from the past exams, you will surely get an A.
The best professor for math 150! Very accessible and willing to help during office hours.
The best professor ever! If you want to take math 150, take his class! He is willing to help outside class. You can ask anything related to the course during office hours.
Great professor! Very accessible! Best Professor for MTH150.

comment: He is a good professor and does really care about his students. The lecture material is quite complicated, but he does his best to explain it. He's helpful during office hours and the webwork is very helpful. Make sure to do the webwork and practice exams. He kind of has a thick accent, but he's willing to repeat what he said.

If you have to take MTH150, make sure it is with Sevak. He is by far the best of the four teachers who teach it. The subject is extremely difficult, there's no getting around that, but he does it the best. You walk in, and the lecture starts immediately, and goes until the minute class is over. He never wastes a second of your time.
mth202 is hard class but he is very good teacher

Very good professor. Make sure you do your webwork and practice tests before each exam to do really well. Not the easiest class, but going to Sevak's office hours and doing your work definitely makes this class very doable.

Easy to follow along and always willing to answer questions. 162 is a very tough course but Sevak is one of the better professors to prepare you for exams. Use the textbook to supplement before or after lecture

Sevak is generally a good professor, not the best out there but better than most of those teaching MTH 162. The class itself is pretty hard but I think he's one of the most helpful professors. Use his office hours, he's really useful in them
Very helpful and approachable. Gives lots of examples, and is always willing to go over a concept again in class. However, you will have to go through the textbook to supplement your learning.

Explains concepts really well through examples. Attending his lectures and practicing problems from the textbook helps. He is extremely helpful during office hours and is ready to explain a concept from scratch.
Flies through lectures but if you ask him to explain will take the time and provide extra examples. Expects you to try it on your own and read the book first.
He is great.

He is very funny and lively, so "lecture" is entertaining. He's also very nice and approachable. The workload really isn't much at all- just a couple research projects take a while. He's also pretty clear, and tests/quizzes are pretty fair.

Ken is an interesting guy. The class is not easy because you need to do the work. The drag of the class has to be the tests about the book and vocabulary. Ken is a very good professor. He is extremely approachable and possibly the nicest professor I have had here. Tough class. Lots of work but I learned more than I have in many others. People complain about his style, but pay attention and it all comes together ...

Ken is super funny and he has tons of hilarious stories. Lectures are not the easiest to follow.Notes on the board are hard to understand but he will always answer questions during or after class. Although an extremely funny guy, Ken's lecture notes and style is very messy and difficult to understand. This class is a ****load of work!!! BE WARNED! If you can do it all, you will do well. Do not get behind, and attend every class. Ken is amazing, and definitely makes the course worth it. Ken is a funny guy and a good teacher.  He teaches in a very down-to-earth style that makes the material much less intimidating.  Assignments take some work, but they aren't too difficult. Very nice, friendly, funny.  Not a great teacher.  It's kind of unclear how knowledgeable he is about his field, but he does have pretty impressive credentials.  The class was boring to me, but he did his best to keep it interesting.

He's the man. A very interesting and funny guy who teaches a good class. He knows his stuff as well. Class starts out a little boring but gets good once it gets going. Blankenship started off rough and gave us a lot of homework/tests that we didn't really have the capacity to finish, but that's just because he came to a River Campus elective class with an Eastman degree. Michael was a very nice guy, but was very unorganized making it difficult to know what we were learning about. We never followed the syllabus and he moved at such a fast pace, we often had to redo tests and quizzes because he eventually realized the class did not understand the concepts yet.

Dr. Dove was my favorite professor this semester by far. She was everything you would ask for in a teacher and more. She was accessible, clear, and a very fair grader. Dr Dove was an AMAZING human event professor. Kind and helpful, she was excellent at facilitating group discussion and creating a class that was surprisingly very interesting. Dr. D. has a very interesting approach to her subject and you can tell that she is passionate about it.  It's easy to ask her questions and she is more than willing to help in any way that she can.  She provided the class with entertaining projects and helped us to improve in areas we were struggling in.

she's a pretty cool and down to earth professor. helpful when you need her and is always smiles. she tries pretty hard to make the class interesting and the films for the class are pretty good as well as the paper topics. she grades pretty fair- you get the grade you deserve

Semi-regular homework assignments, dull lectures, only one credit. This add on was begging to be treated like a class in its own right. Just go to lab and do the assignments and you will do fine. They removed the need to do lab reports so it'll be a breeze.

Terrible teacher.

Dr Stanford is a very good instructor.  She is very well prepared and presents things in a organized manner. She does make you work for a good grade,

Geier Is AWESOME! Really nice guy. I took his intro greek class as a potential for my cluster and his classes has definitely been some of my favorites. His classes are what you think college classes should be like...before you actually start college

Honestly I think Prof.Jay is great. She is helpful and energetic. She encourage you to go OH everytime. But since it's a huge lecture. It can't make sure everyone get treated. I had this professor for MATH 162, one of the hardest classes in the basic calc sequence here. He had a mazing lectures with lots of examples and was easy to reach via email or in office hours. He even did a great series of review lectures at the end of the year

the worst... the most critical as if we are submitting to the highest rated medical journal out there. Often inflexible, unrealistic expectations for reading and comprehension. Rigid with high expectations. Unsure how a student is expected to pass if they have not yet completed the writing lab course, because skills we learn there are relevant.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']

comment: I do not mind a tough grader, but this instructor is so hypercritical that she is looking for missed periods, missed spaces in your APA papers. If you make mistakes she threatens to reject future papers. Absolutely no sense of compassion and care. A robot. Does not teach, just throws redundant reading. Instructions unclear, students must clarify.

I found his monotone voice quite good actually, grading is done by TA so don't worry, he might just have higher expectations and he doesn't like grading. Will give long detailed answers to your questions. Will work with you if you need accommodation. Best person I've met through UR.
If you go to class, go to office hours, and do the readings and you'll be fine.

His lectures are really interesting but your grade is heavily dependent on the TA you are assigned based on last name, since he doesn't grade your assignments. Super valuable class to take but somewhat unlucky on the grading front.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Extremely boring lectures. Mandatory attendance (done with paper instead of Blackboard codes for some godforsaken reason). If you're confident you can stay awake, you should be fine grade-wise. Though I agree that he is a pretentious and obnoxious grader at times.

Very passionate professor- he explains everything thoroughly. The TAs, as of now, are pretty strict, so you should take the time to talk with them outside of class to get feedback. I will say that the TA I was assigned is extremely unkind over emails and pretty harsh, so prepare for that if you can.

I enjoyed this class up until the final week... The content is interesting and he opens up the lecture for discussion a good amount. That being said, he took out his stress from the TA strike on the papers that he graded during finals. Gave no solid feedback and marked down for disagreeing with his opinion. Meanwhile, the TA gave everyone else As.

VERY boring class.speaks monotone. Reads off slides.preferred 103 instead. 255,gave his opinion way too often.TAs graded the papers way too harsh.During the strike…Fitz graded the papers and brutally terrorized them-and according to HIS OPINION.I don't see any rubric for this grading.I answered questions w/my opinions. VERYbiased-his opinions or 0!
Phenomenal professor.
Mandatory attendance marked by in-person homework submission. Lectures are interesting and easy to follow. Nice professor outside of class. Tests are taken remotely and papers are easy.

One of the most boring professors at the school. Every lecture is read mostly off slides and spoken in a monotone voice. Unlike every other professor I have had, you have to buy an expensive textbook to do the 2 assignments(cant find free pdf anywhere). It is also very easy to see his personal biases shine through his teaching.

Does not give room for proper discussion and just his opinion and refutals to a philosophical theory. Always runs out of time so even in the small discussions he does, he won't let you speak and will interrupt you for the sake of time. Good guy to talk to after class.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'So many papers']

comment: Very nice and approachable professor. The material in phil103 is extremely interesting.

Fitzpatrick is one of my favorite professors and his class has sparked my interest in ethics. I really like how he fosters thinking and curiosity rather than memorization. He promotes that by requiring homework and by making tests open note. Tests and papers are graded a bit harshly but the criticism is very fair. Great class to introduce ethics.

mandatory attendence for a 9 a.m. course? no videos?
banned the use of chatgpt for everything, too old school
with midterms plus two papers
workload is too much if you take this one for cluster

He cares a lot about his students and definitely knows a lot. Very prepared. Lectures can be a hit or miss. Either very interesting or incredibly boring. Def go to class and take notes. TAs grade papers way too harsh. Textbook is so expensive so I didn't get it and I was lost half the time. Prepare for group discussions everyday.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Short homeworks and reading due before every class so you have to go to lectures. Is a tough grader but all exams are open book and open note. Overall a good and interesting class

Great professor, horrible TAs. Fought for my paper grade that my TA put in the dumps and Fitzpatrick was very supportive of my argument. 225 was more interesting to me since it had less philosophical theory to it. The examples used in class are very interesting. Would highly recommend going to his office hours to review your paper outlines.

Amazing professor and I learned a lot! You could tell he knew what he was talking about and how to convey it. He liked to hear what students had to say and you could tell he genuinely cares. Class was graded based on HW each class(v easy), open note midterm & final, and 2 papers. Make sure to go to OH for papers and use the study guides(v helpful).

I think he's a great professor especially if this is your first time taking a philosophy course! Class is solely graded on 5 things, 1 Midterm, 1 Final, 2 Essays, and homework (assigned for every class). It's pretty manageable, make sure to utilize all the help and make use of your time. TA's do majority of the grading, they can be a bit hash...

Prof. Fitzpatrick is a knowledgeable and respectable professor. Good lecturer and well prepared for every class. There's homework assignments to submit at the begnining of each class, as attendance. Papers can be tough, depending on TA- office hours should help. The exams are fair and pretty lenient. Overall, great class with interesting topics!

I learned a lot of interesting philosophy ideas from this class. He was a really nice professor, lenient on late papers but only if you have a good reason, not too hard of a grader in my opinion and felt like he really cared about his students. The only thing I would've liked better is if we had had more open discussions in class.

PHIL225 is an interesting class (as far as philosophy goes) and his lectures were quite engaging, but boring at times. Class is graded by two papers and one final. The open note final is really not bad. Papers are graded by TAs so it's completely up to them how your grade turns out. Would recommend putting a lot of effort into papers.

Professor Fitzpatrick is a really great guy, he's super knowledgable about the subject and really helpful if you go to office hours. The tests are open note and really easy, and you don't need to study if you take good notes because his slides are very comprehensive. The papers were very manageable and easy to write because of the clear criteria.

Probably one of my favorite professors of all time. Professor Fitzpatrick is truly knowledgeable and passionate about his subject and will teach you a lot of things that are both useful in and outside of class. Showing up to classes is required and the workload is very manageable!

Really recommend taking this class. Grade was based on 2 papers, attendance, homework, and a final which was entirely online. Attendance is mandatory but the homework is very easy and the class is manageable. A very approachable professor and if you put the time in it's an easy A.
I loved Prof. William FitzPatrick. His lectures are very straightforward and super interesting!

Good intro philosophy course! Fitzpatrick broke down all the material really well and is very accommodating. The lectures could get boring, but was over all good. Turning in homework at the beginning of every class was used for attendance, and he doesn't record lectures. So attendance is definitely mandatory which is a little annoying.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Clear grading criteria', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: William is the best professor I've met so far because he is super polite, gives wonderful lecture, and a wonderful logician. I often email him for minor questions and he always responded with few paragraphs to make sure that he is clear. He is also very handsome and dress in good taste!

One of my favorite Prof's I've had at UR. Super engaging if you sit near the front of class - more difficult if you don't because the class is so large. If you participate and build a good relationship he'll be more willing to bump your grade if you're in-between letter grades. Seems intimidating but is kind if you show you're willing to work.

Super engaging lecturer; ask good questions and sit near the front and he'll be sure to remember you. As an aside, the TA's grade all the papers and their feedback can be confusing, so be sure to contact him with any questions about topics your papers are on during office hours.
Great Professor. Lectures very interesting and he breaks down the concepts well for students. Available for communication with students and willing to assist.

He is the greatest philosophy professor I ever met! Give specific study guides for each exam and give out essay prompt a long time before it is due. As long as you give out good logic in your paper you will pass. He covered a lot of topics in his class but give out good examples to make them very easy to understand. A very good introductory course.
Nice guy but a tough grader. Not a breeze class.

Professor Fitzpatrick recognizes that he has a monotone voice. That's why he chooses early mornings to lecture. When you're having trouble sleeping, attend one of his sluggish speaches. It'll do wonders.
Fitzpatrick was a really good lecturer - engaging and interesting. Outside of class, I relied a little more on the TA for help, because he seemed kind intimidating. #silverfox
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures', 'LECTURE HEAVY']

comment: Fitzpatrick is interesting but not mind blowing, assigns a very easy homework assignment every class, and a little annoying about technology- no phone use or laptops in class. He will make you feel a little like you are back in high school, but is a fair enough guy. When you get past the history of philosophy, Socrates, etc, the class gets better.
Miserable class. Boring lecturer. Avoid this class.
PHL 103 is an awesome introduction to Philosophy and FitzPatrick is a great professor. Definitely take advantage of office hours and talking to him after class, you'll get a lot out of it.

My favorite professor at UR. I took 103 for fun and decided on a philosophy minor because of Fitzpatrick, and took 225 just because he was the prof. He's a fantastic lecturer and down to earth--just all around an awesome guy.

The most boring class I've ever taken in my life. He's a nice enough guy and intelligent, but he just repeated exactly what we were supposed to read the night before. The exams were kind of difficult, but I was also a freshman first semester, so I probably could have studied a bit more. Definitely not a breeze class. I fell asleep a few times.

Very clear professor. If you go to class and pay attention you will do fine in the class as he is very clear in what is important in the readings. The TAs grade the papers and tend to be a bit harsh, but he is also flexible with changing your grade if you feel it was unfair. Great professor!

Best professor I've had at U of R so far. Incredibly bright guy, makes the material and clear as possible and presents it in a logical manner. He does tend to talk for long stretches of time, but makes it very clear what the main points are and brings up a lot interesting ideas. Overall a pretty easy and super smart dude, such a great professor

Overall a wonderful professor.  In class, he tended to ramble a bit, but if you paid attention and took notes, you learned a ton.  FitzPatrick is also a really cool guy--go to his office hours and get to know him!  He loves to talk to students and share his passion for philosophy.
Stay away.  Awful class. Rambles on and made me fall asleep every single class. The TA's were way too harsh and I did not learn a single thing from the course.
He is a bit boring, but a good teacher

Figlio is great! Public is easily one of the best classes at UoR. It's rare to find a class that is both extremely easy and fascinating at the same time. I appreciated how he balanced conceptual teaching with class discussion. Also, go to his office hours- had many great and thought provoking convos.

Professor Figlio was the best econ teacher I ever had! He made the material fun and understandable. After struggling in previous econ classes, I could not have been more fortunate to have him as my prof. He genuinely cares about his students, both in and out of the classroom, and is great to talk to. I'd happily take his class again!

Knowls and Matson are def hard teachers to get by, their lectures are fast paced and confusing and tests are almost impossible. Clearly they know the way they teach is flawed because the amount of Extra Credit this course has makes it literally impossible to not gen an A. While you might suffer a bit just focus on the EC and you'll be alright

The class is on a point based system, so go to lectures to get attendance points. Highly recommend doing test corrections and the extra credit assignment. The tests are very direct, so as long as you know the material you should be fine. The final exam is optional, so if you have enough points you don't have to take it.
just show up to lectures and workshops, pay attention, do the homework and you'll be fine.

Even though it is easy to get an A in this class, you would feel that you would not be learning much. This professor is monotone and reads off her lectures. It is hard to follow from this professor. I would advise that if you have this professor for chem 131 you need to review again thoroughly afterwards to prepare for chem 132.

Easy to earn an A without learning much. Knowles would be passive aggressive at times telling everyone to shush. Spoke so quietly, no one could not hear her lecturing most days even with the microphone on. Matson, on the other hand, actually seemed interested on what she was teaching.
Bad professor. Bad lectures. Extremely easy class if you took AP Chemistry. Very low cut off for an A (you can fail every single exam and get an A if you do all the easy extra credit).

Literally does not explain anything, simply reads the slides, which are barely helpful anyway. Also gets so peeved about people lowkey just existing, like yeah one person is talking, why are you interrupting the whole class bc of it.

Genuinely just reads the information off of the slides and doesn't explain anything. The information on the slides isn't even really helpful.  Exams are generally difficult with no curve. She did let us do exam corrections this semester though.
Same as matson, knowles can be passive aggressive at times and not helpful, and I am just glad I am done with my cluster with this class, despite not learning a single drop of knowledge of chemistry.
Tests are hard but fair, expect tests to be math heavy but the study guides prepare you well.

This class back in freshmen year was completely underwhelming in my academic journey, and I don't think I learned a thing from my time thus spent in her class. Both knowles and matson don't care about actually teaching you, more so just speed running slides and then testing you. If extra credit wasn't a thing, I wouldn't have passed...

Knowles is thr goofiest, most profoundly silly professor that I've had the displeasure of being taught by. She is so slide heavy on complex topics that it doesn't surprise me that UoR is dropping ranks.
Can't lecture

1. The professor has limited teaching abilities, so it is necessary to attend office hours.
2. The course offers a lot of extra credit, so you can get an A without studying (although I think this is unreasonable).
3. A terrible learning experience, too many extra credit assignments fostered a negative attitude toward academics among students.

Not a huge fan of her lecturing style; it can be difficult to follow. Has a decent amount of office hours, which are very helpful. She's friendly and will walk you through problems step-by-step.

Same with Prof. Matson, tests are difficult but extra credit is plentiful. An A is possible even if you bomb every test.

Prof Knowles may genuinely be the worst teacher I have had in my life. She has no idea to teach complex topics, recognize that the class is lost, or even do example problems clearly! Plus she's sometimes rude in class or in office hours, not extremely so, but enough to be a little off-putting.

This class was honestly a very funny class hence the tag. Knowles read off the lecture slides nd that was it, not good at explaining content at all. There was this one time where she didnt know how to answer a question about chemistry on a certain topic and another student in lecture answered for her which was lowkey funny.

The only saving grace for this class is the amount of extra credit. Matson and Knowles assume students know everything and make the exam questions impossible to answer. You will learn NOTHING cause the extra credit will be the only thing keeping you afloat
not very good its not very good run run run its bad run the thermo is bad run

Very rude, and when asked questions in class responded more often than not in an unkind manner. I lost 50% of my points for incorrectly addressing a scientist ONCE in my paper on accident and lost more points after that on the rest of my work because she took it personally. Brings politics into the chemistry classroom which is unnecessary.

Doesn't take class seriously and sometimes in lecture she brings new concepts as if we already know them. I needed to do a lot of studying outside of class just because her lectures were a waste of time
I think Knowles' lectures are a bit more helpful than Matson's. Both professors are very accessible outside of class. There are a bunch of opportunities for extra credit.

Everyone says her lectures are bad but they're fine. She's really nice if you talk to her. Class is on points system + has lots of extra credit even if you don't do super well on exams, but EC is graded super harshly. Get points for going to class but lectures are recorded. Only took 2/3 exams and still didn't need to take the final to get an A.

Lots of the reviews are a bit harsh. I'll give a real review. Knowles is an okay professor. Not the best, but not as and as some of the other reviews. Knowles is probably at her best at thermo and worst at quantum mechanics. Other than teaching, Knowles is very nice and is patient with teaching (since Knowles teaches the harder concepts).

Dr. Knowles was at least a bit more consistent than Dr. Matson. Her lectures however were boring and super dense, and often it seemed like she was skipping over or assuming students understand the material. I appreciated that she didn't talk down to students like Dr. Matson did, but I feel like the quality of teaching was no better.

Honestly, not the best professor I have had. Her lectures are confusing and exam grades are really low. Her and matson teaching does not work at all. It feels like they are on two different planets. The topics are hard and go to class. Recitations will help you so much so GO TO THEM.

Knowles is the second chemistry professor that made me appreciate Dr. H more. She is not the most accommodating person and tends to speedrun her lectures. Exam grades were low because she and Matson cannot teach well and fails to give out sufficient exam practice exams to her students.

Knowles is very caring of her students. She sometimes included problems students had trouble doing. She is not very good at teaching though. Her lectures are fast paced and some of her test questions felt like they weren't representative of the content learned. Overall, I think she needs time to become a better professor.

This professor looks like she tries, but simply can not teach. You can definitely tell she has very little experience teaching the course. Lectures feel like eternity and the slides are not fun to look at.

i think she genuinely does care about her students, but she just is not good at teaching. i do get that this was her first year teaching. she kept assuming we knew foundational information to understanding concepts when we didn't. whenever someone would ask where she got this information from, she would say that we should just know how to do it.

Unlike the other 132 prof, she's actually a nice person and cares about you. However, this doesn't erase the fact that she is a terrible teacher. She speeds through slides, makes test questions so hard and long that no one finishes the exam, and doesn't know how to use a mic. She doesn't know how to do her own problems, but expects us to. Pray.

Super sweet and accommodating professor. I understand it was her first year teaching, which shows. She goes through complex lectures quickly and really likes calculus for some reason. I believe she could be a great teacher once she gets more familiarity to students. Tests were tough, but with the amount of extra credit, 132 should be an easy A.

Personally, I think Professor Knowles was the better of the two professors. She paces her lectures much better and spends a lot of time on practice problems. She was kind and accommodating. My only issues with her are the cluttered slides and lack of energy. It's clear she is not used to lecturing to such a large class. Overall, she's decent.

This year was her first year to teach, and it could be seen. She was very nervous and unconfident. She essentially just read off of her slides, which she posted on blackboard. I liked her a lot better than the other professor, because she was nice and very approachable. I loved her modules as they were more interesting to me. She talks very fast.

I left Dr. H's class thinking I'd have a better experience in CHEM 132. Let me tell you, that was a funny assumption... I was so wrong. The average for every exam was consistently below 50%, and that really shows how horrendous the class was. The only reason I survived this class was because of the extra credit. I don't recommend this class at all.

Someone needs to tell miss girl that flying through slideshows at 4523648768mph and assuming that your students just automatically understand everything isn't teaching. Though considering the overall poor quality of U of R's chem department, I guess the bar is pretty low.

If you are searching for this professor, I'm sure you came across Professor Robert Minckley before. One of his ratings was "I drove without a seatbelt and hoped I got into a crash on the way to campus." 
Compared to Professor Knowles, I Love professor Minckley. Knowles' lectures are so fast, It's almost like she assumes us to understand immediately
Mostly just horrifically boring.  Bring things to do in his class and drink caffeine!!

Rose was an awesome professor. She really genuinely cared about her students both as people and as writers. Homework and essays were very clear and class time was very helpful in understanding college writing. She gives personalized feedback that is very specific and really gets you thinking. Would 100% take her class again.

comment: This class was incredibly easy as long as you did the work.  Prof. Manni is so sweet and funny in class and she genuinely wants her students to do well.

Professor Manni is really sweet and definitely cares about her students.  She is a very easy grader but makes you want to do well.  She does expect you to already know a lot and sometimes doesn't understand what you're confused about since she's a native speaker but will always try to help. She made herself very available and was overall wonderful.

She does blow off some grammar structures that she thinks you already know but if you ask her questions in lecture she will definitely answer them and go over something again or in a different way. She certainly cares about her students learning and tends to be flexible with deadlines.
very clear in class. provided good material for taking the exams.
He's pretty good.  Doesn't have patience with people wasting his time.

DMST 272 is the best course I've taken in the DMS Department by far. Everyone in the course has improved so much, and it's a testament to Nancy's teaching! It is definitely more work than DMST 171, so be prepared to spend some more hours each week working on your projects, especially if you've forgotten or are not familiar with Adobe software.

Nancy is amazing! If you're interested in learning graphic design from scratch, do not hesitate to take this course. She's super funny and very knowledgeable about the topic. If you need help, she and her TA are always open to giving you resources and feedback. Her class is not very lecture heavy, and you're given class time to work on projects.

Her passion for the topic shines through her lectures. You want to participate in class because she is so caring and energetic that it feels bad to sit and let class happen around you. A super relaxed and fun course, taught by someone with a genuine interest in making sure students get what they want out of it.
He's nice.
I was in his class two years ago, he's great at explaining new concepts, but you have to really focus on the lecture.
He's very helpful and offer extra office hour.
He showed lots of examples in the class, which is helpful for me to understand the concepts.
He literally cannot teach . Hell do the math hisself on the board and give his own un understandable explanation .
He's nice, knows lots of stuff and very helpful.
The instructor is good but this course is so difficult to me. His office hour helped me a lot.
This guy is smart and the lecture is amazing. One thing you need to be aware of is that the exam (especially the midterm) can be so hard but the grade is curved in the end.

For a creative writing class, I found Prof. Higley's in-class feedback to be consistently highly critical and disrespectful to students, noticeably impacting class morale. She seemed to struggle taking any feedback or feelings into consideration. She didn't add a content warning for assignments, even after being asked. Not professional or unbiased.

She's tough and takes no disrespect from anyone, but she knows the material she teaches very well and gives interesting lectures. She cares how you are engaging with the material and wants to hear your thoughts. I found her to be kind and caring, but she also liked me. I saw her be... blunt with others. Regardless, she's a great teacher.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Gives good feedback']

comment: I can't stress enough, do NOT take a class with her! She's a bully! She talks down to her students, makes them think they're a bad writer, etc just bc she doesn't personally like their story. If you want to be publicly degraded and humiliated, take a class with her! If you value your self esteem, avoid her (she's not intelligent, just opinionated).

This professor is disrespectful. Don't take her classes. If it's a requirement, find another way to satisfy the requirement. She speaks down to students as if she's superior. Her mood will change in an instant. Assignments are vague and arbitrary. She grades harshly and punishes you if you share any ideas in your paper that she doesn't agree with.

DO NOT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER! She is the worst professor I've ever had! She bullies her students, is rude, moody, cranky, and an overall terrible person! No matter how hard you work on your story, if she personally doesn't like it or agree with the ideas in it, she'll give you a terrible grade! She traumatized me and made me cry a lot. AVOID HER!

Dr. Higley's strict but I think she's fair. Her class is solid, but be careful. Put extra effort into your paper. Double-check your citations. You do NOT want to be on the receiving end of her sass. Also, you should probably email her if you're going to miss class.

Awful Professor. Will yell at you if you disagree with her in class. Gets really moody and cranky and is sometimes very insulting towards students if they don't agree with her. Overall bad experience. Wouldn't recommend.

The worst professor I have ever come across in life. She says she "sympathises with students with anxiety,.blah blah" but makes condescending and personal comments about your mental state when you go to her with your problem. I had the worst experience with her and would never want to see her again in my life let alone take a class with her.

Professor Higley is engaging and is clearly passionate about the materials taught in the class. The only thing I disliked was the way that she acted towards students, as she can sometimes be very moody and impatient with them. All in all, a very good course. I would take a class with her again just for her outstanding abilities in teaching.

She reminds me of a nice version of Meryl Streep's character in The Devil Wears Prada. She's smart, funny, and passionate about the subjects she teaches. I think some people get intimidated by her (she's sometimes a lil'bit moody, who isn't?) but if you think she's being "mean" or "rude"... you might be taking things a little too personally!

Kind of flyaway and disorganized, but engaging and passionate about the material. Wants you to think, not regurgitate or give her what you think she wants. Values communication, very understanding, gives you slack when you need it as long as you've demonstrated that you care about the class.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: Amazing professor. Doesn't speak down to students, expects actual scholarship (GASP), and is genuinely concerned about each of her students as individuals. It's ridiculous to me that so many complain that she has actual expectations of them. I suspect their parents are paying, and always will be. Show up. Behave like an adult. Be a scholar.
Higley is the abject fecundity in the best way

Higley is funny and amusing, but she is also very insulting. In both of my papers she would write rude demeaning comments. I disagreed with her once in class and since that point she has consistently called my points "wrong" no matter what I argue. Her essay prompts are extremely vague. Get a different teacher.

Really enjoyed the classes I've taken with her. She is funny, passionate, eccentric, and awesome! If you tire of boring, stick-in-the-mud professors, definitely take a class with her. She can be intense, but only if you didn't do your homework, participate, or were late. If you're responsible and take college seriously, you are good.

i would suggest not taking a creative writing course with her.  very awkward to hear her call out people for 'mistakes' when the class is about CREATIVE WRITING.  comments were very disrespectful sometimes- its called CONSTRUCTIVE criticism jeez
She is a wonderful professor. Passionate, fun, knowledgeable, and her classes are creative, as she is open to suggestions of all kind.

lots of material but altogether eye-opening class.  higley's a brilliant woman with an unique personality.  get involved in class discussions.  don't come to class late.  she can be moody at times so best to learn sooner than later how to navigate that - it could be hard to recover from a bad encounter or even a moment of memorable disagreement

She is a very enthusiastic and knowledgable professor, and clearly a nice person.  However, she is very fervent about gender issues.  You don't come to it until the end of the semester, but she definitely holds a some sort of grudges.

Very good professor. Bring a "Get tough or die" approach to her courses - i.e. don't come late or unprepared, don't b.s. her, get involved in the discussions, and defend your ideas. In my class, the people who disliked her were the ones trying to just coast through the class. Then, of course, they'd accuse her of favortism. Whatever, dudes.
She's a good professor, very cooky. However, I truly believe she hates males.

Sarah Higley is one of the best professors you will ever meet. Yes, she plays favorites, but if you work hard, you won't get shafted.   She is so funny, it is not unheard of to leave class with aching sides. I miss her lots.

Although Higley is an extremely intelligent professor, it seems like she allows her personal life to interfere with her emotions often. For instance, one day she broke down crying for some reason, and wouldn't explain why. This was in addition to her regular eccentrism, which is somewhat tolerable. You also cannot show up late or even have a cold in class (I'm not joking), because it "disturbs the class". Workload: medium - heavy.

Okay prof, she's knowledgeable and you will learn something from her course.  She is engaging enough as a lecturer but plays favorites.  She is given to dramatics, and is rather childish about discussing sex, with a lot of giggling.  I didn't dislike her class but I did dislike the favoritism.
be careful of her bite, but don't let it intimidate you.
good teacher, but could improve by having clearer objectives, is set in her ways
No Comments

she's insane.  if u ever ask her to clarify an assignment she'll go into hysterics.  she's very intimidating.  the classes she teachers are awesome tho... middle welsh, brit lit, chaucer, old english.  u'll survive if u'r her favorite.
She's very flaky, but OK overall.

She is very educated and enthusiastic about the material she presents in class, and she a fair grader overall.  Also, she teaches classes that appeal to a select few, like Middle Welsh and course that translates Beowulf.
She is very fake and artificial...very enthusiastic though...Insipid discussion and shallow topics at times. Some people liked her class a lot though.

the class was far too easy. i handed in papers that woud've gotten me an F in high school and was praised. also, she goes on boring, meaningless tangents for hours. harmless enough, though, if you stay on her good side.
she is crazy, but in a good way, mostly
No Comments
Teaches interesting classes, but she's not very clear about what she wants

As an intimidated beginner (as explicitly mentioned in the syllabus) I found myself often in a panic or completely unsure of what to do. The professor is very kind and willing to help you with things you don't understand, and I think that what she asks of the students is only to spur their potential, but it can be a bit past 'intro'.

I took the intro bio coding class Bio198 and it was anything but intro. Not only did exams take over 12 hours to complete, but extensive coding was required on hw as well as on exams. She is a very nice person and holds office hours, however, her teaching methods are lacking.

comment: I took BIO/STT214. She doesn't teach very well at all, would've been better off with just the textbook and no lectures to waste my time.

comment: I took genetics with her over the summer. She is a very sweet and funny woman and genuinely cares for her students but, teaching is not her strongest suit. Her lectures were somewhat confusing. Tests were doable. There was also a paper and presentation due towards the end of class. Needs hard work, but definitely easier than the Fall 198 class.

Professor Glenn was passionate in what she taught and brought that positive attitude to class. Her lectures were very straight forward and the tests were what you should expect. She can be a serious professor, but she commands respect and often times would subtly crack jokes and make the class laugh.

Professor Glenn is an amazing professor. Her lectures are interesting and clear. She takes time to answer peoples questions and she knows the material well and almost always has an answer. Not only does she understand the material that is current, but also thinks about where psychology may go in the future. Overall a wonderful professor.
Very nice professor, and gives very interesting lectures. Very nice when giving grades and I am lucky to have her for this course.

She's the coolest prof, but you have to work for what she gives you. Also make sure you do your readings when she assigns them, or she penalizes the class. Just gotta show up and do your work- she doesn't expect much else
If you are interested in the topic area, you will love her class. Very knowledgeable about her field.
Easy boring class
She is a great person to talk to in terms of help. Her class is very interesting and if you're interested in African Americans in the quest for political freedom, it's for you.

She obviously knowledgeable about what she'd teaching. She's engaging and enthusiastic. She discusses reading extensively in class and is pretty clear about what will be on exams. Discusses race and gender, but tells you that right at the beginning of the semester- no surprises. Overall, a good teacher.
She is a very interesting woman! She has a ton to offer and has been a great help as my adviser. Her randomness makes studying for exams and writing papers hard.
Can't work a computer, so that cause many class delays.  Gets off topic, but it's interesting.  LOTS of thick reading with odd formatted exams

TERRIBLE professor. Avoid at all costs. She is horrible with technology, yet used powerpoint for all the lectures. We usually got through a few slides a day. Terribly boring and not welcoming. Tests are not good measures of the material, little class discussion, everyone just surfs facebook. AVOID HER.

While she seems like a knowledgeable person, her strength is clearly not in teaching. Her voice is monotone; it sounds like she's reciting facts. The textbook readings are long and often extremely in-depth for a 105 class, and she covers a lot of the key points in the reading in her lectures (if you can pay attention).

She expects her students to read upwards of 100 pages of dense, textbook reading per week, but she does not hold herself to the same rigorous standard. She shows up late, and is an inconsistent grader. She is obviously knowledgeable on the subject matter, but I wish she would spend a little more time on how she teaches the class.
she is the best prof at the Roch!
very nice professor, with interesting reading materials (most of the time)
No Comments

I transferred from UR, but I would have to say that Professor Sinclair-Chapman is an excellent professor. She is a savant in her field, intelligent, eloquent, insightful, and dedicated. Also, her approach to the topic of race is veracious.

Stimulated good discussion, didn't let people get away with just spouting off on things, even if she may have agreed with what they were saying.  Interested in students, maybe a bit too easy with grading.
Thinks everything in the world is about race. Can't admit that there are other views than her own. And told me that I was wrong, because i disagreed with her.
Good discussion, isn't always clear

The problem with Rochester students is that they want to bury their heads in the sand and pretend that race doesn't exist.  At least she is bringing an important issue to the forefront that no one else has the guts to discuss frankly (i.e. the admin.)
No Comments
very very easy, but very very boring
Very intelligent...edgy...talks about race WAY too much!
We did work out of a textbook for another class. The name of the class is The Meaning of Life, if I wanted to take Logic and Inquiry I would've signed up for it.

Took this class over the summer. Easygoing, laid back guy. Definitely knew what he was talking about. No powerpoints, only lectures, so be sure to take notes because what he says shows up verbatim on tests. Read your book for HW assignments and so you won't be lost in class next day.

Good lecturer, paces things well. Difficult topics and important topics are given appropriate time, while simple afternotes aren't overtaught. Spends lots of time making sure student intuitively understand topics which in STEM classes is a such a nice change. HW and exams are reasonable, hard but not unreasonable long like MATH and PHYS courses.

Professor Buckley is one of the better professors I've had. He paces out his lectures and assignments well, and he tries to avoid overwhelming students with several overlapping assignments. Homework can be difficult, but if you go to office hours you'll be fine. Exams tend to be a little harder than homework, but it all works out in the curve.
He's a good guy, but he really doesn't know how to teach in a class with many people.
He is really knowledgeable about the course concepts, but be ready to read with you getting a full book every week. And make sure to attend lectures, as attendance is taken seriously.

Prof Sierra is a great guy and a very knowledgeable professor. Definitely a tough course for a 100 level, lots of reading and a research heavy final essay, but if you put in effort you will get a good grade. Tries to make class enjoyable and is approachable and understanding.
Very knowledgeable and passionate. Definitely was more work than your average 100 level class, but he's very nice and enjoyable

He is clearly more interested in his research than professing beyond lecturing. No guidance on the final research paper. regret taking the course and wish i would have dropped it when i could. Truly a waste of my time and credit space. Did not encourage much critical analysis or direction beyond understanding what occurred, i.e. a history lecture.
Pompous and oblivious. Takes forever to grade. Makes you feel like he is too important and busy for you. Does not give sensitivity to outstanding circumstances.

comment: I definitely could have tried harder in this class, but I noticed all my assignments got the same grade (84) in this class no matter the effort I put in. I loved him as a person but I think his lectures could have been more focused, they had good information, it neither felt introductory or an in-depth and specific, but rather some in-between.

comment: Course has good lectures & discussions. He is open to questions (tagent ones too). "Mexico thruough time" does have a lean on social history (more readings), but that is also by the nature of HIS200 courses. I personally find the classes very enjoyable & interesting, but we did lose 50% of the class by Day 2 (16 -> 9 ppl). Doesn't hurt to try tho
Great lectures and awesome professor. Hes always finding ways to make history interesting. Papers are long and readings are long but doable. Great professor!

Professor Sierra is a fantastic scholar, professor, and person. His survey courses are demanding in terms of workload, although the work itself is not difficult. His lectures are engaging, and the discussions we had in class were excellent.
great professor !

Professor VanWijngaarden is great. He is accessible via email, understanding on assignments/due dates, and clearly knows the subject matter well and is able to teach in an engaging manner. Not sure if this was unique to this semester but the mix of in-person and online was oddly perfect.

He is a very esteemed professor and knows a lot about the environmental field. He is generally a pretty understanding and nice person. Lectures go by really fast so I had to rewatch them often. PHLT201W case studies are graded somewhat harshly.

243 is a joy to take. Lectures are well taught, and although a bit vague at the start of the course, they become in-depth and interesting after the first exam. Exams are not difficult, workshops are helpful. Other student's opinions are due to laziness.

Despite being difficult to follow, the course is highly valuable for anyone researching epigenetic regulation, chromatin organization, or gene expression, as the material frequently appears in scientific literature.
As of 2025, Advice:
- The Workshops are your friends, LEARN and MEMORIZE them, exams will be "easy"
- Use slides to understand the WS.

DONT take this class if you dont need it. Prof. speed runs PowerPoints of 50+ slides, each slide containing enough for 10 mins of content. Often wouldn't finish slides and tell us to go over it on our own. VERY DISORGANIZED. Exams are ridiculously difficult considering the amount of information you need to take in. Only 3 tests = overall grade.

If you don't have to take this class, then don't. Her accent is pretty hard to understand. Her grammar and sentence structure is even worse. lectures are disorganized. her exams focus on like 4 concepts. In other words, knowing 8 slides well can get you an A. But the exam covered literally 380 slides. Worst bio class i've taken besides physiology.
Very kind and helpful! She gives a lot of information in lecture, but really works with the students to help them understand the material. One of the biology classes I've learned the most in.

Really sweet lady but a pretty lousy professor. Her lectures are incredibly disorganized and difficult to follow. You have to put in a lot of work outside class to make sense of what's going on. Her tests are tough and there are only 3 of them. No textbook, it's all based on papers (you can skim them - no heavy reading).

Pros: extremely intelligent, kind, knowledgeable, helpful  professor. Cons: I personally had a lot of trouble following her lectures. Her accent is not difficult at all to understand, it is the lack of a flow in her sentence structure and in her lectures. The figures in her slides are equally fragmented and esoteric. Her exams are very detailed.
I liked the class, but I saw her once during office hours and she was really rude and unhelpful to me for no reason...it was such a bad experience it ruined the class for me :(

Dr. Benyajati is difficult to adjust to because of her accent and communication skills, but when you get past that she is absolutely one of the best professors here. She really wants all of her students to do well and will be as helpful and supportive as she can. The class was interesting too, a lot of writing, but Tip made it manageable. Love her
Miserably difficult class. I wish she'd have made better slides or at least labeled the figures. But she's really nice and helpful.
Really smart professor, goes very fast in lecutre which can be annoying, but good staying after to help you.  The textbook is really good for clarification.

Dr. Benyajati is one of the most knowledgable professors.  She does have an asian accent, but once you get past that anybody should realize how great of a professor she is.  She has always been there to help me, and she is willing to help those that ask.  Don't expect a platter with your name on it.

Really fantastic class taught by an even better professor. Prof. Singer cares deeply about his students and the subject matter, and shares that passion and enthusiasm with his students. Lectures are engaging and interesting and he does a great job engaging the class in discussion while maintaining a lecture environment. Highly recommended!

Not a bad professor. Still pretty young, and hasn't had a ton of teaching experience, but definitely intelligent when it comes to the great philosophers such as Hobbes, Locke, Mill, Rawls, and others. The class goes through about one book every week, so be ready to read a ton (although he recaps most stuff in class).
He could be a decent teacher. but pretentious and self centered sometimes. Class was VERY BORING. TOUGH GRADER. Unless you are totally into what he teaches and LOVE writing, DON'T take his class.

Mr. Chandler is a good guy. He's very helpful if you ask and often emails what the homework is if he assigns it during class. The class isn't the most interesting subject and he is a fairly tough grader, but it is not impossible to do well. You get out what you put in, and he's willing to help you out.

Idk why the ratings r so bad 4 him b/c I found him to be very helpful, friendly, & engaging. He gives great feedback on essays & provided u take the time to go to his office hours w/ ur rough drafts or even email urs to him, he will give u plenty of advice. I think it was fairly easy to pull of a decent grade as long as u do the work.
bad

John Chandler is very potentially the worst teacher I had my freshmen year.  He was extraordinarily disrespectful to me and constantly attacked me during class for simply stating my opinion.  He is obsessed with his fairy tales and is honestly a little kid who just never grew up.  Do not take his class unless you have an interest in faerie tales.
comics...woo...

People say he is bad guy. But really he is nota  bad guy. Chandler is really very helpful and knows alot about what want to learn. Always wants to help with ofifce houcrs. But really class peers fall asleep and do not try to learn what they want to learn.
Major headcase and quite pretentious. Do not take this class!! Difficult grader and very very boring.
Difficult grader, randomly walks into classroom objects, class moved slowly, he brought food the last day

I took 19th Century British Lit (Engl 221) with Prof. Rajan. Overall it was a fun experience; there's a lot of interesting stuff to learn. Sometimes discussions felt a little unfocused, but Prof. Rajan has a nice dry sense of humor which kept things interesting. Fairly easy grader in my experience.

Took this course as a freshman. Expectations were clear and the workload was reasonable, but the class wasn't engaging and the material was just okay. For me, it didn't feel worth the time compared with other options.

Fall 2024 course-Charles Dickens (453). Failed to provide clear expectations for assignments, feeling confused about what was required for a good grade. Lectures were tangential and lacked focus, difficult to grasp key concepts. Feedback on written work was vague and unhelpful, leaving students feeling unsure how to improve their writing skills.

comment: As a transfer student I expected better quality professors but this one didn't meet expectations. She wasn't teaching the course as stated. She's hardly on campus or in her office. I had to seek others assistance in questions and clarifications I needed. I wouldn't recommend this class with this professor.

This class was very discussion heavy, but the discussions were really interesting, and Professor Rajan was always willing to answer questions. It was a lot of reading, but the grading was fair and the feedback was really helpful. The amount of writing was also reasonable. I would definitely recommend this class.

comment: She's cares about and shows respect for student perspectives, and takes time to understand what they're saying, and does a good job balancing lecture with discussion. Only place for improvement would be that sometimes assignments are a bit delayed being posted on Blackboard, but I never found that to be detrimental to getting an assignment done.

Lots and lots of reading. A one-page paper is due every-other week, but I found them helpful for staying on track and tackling more difficult poetry. The tests were difficult for me, but all of it is quite doable if you keep up with the reading and pay attention in class.
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']

comment: Rajan is a really sweet woman and a good professor. I found her lectures to be a bit dry, but it was obvious that she is passionate about English. Her grading was average. The class was decent overall, but probably my least favorite out of the bunch so far.

The amount of reading in both classes was excessive (even for an English class) and the response papers got incredibly boring week after week. That being said, the material she chose to read was interesting, and papers were graded fairly if a little harshly. If lectures had been shorter, it would have been easier to pay attention.

I love Professor Rajan.  She does a terrific job engaging students in discussion.  She is funny and bright and loves literature.  She is also very fair and gives students opportunities to rewrite papers.  Highly recommended!

Loved her so much! A very sweet lady, and extremely helpful - gave me suggestions of sources to use for my final paper unsolicited. Class discussions and lectures were very engaging. Highly recommend this professor.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Helpful, nice, engaging, and above all, passionate about what she was taeaching. I've taken two classes with her, and loved them both. She is eloquent and everything she says I want to write down. I would take another class with her in a heartbeat. She's a hard grader, but her classes are worth the work.

I found Professor Rajan to be extremely approachable and very helpful! I went to her office whenever I was confused about something or felt as though I was falling behind. Additionally, I found her lectures very enjoyable as well. She is passionate about her class and that translate well to her students. She may seem strict at first, but she's not!

I thought she was a very effective lecturer who tried and succeeded in pumping some life into Brit Lit II. I thoroughly enjoyed her class although I wish she did not assign response papers for the weekly recitations. These to me seemed like busy work. Other than that she was great.

Very rigid. Class involved a lot of busywork for a literature course - quizzes on minor details in the reading, weekly short essays, etc. Not very understanding in terms of extenuating circumstances - I missed a few quizzes for medical reasons and my grade suffered.

Pretty interesting lecturer.  Rigidly particular, doesn't cut anyone any slack.  Complained one day about latecomers without bothering to inquire why (she would have found out that the parking lot was jammed).  Came in late herself the next day.  That kind of thing.  Picky to the point of "anality" on paper grading.

Boring and disorganized lecturer. The grading seems straightforward until assignments are actually graded. Misleading instructions which the TA also misunderstood led to bromine gas filling the lab for the class to inhale and get splashed by. Dr. Olsen saw this and only evacuated himself, claiming he would take off points.
He's fine.
Very boring lecturer. Lab lecture for Orgo lab didn't always match up with class but was very helpful when it did.

comment: Very boring lectures, does not know how to keep his students engaged. Unfortunately, all pre-med students must take his classes so be ready.

Dr. Olsen is by far one of the best professors I have had the privilege of learning from during my time at UofR. He genuinely cares about his students' success, and cultivates an environment in which students may learn uninhibitedly--not fearing the prospect of making mistakes. Dr. Olsen is far from condescending and always willing to help.

Two exams in total. Weekly assignment, quizzes, and discussion post. He is nice and can extend deadlines for you if you had a good reason. He was inaccessible halfway through the semester with late to no replies. The first exam was more focused on the theory than the code.
Took his class in Fall 2018. One of my favorite professors. Lots of reading and lecture heavy. Exams are super fun and interesting. He clerked on Supreme Court and knows a lot about the subject.

the best professor i ever had. Extremely intelligent and very helpful. Fair grader. Lectures are very inspiring. Make sure that you are really into the course material though, otherwise the lectures may seem to be too long

His lectures do seem to drag on for quite a while. Yet, if you can take good notes(or get them from a friend), you should not have any issues doing well. If you ever try and talk to him he is very approachable and friendly.

Jackson's best attribute is that he is a legal genius. He provides so much insight into each case. Sometimes his analysis is quite heavy, but he does not expect you to think at the same level as he in exams; students would be at a great disadvantage, seeing that he is the ex-president of the school and is crazy smart.
Not very engaging, but the topics he picked were all relevant to the class. A lot of reading, especially for a topic this dry.

Professor Jackson knows his stuff, he's extremely bright.  Has his law degree from Yale and clerked for Rehnquist on the supreme court.  He likes to get up and just keep lecturing the whole time so it's good to ask him questions.  His tests aren't too hard you just have to study for them.  He's also got some great stories from the supreme court.

Professor Paine was very passionate about the content he lectured on. I enjoyed the content of the course and each of the six assignments was straightforward enough. The only thing that would have made the class better would have been a more exact rubric for the papers as many essay prompts can be a bit open ended.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Prof. Paine is incredibly mindful of his students and willingly explains concepts repeatedly to clarify them. Grading is straight forward as long as you follow all the guidelines. There are a lot require readings but there are some that you can generally just skim through and look at more in depth if needed for writing the essays.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Prof Paine has potential, but tends to let his lectures get sidetracked by the students asking questions every 10 minutes. Though its nice that he cares, he just needs to tell them to come to office hours, rather than letting them make a lecture into a QandA.

Professor Paine is decent. The class is not as interesting as I thought it would be, and a lot of reading is assigned. Though Prof Paine lets you know that skimming is expected, if you are someone who prefers less reading, but in depth, this is not a good class. The lectures can be interesting, but grading is harsh. That may be the TA though.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Graded by few things']

comment: He assigns a lot of readings each week (100-200 pages), but they're pretty interesting for the most part. All essays clearly reflect class material and are easy to answer provided that you did at least half the readings. If u follow the essay directions to a T, you get an A. He's really dorky and passionate abt the subject.
