comment: 23 years of experience, yet he still can't teach. If this class were not a requirement, you would never see me. Too difficult to deal with, but gives extensions.

Review your knowledge in ECE 221 since most of his lectures are built upon that course. Also, his lecture slides are sometimes hard to look at, so read the textbooks listed in the syllabus for better understanding. HWs and labs are quite difficult technically, but not graded harshly. Overall, great professor, great class, you'll learn a ton.

Hui Wu knows his stuff and explains it clearly, although his lecture slides can be difficult to read at times. Most of what he teaches builds upon ECE 221, so you may need to review to avoid falling behind. Great professor and great class; however, the labs could be improved and elaborated on a bit more to enhance students' understanding.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Generous graders, lectures are boring and not very useful. Youtube and textbook will be your bff on the homework problems. Everyone is confused on the labs and no one knows what they're doing so start early, ask for help, and if you can't get a part to work correctly, just explain it in your report and they'll still give you full credit.

Giving a 5 just to balance the score
Only who expect to learn about IC will appreciate the course materials. There're not many of them among UR undergrads unfortunately. To be fair, the course is not graded harshly.
It requires a strong foundation especially in 221 and 241 to keep up. Don't expect to understand everything just by attending lectures

Run away!!!! he doesn't teach you anything but expect you to be an expert by the requirements and harness on his homeworks and labs which are not related to his disorgnized and meaningless lectures at all.

I am speechless. This class is a complete waste of time and the professor should be prevented from teaching ever again. He is extremely disorganized and you will spend the entire semester having absolutely no idea wtf you are doing or learning about. Lecture barely touch on content and he expects you to an expert in the first week.

Very disorganized, terrible lecturer. The fact that very few out of 30 registered students regularly attended class speaks for itself. Unclear grading criteria for the final project. No feedback on exams or HW. The TAs have no grading rubric and apparently not even the answers to the homework problems. Reading the textbook is only way to get an A.

Dr. Kipper is a very intelligent and kind man. You can tell he knows what he's talking about. Exams (2, midterm + final) are easy to study for, define terms and be able to explain concepts. Oftentimes homework questions are on the exam as well! Homework is always a 100 if you show effort + make due date) He's awesome, would take this class again.

He should be more specific in the grade criteria. He should offer different types of assessment. He should grade students' exams instead of give them to the T.A. There is none feedback in the final papers... we don't know what should be improved =/

Overall amazing professor. Homework is almost always an A as long as you finish them on time. There are extra credit for both the midterm and the final, and even if you don't answer correctly he will still give you as many points possible. Only minor complaint is that for the final paper the word count is a bit high, do it early if possible.

comment: She is passionate and funny yet expects a lot from her students.

She is terrible. Treats 153 as a review and expects you to know all the grammar. Never assigns hw or follows the syllabus but randomly expects you to have done practice problems in the book and quizzes on the answers in class. Only grade is the final which is over grammar that is never taught - just mentioned. Regret taking the class with her.

Douchin is one of the most passionate teachers that I have ever had. Period.  But if you're looking to improve your FR, this is not the class for you.  Skips midterm, doesn't follow syllabus and expects you to already know your grammar and vocabulary.  The only grade in the course is the final-which is mostly grammar that you won't learn here.

The most passionate professor or  teacher i've ever had. You will succeed in her class if you complete the assignments, do the homework and study the textbook. She gives MANY opportunities to improve your grade. Take advantage of all the extra credit assignments she offers, and you will get an A as long as she knows you care and are trying!

She's simply a lovely and charming woman. I looked forward to every french class. Often she'd tell inspirational stories and try to engage the class in debates. She doesn't really follow a syllabus and doesn't use black board. It's hard to know what she expects, but if you approach her, she is very helpful. One of the best professors i've ever had.

A generally very nice old lady --  was very excited during the first class. Interest waned somewhat; she's very disorganized and her grading confuses the hell out of me. But, overall, I'm thankful to have taken the class. Use the textbook: memorize everything and don't skip class.

Honestly, she should not be teaching 153. She believes that you already speak Fr when you enter her class. You do not go over grammar or vocab. You only read stories. She never uses a syllabus, everyone in class was lost each day, midterm was simply skipped, then added on to the final.Very nice though. Great teacher if you already speak fr.

She is entertaining in class but assignments are very ambiguous. Find out when her office hours are (doesn't list them or her email in the syllabus) and go see her often. There are hardly any real assignments but if you want to make a good grade just pick a random page in the book every couple weeks to do for extra credit and turn it in TYPED.

I can understand why some students don't like her teaching because it seems unorganized and unvaried, but she passionate, funny and her spoken French is easy to understand. She's also really helpful if you go see her one-on-one, which is a good idea. I really liked her as a teacher.

Fun, funny and eccentric as a person, but awful as a teacher.She's ambiguous about what you're supposed to do for hw, she NEVER puts down a letter grade for any work that you do (so I'm freaking out about my ambiguous final grade), and she's clearly one of those teachers who has favourites and rewards them the most. I regret taking her class.
awful. just awful.
The title of the class was Aspects of French Grammar, but in this class u will not learn any grammar!
i hate her class. she forced poetry on us

avoid this professor for your own sanity! she will drive you crazy with her senseless grading policies and other ridiculous things (she leaves office hours a half an hour early even when she gets there 15 minutes late). she is awful and of top of it all...I can honestly say that I learned nothing.

C+ here as well.  She tends to love giving those out to people she doesn't favor as much in class.  Wasn't favortism a thing of the past? Apparently not, I really did HOURS of work for this class and it all went unnoticed.  I would advise you STRONGLY to not take this class.  If you are, be on top of your grade.
If people have issues with her, it's their own fault for not doing the work....  I thought she was a really funny, cool, cute French lady.

I took AP French in HS, and was technically exempt from this class. But, i took it thinking it would be easy. Boy was I wrong. I was easily far ahead of the rest of the class, did the work, participated and got shafted extra hard in the end. Extremely unorganized, we strayed away from our syllabus a few weeks in.

HORRIBLE! Diligent worker here and got a C+..and know a few others who received the same grade with even better work ethic.  She has a very traditional style of grading and doesn't really write anything down on your paper. Your surprise comes when you check your final grade...and voila...not pretty. If you take this class, be alert on your grade.
she is absolutely hilarious and makes the class really fun.  on the other hand, she is poorly organized and you are constantly wondering where you stand in your grade.

I had her for recitation, so i can't really comment on her grading style or fairness, but she is HILARIOUS! tell us about her ex-husband, and tells us to shape our mouths like the anus of a chicken to make the correct "oo" sound.

She is fun-loving and great to have in class (as long as you agree with her), but then she absolutely shafts you on your grade. Even if you do all your essays and participate in class every day, it doesn't matter. Likes it when you visit her during office hours, but frequently won't be there herself. Misses appointments - very unprofessional.
Nice lady. Not very organized. Fun conversations in class.
Very nice and flexible.

If you don't suck up to her or have the same opinion as her, she won't like you -- no matter how good your papers are. My advice is to agree with everything she says... even if it kills you. Suck up enough and go to her office hours? You'll be fine.

Definately a good professor, energetic, knowledgable, and enthusiastic about the language. The only thing is the GRADING. The hardest grader i've ever had. even if she likes you, she still might give you a bad grade, so don't slack.

what a crazy old bat.. so nice..but thats part of the plan she makes you think you're doing great.. infact she even said she would let me know if i was gonna get anything less than an A..a B+ later i decided she really doesn't care

The definition of eccentric, but an interesting woman with a wealth of irrational stories.  Once forced me to try her reading glasses on during class.   I would suggest her as a professor for people used to energetic professors.

Energetic yeah but never gives you a sense of how you're doing in the semester even when you ask, then you end up with a less-than-expected grade. Lets you revise papers but class discussion is unorganized. Overall enthusiastic but poor at organization.
Energetic, eccentric, but understanding and extremely nice.
so energetic, interesting, helpful, and a pleasure to learn from.
fun, energetic, knows and loves the language.

Kinsler's econ of education class was awesome. The material is very relevant and very interesting, so except for the beginning, which is almost all econometrics, it's very easy to pay attention. There are 2 papers, 3 tests- standard fare for a 4000 level class. Go to class, take good notes, and it's not a difficult class at all. You'll learn a lot.

comment: His exams are ridiculously hard and he goes very quickly through lecture. If you fall asleep for even five minutes, then you're sure to miss probably the most important part of his lecture. He also loves going over class time by a couple minutes, so get ready to be late to your next class.
You need to go to class. His exams are hard, and require you really understand the material. That being said, he really will help you and if you do the hw properly you can succeed in the class.

Spends 5 minutes of lecture on a difficult proof that will show up on your hw/test, then 30 minutes on calculating the slope of a line that you've been able to do since 10th grade. Lectures are tedious, but you need to attend (and stay awake -- challenging!) so you don't miss the 30 seconds of vital info.
One of the best teachers I've ever had.  He's absolutely crystal clear, I don't think anyone could teach econometrics better.

Class is a waste of time, as he posts all powerpoint presentations online. He is a horrible professor and the class is one of the most boring classes I have ever taken. There is a large curve in the class since he makes the tests (especially the final) extremely difficult. The TA's were extremely useful and helpful, however.
Great professor, excellent lecturer

Was hoping I'd have a change of heart about him but I feel too strongly mid-semester not to chime in. He's smart and not a bad person but the way he teaches is unbelievably confusing. Nothing at all to do with his accent. The course content has become very redundant, syllabi+assignments are messy and grading is extremely unclear. Avoid if possible.

comment: The way Professor Cilas teaches is he talks then you discuss. There's a lot of reading and writing for both papers and exams. The content that he is teaching most of the time literally does not have definitive answers thats why it can seem like the way he marks is unclear but if you meet with him outside of class he can give you specific feedback.

WORST professor ever.  Instructions always unclear. Insists he follows syllabus, does not. Exams are ridiculous. Forgets about assignments and blames us when he magically remembers.  Avoid at all costs.

I found that Dr.Kemedjio was, when independently sought after, very helpful. His assignments did a lot to help students stretch their understanding of the topics at hand. Group collaboration was encouraged. The selection of readings and films for the class was, in my opinion, very well curated. I enjoyed his class.

One of the worst professors I have ever encountered. Not only he is very bad at explaining new grammar or forming discussions, he is not helpful at all either. Do not expect him to respond to your emails. Also, his HW is ridiculous and his grading does not make any sense. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASSES!!!!

If this guy is teaching this class for the semester, do not sign up.  I'd recommend signing up for 204 with another professor. Doesn't seem like he's there for the well-being of the students.  His grading is non-existent and you're all of a sudden slapped with whatever he thinks you deserve.  B+ here but nothing to show for it!

For the more advanced courses, this class SUX! This class is the epitome of boring and I'd honestly rather have spent my time finger painting! I took 2 of his courses and regret every bit of it. Consider dropping the course within the 3 weeks of exploring the course!

I like clias as a person alot. The first day of class i could not understand a word he was saying, but by the end of the semester, i understand practically every word. He really deosn't teach new points well, u really have to teach urself, which sucks, but i got some text books that teach french in english, which helps alot. A really easy grader.

i can tell he must be so respected in mathematics, but he is such a poor lecturer. his class is dull, the explanation of ideas is too theoretical without clear examples so it is so hard to follow and understand. even tho he always uploads his notes, its HARD to understand his idear or his handwriting. i feel bad for him but I feel worse for myself

Actually, he is patient but not helpful at all. The practise matrials do not have key answer and the practise exams are far away from the real exam. He can convey the material he want to discuss, but he cannot let students to understand them.

He has lots of thoughts that can't convey to his students. He is patient and responsible. He uploaded his notes quickly every time after class, and the notes is clear and well-organized. However, his classes are sleepy and not attractive at all.
Not good, do not go to his course and just study yourself.
POOR GUY! Just talk example in class, not very helpful.
Very poor lectures, terrible exam and grading curve.
Practice exam not helpful. Everything post was late!

Professor Greenleaf clearly cares deeply about the content that he is teaching. Given this, his ability to explain what he is doing on the board is very challenging to follow as he primarily focuses on theoretical values and fails to use practical examples to make the content understandable to anyone not interested in proof based mathematics.

Prof. Greenleaf is a brilliant man, yet his lectures make sense to everyone no matter how much you are struggling. His lecture style is fluid and easy to learn from. Very attentive and wants to make sure you understand the material

Dr. Greenleaf is a very thorough lecturer, explanations can be a little long-winded, but he moves at a good pace. He is always respectful to his students and is very helpful during office hours.  He is also willing to accommodate for any conflicts or issues you have. Be aware, tests are very hard.
GREAT PROFESSOR.Very clear during lecture and very helpful. BUT becareful about his exams, sometimes really hard.

Gifted Lecturer.....however you will suffer gradewise as his system is skewed and he gives random pop quizzes on material from lectures over a month ago...So unless you are studying your entire months worth of notes before every class that 15% quiz grade is a killer.
Very good lecturer...Unfortunatley his grading system is absolutely awful, so be prepared to suffer grade-wise.

He's a very thorough and good professor. His lectures are very clear and caters his lectures to making sure even the slowest person understands the material. He should be teaching more classes - at least more than Harper does. (I'm not saying that Harper doesn't have entertainment value though!)

This guy is absolutely top notch. His grading is reasonable and he doesn't pull fast ones on tests, but at the same time you'll only do well if you know the material. He has, by far, the best lecturing style I've ever seen. His lessons are fluid and superbly planned. Overall, a gifted teacher.
No Comments
He seems like a nice guy but be prepared to suffer.  His grading system is ridiculous and his homeworks take forever, I wouldnt recommend taking any class with him.
Greenleaf is very theoretical, but you just have to adjust to the way he teaches.  Personally, I think he is the greatest!!!
Boring and too theoretical to teach anything other than 170 series math.

Greenleaf makes it apparent to his students that he is passionate about mathematics- but he neglects to teach them!  If you're registered for 171Q series classes, be prepared to learn out of the book.

Highly recommend. Better than ECON288. Good mix of theory and application. Prof is a good lecturer and easily available outside of class. Clear and reasonable grading criteria, and lectures are recorded. Attendance is required. Fair extension policy (up to 6 late days total). 6 HWs with minimal Python coding. 2 Midterms with a cheat sheet allowed.
Nice professor!!!!!!

Good, engaging lectures which cover substantive, insightful content. Really nice professor who cares about his students and puts in significant effort to make the learning experience smooth. Grading criteria is generous and clear.
he is brilliant!

Well-run, organized course. It's not hard to get an A but the content is not trivial (you'll learn something). Anson is a good lecturer and the grading criteria is both very clear and very generous. Sometimes his lectures can get really tedious and I didn't feel like he was amazing at explaining challenging concepts.

Brilliant professor, articulate speaker and good pedagogy. All lectures were recorded and all work done in class is on a tablet, which makes for easy revision! Much better than chalk. 

CSC489 was very well designed course: good extension policy, dropping the lowest homework grade, attendance-based grading components, and reasonable exams.

5 homeworks, 2 exams, and you must attend classes in person every lecture. The tasks are average so it is not difficult but still requires much attention.
The lectures are very interesting, and yet the notions are often quite confusing so i'd be better to email the professor for office-hour appointments.

Engaging, passionate, excellent lecturing style. Does a very good job explaining the material. Cares about his students and will help you out if you're struggling. You can get by without doing the optional homework. Easy A if you pay attention to lectures and start the projects early. Pretty light workload. Absolutely one of my favorite professors.

By far the best professor I've had at Rochester when it comes to lecturing. The material taught would be extremely boring if not for him. Projects can be hard especially if you do them by yourself, and you have to study moderately for the tests, but overall not too demanding.

I didn't pass the first two unit exam for csc173, it's my own fault didn't do the HW and take notes though. But after that, I took notes and do his optional HW(not project), I got average of 85% for the rest of the 3 exams. His exam is literally a duplicate of hw, as long as you understand hw, you'll able to do the exam.

Good prof, interesting class, reasonable workload. I recommend starting projects early in case you have questions and want to go to study session (with TAs) because they tend to get very full close to the deadline. He posts optional homework after each class that helps to understand the material. He can be a little condescending in class at times.

Best lecturer I've had in the CS department so far, he explains things very well and is very approachable outside of class despite how he can come off as rude. Go to lecture in person, the tests I did poorly on were because I skipped the lectures and watched recordings after the fact.

Ferguson is amazing as always - easy to understand, and both his assignments and exams are very very fair. He has such an engaging way of explaining things, and I wish there was another class I could take with him! I do think he made 254 a little too easy at times...

Professor Ferguson's lectures are the best in CS department and no one else ever even gets close. Anyway many people say he's mean. I feel like all smart people would have some sort of this problem and clearly Professor Ferguson is way above the threshold of smartness.

One of the best teachers in the department. He has a very specific system for his teaching, but if you engage with it, it works well. The lectures are mostly 1:1 with the free textbook but they're worth going to because he breaks things down well. Stay off your phone, read the textbook, go to study sessions, and you'll learn a lot.

Definitely one of the best professors here. He makes concepts clear and not too hard to learn. First couple projects were a bit tricky using C for the first time, and later ones were easier. All projects were doable, and tests were not hard. Awesome experience.

Professor Ferguson is undoubtedly one of the best professors I have ever had. He's truly passionate about the course material and CS in general, and gives optional homework to solidify your understanding. His lectures are very engaging, and the 5 online exams and projects are quite reasonable - going to class is super helpful and a must!

comment: Overall, He is a good professor. His lectures are interesting and not as boring as other computer science professors however he is a bit condescending and rude especially when you disagree with him. The first three projects were really difficult and time consuming but other than that the content were pretty easy.

By far one of the best CS professors at UR. His lectures are actually pretty fun to listen to because he is very animated and engaging. Tests were not that hard, but first few projects might take a while to get used to (since he doesn't teach you how to use C, you have to teach yourself)
Very passionate about teaching and holds engaging lectures. Exams and projects are relatively easy
He's kind, as far as I know. But you must take his course to major in CS or DS anyway.

comment: Took 173 & 242. Pretty great lecturer and since covid has continued to upload his lecture videos. Yes, he may shame you if you're late and might not always respond best to in-class questions. But, if you see/email him outside of class he's really helpful+accommodating. A health issue took me out of class and he was extremely kind and understanding.

People think Ferguson is mean because he tells people off for using their phone in class and rushes people when they show up late. IMO he is well within his right to do that, if you need your phone that badly you can always step outside. He is actually very friendly to students who show up and are attentive. Very strong teacher as well

Fergie is an excellent professor. He is funny and engaging even when the material isn't because of his passion for the subject. His projects are range from very easy to challenging but fair, and his tests are very easy. He seems tough and strict but is actually very fun and casual. You will learn a lot and it won't be too challenging. GOAT

Delivers lectures pretty well in both 173 and 242 and is clearly very organized, however is a bit demeaning towards questions. 173 projects are graded pretty harshly. 242 projects are much easier but a lot of the material itself feels like he is just reciting the textbook.

He is very rude. If you are late to class he will hurry you to sit down, if you are on your phone he will take two minutes out of lecture to bring attention to you. He is super rude in emails and rarely cuts you slack. Since exams are auto graded you have to enter the answer exactly like he says or wants it, or he wont give you any points.

He does fairly well at explaining the information, except he uses the textbook word for word. If you are confused on examples in class, reading the textbook won't help much because he basically just reads from it. Usually I am able to do 100% of the projects in pervious classes, but in this one I could only do certain parts. The exams were easy.

I wish he explained things in a way that was easier to understand. He talks through things very fast, and I have a difficult time processing things in general- so if I have the time, I do my best to go over material before class. Yet, if I cannot find any specific information online, then I'd have to use textbooks, which to me, is not that helpful.

Professor Ferguson was the most real professor I had the pleasure of learning from at the University of Rochester. Sure, the class was difficult, but he made himself always available for questions and was very honest with me as a student and offered thought provoking questions about students' motivations for being in computer science.

comment: I took both 173 and 242 with him. He is a good teacher imo but he is a mean person. I understood everything from lectures. Never used textbooks and I got A in both classes. His exams and projects are hard but they can be done using lecture materials. He is so mean towards students and usually respond to questions with with: Go to study sessions
Best lectures. Start projects early, install Valgrind, and do the homework.
Such a mean person. He is not there to help you. TA should gets paid more for saving his bad teaching. Be ready to study everything by yourself.
He basically explains very quickly. He doesn't give examples of theoretical explanations well. (He often just explains and finishes.) So, you have to refer to the textbook yourself.

Fergusons classes are basically just a test on your ability to execute pseudocode by hand. He doesnt ever really explain the intuition or reasoning behind anything, and all his tests are simply asking you to execute algorithms by hand. Not very interesting, but not difficult.

comment: CSC 173 was my first experience with professor Ferguson. comment: Professor Ferguson's classes were a delight to experience. He has a precise understanding of the material, making him one of the best professors in the U of R, in my opinion. His Artificial Intelligence course was very noob friendly. However, you must have a strong foundation of computer science and programming to succeed in the course.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Fergie's group projects are so hard, you really need to work in a group. Got laid though, made the work worth it ;)

Whoever gave him a 1/5 is wrong. He was so helpful. When someone asked a question, he NEVER dismissed them, and instead really thought about it, and would answer them when he had a good one. Once he emailed me two weeks later the answer to a difficult question I forgot I asked. Best, most caring professor I've had so far.

Amazing lectures, incredibly engaging, don't skip them. Projects don't take too long if you understand the material well. Homework is optional but highly recommended, he models his test very similar to the homework. Good opportunity for extra help from TA's.

Ferguson is a really good lecturer; probably the best in the department. He comes off as a bit of a hardass, but he does care for his students and is genuinely a nice and funny person. comment: Lectures are awesome, but you still really need to spend a lot of time going over all the materials and reading the textbooks after class; otherwise you will have great trouble in projects and exams.

Great professor, extremely engaging and caring. Isn't too accessible through email but office hours are good. Graded very strictly but if you do what he wants its not too difficult to do well. There is absolutely no room for flexibility or partial credit on tests be aware, HIS process not product!
Best professor in the department. Lectures are extremely organized. Projects need some efforts but are very reasonable and helpful for understanding the content.

Although professor Ferguson might not be the smartest computer scientist, he is definitely the most organized and caring instructor I have ever met in the school. I am so lucky to study my favorite topic with such an amazing professor. He had good jokes but its a pity that we comSci nerds are quiet in class. Hope he could teach more courses!
Fantastic professor, probably the best in the department. Exams are straightforward, projects are sometimes too easy (lots of starter code).

Best lecturer Ive ever had! Interesting topics including intro machine learning concepts. Projects were useful, exams were fair. Just he can be condescending at times and makes you not want to ask him questions...

comment: Professor Ferguson is the best professor I have had for CompSci. His lectures are amazing and organized properly. tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Amazing lectures']

comment: Great professor, best lecturer in the CS department. Funny guy, too.

Professor Ferguson is one of the best lecturers in the department. With that said, his courses are extremely content-rich and can be hard to digest. Usually has 4-5 exams and projects, and they are always due at the same day which is annoying. Very passionate teaching style but picky on students at the same time.
Best professor in CS at the UofR. You ACTUALLY get to learn something useful from his lectures. I've taken his 173 and 242, and I'd take any other class he teaches.

I've loved every class I had with him. Engaging lectures, kept me awake even in the 9:40 time slot. :)Unit system for 173/242 is very intuitive, just don't start the project after the exam or you'll so regret it (which he tells you every unit). He cares a lot about the material and his students, and it shows. Do the reading and hw you'll be fine!
Lots of exams and projects, and the wording was vague. Not interested in helping students. Projects are extremely hard. The code he provided was tricky and usually didnt work.
Fergy is a homie. I took CSC 242, CSC 171, & CSC 173 with him. He may have a tough exterior, but he's really nice if you respect him and work hard. One of my favorite professors.

Tests are very expected based on the homeworks. I have had Ferguson for CSC171, CSC173, and now CSC242. He runs his class the same way every time. Projects and Tests for every unit and a final, but again very expected. You have to work hard but it's possible to succeed in these classes. Love taking classes with him.

comment: I have had professor Ferguson for 171&173. I found 171 to be very easy. 173 is much harder but still doable. What makes me really like Ferguson is that he is a genuinely good person. He is incredibly understanding. If you are having issues in your life, he understands and will give you extensions. If you just talk to him, he will make class easier
He's very inspirational, making the difficulty of the class a source of excitement

Class extremely hard. Expect lots of project assignments , daily homework and extremely difficult exams.  Knows the material for the course well. Seems not interested in helping students. Every time he says "I will have to think about it" when you ask him a question, usually you will not get any response.

Great lectures, engaging

Doesn't like to help you or answer questions, likes to yell a lot, I am glad he no longer teaches this course, because he was definitely not passionate about DMS, but he is about CS and is a much better and happier CS professor!

If 171 is your first exposure to programming, go to class, start your weekly homeworks early, ask questions, go to lab and workshops, start your projects early, go to CSUG tutoring or CETL tutoring for things you don't understand. I did this and I got a very high A (98.X%). You will succeed!

Compared to other CS professors, Ferguson is one of the best at this university. Relatively, he's a great lecturer, really passionate about the field, and pretty straightforward and clear most of the time.  That said, he can be very dismissive of questions and is not very accessible outside of class, he's just not a very kind or caring professor,.
um no

Great teacher, he is clear in his class. Only mandatory attendance is workshops, which help you learn to think through different types of problems. Homework is given weekly that you can learn most everything through. A great way to be introduced to computer science

Great teacher, he is clear in his class. Only mandatory attendance is workshops, which help you learn to think through different types of problems. Homework is given weekly that you can learn most everything through. A great way to be introduced to computer science.
Not too difficult, yet very distant from students.  I received an A off basically my extra credit on the 4 projects that are assigned.

He gave really funny lectures, and really knew the subject matter. As long as you actually did all the homework and projects, you don't really need to attend class, study, or read the book at all. Would love for him to be my drinking buddy.

Great professor, knows his stuff and teaches well in lecture. However, don't expect him to have a lot of office hours for one on one help (due to the sheer size of CSC171) but will indeed answer questions in class if you speak up. Assignments, projects, and whats to be expected throughout the course are always clearly posted online

He is funny and a good lecturer, but I think the course is difficult for one who has no experience in programming.  It's a steep learning curve.  Though you probably won't easily find help directly from the prof (it's a HUGE class, after all), there are plenty of TAs who are eager to help.  His projects and labs aren't easy but are manageable.

Fantastic teacher. Incredibly enthusiastic and helpful. Assignment directions are clear, and he offers a lot of extra resources if you need help. Hands-down one of the best (if not the best) professor in the CS department.

While it's very difficult to get an A in the class (in his own words, it's reserved for *brilliant* students), it's clear he's looking out for you the whole way through. Gives good, clear lectures, and offers a lot of resources to help out on projects and to gauge your progress in the class. Very easy to get at least a B.

He's a fantastic lecturer, one of the best and most dynamic in the department. He's also cool and a good research advisor. If you visit his office expect to be there for at least an hour, he'll chat you up.
Great sense of humor with very entertaining lectures. Gives relevant lectures to the book and is very clear. He also gives tons of starter code for the project and is a fairly easy grader.

Seems like a pretty nice guy, good sense of humor, entertaining lectures for the most part. My only complaint is that the projects are VERY complicated, meaning that he has to provide code to jump-start you, and that code doesn't always work.
Don't go in with the expectation of learning anything and you'll really enjoy the class for its humor value.  Has some really interesting anecdotes.
Worst professor in the world. Terrible teacher and terrible person who takes every opportunity to insult you.

Provides info about quizzes and assignments last minute. In class we just read passages from the textbook and rarely focus on important grammar. Homework is posted sporadically and due on random days/times (doesnt follow the syllabus). She makes some questionable comments in class. Prepare to be called on. She's a nice person but not a good prof.

Prof RR doesn't use BB making it hard to tell your grade (participation accounts for 10% too). Class consists of discussions about textbook pages with seemingly irrelevant info...feels like wasted time. Tests are heavy on vocab and grammar that's covered for about 15 minutes once. Information is given last minute.

comment: None of the tests or projects are in the syllabus. She'll announce them the week before and then not write anything down so you need to remember it yourself. Kept lecturing us about being polite over minor things such as not saying "present" when called on. Show up to class, participate, and do the homework and you'll be fine.

all of the reviews on here are right to some degree. the class itself is very easy. lots of participation is required in class, so if ur an introvert keep that in mind. as long as u don't get on her bad side, you'll be fine.

She is a great professor, all you have to do is show up on class and hand in assignments on time and you will be fine, and even with that kind of stuff she is incredibly understanding. She is clearly passionate about the subject as long as you listen you will learn a lot.

Never be late. Never miss class. Hand things in on time. You'll be fine if you do those three things. I definitely see why people don't like her but in class, she can be very funny and charismatic. Just don't get on her bad side.

One of the WORST professors I've ever had. Not compassionate at all, yells at her students, and gets easily frustrated. If you have to take SPAN 151 or 152, take it with Komocki instead, he's the exact opposite and so incredibly nice!

Never had a problem with her. Then again Im well-behaved and do my work on time. There are a lot of tests but theyre very casual. Horrible. Consistent attitude & don't be shocked if she blames it on her health condition. She gives multiple due dates for each assignment, and treats you with near 0 respect. I am almost certain that she wrote the other reviews here.

She's an amazing teacher, but the class feels harder than it needs to be. Lecture's are great, she's really caring and funny, but expect to participate a decent amount. I'd say the only downside is she doesn't really know how to make tests since they always take way too long to finish. It's not a very hard class if you do the hw and study for tests
Truly cares about her students and will make time outside of class to help you

comment: Profesora R-R is awesome. She's very clear and funny but her class isn't the easiest - you have to do the work. She cares about the wellbeing of her students as well as their academic performance. She calls herself Mother Theresa, she's SO right.

I can say with confidence that professor Rojas is by far the best professor I've had yet. She is amusing, funny, understanding, and very helpful - which isn't to say she's a pushover! You will learn a LOT from her!

Professor Rojas is extremely fun and interesting, my favorite so far at the University. She is engaged and makes a huge effort to help her students and get to know them. The class isn't ridiculously easy, but it is fantastically rewarding and you'll learn a great deal. She is a native speaker and generally only speaks Spanish in class.

Yilmaz was approachable, but doesn't possess very good teaching abilities. Material was difficult, and he just wasn't able to explain the concepts very clearly. Most people attended the lectures, but many just ended up studying with others or self studying to learn the material.

Had Prof Yilmaz this past semester. He's a bit quirky, but has a good sense of humor. I went to all of his classes and I enjoyed his lectures. He sometimes went over HW questions in class which was cool. Exams were tough but his curve is nice, and he even offers hints sometimes during exams. All around, he's a great guy, and this was a solid class.
so bad, so boring, study by yourself.
The accent might be an obstacle to some, but give Professor Yilmaz some credit; he's really funny when you least expect it.

Read the textbook. His assignments go with each segment of the textbook, and you will NEED to read the textbook. The class seems really easy the first four weeks, and all of a sudden the material becomes unbelievable. Get ahead and stay ahead. You might as well not go to lecture, he does not explain or emphasize anything well. Read the chapters.

He is willing to offer help during office hour. He goes over whatever the textbook covers and strictly follows the sequence of textbook. However he doesn't teach extra stuff.  If you thoroughly read textbook and spend time doing homework, you will be find on the exams. He won't give very challenging questions on exams.
He has a good rapport with students. He is there when we need help.
He is a really nice and helpful professor.
Lectures are very dry and boring. Doesn't clearly explain concepts. Exams are very difficult.

Language is most certainly a barrier for Professor Yilmaz- not merely in terms of speaking but writing (exams) as well. Exams were poorly worded or outright contradictory. He makes things more complex than they need be. And worst of all, he seems to think he's a great teacher.
Follows Landsburg textbook, which may or may not be a good thing.

One of the best professors I've had at the UofR. Genuinely cares for the students and their success. Encourages participation and always welcomes feedback. Is willing to help at anytime. Most valuable course I've taken.

Take this course.

One of the most valuable classes I've taken in college. I always struggle with public speaking, but now they are not challenging for me at all. Lectures are more like workshops, and the professor is like a coach who pushes you more. Like others said, he sticks HEAVILY to rubrics, but as long as you do what he wants and put in work then you're good.
He's a very nice guy. Solid class which is useful for life.
This class is not an easy A but would recommend taking it if you want to get better at public speaking, definitely got so much better. Vamos!
He's tuff!
Professor went above and beyond to help this semester which he didn't have to do. and Showed much grace to when I had to bury to family within two weeks. I am thankful truly

Prof. Marsherall is a diligent professor; he gives feedback and suggestions to every student. However, he is very strict with the rubrics, so you'd better follow all his steps and not add additional thoughts. To be honest, sometimes I feel really frustrated in this course because of those limitations.

Dr Drew is a genuinely nice person. He will go to extra lengths to help you out provided that you want to improve. He really cares about teaching and his students. His grading is not lenient; however, he does provide clear grading rubrics for each assignment so us students can know what we are being graded on. Do take this class if you have time!

I dont recommend you guys to take Prof. Drews communication course, well, if you have a chance to skip it. First, workload is heavy. Frankly, some of those help you to construct your points, but the others are repetitive work with no specific meaning. Second, grading criteria is stiff and the way he communicates is hidebound.

Drew will always go out of his way to help ya out. In addition to making me introspect on my public speaking abilities a lot more than I ever would have, he provided the explicit tools in order to bolster my own strengths and to identify and patch my weaknesses. I would highly recommend this class to anyone who has a desire to better their speaking

He is very passionate about the anthropology of world religions because of his field work in this area, which makes lectures interesting but makes it a lot more of a discussion-based class instead of purely lectures. The syllabus has a lot of readings on it but most are not mandatory and he'll make that clear during the first few weeks.

For both ANTH 207 & 205, I second the previous review. Gibson is the GOAT. Very very knowledgeable. His lectures may be boring at times, but his discussion posts and comments are all very engaging and thought-provoking. Also you should definitely go to his office hours. I sometimes feel like I learn more from chatting with him than reading a book.

The GOAT. He genuinely wants you to succeed, as long as you communicate with him he will find a way for you to do so. He's so knowledgeable but not condescending, he still listens to every student as if he has something to learn from them. Very fair grader, just do what you gotta do and you'll be fine. 100% would take again.
He's my favorite professor here. He's knowledgeable, and he's kind. Definitely taking his class again!

comment: He is absolutely the best professor I met at University of Rochester. So inspirational, knowledgable, and caring for student. Lectures are amazing! Definitely choose his course if you can!

cons:
- Contact outside of class is hard bc he doesn't like to use technology
- Classes are pure lecture. He talks the entire time, often with no clear purpose.
- No slides, quizzes, units, objectives, etc.
- long readings
- mandatory weekly discussions in person and online via blogs

pros:
- generally friendly
- few assignments

Although his lectures can be a little boring, he is obviously super knowledge and cares so much about the topic and his students. As long as you do the reading and write the essays, the class is not hard and discussion sections are pretty interesting.

Professor Gibson is one of the kindest professors. His lectures are sometimes long and scattered, but he's very knowledgeable and passionate about what he studies. Graded on three papers (synthesizing readings and some analysis) and participation. If you do well on the papers and show up to class, you'll do great.

Knows his stuff for sure. Sees students as future activists so he genuinely wants people to take stuff away from readings & apply to today (criticize, reflect, etc). One class is him talking the entire time about next week's readings (he knows u won't read all or just skim and it's fine, just read what most interested in) and other is discussion.
Lots of readings to do in this class, so get prepared for it. I probably shouldnt choose it as my cluster...

Fascinating stuff. Tangents a lot but I think they're interesting. There are a lot of readings and you do have to read them but it's definitely worth it. Easy to talk to outside of class. Really cares about his students. A+ would learn from again.

Overall great professor. He is very intelligent and does pretty well in keeping the class engaged on discussion days. The class is pretty easy only 3 essays. Just try and keep up with the readings and actually listen to what he says during lectures. Typically its all pretty darn interesting if you ask me.

Overall I find him to be a great professor. This class is given on tues. and thurs. so he has one day to lecture about the readings and the other day for discussion on them. During discussion days he doesn't talk at all and lets the class handle the discussion. Since the topics are are interesting its a pretty good class. Heavy readings though!

He is a nice enough guy, but he can lecture for a full class period and I have no idea what he's talking about.  His lectures are really scattered and unclear, but they don't seem to matter for the homework and essays.  There's no tests so the class is easy enough and passable but sitting through it twice a week is a struggle.

Gibson is incredibly intelligent and very familiar with history, politics and theory.  His courses are great if you are interested in theory, but those who might not be will find it a waste.  He is slightly monotoned, but the material is fascinating enough to make up for it.
get coffee before class...very smart guy
It's too bad such an intelligent guy has such a monotone.

Tom is a great guy, who tries to supress his liberal views.  He has a wealth of knowledge about the world.  His voice is pleasant, almost too pleasant, just get some coffee and you'll be glad you paid attention, he'll blow ur mind man...
BORING
He is interesting if you can stay awake, which is pretty hard because he has long pauses and a soothing voice.  Very interesting but not really charasmatic.

Very boring lectures but he takes attendance for the first half of the semester.  Lots of reading if you actually do the readings, but only 2 essays overall so not too much work outside of journal entries.
Hard Grader
Hard grader.

Professor Kocherlakota is a great lecturer who does a great job at connecting the course material to current events. As the former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, he adds to his lectures his own insights gleaned from his experience, a real plus considering his class is all about monetary policy.
He is super smart and inspiring but he makes his classes super boring. Also he's not that accessible outside of class.

He was the former President of the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, so he lends a lot of personal experience and insight to his lectures. He presents info from the readings in a really digestible way, so going to lecture is a must. However, he'll still ask questions on material not brought up in class, so do the readings as well.

comment: One of my favourite econ professor! Inspiring lectures.
She's an expert in her field. But as undergrads, we are mere fetuses. She'd have a legendary recorded lecture series.

This was one of Professor Nichols first time teaching a college class and at times it was difficult because she was new to lecturing but by the end she did a great job. She moves a little fast in lecture so pay attention, but is super caring and always makes herself available for extra help. The concepts in this class are moderately difficult.
Grade your "Grade on Completion" Homework for six weeks, never respond to your email. Does not follow the grading rubric.

I created an account purely to give a review for this professor. He is the most disrespectful inhumane professor I have ever had to interact with. He doesn't have a drop of morality in his soul for anyone and constantly takes out his anger on his students.
The professor gives great lectures but is unusually strict about a few things that aren't in the syllabus.

He should not be teaching courses. He didn't seem to care much about students or actually coming to class. The course was not on a hard topic but his lack of teaching made it difficult to grasp the concepts and he blamed the students for not understanding. He is extremely strict on deadlines and despite missing a quarter of classes gives no leeway.

I wouldn't say Criswell is a lazy person, but he definitely is a lazy professor. Lazy with returning work to students, responding to emails in a reasonable amount of time, and posting lecture material. But he'll make a big stink if you walk in two minutes late because it's a "reflection of your character". Kinda insufferable and the work is hard.

Slow grader, slow responses to emails (will not respond to emails sometimes), and does not upload lecture materials. Programming project writeups are confusing and the tools you have to use for them are difficult to work with. Can be condescending and full of himself at times. Would've gotten more out of an online course if I'm being honest.
This class was incredibly well-taught, I almost forgot I took this class!

Professor Criswell's CSC252 is an exemplary showcase on teaching with passion. His lectures are filled with fun moments and performance arts, alone with energy that can only be found in hospitals. The lecture is very informative and usually require a whole page of post-it note for every lecture to fit in all the information taught.

This course by professor criswell was an amazing example of why all CS researchers aren't fitted to teach. In this inspirational course, I have accumulated knowledge that can be distilled onto a single 8x11 standard printing paper. His lectures have never failed me, if sleeping in his class was my goal.

Took CSC 252; this is one of the best professors I've met. He has clear grading criteria and words he uses are exquisitely labyrinth; the quizzes are well phrased and weighted reasonably where one question on the quiz is only worth single digits of your total grade. He gives timely feedback; homework is graded usually within 5 to 7 business weeks.

I was in Prof. Criswell's class for both CSC278 and CSC256(not currently available in the course selection field). Prof. Criswell is one of the best I have had the pleasure of learning from. His lectures are great. He explains all the concepts in a way that is fun and very easy to understand. Plus, he is always willing to provide guidance.

Prof. Criswell is condescending and disrespectful. He doesn't have the students best interest in mind and frequently brags about how he gets to do things (like be forgetful, not respond to your emails, not show up for office hours) because he is a "professor". You need ask the TAs for coding question (he doesn't know much about Linux internals).
Grades late, not receptive to feedback. Doesn't post lecture slides. Course is uninteresting.
Ms. Kiggins is "cool", "calm" and "collected" and she certainly brings a breadth of practical experience and expertise.
the first prof that impressed me profoundly

He is my favorite math prof at u of r. He laid the foundation of my mathematical mindset that benefited my later math-related studies. As a first semester freshman class in the university, it was a hard transition from high school math to proof heavy analysis but he helped me make it interesting and worthwhile. I cannot thank him more
Professor Haessig gives very well-organized lectures and is willing to answer students' questions.

He is very smart, gentle, polite, nice, organized and patient:) He teaches u how to think and his class is full of logics. I think all the students in our class love him!!! Because of him, I decide to change my major into math. Never need to be afraid to ask why and expression my confusion, feel very comfortable to learn math with this professor><.
Very nice professor. I'm considering going to math graduate school after taking his course.
My best decision at this school was to take this class. The lectures are clear and well paced, the content is extremely interesting, and the grading is very fair.
Really good professor. The class was fun and you actually get to learn. The book is really useful too.

The professor often starts class with a good story related to the matter. He jumps into teaching soon enough, and may be fast on some topics, depending on the student. Don't skip class, because you can find yourself lost in the next lecture. And don't expect to read the online notes; the notes on the projector are close to illegible.

comment: He is really helpful. He explains things patiently and clearly in his office hours. He doesn't give an easy curve though. A lot of students got pretty bad grades in this class. Overall, he is definitely one of the better professors in math department.
Great professor. He really did a great job at teaching the material. He made sure that students understood what he was talking about and he prepared us well for the midterm. Great guy too.

Definitely the professor to take!  He is a math genius who is super approachable and nice and who genuinely cares.  Even the following semester he remembered me and asked how I was doing.  If you don't understand something he is always there to help, and his problem examples are perfect for studying for the exams.  Take him!

Prof. Haessig was a very good professor. At times he seemed a bit unorganized, but it's clear that he knows what he's talking about. He also does a very good job of explaining why things are a certain way and relates to students well. The class isn't super-easy, but it's very manageable. All in all, Haessig is a good choice for a Calc professor.

You quickly realize how smart he truly is. He genuinely cares and wants you to understand the WHY behind math. I actually enjoyed coming to this class although math isn't my favorite subject because he's such a great lecturer.

He is really nice and always is there to help the students. If you have any questions be sure to ask him or just go meet him during office hours. And if you have the slightest interest in majoring in maths or joining research, he is probably the most helpful person around.

Haessig is a nice guy, sort of awkward, but in a good, funny way. Lectures aren't super exciting, but he does a good job of preparing notes that are helpful.  If you go to his office hours he's great.  Exams aren't bad at all if you go to class and do the homework. He really wants his students to do well, and is very willing to help

I love this man. Everything he does makes me laugh, and I was always disappointed when lecture was over. Very clear instruction, the notes I was taking were so useful I felt like I was back in high school. :)

Prof Haessig is a wonderful math prof- and I wish we had more like him at this school. He covers every topic at a good pace, makes sure we understand it, and is very approachable. He always has fun jokes and is always smiling. He genuinely cares about his students and is, over all, a great guy. I am very glad he was hired for a professorship at UR.
This class alone was very difficult, but he in no way made it easier. the only reason i would go to class is because he is hot.

The class was mind-boggling hard.  It was all proof-based, so it sucks for all math minors and majors.  The prof likes to talk to himself during class and then makes crazy exclamations that make no sense, especially if you could not hear what he was mumbling about.
Great professor. Explains concepts very clearly and is extremely helpful. MTH 162Q is a hard class, but grading was very fair. Highly recommended.

One of the top 3 professors I have had in college.  I've had him for 282 and 233, and his lecture notes are flawless.  He really cares about his students and loves what he does.  He even took time out of his busy schedule to have an independent study seminar...please stay at UR Doug!
Good Lectures, feed back, character. Tests are hard, but appropriate curves.

Great teacher. So many teachers at UR are either smart but can't teach or are nice teachers but don't know their stuff. But Haessig is the perfect balance of the two. He's really smart, but still great at explaining difficult subjects. He's very fair when it comes to grading, and he makes class enjoyable with his enthusiasm and sense of humor.

Best teacher I've had at UR (MTH 141+142) He is approachable, friendly, and can make sense out of anything. EXTREMELY helpful; this guy would stay past dark in his office helping me with problems. The class material can be a little tough, just stay on top of WebWork and you will be fine. The tests are almost verbatim from WebWork so do it.
Haessig really wants everyone in the class to learn. He is extremely helpful especially with homework questions. He also will let you turn in homework late and redo your homework if you ask him.

Had Doug for 141 and 142. If you took calc in high school, dont bother going to lecture.  Just do the webwork.  Doug will help you if you have questions, or just go to recitation.  Exams are easy if you've kept up with webwork.  Doug seemed like a good prof, but I didnt go to class much.  From what I hear, the other 141 professors are terrible.
He's a pretty nice guy who honestly wants to teach you the material.

He looks like the dude from scooby doo. (lol) Well he was prolly the best math professor i had at uci. He is clear and concise unlike all the asain math teachers at uci. His tests are straight forward and you should ace his class if you go to lecture.

Professor Jessica Robinson, does not give good feedback. Her feedback's are mostly a comment " I agree" in response to the peer feedback a student gives on the paper. Moreover, if you go to her office hours for feedback, She says no to give any feedback and says if I give you feedback, I will have to do that for all students. She is not helpful.
Not approachable and biased grader

comment: Interesting class, very reasonable professor who's invested in your learning.

Professor is clearly invested in his students. Approachable for sure and gives amazing feedback. In class, he always seems to brighten the mood with his teaching style and takes the questions of his students seriously. I definitely improved on my writing skills after taking the course. Awesome professor.

He really cares about phil and students - he went out of his way to meet with me in the evenings bc of my busy schedule to make sure I understood concepts. He also helped me with another phil class b/c I was struggling. Lectures are long but philosophy isn't exciting stuff - puts in more effort than any other PhD I know - worthwhile class!
Clearly cares about students. Lectures can get dry and long.

comment: Classes are absolutely useless and extremely boring. Readings are boring and terribly useless, too. Gives good feedback and is a pretty (I'd say overly) cooperative guy with deadlines. Just skip classes when you can (cause participation is part of the grade) and don't waste your time on readings, they don't matter at all for anything.

Professor Rowley is a really good guy The class is boring and very dry, again it's not hard or impossible but Ethics at the Edges of Life is a very dry class, but he's a great guy and it's good he's teaching it. I can say I definitely became a more purposeful writer after taking him. He gives great feedback on your papers so you can correct them
Great professor. He tends to ramble on a bit though. He gives great feedback on papers and is clear about what he wants. Interesting topics as well.
Great professor. Hard class, but interesting

I love Julie! She's such a nice professor and this course is also pretty interesting. And we got chance to sing with those amazing chamber singers which is so cool!!! I will definitely take it again next semester and probably for every semesters in the future. Grade is based on attendance and two concerts only, so come and have fun!

She is such a nice woman, and she is very understanding. She never asks too much of students, and she's very chill all the time. If you like singing and want to relax, join. It is a nice thing to do once a week, and it's not very taxing, mentally.

Professor Otis is great. He was my favorite professor freshman year. Very kind and respectful, and lets you know what he wants. Very approachable, and great at writing. The work load Is very doable and light. If you're going to take a writing class, take his! GOAT

Good guy. If you want an easy intro to ethics, this class was fine, but it was honestly too easy. I don't feel like I walked away with much. If you're really interested in philosophy, other classes are likely a better use of your time. However discussions among the students on their ideas were always interesting, and I liked his use of class polls.

Professor Otis is very nice and has good and interesting lectures. He also gives feedback on the quizzes and final paper before you turn in your work to help you get an A. Highly recommend his class to any students looking to gain a basic understanding of philosophy and ethics.

Man Machine and Morality is a great writing class, not too much work and Otis gives genuinely good feedback and can provide more if you ask. The structure of the class is writing focused so you don't learn too much the second half of the semester outside your own research but it serves as a basic philosophy intro. Otis makes things clear and easy!

he is a little bit lazy and sometimes slacks off
but i promise there's no easier way than taking his class to get A and 4 credit, just submit every assignment then you got it

Professor Otis is a nice guy who will give you great feedback when you need it. If you follow the directions and put in reasonable effort you're almost guaranteed an A. If you're struggling to choose a Writing 105 class and you want an A, Otis is the best pick. He'll almost always give you an extension if you ask.

Clear grader on writing, and very good at providing feedback outside of class, and a fun professor to talk to. He makes it easy to succeed if you put in the work (which isn't much compared to the other writing profs.)
BEST Writing Professor!!

Man, Machine, and Morality is probably one of the easier WRTG 105 courses. Very little reading outside of class, and the only big assignments are the short essay and final research essay that all the other 105 courses have. He also gives good feedback on drafts, so it's very easy to get an A in his class.

Man, Machine, Mortality was the easiest class ever. As long as you come to most classes and try the slightest bit you will get an A. If you are looking to genuinely learn then this not the class for you, however, if like many you are just trying to fulfill WRTG105, this is the best class.

100000% recommend taking his writhing class. It is not hard and it really helps you develop as a better writer. He is understanding and really cares about the topic. He drops 2 of your lowest informal assessment grades and grades a lot of things based off effort. I learned a lot about the ethics of AI in this class and would love to take another.

super chill professor, is willing to give extensions if you just ask and tell the truth, topics revolve around ai and morality, you're graded on some in class informal assignments (3-6 pts), a short essay (100 pts), and the 8 to 10 page research paper (you will not pass if you dont turn it in). miss 1 informal assignment, it wont hurt your grade

comment: Super nice guy, and very willing to give extensions. The essay criteria was super clear and the assignments were easy enough to do. My only gripe with him was just that he didn't give a lot of assignments so if you got a few points off a formal assignment it kind of did a bit of damage.

Professor Otis is great. He has clear guidelines on his papers and understands that most people going through his class aren't English Majors. He is very accommodating and gives great feedback on papers. He also lectures well and gives good advice on how to approach argumentative essays.
tags: ['Clear grading criteria', 'Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: Man, Machine, and Morality turned out to be way more interesting than I thought. James is very engaging and knowledgeable on the topics discussed in class. He is also very empathetic with students and understands our busy schedules. He is incredibly kind and truly wants you to succeed. Take his advice carefully and you will be more than fine.
Such a great professor. Easy A if you attend every class and complete the project on time.
Would like to take this professor's class again

he is a great professor. i am a stem person but i found his class very interesting. flexible teaching style, go with the flow guy. no final, just 3 short essays. does miss class sometimes but usually gives enough notice. you're able to submit your own topics to talk about. no hw, some in-class assignments.

Somewhat reading heavy at the start of the semester, but once we got into the writing portion not so much. Less writing assignments compared to what other WRTG 105 classes had, and he is a pretty fair grader, and can be lenient with deadlines if you ask.

Easy to follow lectures and lenient grader. Majority of assignments are graded by completion, including part of the grade for the final research paper. Half the classes at the end of the year are just doing your work in class, which should be optional to attend, but he randomly check for attendance. Easy A if you do the work.
He is very sympathetic with students. We had good discussion in the class. Grading is not hard at all!

I took "Man, Machine, and Morality" and it was a super fun class. His lectures are short and sweet and encourage class participation, and he gives plenty of time to work in class so there's not too much work to do outside. If you want to write about something a little different from the prompt he's, laid back about it as long as you do it well.

Really good professor. Makes it clear exactly what he wants in the papers and is very easily accessible outside of class. He understands that writing isn't everyone's strong suit so he gives plenty of time in class to complete assignments. Often makes attending class optional.
Good
Good professor, cares a lot about the material, and makes it challenging but fair. If you really commit to this class, you'll learn a lot. You get out of it what you put in.

Professor Oakes is a bad professor. He simply derives equations in class, and then quickly and poorly goes over examples. He does not explain concepts well, nor does he really teach understanding. Like said by others, his tests are not similar to the hw. The only reason I got an A is because I took AP Physics. Do NOT take his class, take self-paced
Do not take this professor' class!!! You will learn nothing because you could not understand anything.

All he does in class is derive equations. His exams are nothing like the homework or workshops, which he claims to base them off of. Overall, not a good professor, but is very knowledgeable as a researcher.  He curves this intro class to a C. Those who do well seem to have taken the course before. Good luck to you if you have this professor.

He is a great teacher! He has a presentation for each lecture. The way his test work is that he makes it really hard so that the average is around a 55% however he curves the median to a 75 so usually curves are +20 points. He is understanding when it comes to mistakes on a test. Great professor. Dont trust the last review.
Tough for people who aren't familiar with his teaching style.
Rebecca is an amazing writing teacher. I feel so much more confident in graduate school after taking her class!

comment: This instructor is nitpicky. She looks for spaces, periods missing or inadvertently present in the APA format, claims that citations are missing when they are there, gives written directions that change when grading. Weekly APA quizzes, assigned reading from an APA MANUAL. A five page paper with at least 3 revisions, all for a ONE CREDIT COURSE.

Prof Tzeferacos clearly cares about his students and about teaching - he always answers questions in class and will meet with you to go over stuff you don't understand. However.. his lectures are a mess if you're in the class to learn. He goes over super complicated examples but doesn't really teach you the basic concepts. It's unfortunate.

Maybe he saw the reviews and changed things cz i don't get why people are complaining. Content is hard but it's easy to get an A, I barely studied. Lectures might go off into unnecessary integrals sometimes but I don't think he was bad at explaining things. Kind person, clearly cares for his students, wants feedback, curved the final!!

Easily the worst class I have taken at the U of R. E&M isn't easy to begin with and he absolutely does not make it easier. Thank whatever you believe in that lab and workshop count as a notable part of your grade. He seems like a genuienely nice person that does care lots for his students though. It's unfortunate that the lectures are not helpful.

To the rising sophomore at U of R who needs to take 122, do not fear. Do not fall for the horror stories. I don't think Petros is the best lecturer I've ever had but he curves so generously and genuinely cares about us students. Read the textbook, try on the homework, and you will be completely fine.

He is trying to make this course better and it shows. He provides in class review sessions before a midterm, and the class averages on exams have been around a B+ or A-, the semester I took the course. If you just try in the class, you will pass. The office hours are helpful, and if you did poorly on an exam you can still bounce back.

comment: Physic 2 is really hard, but he does not make it easier. Really nice guy that cares about the students, but he lectures are a waste of time and he never explains the concepts of what we are learning. He cares more about making crazy integrals on problems. But you can get awful test scores and still get a passing grade.

This course is hard, but he doesn't make it any easier. Lectures are rushed and he opts to go through complicated problems instead of teaching the concepts needed to understand them. Reading the textbook and seeing a tutor is far more beneficial. The TAs are wildly inconsistent with their grading, so HW grades largely boil down to who your TA is.

Worst class I've taken at UofR. Had to watch Youtube videos and read the textbook to learn this course. Lectures make the course seem more complicated then it should be. He is obsessed with academic dishonesty. He posts fake answers on Chegg and will edit old HW answer keys and make them wrong in order to catch people for academic dishonesty.
Nice guy but awful incomprehensible lectures done quickly on slides

comment: Grade class

The professor is excellent; his personal qualities are understanding and helpful. This professor does not have much to do with pedagogy and researcher than a professor. Lectures are complex and incomprehensible.Students stopped attending lectures after the second exam, and there was no class activity, hence the lack of motivation to attend lectures

He clearly cares deeply about the students and is a nice guy, but lectures are difficult to follow, confusing, and not super well organized. After the first month or so we were at about 40% lecture attendance and it gradually declined from there. Get a good study group, get ready to read the textbook and watch videos.

Lectures are pointless, you will not learn anything from them, he rambles through PowerPoint slides, going over complex integrals and theory as opposed to the actual inner workings of E and M and focusing on genuine understanding. Read the textbook.

comment: Professor's lectures are a bit convoluted and winding, but he is super kind and willing to help. Homeworks are killer, but the tests not so much. Class structure, with the workshops and all, is very helpful.

Professor Tzeferacos is a very nice man and is very accessible to students. This class is the hardest I have taken at the U of R. The material is very difficult and the workshops are long and treacherous. With that being said there are ample opportunities to get an A in this class with several point opportunities.
He is a fantastic professor. The course is really hard; however, there are a lot of ways to get the final grade higher.

His lectures sometimes were a little unclear, but he clearly wants you to succeed and there are many ways to boost your grade (HW, labs, extra credit) in the class outside of exams. Workshops are helpful, so make sure to attend them.

He is the worst Professor I have ever had at this school. He teaches the material poorly and tests on concepts that are not made apparent in the practice exam. The midterms make zero sense, and he truly sets you up to fail.
Dont even bother going to his lectures, it is totally useless. Practice exams totally irrelevant with wrong answer key. Doesn't post all information for exams (hw/workshop solutions etc)

comment: He clearly knows the material well and is passionate about it. His lectures can be a bit confusing as there is a lot of information on them, but they help a lot for the homework as some questions are exactly the same. The TA's can be a hit or a miss, luckily I had a good TA which really helped with my understanding. If not, read the textbook!!!

Avoid if you can, if not it'll be okay. He grades nicely (85 is an A), but learning anything from his lectures is impossible. Also, the TAs are very rough. E&M is a hard class. Completely learned this course from the textbook which is good, so recommend renting/buying that.
Do not write. Most of the explanations are done through slides (maybe because of the online classes, it's 2020). Not very engaging but is flexible on gradings.

A lot of homework, I hate engineering process procedure, that's a waste of time for easy questions that you don't even need to think about the steps and you can solve that with 1 simple formula used. The professor is good btw.
