comment: Kind of weird grading scale, but great professor. Homework quizzes are easy if you did the homework.

Dr. Brown is super helpful and cares for his students! Unfortunately, the class is very difficult. There is a ton of homework, and some weeks I had up to 10 hours. The homework is a very good reflection of the tests, though! The lectures are sometimes helpful, other times not. Lastly, I S/F grading and got S.

Writing 10 pages of homework that requires reading 20 pages to do, 2 hard midterms, no past exams, final as a group presentation project, grade ranking instead of grade curve, all means this is an extremely hard 101 course. But Dr Brown is not a bad professor by any means, and an A is possible if you put more time after lecture than your peers.

All around great professor. Really good at what he does, and his passion for biomedical engineering really rubs off on his students. He is the only professor that teachers BME101 so first-year BME students do not have a choice but to have him, but he is such an awesome teacher that I would not have it any other way.
He is a nice person, though the assignments are a lot and he really cares about the sig fig. Also, the criteria are vague so you won't get detailed feedback on your final grade.

Great Professor, take the time to do the homework and attend office hours. Go the extra mile to make sure all instructions are followed (i.e. pay attention to sig figs/boxing answers/etc.) ASK QUESTIONS IN CLASS!! Dr. Brown responds to emails so don't be afraid to reach out.

Dr. Brown is a great professor and a great person. I really enjoyed this class. If you want to succeed in this class, GO TO OFFICE HOURS! There is homework every week graded on accuracy. Its a tough class and you need to put in the work
love him but also hate him. You will never know your grade until the last moment

A lot of people struggle with BME101 and here's why: nobody expects that it will be hard so people go in thinking they can barely study and be fine. The average for the first exam was 35/78. The exam time is just 50 minutes, so don't expect to finish, it's okay. The average of the class is weighted to a B-, so just hope you are above the average.

Clearly passionate about the subject, but not great at explaining topics. Makes the course frustrating if you haven't taken physics courses before. He instructed the TAs to grade more harshly midway through the semester because he wanted a "wider spread of grades". Overall felt like a weeder course for BME students. Interesting material though.

Dr. Brown was very understanding and always willing to help his students. The class is tough but if you put in the work and use the TAs office hours, you will be ok. Put a lot of effort into the homeworks because they are worth a lot. Brown is a funny guy and his class is enjoyable too.

Not an easy A, probably because this is not an easy major. Professor Brown is so funny and gets the material across, but ultimately it is up to you to do well. The readings are helpful to do before class and a lot of material comes from them. I had fun though and would definitely take him again.

Focuses in class on the math parts of the class, but you need to read BOTH textbooks for the homeworks and labs. Homeworks are pretty hard and the TAs are useless, but the prof is great. Charismatic and you can tell he genuinely cares about what he's teaching. If you can, get on his good side and get a letter of recommendation from him.

The tests in this class are brutal. Nothing like the practice ones that are posted. They are also in class so you have very little time to finish. He's a nice guy and an interesting lecturer, but this is a very hard class. There's a reason lots of BME students switch majors.
tags: ['Lots of homework', "Skip class? You won't pass."]

comment: Dr. Brown's BME 101 is a very physics heavy course. Homework is heavy but managable with good planning. Put effort into the HW because it prepares you very well for the exams. THE EXAMS ARE TIME INTENSIVE, RUSH THROUGH THE QUESTIONS AS FAST AS POSSIBLE. You are not expected to finish every question, get as many points as fast as you possibly can.
tags: ['Respected', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK']

comment: Dr. Brown, who most BME students will take for BME 101, is an absolute gem of the university. I strongly recommend that you take his Biomedical Microscopy course, BME 270. He takes the class seriously, because it is his passion, and that passion bleeds through every lecture and activity he prepares for the class. Take this course.

Dr Brown is the most energetic teddy bear. He makes any topic fun and interesting because he is clearly so passionate. He is a bit all over the place so it is hard to know what to expect from homeworks and tests, but you will understand the concepts.

The intro to neuro class is a good introduction to neuroscience at UR. His class is fair, but hard, and the tests are easy if you study hard enough and listen to lectures. Bring a recorder, his slides are only pictures.
He is very nice, but his class is very hard
He leaves no holes in his explanations, he is my favorite neuroscience professor at the University of Rochester
good lecturer, knows the subject really well

He's an exceptional lecturer: while he's not funny nor animated, he is very clear, organized, and genuinely interesting. Be sure to bring a recorder, as the slides only have pictures. The class is challenging, but the practice exams help a lot. If you're interested in neuro, you'll probably enjoy his lectures. NSC249 is much better than NSC201 IMO

Nordeen (the man...he also has a wife who teaches) is a very organized lecturer and clear on the material. He is, however, kind of boring. Slides are useless unless you have the lectures recorded (the ppt's are only pictures, no words).
slides fairly useless for studying but pretty good lectures

I thought he did an alright job.  He is always there to meet with you in office hours if you need it.  The tests are not hard if you do the back ones.  He is kind of boring and not excited about the material.  But overall not bad

Instead of worrying about fluffing up his vocabulary in lectures, he should turn his attention how he treats students.  The intro neiro class is used by him to pick out the brightest students to work in his lab.  He told me getting my masters in Neuroscience would be a waste of my time.  The favortism is sickening.
No Comments

Prof. Nordeen didn't care the least bit about the fact that I couldn't write a paper because my mother was sick with cancer and eventually died later that year.  There is another student I know who had a similar situation and he didn't care there either.

Horrible lecturer, simply just read his slides. Somewhat responsive to his emails, but doesn't work efficiently. Unclear about what he wants in homework/projects/exams. Your codes could execute all the things he asked in question but still would deduct points because you didn't do it the way "he expected".
Professor Schwarz is a good professor with passion; I would definitely work with him again if I have a chance to become a TA.

This course is honestly the most speechless course I took as a BME student. He assumes everyone has a good foundation in coding and starts giving extremely hard midterms. We don't even know what exactly are his expectations for a good presentation. Also, the final is like a pain in the ass. He just likes to see his student suffer from tons of tasks

Ok, the course itself, fine, the labs especially were helpful. Lectures on the other hand, not very helpful. I went to most of them until the end and honestly I did better on my own versus going to lecture. The project at the end was a nice topic but good luck trying to get a group to work well together. At least he responds to emails?
tags: ['Beware of pop quizzes', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Let me preface this by saying that this course is NOT beginner friendly. Do NOT go to lecture. He says the same things on the slides (better off on your own). Comments are very important in your code so don't skimp on it. His attitude in class is very monotone and not engaging. He will give you pretty much no help on the project at the end. GL!

The professor only reads off what is on his slides word for word and does not explain much after that. The textbook is optional and you need to do practice outside of class for the midterms. He does demonstrations, but most of the hand-on coding will come from the labs and the TAs.
Very easy class, don't actually have to do the readings for class, BUT you do have do do them to write the two papers required. If you actually attend, she's a good professor and you'll learn a lot.

Bigelow seems like a nice guy, but he is near-unintelligibly quiet in lecture, doesn't respond to email, and generally explains topics very poorly. Even if you learn from the textbook, there are certain things you will be tested on that he does not give outside resources for. He will also not give you an preparation for what will be on exams!

Aside from not posting a syllabus (he announces everything each lecture). He is a very straightforward professor and incredible lecturer. He not only introduces basic quantum, but prepares students with more advanced topics such as Entanglement and Dirac notation. Contacting him takes time, so don't be afraid to talk him about meetings after class.

He has short lectures and while they do have examples they can be a little too much theory. He can be hard to reach outside of class and tended to post homework late and not actually do the weekly quizzes
Easy to get an A in his class and he is a good researcher, yet he is really bad at teaching.

Did not attend more than 5 lectures for the entire semester. Prof Bigelow is a very nice guy and cares a lot but his lectures are not useful at all. He presents the slides and then reads and explains them. There is no working through long problems in class. Workshops are a complete waste of 3 hours. Class material is not bad if u r in engineering.
His grading is very inconsistent, as he says he will have quizzes every week but at the end of the semester we've only had 2
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Lecture heavy', 'Graded by few things']

comment: Learned a little, but mostly was frustrated by group assignments and professors style. He definitely likes the sound of his own voice and has a large ego. This class is required.

I think of all the stem professors I've taken in this school, Professor Bigelow ranks in the top 5. His physics 113 was not graded on a curve but he didn't need to. His expectations were clear on what to do to ace the class in terms of number of points needed to earn for certain grades and was available outside class for help!
Possibly the nicest human ever. I had to take Physics and I am terrible at it. He was super helpful, caring, and patient. If you have a class with him, you are lucky!
Incredibly knowledgeable, helpful, and all-around friendly nice guy.  Take a class with him if you possibly can.
No Comments
A difficult course (but then quantum always is), but an EXCELLENT teacher and a great all-around guy.  Very busy, though, so be sure to *schedule* office-hours & other appointments.

She is, although a confusing lecturer at times, good at clarifying what she means, and very accessible. Her exams are also very fair, and if a question is missed by a majority of the class, she will often remove it from grade calculations.

Make sure to attend lectures and learn from the lecture slides. Tests were pretty okay. She's a very sweet professor and tries to give extra credit opportunities to boost your grade. She often goes overtime during her lectures though. Try to find a good studying/note-taking method for this class.

Took her Bio 112 this year and her lecture style is not for the weak. If you are coming in wondering if you should use your AP credit and take this class and you are on the fence about your decision, I recommend you don't take this class. She is a very sweet person, but her lectures get super off topic and she hardly finishes her slides on time.

Her lectures are all over the place and she seldom finishes her slides in time. She's a really sweet person though, and her tests are very fair. There's a lot of material per exam and no cheat sheet but overall it was manageable. She's very open about grading and gives opportunities to boost your grade.

Took her 112 and attended all lectures. Usually easy to understand but can occasionally get off track. A good but not great lecturer. Her lectures on mechanisms (DNA replication, translation, etc.) are the most comprehensible. Guest lecturers are usually a tad better but can be worse. Overall a good professor, and an incredibly sweet person.

Really sweet professor that will help you if you put in the work to understand class material. Slides don't have much text, so you really need to understand the concepts. Make sure to sit in the front and record lectures if possible. Overall, just make sure you are making a faithful effort.

Very memorization heavy exams but nothing difficult. Lectures are not recorded so you should go even if it's not factored in grade. Strongly recc. flash cards & study guides before each exam especially to keep up w/ all the terminology

Lock in and you'll be fine. She DOES NOT RECORD LECTURES! The information in lecture is overwhelming and excessive relative to what is tested on, but it's interesting and she's clear about what will be asked about (you'll catch on eventually). Exams are not that bad, and she's very much willing to work with you to set you up for success!

If you go to lecture and put in the work outside of class, you will be fine. The entirety of the grade you receive will be focused on how well you do on the 3 exams. Overall, it is a tough course, but not impossible. Mary is willing to help you out if you need clarification. USE OFFICE HOURS.

The most unorganized professor I've ever had. The first test was impossible, and nobody finished because she made it twice as long as it should've been. Her lectures consist of her stating random facts that nobody understands. There are no words on her slides, just hundreds of slides with pictures. Class isn't recorded so attendance is a must.

The rating seems low because he teaches a lot of intro courses and people don't like coding. As a CS student who has taken several courses with him, he is a very knowledgeable, intelligent, and helpful prof.

Honestly, people don't appreciate the effort that Ted put into organizing this course. The materials are actually very clear, the textbook is easy to follow, and the labs have straightforward instructions. The structure is THERE, you just have to keep up.

Most boring lectures of all time, expect to have to force yourself to go to them. Instructions on labs can be confusing. Expect to learn most of the material independently. If there's another professor you could choose instead of Pawlicki, I recommend choosing them instead.

Pretty chill guy! Gave extra credit on the last day of class just for showing up. His exams are on the tougher side fyi. 5 homeworks/projects, 2 midterms, 1 final. Homeworks weren't that hard, exams are tricky. The material is difficult to begin with so all in all i had a good experience.
His lecture is confusing and unorganized, hw interaction not clear, would not take with him again

Exams were difficult!!! 5 homeworks in the class aka cs projects. Professor Pawlicki is not the best at lecturing but at this point in my cs journey it doesnt make a huge difference in my learning. He uses his exam questions out of the textbook so there will be some reading. Overall i had a good experience.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Get ready to read', 'Accessible outside class']

comment: His lecture is a disaster and a total waste of time. PPT makes no sense. If you wanna really learn something, you can just google CS 188 Berkley and watch their recorded lecture. Not recommend going to his lecture.
I fw him heavy
The exams in this class are very bad. They ask you a bunch of random obscure questions about the textbook like its trivia night.

I would say the course was difficult but not that bad. Lectures are not top-notch but taught with passion. Be prepared for really heavy readings before exams and even if you do so, don't expect to receive a decent exam grade. Fortunately the curve was pretty good.

It is beyond me that UofR still lets this man teach this class. Horrible lecturer, never lectured on anything that was helpful for our projects. The projects would have extremely confusing instructions and often would be straight up wrong. The only good thing about this class was how easy it was graded.

Poorly run class. Few attend lectures which are hardly useful to either test or understanding. Slides taken for granted from UCB CS188, HW from former lecturers w/t changing their names. Tested subjectively on part of irrelevant AND untaught materials on books. Vague instruction on exam preps. TAs are the good. Get ready for self-study.

Prof. Pawlicki is a disorganized lecturer, often switching topics without clearly explaining any one thing. He assigns tests such that you are required to do them on weekends. He is curt at best and snappy at worst if you go to talk to him outside of class. Though lab assignments are helpful, the instructions are often poorly written and confusing.

I believe Prof. Ted Pawlicki is an excellent professor. The negative comments he is receiving likely stem from his willingness to express his views openly. He is highly experienced and has a strong command of his subject matter.

DSA is supposed to be hard but to be honest, I actually learned stuff because of him. Not because he taught well, but because I had to teach myself. If you just need the credit, take this class, go to workshop and watch Abdul Bari and you are good to go lol.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'EXTRA CREDIT', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Fake Professor
True Professor!!! Lectures are told to be bad but they are actually helpful! The test weren't hard at all!! Projects are also easy!!! True Professor!!!!!
Decent professor, lectures could be dry but class was easy overall. Lots of extra credit to boost grades. Unstuck Study AI was a big help for exam prep.

While a mediocre CS Professor at any other university, he is one of the few alright CS professors here at UofR. His classes are brain numbingly easy, but there is usually A LOT of busy work within these classes, and almost no real application of skills into projects besides a couple classes here and there.
Very weird guy, seems disorganized and often has unclear instructions for assignments and weird/pointless assignments.

I haven't even finished this class and he is by far my least favorite professor at the university. His profiles shows a trump 2020 shirt that he's wearing which tells you a lot. His teaching style in unclear, his projects are vaguely worded and i have the heebie-jeebies every time i walk into that lecture. TAKE THIS CLASS WITH A DIFFERENT PROF.
Takes 3+ weeks to grade coding assignments for a class of 20 students or less (summer asynchronous). Pretty pathetic considering there are professors who have to manage classes 10x that size
Excellent
Excellent. True professor.

By the end of the semester, lecture attendance was about 20% and he was giving extra credit to people who showed up. Lectures are pointless since the online quizzes every other week are about things that aren't covered at all. If you ever need help with the projects, just go to the lab and ask the TA's, they are very helpful.
No body come to the lecture
Always available outside of the class and is willing to help. His lecture is not that good, but there are extra credits and lenient gradings.
Trash

His lectures are not as engaging as top professors, but they aren't mandatory so you can choose to learn from other places. If you aren't busy, go for the extra credits in lectures. 
Really easy grades, online exams, all multiple choices. For those who are willing to learn yourself, this is the perfect course to earn an A+.

He was actually an okay professor. Was not good at lecturing but it didn't matter because he gave us all the resources to do well (Zybooks textbook) and he did care about our success. Class was not too hard and gave lots of extra credit.

I really don't get the hate for Pawlicki. His lectures were decent and covered the material promised (along with some additional topics towards the end of the semester). Projects were interesting. He was always accessible during office hours and willing to answer any lab-, project-, or quiz-related questions. Also, a lot of extra credit.
Lectures suck but attendance isn't mandatory. Assignment directions are confusing but it's almost impossible to fail the class. However, the online textbook is $90.
Lectures were dull but the projects were pretty cool. Everything reused from past years. Easy A if you are willing to do the work and time manage well.
Bad lectures. Also Bald

Pawlicki took whatever interest I had in game dev, and tried his hardest to throw it out of the window. Lectures are boring and useless, with the occasional sexist remark as well. I had to learn EVERYTHING from YouTube which was a thousand times more engaging. The only plus is that quizzes and assignments are super easy, so his class is an easy A.

Somehow easy homework,  many many opportunities for you to get extra credit and fixed A lines, so it s pretty easy to get an A for CSC172 he teaches. In fact, many of my friends even get 100+ in his class so A+ is quite common (tho he only uses A in workday).
However, he's awful in teaching, so get ready to learn everything by yourself via youtube.

Lenient with deadline extensions. Online quiz, no midterm & finals. Quizzes are reused from last year, sometimes with questions not covered in class. No one goes to lectures. It's a dull but easy A class as long as you do the work.
He will reply to your email but will never solve your problem. Seems to be responsive but not caring at all
love this guy
Pawlicki and Zhupa's lectures are as difficult to read as their names.
TRASH. HE IS JUST TRASH.

Completely useless. If you want to do well in this class, utilize the TAs and put in the effort for the projects and labs. No one goes to lectures once they realize that he just repeats the textbook, but explains it in a worse and more unclear way.

His tests are the worst. He recycles questions EVERY single test, but it's not material found in lectures or online really. ZyBook will be your best friend. Should have worked with a partner to get a better grade. The extra credit assignment is what saved me-- bumped it up a full letter grade, so def do it.
I learned everything from YouTube & Zybook. Don't go to the lectures. There is a big extra credit assignment, which is nice.

Contacting this professor is easy, getting help is not. Zoom chat was an unmoderated distraction, his long lectures made no sense & he had a sour, dull demeanor. His CV is nowhere to be found. Main textbook is a work of art, wish the author taught it. Online made it 10 times harder. Horrible way to begin CS. Use YouTube. Avoid at all costs.

Did not enjoy the lectures, were all over the place, and learned everything through others or online. If you do the work though, you'll get an A. He did post lecture recordings online, even when classes were in person, so that was nice.

Horrendous lecturer. Crappy tests. Labs and projects have very poor directions and he is not very accessible outside of class either. TAs will be your best friend in any of his classes. But overall not a harsh experience as the grade scaling makes it very easy to get an A.
His lectures and readings are not related to quiz.

Prof. T is kind and helpful and accessible outside the class. He is also willing to extend deadlines for students. However, his lecture is a little bit dull for me. Be ready for a lot of reading on Zybook if you want to take CSC172, it is really important. I learn almost everything from Zybook.

comment: toooooooo much tedious work ughh, 131 is def an evil class ...................

Responsive, and always available. People speak to the difficulty of assignments, but not about his amazing office hours. Always dedicated to working with you until you fully understand the assignments. Lots of example code that helps directly with the projects and is available for personal use.

There're ten sympathetic inevitable tragedies i.e Pompeii, Hamlet. And then there is TP's CSC 172. He is the Mount Everest of computer science that wields all the power for all explorers to CS and only if you had help or luck, you may not pull it off. And just like Shakespeare, he makes sure the pain is prolonged and sinking in your puny sad soul.
Bad experience of my CS journey.

Boring lectures, Pawlicki always starts a new chapter each time even if he did not finish the previous one before, and just reads the slides. His weekly online quizzes are worthless as few questions really focus on the key concepts and you can always find the answer with Ctrl+F on the textbook. Try to avoid him! If cannot, then just teach yourself.

I really loved the course material but the lecture was not useful at all. O totally depended on YouTube and the textbook. The professor is a bad explainer he fails to explain any complicated topic. He is a a slow coder so the lecture is always wasted while he is trying to show us example code.
High quality lecture slides. Lab assignments are easy but projects are pretty hard. I do not recommend this class to person who has not any CS background knowledge.

Honestly, you could learn nearly nothing from his lectures. All of the quizzes, labs, and projects are directly taken from previous years without change, even if there are tons of mistakes in these materials, including misleading instructions and wrong questions. Quizzes, lectures, labs and ZyBook are all grades but totally irrelevant to each other

Same as many poor guys here, I say that his lectures are worthless and disappointing. My suggestion is to complete self-learning before the semester begins. 172 with TP is an inevitable misery to many ones. When you feel down, cope with it, and don't let it ruin your expectations for future CS courses. CS should be hard, but this is undeserved.
I'm not mad, just disappointed.

CS172 equips its students with some of the most important knowledge of their cs career. This should be a fun and enriching class, though Pawlicki turned it into a nightmare. The two textbooks, assignments, exams, and lectures are completely unattached from each other. Just self-study... DONT WASTE YOUR PRECIOUS TIME GOING TO LECTURES.

Do not take this professor. Unfortunately it's impossible to major in CS without him as he is the ONLY professor for CS172. Even one of his TAs left him. He doesn't explain anything. The only way to survive his course is to teach yourself from the textbook. His political views are quite scary too, but that's for a different site.

comment: This professor is trying too hard to make it harder for students to understand the material. Instructions in his assigments are not understandable and tremendously incomprehensible
tags: ['Lots of homework', 'Get ready to read', 'So many papers']

comment: Absolute dogwater! Disgrace to the CS community, anywhere.

I honestly feel bad for the CS kids at UR. They're all talented, bright, eager to learn, and have extremely creative minds. It's sad that they're not being supplemented with a quality professor for a class as important as data structures & alg.

One of the least specific and detailed professors in computer science I have had. I respect professor Pawlicki's charismatic personality and hilarious charm, but he is not a good educator who seems to care about holistic learning, but just sits and watches students. If you want to take data structures, I highly urge you to take it in the fall.

He really make algorithm very unclear. It is hard for you to study from his lectures. Please go to other materials, learn from greeks for greeks and other platforms. The lecture slides can then guide you the list of thing you need to know. But do not try to just rely on slides, you can not understand without very clear explanation.
Students may not like his political views. But I personally found him entertaining. Fun guy.
Mental breakdown simulator. Except it's real.

CSC172 is an extremely useful class full of fascinating algorithms and clever data structures. But Ted Pawlicki nearly ruined it for me. Two labs a week forced me to rush through material instead of fully learning it. In lectures, he explains the material in a way that only makes sense if you already know it. He is also rude to students.
You will regret taking his class.

I can't help to feel like I am paying to self-study here. I mean, I used to like doing homework and practice questions. Not anymore. The homework, along with EVERY OTHER CONTENT, is so not clear. I don't even know what he means in some homework questions. Cost me a lot actually.

He turned what used to be a 2 Midterm class into a 5 Midterm + 1 Final class. I would not say he himself has bad intentions, but also adding an additional set of homework each week (so from 1 set per week to 2), I don't necessary have the time to think well of him. My conclusion? This has become a class made for students to STRUGGLE!

yeah, we all know about the notorious FB post he made, and I was wary of being in his class too. But I've found he's probably one of the kindest teachers I've had. I'm in CSC131 so it may be a different experience than 171/2, but he seems to genuinely care about his students and explains the material well, too.

comment: teach well, not possible, not for this life. good lectures not capable, just hua water to keep life. 171 boring, 172 online is like home! Students are all self-study genius and can do 100 labs a week, wow!! very like 172 online.
Homework and Projects will suck up every single second. A lot of questions are not related to the lecture or the book. You will need to find resources online often. Why?

Very accessible outside of class, and really gives you all the tools you need to succeed, even if he doesn't always have the best lecture slides. So few students regularly attend his class (since attendance isn't mandatory) that I find it hard for so many students to give him a bad rap without taking advantage of what he offers.

Starting this semester (2019 fall), this course requires textbook online. It takes 60$ to use, and it counts for 10% of the grades. Also, the professor barely cover any useful material in a logical way. This means CSC 171 is a self-teaching course which cost you a lot of money besides tuition, and the professor is useless.

Prof. Pawlicki's lectures were usually a loose run-through of how to use parts of Blender without any real structure. Most of the time I think he was just playing around with the program and sending us off. It was enough for the lax nature of this course, but with a more intense class like CSC 171 I'd stay far away.

Worst teacher ever! You would never want to have any classes with this guy! Tough final, useless lecture, and endless homework. He doesnt know the material, and he is not able to answer questions. By the way, you never know rubrics for guest lecture report.

Probably the worst professor at University of Rochester. I could learn more java programming through an online python course. Talks more about his wife than java. If this is your first time coding, don't let this class deter you from further programming.
Lectures are relatively useless. Easy class to do well in. Just do the assignment and self-study and you'll be fine

He is the worst professor at this university and sadly he is the only one who teaches CSC 171 for both semesters. I can honestly say that its is not a "Introduction" class its more like review for people who already know java. During lecture all he talks about is his wife then briefly cover the material. The two assignments each week are difficult.

comment: Stopped going to class midway through the semester. Got an A. Self study, learn from the TAs and online, and you'll be fine.

This course is really quick for an intro course, especially for anyone without any prior knowledge in Java programming beforehand. TAs & Google are your saviors. Read recommended books; they are more useful than Ted will ever be. Ted is at least fairly lenient with extra credits for projects, so work hard on those. It is rough, but not impossible.
His lecture is extremely useless. You can come to his class and laugh and do other things, but you will not be able to see the whole code and you won't learn much. Go to TAs, they are better.

Don't take his class. If you want to major CS, and come to UR for fall semester, just explore the first semester and hopefully some other professor will take CS171 next semester. He cannot teach and just assumes you have all the knowledge you need for Java EVEN THOUGH ITS AN INTRO CLASS. He is bad for your self esteem and your future in CS. AVOID

He cannot teach. Period. Don't waste your time in his lectures, go to CSUG, go to CETL, get a upperclassman willing to help and use the internet to learn. Read the books, and you should be able to learn by yourself

If you have no prior exp with Java, don't take this class. This man will not teach you anything and if you're very very lucky you will get a good lab and workshop TA who will guide you. He doesn't go over basics even though it's an introductory course and you're not supposed to have prior programming experience.
The worst class I ever had. This was supposed to be a introductory class. He teaches as if he's reviewing everything we already learned. Horrible class AVOID if you can

comment: I am not sure how Pawlicki has managed to keep a job for so long. It's currently week six and he has not even made a syllabus yet. And No Ted, sharing your course "calendar" spreadsheet with wrong dates is not a syllabus. Selcuk Kose is a brilliant professor that cares about his students success. He is always there to help. I found his office hours useful. If you want to get an A, don't miss the lectures.

Prof. Kose is one of my favorite professors. He is very helpful both in and out of the classroom. The course was challenging, however, Prof. Kose was always there to help. I would definitely recommend taking his course(s).

The professor himself is a great guy but he needs to redesign the course a little bit. He teaches off of a boring Powerpoint slide and in his lectures, it is very hard to stay awake. The first half of the course is do-able but the second half is where stuff gets crazy.

Dr. Kose's taught well but he was sometimes a bit rough around the edges. He really only cares that you get near the right answer, not how much work you put in. He's super willing to meet outside of class and really wants his students to attend every lecture. For my class at least, he gave extra points to people who came every lecture.

Literally the easiest class I've ever taken. It's just basic statistics. If you have a pulse, you'll get an A in the class. The tests are copy and pasted from the review, with some numbers different, and some exactly the same. If you want to do well, just memorize the review. Overall, ridiculously easy class
Extremely kind professor, who is very passionate on the topic of abolition. Although I might not agree with every single one of his views, I thoroughly enjoyed his course.
Prof Dubler is an incredible lecturer and can tell really cares about the topic. He is very understanding and doesn't assign much work, mostly weekly discussion and like a few papers.

Don't really have any critiques about Dubler, more about the course. It is not the inspiring, life-changing, mind-altering course they tell you it is. Some of the readings were interesting, but others as well as many discussions were just buzzword after buzzword-- lots of loud people who think they're far smarter than is the case. Easy A though.

Recommend going to first two weeks of class then dropping it. Ideas are new and interesting only until the second week. After that it is almost merely repetition of the same ideas. Not very in depth nor very practical/empirical. Required discussion sessions are waste of time. Community engagement opportunities are great though.

One of the most inspiring people I've met in my time at this school. Very passionate and well-connected around the subject matter. His course was very unique and fostered lots of engagement in and out of the classroom.
Incredible class so inspiring

He is awesome. Very passionate, caring, and doesn't try to kill you with work. The class is graded on a couple papers that he grades very easily. Lots of reading, but you don't have to do it. I would recommend doing some of the reading- only the ones on topics that particularly interest you. Everyone should take this class- you will learn a lot!

Overall I enjoyed the class and thought the topic was interesting. However I thought much of the material was too hypothetical and overly optimistic. I wish the course looked at more tangible solutions to incarceration, and that the course wasn't so biased towards compete prison abolition. The guest speakers were the highlight of the course.

Josh is by far my favorite professor. He encourages students to actively engage with the community, goes out of his way to bring in a variety of perspectives, and is always willing to spend time talking to students about their own views and lives. I've learned so much about the structures in society and so much about myself in the process.

This was a super interesting class and I learned a lot from the lectures and speakers we had. I wish the class wasn't cut short by covid, but still solid online. Make sure to do the readings and pay attention to the authors and quotes he points out and you should be fine.
Meliora Seminar Class - Open to help - Gives good feedback and opportunities to boost grade - Class based on weekly book readings and papers
Super easy class just show up and study hard for midterm and final. Need to do the readings and Dubler is a great guy. Very passionate about his work and everything he is involved in.

He's very understanding and it's clear he loves his job. He's always available for feedback or for working through the heavy topics brought up in lecture, and he truly wants his students to think for themselves and learn how to analyze what they're reading. He's also a great facilitator of discussion! Dubler is the best.

Great guy! Always willing to meet outside of class for help. Has answered numerous questions even unrelated to class through email and even, per request, created a meme board for the class for a bit of a laugh. Lots of reading. Acknowledges his faults. Intelligent, lots of big words, so sometimes confusing. Likes hearing opinions/debating - A+

comment: Worst class Ive ever taken. Hes the most subjective and biased grader Ive ever experienced. He also thinks hes WAY smarter than he is and it comes across as condescending. The class didnt teach me much that I didnt already know, either. Got all As in other classes, this was the easiest by far and got a B because hes biased.

Exams are slight variations from textbook/webwork/workshop/lecture examples. Workshop get 100% for showing up. Quizzes are group and are from examples you will have seen if you look at the upcoming week's workshop sheet beforehand, do webwork a week early and read notes/book sections for current topics (get 100%). Curves heavily 45%/55% ->80%/90%
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'Tough grader']

comment: So as a non-math major this class was hard af, but he's really nice and helpful and will do everything he can to help people out, including going over confusing hw problems in class before they're due. He can go a bit fast at times, but he's happy to explain things in more detail if asked. Genuinely good person who cares about his students

Explains concepts very clearly and logically - makes lectures engaging and easy to follow. Exams were kinda difficult, but they were prepared by another professor from the Math dept. Yamazaki is very caring and wants his students to do well.

This professor is knowledgeable in his field, but he really is not a good teacher. Honestly, you will learn more if you do not go to class and just teach yourself out of the book. He just makes the subject material confusing with his poor explanations. Again, he's a nice guy, but a bad teacher.
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'LOTS OF HOMEWORK', 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS']

comment: Nice guy, and means well. English isn't his first language, but he talks faster than I can understand it (it is mine). Really difficult class, and I never felt like I understood a concept before the homework was due. "If you aren't getting it right, try again, and if you still aren't getting it right, try harder".

Very strict grader-- in math there's only correct answer and incorrect answer, so instead of arguing for partial credit you might just as well practice and get it right the next time. That's the important thing I learned from this class. He makes concepts really clear and easy to comprehend. A is not impossible to get as long as you work hard.
Explains in a way that makes you understand the questions easily, gives funny and creative examples to support mathematical concepts.
Get ready to read. Hard exams, tough grader

Favorite professor EVER. Cannot say enough about her. I found myself interested and moved by her every class. Also HILARIOUS and has an amazing sense of humor. I would take any class of hers just so I could listen to her lecture!
She's a busy lady, but she's interested in what she teaches and she teaches it well. If you memorize the material, the tests are easy... and there isn't that much material.

Dr. Ghera was a good lecturer. Her enthusiasm and humor made classes a lot easier to sit through.  The class was pretty easy, but her presentation of the material was well done. She's always good about giving tangible examples to whatever concept or theory she's teaching.

I loved her class.  She was engaging, entertaining, and educated.  Yes she has a lot on her platter with working at two colleges; but whenever I needed help on something she always managed to find the time.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Tried to be funny and appeal to teenagers but it was completely unfounded. Class was a complete waste of my time--a child could have done a better job teaching. I just feel sorry for her children because they will grow up with the knowledge that she shared personal details about them in her classes.
She was super entertaining and her anecdotes were extremely helpful. Definitely worth going to class

Perfect example of an adjunct with "better things to do". Never felt like UR was on her priority list. Let's the students who like to hear themselves speak do just that and never curtails their tangents which resulted in a whole lot of wasted time. She did share some funny stories and had a good sense of humor, but overall- horrible experience.

Don't listen to the other reviews, I took his Self-Help writing 105 class and it was awesome. There's a good amount of work per week, but it is engaging, and he is a really great guy and very engaging

Lots of readings and essays due every two days of class. Class is about "self help" but leaned more into ancient philosophy/religious readings. Leaned into redpill rhetoric sometimes during discussion? (Read his articles on the Good Men Project). Don't write too well on your first drafts or he grades your final drafts way more harshly.

confusing feedback, no grades/feedback for informal assignments (there were 10 and they were worth 20% of our grade?), course had interesting topics but kind of felt like they had a misogynistic lean at times
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Lots of homework']

comment: Dr. Hinds is a very straight-forward teacher. She sets clear expectations each week of what must be completed. She can be a little blunt and seem uncaring, but her ability to give fair and clear feedback is noticeable. The class is an easy A if work is put into it. Do NOT expect to sit around waiting for it.
tags: ['Get ready to read', "Skip class? You won't pass.", 'SO MANY PAPERS']

comment: There is a lot of material to cover but this class really gives you an idea of all the interesting fields of study for BCS.  I really like Hinds as a teacher and I like that the tests are about applying material rather than just memorizing facts.  I would definitely recommend this class.

What a waste of time this class is. Don't skip lectures, but ignore the book. Recitations are a waste of time, and the tests are just a matter of being able to speak Hinds' language. You will be able to narrow each question down to 2 answers, but for a small sample of the test the 2 answers you're left with will be indistinguishable.

I wish Poujet still taught this. The tests aren't hard, they're just chalk full of terribly chosen and badly formulated questions. Hinds says this class is not about memorization, and she's right, it's about figuring out what the hell her questions are even asking. Lectures are unclear and I'm not convinced Hinds is knowledgeable on the topic.

The topics covered are interesting, but Hinds teaches directly off of the powerpoints.  Can you skip class because of this?  Perhaps, but it is always helpful to hear the material from her and take notes then in order to lower your study time.  Overall an easy class, but you should be able to apply the topics learned to different situations.

Nice woman but HORRIBLE teacher. Obviously knows her stuff but doesn't know a thing about how to teach. She teaches through Powerpoints - you can skip every class and get a decent grade. Many required readings but no textbook. Texts are somewhat easy but require lots of studying. Not the worst class ever but SO INCREDIBLY BORING.

The lectures are kind of boring and it feels like you don't actually get through much material because she spends half the class asking rhetorical questions. But her tests are really awesome. She is somewhat understanding. But she works here part time so it's really hard to meet with her if you need to talk to her.

The class covers many topics which is why is moves so fast. Overall, you can learn everything from her slides and do decent on the tests. Read the textbooks, because it will help you understand the concepts well enough to apply them on the tests.

Hinds is really intelligent but the lectures are drags. She tries to put an effort into teaching but it's as if she mostly does it for the purpose of being able to do research. The tests are difficult if you can't apply the material, which is really important if you want to pass. She posts slides online, so you can skip as long as you study hard.

admittedly her first course after receiving her doctorate -- hinds makes an entry level "organ grinder" class as engaging as possible.  A broad spectrum of topics over one semester -- would have liked more on clinical cases and abnormal psych, guess i'll have to take an upper division course for that.  very helpful during office hours as well.

She is the type of teacher that reads off of her powerpoint slides with very little commentary. You can tell that she knows a lot, but she seems to lack passion during her lectures which makes attending her class a dry experience. Her exams are fairly easy; you just have to put in decent study time and utilize the textbook for clarity of material.

Hinds is knowledgeable and seems very passionate. Lectures are dry because she talks "at" you rather than "to" you, but the quality improves over time, as the materials increasingly allow more interactivty in learning. Exams cover only lecture materials, but extra reading is recommended for clarification, as huge topics are rushed through in class.

Lectures are dry and not engaging. Attending class is not necessary as all the material explained with more clarity in the textbook. Her lectures move too fast and she touches on each topic too briefly, but she is somewhat helpful during office hours. Overall, her class is easy if you are willing to put in a lot of independent study time.
Grading criteria are clear from the very beginning. This class requires some prior understanding of chemistry or a lot of reading. He is incredibly nice and funny both during and after lectures

TOUGH CHM 173 CLASS. Lectures are very broad and general, doesn't really go over examples in class, so make sure you take full advantage of workshops offered. Sign up for a tutor asap with CETL because for this class, they get booked fast. Cares about students.
It's a tough class, but he is on the students' side and grades generously. He doesn't stress the math as much, but focuses on the concepts. He is very fun and always willing to help.

People who say he doesn't curve/add points didn't listen. Everyone bombed the first exam because it wasn't identical to old exams (oh no, it's not like this is college) and he gave a chance to get all those points back on the final. He's a fantastic lecturer, he's inspiring, and he's super nice to his students. He's the best professor I've had.
Maybe he's better teaching upper level classes?

He will not curve. In my class the average of the first exam we took was 28% and he would not add points or anything. He's pretty tough that way, but I also feel like a learned a lot more with him than I did with other Chemistry teachers. If you take him, be ready to put in A LOT of time and effort.

Awesome teacher. He teaches you everything you need to know plus makes it interesting. Very fair exams, very approachable. Read the book ahead of each class and you'll understand everything he says. Anyone who says he expects you to know chemistry before just didn't try. It's not hard if you listen to him and read. One of my favorite professors.

Bad teacher. if your schedule allows you to take it with a different professor then do. The class isnt too hard but he complicates everything, doesnt teach whats on tests and expects everyone to already know the material.  His test used to be like practice tests but the last two years, this year especially his exams are getting harder and less fair

Attendance is not mandatory, but he gets really angry if you don't come. I did not particularly enjoy his lectures and was often bored and distracted. Overall, he is better than the other professors for the course, but that isn't necessarily saying much. The material is also not his strong suit so he isn't that enthusiastic about it all the time.

Of all the other professors for this class, he is the best choice - TAKE HIM. You should go to class or else he will get mad, although it is not mandatory. WORKSHOP will teach you everything! Class is very unorganized so you need to review the notes he will upload online. Do the practice exams, although the actual test might be totally different!
Literally one of the worst professors I've had. He was really unfair. Tests were reasonable, until they became impossible because he had a personal vendetta against the students.

Farrar is constantly using environmental or other examples to create a true understanding of the application of the material. He is funny, makes lecture enjoyable, and definitely cares about his students and their level of comprehension. Tests are not difficult as long as you attend workshop and study with practice exams.

Farrar is probably one of the best professors that you will have if you decide to take his course. He made the material very understandable and really helped me to develop a passion for chemistry. He is entertaining in class and I look forward to going all the time. Tests aren't hard if you study and go to class. He's the man.

He's not a bad lecturer, and it is possible to learn the material from lecture, but it's probably the most time consuming and confusing way to do so. Very little of what he says in lecture is on a test (1 to 2 formulas per lecture if you're lucky). Just read his lecture notes, do the homework, go to workshop and you're good. Lecture is unnecessary.

Farrar is the man!  His lectures can be confusing, but if you read the chapters and do the homework, you'll be fine on the test.  Farrar is probably one of the smartest professors here and amazingly funny at times!  Great class overall.

DIfficult course to understand. Exams are difficult and lectures move too fast to prepare you for exams but workshops help. Chem Engineering majors seem to struggle with the content as its geared more toward (what seems to be meaningless) derivations.

Although I found this course challenging, Prof. Farrar made it manageable.  He always made time to help students outside of class and always welcomed students to office hours or set up more convenient times to meet.  Lectures were interesting and exams were fair.  I feel that I learned a lot of physical chemistry in this course and enjoyed it.

CHM131 is a difficult course, but with sufficient work put into it, it can be done. Farrar is an extremely smart guy, and seems to help the students with what they need. Probably one of the most hip professors on campus. Lectures get very hard to follow at times, but notes are always online to review.
Farrar uses the chalkboard to teach, which I found quite helpful.  He is willing to meet with students and answer questions.  Workshops are very helpful.
farrar is one of those teachers who is simply too brilliant for an intro level class.  it takes him a whole class period to explain not too difficult a concept
Haaaarrrdd Class.  Prepare to be challenged.  The TAs are helpful.  Farrar is confusing in lectures but recitations help you understand the material.

Awesome teacher, very helpful and caring.  I struggled through the first test, but then went to his office hours regularly, and pulled off a good grade.  Definitely go see him after exams, he will do what he can to find you an extra few points!!!

Very nice and extremely helpful. Take the advice and go over all your tests with him afterwards! Who knows, there might be an error or two in your favor! TOUGH exams! He does hold review sessions and stays until you exhaust the questions tho!
A-mazing.  He is an awesome prof and really helpful. take the time to go over your tests with him...its worth is.  hes also a snazzy dresser.
Good teacher at first then lost his love for the students and killed wveryone in the final. Very disappointed at him.
This man and Professor Krugh are practically the same.  They are both the top 2 nicest people in the entire country.  But man, do they give tough exams.  Farrar is tough if you never took AP Chem.
good professor
I find his teaching very good. I pay attention and actually stay awake.
No Comments

At first I thought he was great because he wrote his notes on the board and that forces me to take notes/learn better.  However, he spends a majority of his time derriving equations and going into irrelevant facts that further confuse people.  Going to class was a waste, he never taught us how to do problems.  Use the textbook, Zumdahl is the man.
Interesting class, nice guy. Knows a lot and is not afraid to share it.
Boring as hell. The man makes the same jokes repeatedly and is totally dry. God did not grant him the gift of speaking at all.

I can't believe people are giving Farrar good grades.  He is the worst professor I had so far in my college career.  The dude DOES NOT teach anything.  We'll come to recitation and we'll see stuff we've never seen before that we were supposed to have learned in class.  He's horrible.
the class is long and boring...so sometimes i doze off....but it always leads to a sticky situation....the man is soo hot that i cant help but want him...wet dreams are dangerous in class fyi

lectures are boing and he tends to do a lot of unnecessary algebra with equations.  however, he does tend to crack some jokes and loves "liquid water"...  sit in the back of class and make your own jokes to make note-taking bearable.  he's a cool enough guy, though, i guess...
Jimbo is the man.  He is a great professor and an awesome guy.  Sometimes lecture can be a bit dry, but when he cracks a joke its worth it.
He is always willing to help. His classes are kind of dry, but he is a very kind teacher. And a very kind grader.

All around, he is not that bad of a professor. Disorganized at times, but a few minutes at his office hours can clear up any questions. He gives lots of practice problems (and answers) before every test, that are very similar to the actual test questions. The notes are very thorough and the papers are really easy.
Very disorganized, no idea what he's teaching in the class. The exams are not consistent with course materials. Terrible experience. My sincere advice - avoid him at all cost.

This guy has no idea what he's teaching. He actually does not know the class material and makes mistakes every 5 minutes. He is most definitely not qualified to teach and should not be allowed to teach this class. Do not take his classes. Naturally his notes are completely useless as well.
Highly quantitative mixed with a very dry professor. Tough class with some exam questions unrelated to the course material.

Yes, he reads off slides and his lectures aren't too helpful. But he is very accessible outside of class, is quite good at helping individually, and is very enthusiastic. Depending on the class, homework may be difficult, but exams and quizzes are always written easily and he grades quite leniently. Far from your worst choice for a professor.

Probably the worst lectures I have been to for any class. Uses slides which are copy and paste from the textbook and somehow explains the concepts worse than the textbook does. If he picks up chalk the rating could definitely be higher.
bad at lecturing. for a heavy calc class, he just reads powerpoint slides. its identical to highlighting and selecting text to speech. has never picked up chalk.

ASTR111 is one of my favorite class! The professor is really interesting and fun to talk with. He gives helpful advice, is patient, and always willing to guide you through the assignments or chat more about astronomy! The homework is hard, so you need to put time to it. He do speaks a bit soft during lectures, but overall, it's a great class!
He was very helpful when it came to assignments and talked about the lore behind subjects not just the content itself. Also is ALWAYS fitted up. Overall 10/10 for the suits

Dan Watson is a beautiful human being. His lectures can be a little boring, but his passion for the topic of astronomy and his amazing suits make lecture worth it. The grading of exams is extremely fair as Dan looks for any excuse to give partial credit. All around an amazing person, I cannot recommend taking him enough.

Dan Watson is an amazing professor. ASTR 111 is challenging, but he grades kindly. If you put the work in you'll learn a LOT. Watson is really kind, helpful in office hours, and always willing to chat about astronomy. He wrote me rec letters and connected me with alumni in the field I want to go into. Top tier professor, I hope I have him again.

Very enjoyable professor, he makes lots of funny quips and he's very interesting. He does spend a lot of time explaining math that isn't exactly relevant and you do have to go back into the slides to understand a lot of things, but the website and slides are laid out very well

I believe the homeworks were a bit difficult, and they do take a lot of time and work, but I really enjoy Watson as a person and overall as a teacher. He is very helpful and wonderful to talk to during office hours (oftentimes he even gives cookies!). Sometimes I did get sleepy during his lectures, but I really did learn a lot!
Love his class. Great guy, very accessible, and surprisingly funny during lectures. Also, the suits are impeccable.

If Dan Watson has 10,000 fans I'm one of them. If Dan Watson has 100 fans I'm one of them. If Dan Watson has one fan it's me. If Dan Watson has no fans I'm no longer alive. If the world is against Dan Watson I am against the world. 
This man's style is IMPECCABLE, also he is super forgiving with extensions and very available outside class.
Love
Very passionate about teaching astronomy and has easy-to-follow lectures. Would recommend taking the class

If you don't have a science background I would not take this class unless you're willing to work. He goes into extreme specifics that you don't need to know for tests, and the tests are on webwork which sucks. Go to lecture and recitation, and DO THE PRACTICE TESTS, half the questions are on the real tests. He's very passionate and a great lecturer

I cannot believe that my 70,000 dollar a year tuition is going towards this man attempt to teach me physics. Every time I went to lecture I left even more confused than I started. He never responded to emails, tests were insanely hard (over half the class failed his second midterm). His class was harder than the honors version of the same class.

Dan is really bad at conveying any idea to students. He also makes you feel dumb for asking questions and gets some weird joy out of assigning homework questions that even the TAs can't solve. He's also just an all around jerk.

-Assigns homework due the day before a midterm (only two midterms in the class) -Tries teaching Calc-based Physics through powerpoint -Never has homework due on the same day every week (could be Monday, Wednesday, or Friday. You never know) -Tries writing his own homework problems that even the TAs can't solve

Since day one he threw equations that were not explained at us. He knows the course but does not teach it well at all. Does not take into consideration the fact that this is most people's first time dealing with this subject. If possible take this class with someone else or at another place.

comment: He is smart but he does not have the slightest clue on how to teach. He is completely out of touch and teaches a class that clearly requires someone to do out problems by hand, with lecture slides. He is horrible at teaching PHY122. He know the material but does not understand that the people he is teaching may be seeing this for the first time.

I'm not a science person. At all. I heard this class required little math -- not so much. There is Web Work involved. T.A.'s aren't that helpful. Lectures can be confusing/boring, but his eccentricities make them bearable.

Dan Watson is funny, smart, and adorably nerdy. He loves what he is doing and does his best to help students. I learned more in Astro 142 from him than in any of my subsequent classes in higher level astronomy. Only thing to beware of are magically appearing variables in his powerpoint slides.

He may well be the least helpful person on the face of the earth. More than half the class had issues taking a test on webwork and he told us that we probably did something wrong. Oh, he also says "Uh" or "Um" between every word and moves his arms like a penguin.

He knows that most people in the class are only there because of requirements, and he makes it VERY easy to get an A.  The lectures are generally boring / sometimes incomprehensible, yet he is very helpful if you have questions outside of lecture.

I could NOT stay awake during his lectures.  He seems like a nice guy, but when I tried to introduce myself it was awkward; I never talked to him again.  His lecture notes don't make sense unless you hear the lecture.  The homework isn't hard, but the tests are tricky.  He knows what he's talking about, but he's not very fun to listen to.

Lectures are pretty boring, but he teaches well nonetheless. The test is based entirely on lecture, so the book is really just for your own use. The powerpoints usually don't make sense unless you hear him explain them, so you need to go to class most of the time.

Actually, he's a nice guy outside of class and sometimes makes more sense if you go to him for help.  But the class is very dull.  He just reads from powerpoints and puts you to sleep.  Lots of equations, naturally.  But his powerpoints are not very good at explaining things.  And the book is rarely any help, though it can be amusing.

Prof. Ahmed is honestly the GOAT! Not only is she extremely well-versed and passionate about what she is teaching, but she takes the time to listen to student feedback and actually incorporate it into her teaching style. Exams are open-note and full access, but you really still need to engage with the course to do well on them.
Professor Ahmed is one of the best professors at this school. She loves anthropology and really cares about her students, giving engaging assignments but never overloads you.
Absolutely lovely and the most understanding professor ever, she's also really passionate about what she teaches and makes classes really engaging.

Dr. Ahmed is very understanding and wants you to succeed in the course. She's very helpful and caring. She makes things easy to grasp and she is passionate about her studies, classes, and research. She is fantastic.
She is such a great professor!!!!!!!!!!
U of R needs more professors like Dr Ahmed.

GREAT professor!! She's incredibly passionate about medical anthropology so all of her lectures are well planned out and thought provoking. I've learned SO much in this class. She really cares about her students! This class is definitely worth taking especially if your pre-med or biomedical engineering!

Professor Ahmed is hands down the best professor I have come across in my college career. She is caring, wants all students to succeed, and is passionate about her field. If you happen to take an anthropology class, make it one of hers. She may even convince you to change your major!

She is a great professor! She is so passionate about the field she studies. She is also very patient and caring to students. Her classes are not lecture-heavy. There will be group discussions every class. The class will just have two open book tests and one final essay, but she is not a tough grader. Definitely will take her course again.
The lectures are basically watching youtube videos or documentaries. The 1 project was fun, but lectures are extremely boring and it's mainly focused on classical music.

yea grading is harsh. and the course should be called: experience Dr. Harman's music. You either get A or B(with just a single mistake you make on the exam) make you go to concert and unclear what he wants you to know.
If you are in his orchestra, you are more likely to get a good grade in this course.

Dr. Harman is a really amazing conductor.  He tells jokes, gets everyone involved and expects you to give your best everyday.  Because of his high expectations, he may seem arrogant, but he really just realizes everyone's true potential and strives to bring that out every day.

I don't agree with the previous posts. I took Harman's Symphony and the Conductor class and I loved it. Harman is just very enthusiastic and knowledgeable about music so he may seem arrogant, but he's really only passionate about what he does.   For MUR 121 he teaches with more of a discussion-based style rather than a lecture which was great!
he's not the usual conductor, but he knows his stuff and he's enthusiastic
i agree with the people who have called him arrogant. his grade scheme is such that 1 point off on any assignment is 1% off your semester grade. the assignments are also unclear and pointless.
agreed with previous post (4/28)
One of the most arrogant jerks I've ever met.  Fails to realize he's not at Eastman.

Harman is arrogant and not helpful. He makes you go to the concerts he conducts so he can brag about it the next week in class. The only bright spot was the TA, David Plylar, who was very helpful and nice.

Professor Heidi is seriously one of the nicest and most caring professors I've ever had. The textbook is tough, but she gives lots of extra credit and her practice exams are super similar to the real ones. She replies to emails fast and is always happy to help with anything. She's exactly a humorous and patient professor.

Professor Heidi is seriously one of the nicest and most caring professors I've ever had. The textbook is tough, but she gives lots of extra credit and her practice exams are super similar to the real ones. She replies to emails fast and is always happy to help with anything. She's exactly a humorous and patient professor.
This class made me want to drop out of my program. It was very hard. I ended up skipping class becuase she moved too fast and did not answer questions well.

she tends to go off on tangents about her boat and kids. shes very nice but is not scared to show her anger in front of everyone. she reads off of her slides and only sometimes does she add anything to them while lecturing, lectures are recorded. shes the only one that teaches 224/5 so youre stuck with her. talks pretty slow
I loved this professor! Great Classes very caring and explains things really really well

She is the only professor that teaching intermediate acc 1 and 2 so you should get used to her, she goes off topic a lot, tells stories about her boat and kids, and laughs at her own jokes. she is very accessible outside of class, 3 homework assignments and you have to work in a group. first midterm is hard, second and final are okay.

I enjoyed being in Heidi's class just about as much as she enjoyed teaching it. Which is to say, Not at all. I second other comments about the fact that she plays favorites. You can clearly tell that she does not want to be teaching, and takes out her stress on students.
i went to her office hours to see my test and she was very mean to me

comment: Heidi is the BEST accounting professor I have ever had. She is incredibly smart and so nice. She is willing to help you out with WHATEVER you need. She has even helped me prepare for interviews before! I am better prepared for my job because Heidi has taught me so much. You do have to work hard for a good grade, but it's so worth it!

Great professor teaching a rather dry topic. Her exams are fair and the homework can be daunting, but she encourages you to solicit feedback from her and your assigned teammates. Do the work, get a good grade; it's as simple as that. Respectful of the fact that working adults are taking graduate classes. Highly recommended!

She is a great professor and provides all the material you need in lecture and online but it's very heavy.  She does not curve any tests or homework or offer any extra credit so your grade is your raw score.  Because of that there is no way to recover if you do poorly on a test or homework and many people have been known to take ACC201 twice.
Too much materials covered

She likes to play favorites, if you're on her good side you're good; if not, she will be rude to you. She screamed at me once during a midterm when I asked for clarification. Her lectures are okay, but filled with material. She assumes you can understand something in 1 second. Please take Prema Iyer instead, she's absolutely amazing!
Wonderful professor. She wants to teach anyone who wants to learn.
Great professor, is willing to help you if you put in the effort. Very funny and great person.
She makes the lectures fun.
She is tough but will give you all the help you need. As long as you do all of the work, the class isn't bad
She can't stop making unfunny stories. Her exams are really though, and she crams the class to the brim with material.

LOTS of reading, but class was never boring. Professor Rozenski is an engaging and interesting professor who is incredibly knowledgeable about classical + scriptural literature, as well as music, medieval Europe, baking, Internet culture, and more. Quizzes and responses are easy to do well on, and everything's graded very leniently.

Very passionate and has great suits, and overall a super nice guy. I can't say I found old english particularly riveting, but he made me want to come to class and participate, plus there were plenty of extra credit opportunities despite the quizzes being difficult!

this guy made my whole year so much better. i always looked forward to going to this class and honestly it gave me the will to start trying again in school. smart, interesting, kind, hilarious. makes everything interesting. the course material was fascinating and he made everything so exciting and engaging!! my favorite class i have  taken here.

Prof. Rozenski is by far my favorite professor I've had thus far. Super smart guy who knows his stuff, but makes every class really fun and engaging. Lots of reading, but totally worth it to get to talk about it in class. Manages to make tests fun. He's also great with communication outside of class via email if extenuating circumstances come up.

From a STEM major with clustering in classic literature, Rozenski is awesome. He's extraordinarily knowledgeable and receptive to literally any opinion on any topic related to the readings at hand and willing to discuss it seriously. I learned a lot about literary criticism and left the course feeling like I gained something I didn't have before.

Although he's a funny and overall nice person, Prof. Rozenski is not a good professor. I didn't learn anything in his class, and when it came time to write the midterm and final papers, I really struggled. Be prepared to read A TON! We read 100+ pages for each class and 1800 lines of Middle English. Essays are HARD. Class has no structure at all.
Good lectures, easy to pass. Make sure to participate and show up in class, because he grades a lot based off of that.
Adorable. What a great guy.

Wonderful professor and human being--we had to read the frickin BIBLE and he made it entertaining. You can do traditional response papers or creative responses which is always fun. You do have to read a lot, but he does a good job prepping you for the quizzes with study guides. Oh, and he's adorable.

Rozenski is amazing. He's the funniest professor I've ever had, and he genuinely cares about the success of his students. He is also creative and flexible with the lectures and assignments and does his best to make sure that everything is clear and fair. 12/10

Lovely person, but poor professor. By the end of the semester, nobody wanted to raise their hands for discussions because she would always interrupt them to make her own point. It was less a discussion class than a lecture class listed as discussion heavy. She grades at a level much higher than undergraduate, so if you take this class, be prepared.
