comment: While she knows what she's talking about and is passionate about the material, it's difficult to participate in discussion as she doesn't leave space for discussion on average when she is lecturing. Tough grader for papers and leaves lots of constructive criticism. However, I've found she's pretty kind and with it.

I hate her...tough grader for real and she gives vague instructions on her criteria of paper...She said she's liberal but if your idea violates w her central beliefs...be ready for a B and less...She also interrupts when students talk, like a lot of times...
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'So many papers', 'Lecture heavy']

comment: This professor is BORING. All she does is read off of a sheet of paper for the whole class. You will read 100-200 pgs for hw per class. She grades REALLY tough and writes very critical responses to students' papers. The essay exam is ridiculously hard and you have two other long papers. She requires participation but interrupts when students talk.

Professor London is absolutely amazing. She genuinely cares about her students succeeding and learning. I had one 6 page paper where she left well over a hundred comments. She' super knowledgeable and smart, but she's also very approachable for her students. You will read a fair amount, but I didn't find it unmanageable as long as I planned ahead.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Get ready to read', 'Participation matters']

comment: Learned a lot about literary elements. This professor is dedicated and passionate about her material.
Great lecturer and promoter of discussion. She is a tough but fair grader with plenty of constructive criticism. Would recommend!
Prof London is a passionate, intelligent woman who leaves room for discussion while also managing to teach new material at the same time. she is by far the best english teacher I'ver ever had.

Professor London was great! Her class was very discussion based, and she is a tough grader when it comes to written papers. However, she wants you to succeed and grades fairly and takes improvement into consideration. She is very helpful outside of class during office hours. Would highly recommend!

I loved this class. The books were great, and Professor London really contributed to my understanding of them. The writing assignments really made you think, but it challenged me and my writing has greatly improved since I've really learned what makes the difference between an A- and an A paper.

I have had Dr. London for two classes and I really enjoyed both. The entire class is discussion based, so pretty much everyone is forced to get involved. The books she assigned were excellent; she had a lot of good insight to share during class. Also, when you ask for help, she is more than willing to give you a hand, and is very encouraging.

Excellent teacher, she was very helpful with helping papers, more interested in making sure students learned than paper grades (allowed revisions and went over papers with students). She will ask for input in her classes, but doesn't call on anyone. Good class.
Very interested in what she teaches and very intelligent. Understanding and easy to talk to. Great prof. overall.

Very easy class to sit in and not pay attention if you want to...but if you want to participate, its really difficult because she likes to talk. Very opinionated. If you are writing something she disagrees with (shes liberal), she will say your argument is weak (even if paper, truthfully, is good). Annoying mannerisms - including stutter.
She fabulous, encouraging, insightful. She provides feedback and helpful comments and she kept me incredibly interested.

I think Prof. London gives incredibly comprehensive and high-quality feedback on students' papers, something I often find lacking from other professors.  She's kind, sympathetic and very insightful.  I've learned a great deal from her classes and talking with her during office hours etc.
had her for contemporary women writers. it drove me crazy listening to her speak. she said nothing of importance. i watched the clock that entire class...books were decent though.

Woah, I think it's pretty extreme to transfer because of ONE teacher in ONE class. I found Professor London clear, interested in the material and organized in leading discussions. She let you revise papers and books assigned were varied and enjoyable.

I had London last fall and I never knew this website existed until now,  and I am so glad because I feel it is necessary to tell people just how awful this professor was! I have transferred schools because of the poor experience I had with this professor!
One of the best professors that I have had, very knowledgable in his field. I would defiantly recommend you take his class!!
very fake person. exams are terrible.
he's so slay. 10/10 would recommend.

Overall, this was a good course and Professor White was an excellent professor. His homework and exams/projects were clear but difficult enough that you needed to really understand the material to do well, which is expected. Not a harsh grader, and very accessibly outside of class time. In-class questions were answered well also. I would recommend
sucks

I took this class in Spring 2017 and to this day, this was the worst class I've taken and taught by the worst professor I've met at UR. Did not use an ounce of the material from this class at my internships and current full time job. To all ChemEs taking this class: push thru it, you'll never need it again or have to deal with such a rude professor
Professor White is great! His lectures are so useful, and he is also really funny!

comment: The contents of this course is useful. I wish this course was taught by a different professor.

Professor White always wants to teach as much content as possible in his courses. The syllabus updates constantly each year to match some state of the arts tools used in the computational field. But, if you don't have any programming background, you'll struggle in this course cause they are not taught during class.

Professor White is truly outstanding. He sets you up for success in his class. As the student, you have a full control over 60% of your course grade -- homework, project etc (he might/might not change this in the future). Exams are worth only 40% total. He even texted me while I was out of town to make sure that my question was answered.

Does not know how to interact well with students. If you ask a basic question to him, he appears frustrated and impatient. The school should just hire an actual compsci professor for this requirement, as this professor is disliked by the vast majority of ChE students for obvious reasons.

All the lecture notes are posted online and very organized, so it's easy to access them for the homework. There is a lot of homework, but it usually reinforces concepts well so that you can be prepared for the midterm and final. He could improve on how he explains concepts because he often repeats himself instead of explaining things in a new way.

Extremely rude professor and condescending. Not even the suck ups in the class like this professor or thinks he is actually funny. Does not respond to slack messages and needs to reevaluate some of the TAs for this course. Some of the TAs need a serious course in the basics of respect.
Worst class I have ever taken. A lot of material is stuffed into one semester and the class is not taught well and it in general is confusing. Final was absurd. Barely a curve at the end- good luck.

White puts all his lecture notes online so attendance isn't necessary. He basically just reads through the notes for class. He passes on a lot of questions he gets to TAs and has them teach and give most of the examples in recitation. Upside is the final is open everything so you can look through all the notes.

It was his first class as a new professor at UofR, and so some parts were rocky. He got much better at lecturing and connecting with the students throughout the semester. His homework sets are tough but the exams are easy if you've done all your assignments. He is totally reachable and cares about you learning how to program in Python.

This was the first class he ever taught. He improved greatly throughout the semester. Keys to succeed in this class: Go over the lecture notes until you understand them, do all the homeworks, go to office hours when confused. Class uses Python programming so experience with this helps.

Super nice, he let me rewrite my final paper and even told me specifically what book to check out and use a source for my paper. Goes off on tangents about his experiences with certain cathedrals; can be boring if you're not reallllly interested in the subject. Lets class out early in the fall when it's hot (average of 20 minutes earlier).

Walsh reminds me of everyone's favorite grandfather. He occasionally rants and rambles about something vaguely related, but is extremely knowledgeable, and passionate about his classes. There are only 3 papers of average length and he's not the strictest grader, cares more for ideas presented than the manner of presentation. Amazing class.

An interesting course. Walsh makes it very easy to succeed. He is flexible with extensions and edits drafts. Entire grade is three 4-6 page papers. Get a seat at the front, take good notes and don't miss a class and you'll do fine. He seems like a very jolly old man. I plan to take more classes with him!

Prof Walsh is a very nice man, but I found his lectures rather boring, and since there were no exams (only three 5-page papers), attending class was unnecessary. The notes I took in class were not helpful to me. Despite my spotty class attendance, however, I got an A in the course - so either I'm an excellent writer or he's an easy grader!

Walsh is very nice, passionate and knowledgeable about his field, and really wants to help students succeed. He's very soft-spoken so try to grab a front seat. Sometimes his lectures are dry and boring, follow his train of though. Tangents a lot :) This class was graded on 3 short paper (4-6 pgs) - a GPA booster if writing is your strength.
Have taken multiple classes with Walsh all of them easy. You have to write 3 5page papers. Lectures are a little dry but tangents are good. He loves what he does and its evident

Reall nice guy, sometimes a little bit boring, but very passionate about the subject.  You can tell he really loves to teach it.  Just 3 papers which you have to put in good work on to get a good grade.  I learned a lot in the class and it wasn't too difficult.
He's an ok teacher, a little boring at times and a little weird but what can you expect from an AH teacher?

I personally never found a dull moment in this class.  Something amusing always seemed to happen.  My only complaint is that while Walsh was soft spoken and polite in class, I sometimes found him difficult to approach, though he was very accessible to students.

An enjoyable class if you sit up front and can hear him, maybe it was just the room, but you really had to strain to hear him talk, shows way too many art slides (ok i know he does art history) but this is just a history course. I went to every class took great notes, yet i still felt i didnt know much for the papers. Still expecting an A though.

Very knowledgable and the course is interesting. He welcomes questions and concerns from students and makes a point to make himself available. The work is some what demanding but quite rewarding. Walsh is an excellent professor and would suggest taking any of his other courses.
Professor Walsh is extremely knowledgeable, helpful, and entertaining.  I highly recommend any of his classes.
The most boring class of my life!

This class was painfully boring! It had such potential and he ruined it. It's entirely lecture, and he really knows his stuff but shows no enthusiasm. He's a nice guy, but I would rather be one of those artifacts buried in the dirt wasting away than to sit through another one of his classes.
Professor Walsh is extremely entertaining and definitely knows his materials.  His classes are always enjoyable.
Dummit is a great person, who provides detailed notes for the class and excellent lectures.
Such an inspirational, funny, and intelligent professor! He is very helpful, and you can tell that he wants his students to do well.

He is such a funny guy! I love that he gives an opportunity to make up for a bad midterm grade by doing well on the final. He is very helpful during his office hours. Just overall a great professor and the lectures were very enjoyable (he always gave out candy too! )
tags: ["Skip class? You won't pass.", 'ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS', 'Hilarious']

comment: COME TO CLASS AND PASS

Professor Dummit is an amazing lecturer! He explains difficult concepts very clearly and often in a humorous way. He is also very willing to help us outside of class. I will definitely continue taking his class. Who does not like a professor who brings his students candies and brownies every class after all.

He is such a fun teacher! He gives out candy in most of his classes and is a hilarious dude. He is also such a good teacher and a genius! I wish he would stay next semester because he made calculus so fun! Don't hesitate to take a class with him.
A very fun and easygoing professor. He is always willing to help on both email and office hours.

I loved my multi-dimensional calculus course with Professor Dummit.  He is an excellent teacher with a knack for explaining and demonstrating mathematical concepts.  His lecture notes for the course were also outstanding; they can almost replace the textbook.
A laid back but very clear and concise professor, understands his students, and has a nice dry sense of humor!

Professor Dummit is the BEST!!! I took his Number Theory class. And although I signed up late to the class, he was very successful in preparing me through the process of learning the material. Also, HIS NOTES ARE AMAZING! My suggestion is dont buy any textbook or something, just refer to his notes if you need help. In conclusion, he is the BEST!

Clear and concise. Said on the first day of class that you wouldn't need the textbook as long as you paid attention in lecture and he was 100% right. Very intelligent, clearly knows his stuff. Prepares you well for tests, is respectful of student questions. Dry sense of humor is a bonus.

The best of the best for number theory lectures. Very honest and in touch with the learning process of upper level math students. Will publish lecture notes which are as good if not better than any textbook.

Fantastic professor. He's clear, helpful, and posts concise course notes online. Available for help if you need it. Responds to emails very quickly. Very intelligent. Textbook not necessary because of the TeX course notes he types.

She can be a bit more organized in explaining the assignments because she doesn't have clear rubrics or guidelines. However, her class is informative and very fun. She brought in food for us as well. Very sweet and caring professor.
Great professor, lots of readings but the material isn't bad. If you attend the class and do most of the readings, you will be fine.

Professor Ball's class expanded my interest in history through her extensive knowledge on a continent that isn't informationally accessible (due to its comprehensive history and culture). She made the class not only enjoyable but digestible. Recommend both the course and the professor!

She's one of the best professors I've taken so far. Although the class involved a lot of reading (from her "moderate selection" of books), a lot of the information comes from a high school U.S. History class. She could be a little more transparent on what she wants in an assignment, but she's approachable and wants the best for everyone.
Molly was awesome! Great teacher, rally cares.

Really nice class. Indeed, NOT a trustworthy person. He will say one thing to your face, then act like he never said it. He will even say that what you said isn't true, and he is very careful about what he puts in writing. You can learn a lot from him if you are willing to ignore the constant condescending remarks.
tags: ['Tough grader', 'Lots of homework', 'Beware of pop quizzes']

comment: One of my favorite professors ever! Gives extremely clear explanations and challenges students. Enjoyable if you are enthusiastic about the subject.
I wouldn't characterize him as a trustworthy person.

One of the best professors I've taken at UofR. The lectures are compelling, office hours are helpful, and the professor is an expert in the field. But the class is hard. He moves through content quickly and it's easy to get lost.
5 homeworks, 1 exam, 5–10 pop quizzes total. Lectures not recorded. Posted slide decks are sparse, so go to lecture.

Ralf can seem intimidating, but is actually a really nice guy. I chose to have him as my advisor. This was by far the most practical class I took as an undergrad. It seemed that many things I had learned in the past came into an alignment, and that I was in the right place. I would highly recommend it for anyone interested in doing research.
She's one of the best professors in the language department!!! She's super caring and tries to make the class engaging!

I like her, but she kind of has a boring way of teaching. 80% of her classes are just "Talk to the person next to you about the current topic" or "Give your answers to the reading guides." Fair warning the readings can be super dense and quite violent. Also SPAN 200 feels more like a literature class than a composition class

Professor Alfaro is such a kind and understanding person. Attendance is graded, but if you email her and have good reason to miss class, she will not penalize you. There are good opportunities for extra credit, and the tests are straight forward and easy as long as you actually engage in class. There is very minimal homework, and it is all easy.

Professor Alfaro is the nicest professor I have had at the U of R by far. Although I am only in my second year, I don't know if I will have a professor that I will enjoy more than her during the rest of my tenure. Although her lectures can be a tad slow or boring sometimes, she always finds ways to keep us engaged and she wants you to succeed.
Best professor in the languages department!

The best professor ever in the university. I took this class as my second foreign language so this course is pretty intense and covers a lot of material. However, she's just so nice to provide extra help I need and office hours to go over my questions. You need to spend a lot of time ready for oral and other exams. But you will learn a lot!

It was a little bit more work than I expected for a two credit class, but Amy was super chill and caring. I think she is done teaching now but I really enjoyed class with her. She was very down to Earth. She did sort of grade the final project harder than I was expecting. Also her class I a little disorganized.

Don't pick her if you can't handle her energy. I don't know how to describe it but she kinda has like sassy girlboss humor. She's the director of the Speaking Fellows, so she gives pretty good advice when it comes to dialogue and self-image. Yeah, the class is a lot of work, but you can't really blame the professor for that. Blame the department.

Seems nice, but is a unreasonable amount of work for a 2 credit class. Harsher grading than necessary. Was sick halfway through the semester and had some late assignments and it hurt my GPA for no reason. If you are busy and don't have the time to do the excessive amount of work, def take it with someone else as there are many prof who teach it

There's a good amount of work in this class, but its like any other college class, difficult and long! Amy is easily one of the best professors i have ever had, she is funny, kind, and someone who can be there for you!! Amy ily

Amy is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is so kind and very thoughtful to all her students. The work in class is sometimes hard and can feel overwhelming, but she is really supportive and has many great pointers and tips for doing your best!

I did not prepare for a bunch of work that was needed to be done for a 2-credit course. Amy's lectures are full of fun, and she is a good professor herself. However, she is not a good grader, and the criteria is kinda misleading.
Love her she's the best. Took her for the Taylor Swift writing class. Super engaging and funny. Super understanding, just communicate with her. Really fair grader, not hard to do well in her class.

Amy is a great professor at UofR! If you have the opportunity to take a class with her do it! She is so funny and really cares about her students. There are lots of readings for the class, but they are fun and work well with discussions. OYS!

Amy is a great professor! Class was pretty easy and she gives thorough feedback. You could get away without doing the readings. Some of the assignments were corny, ngl. Peer review and discussion are huge so be prepared for that! Amy is super lenient on deadlines and she cares about her students a lot.
I LOVE AMY. She's so kind, so helpful, and so funny.

If you have the opportunity to take a class taught by Amy, jump at it! She is so engaging, funny, and well-spoken, and the class materials might be lengthy, but the discussions make up for it. Amy really cares about her students, and making her courses as perfect as they can be. Feedback is a major theme in this course; peer review is huge!

Amy's Wrt 273 class was great. She always balanced relevant advice instruction with funny stories about her kids. Some of the assignments felt a bit cheesy, but choosing a real reader was a great part of the course, and she was always around to help with resumes and cover letters.

Amy is the best professor! She gave lots of good feedback and taught you lots of good writing strategies. The reading may indeed be overwhelming, but it is all worth after since it is so helpful. It is not an easy A, but it is definitely the class you can learn lots of things that can apply to your future writing. Take her class!

Amy is an amazing professor. She truly cares about her students and wants them to succeed. Her class is fun, and she'll spend quite a bit of time telling stories at the beginning of class, but she always makes it through the material. Overall this class has been an excellent learning experience, and I'd always go for her class if given a choice.

comment: Amy is kind and respectful of all her students. She provides thorough feedback on rough drafts and helps out often. Though, if you are looking for an easy 105 pass this isn't it. You will learn a lot, but its nearly impossible to get an A. (Must get a 95 in the course for an A, and the highest you can get on a formal paper is a 97, then 92)

Amy is super caring and understanding. Her lectures always made sense and felt relevant, and she always went the extra mile to make everyone feel included. Her feedback was always constructive and she genuinely wants her students to succeed!

Super caring and funny professor, really gets to know her students. I took an intro writing class with her and it helped me so much as a writer, whereas most of my friends got nothing out of their 105. Definitely recommend.

Professor Arbogast (Amy) is amazing!! Take her class!!! She gives really great feedback on every single assignment that you submit (quickly, too). I wouldn't say it's an easy A, but it definitely isn't impossible. I actually learned a lot in her class. She's also hilarious and so sweet which makes class enjoyable! TAKE HER CLASS!
Grading is tough but fair. Her class requires great amount of works for a high grade, but it is definitely useful for future writings assignments.
She is a very organized and earnest person, and very helpful out of the class. Although her homework is time consuming, her tests are very similar to homework.

Although this class is overall pretty easy, her expectations may be a little high for her undergraduate students.Ended up rushing through material at the end but her tests aren't bad.  Takes class performance way too personally.She's a little scarey...
No Comments
Hard course but interesting. She doesn't give too much A's.

Prof was really fun, learned a lot. Cares about her students and what she is teaching. Class itself is quite easy and fun. Some troubles with organization and unclear guidelines for assignments/exams, but it clears up quickly.

This professor is so incredibly sweet and she's funny too. As long as you do your work and try, youll get an A. You seriously have to try to fail to get anything below that. Really interesting class and genuinely gave me some interesting and new perspectives beyond anything I expected from this class. 100% recommend this class and this professor.
She really cares about her students and her lectures are very interesting and engaging.

Super fun class where we literally just analyzed comedians and watched clips. One reading followed by a short summary response per week. Dr Marshall always keeps class lively and she's really funny. Just go to class, participate here and there, and do the work and it's an A

This class is so good! You read a chapter a week and write a short reading response. The class is called Whats So Funny and all you do is analyze comedians. In class you watch a comedian and talk about them and theres a lecture. Super easy. Whatever is in the lecture is in the reading. The teacher is hilarious and genius! Loved this class

Dr Marshall's Religion and Hip-Hop class was quite unique. She is a nice and caring professor who wants you to do well and makes it very easy to do so. Attendance is mandatory and there is one short assignment per week based on the reading she gives you. Easy A
Really chill, just do the work and it's an easy A

Prof Dwarkadas is clearly very intelligent, and has a lot of respect for students However, she did not adapt to the online format very well. Lectures are reading off power points and notes are typed in awkward formats, sometimes drawing with a mouse. Recycled the same projects from past years verbatim. Very reachable outside of lecture, cares a lot

I learn nothing from her lectures. She cannot explain anything in a way that makes sense to someone unfamiliar with the subject matter. This is basically a class where you have to teach yourself. If you take this class, don't feel bad about searching online for help.
Worst Prof ever. Doesn't know the material well.

comment: Awesome teacher, very difficult course, but she explained things really well and told us to come to her office anytime for help, not just during office hours. Broke things down and really promoted questions. Ngl hard course, but it's OS, what do you expect?

comment: Good material, good lectures, kinda hard but good it is that way

Class was good. Could be kept more interesting somehow but assignments were tough and again could be made more interesting and less of kernel debugging. Little more coverage of exact kernel material would have been great.
Adorable!
Good lecturer, fairly demanding as well.  Did I mention hot?

She was excellent at teaching. I appreciated the high standard she set for the class; it made me take the class more seriously and ultimately get so much out of the class. The course explored such a wide range of contemporary dance technique. I gained more from this class than I ever anticipated on learning. My favorite class at UR!

Total jerk. Disorganized, terrible with email, emphasized being on time but was always late. Grades based on how much she likes you. Has you write opinion papers but grades you lowly if your opinion doesn't agree with hers. Learned nothing, and her technique isn't even good but she seems to think she's amazing. Wish I had dropped.

I took World Dance with her, I really enjoyed the class and learning more than just one type of dancing.  She clearly knows more than just one type of dance, and demonstrates that in this class. I would have enjoyed being able to dance more than once a week, but the lectures and debates about dance made me look at dance differently.

She is a fanatic about attendance, and I found out too late that she doesn't even record attendance accurately. I dropped an entire letter grade due to her lack of organization.  Dance ability and effort seem not to matter.  Handing something in late, no matter the reason, drastically hurts your grade. Courtney World doesn't check her email EVER.

Disorganized as all hell. A jerk about attendance, even if you have a note from UHS it counts against you. Content is patchy and skips around. Warm-ups take half the class or more. Hopefully things will pick up, I should have dropped the course while I still could.
Lectures are delivered in monotone level.

The longer he stays, the worse this department and the overall education will become. Didn't teach things related to wireless communications, basically recitation of 241, which is not even that hard. Hurting the students by giving them easy points with zero challenge and nonsensical assignments not even related to the course content. Needs to go.

Professor is chill and course is easy as well, quiz/exams were easy and exactly matches the context that he has been teaching us so very doable. Final Project was also interesting and grading was also rlly generous.

Professor Barron is a great professor, and a caring person. His slides are well done, and his lectures are engaging. The most difficult part of this class was how the pacing changed throughout the semester (going from slow-paced to fast-paced.) Participation also matters a lot, as he cold calls.

His slides are very well done and he does a good job presenting the material. The grading is also extremely nice. I would have preferred to need to engage with the material a bit more as the labs are basically following instructions and the quizzes/exams are just regurgitating the slides (like exact problems). Overall a nice professor.

Really caring, very good at understanding the perspectives of students who aren't familiar with the material and making sure everyone knows the foundations before starting new concepts. Has very fair grading schemes and lots of extra credit too.

I took his first class as a professor. He's probably the most caring professor I've had, and is working very hard to become a great professor. Grading schemes & class time can get a little disorganized, but he's always willing to help and receive feedback. I have never done so well in a class that I understood the material of so poorly.
worst professor I have ever met. apparently he knows his stuff but is unable to pass it on to students.

Literally the worst professor I have EVER had. Can't stand going to his class or dealing with him. He is unclear about absolutely everything. He gives you a choice for a term paper but then shoots down everything. Monotonous voice. The majority of the class falls asleep if they even go. Never take his classes. Also, disgustingly hairy ears...

I know few professors who get as mixed responses as Dave Pollack. Personally, I think the man is a great lecturer who always comes to class with something new and exciting. He's very helpful in his office, incredibly knowledgable about his area, and a pretty fair grader. The assignments are sometimes irritatingly vague, though. Overall, great guy.

He is very knowledgeable about Japanese culture but I'm not sure that makes him competent in teaching art history. I'm an art history major and found the lectures to be irritatingly simplistic + one-sided. he did not give us enough social/historical background but just rambled on about the most random details of 1 print for 45 min. The class was OK

Worst class I've ever taken. Apparently spending two classes on a topic doesn't necessarily mean it's related to the course. You have to pick the topic for the large paper (anything related to the class), however it's completely hit or miss if he'll approve it. Save yourself and don't take this class.

This class puts me to sleep. He gives the most boring lectures and the take home midterm is vague, and overly long for the time alotted. Its a 6-12page paper to be written in under 48 hours. If you like yourself at all don't take this class.
Fantastic class environment and a great overall semester. Very difficult class with hard homework and exams but she will work with you if you put in effort.
most caring and understanding professor ever. The content is hard and exams are brutal but 80 is an A. She will work with you to accommodate your needs.

The best physics/astro class I have taken at UofR, but also the most challenging, but Prof. Douglass is always there to help you get through it! Homeworks and Exams are tricky, they rely heavily on approximations and assumptions, which is a useful skill to develop! Overall great class and great professor.

I would jump in front of a bullet for you Professor Douglass. Very informative lectures and also very good at explaining concepts. The class is very difficult but Professor Douglass is very good at making the information clear. The TAs are also very helpful. Overall a very enjoyable class.

Incredibly good at explaining concepts in lecture, and super clear and helpful lecture notes. Also very accessible by email and very understanding with extensions and the like. That said, material was very difficult - homework was very hard and I almost always worked with others and did TA office hours. Also, tests are quite hard and 65% of grade.

comment: She is always willing to help. She replies to emails very fast. 80% is A. It is not that hard to get an A, but it is definitely hard to master all the knowledge in ASTRO 111. The workshop and homework can be challenging. TA's office hours are very helpful for the homework.

Professor Douglass is dedicated, prepared for class and manages her lecture well, although the homework got a bit tough towards the end of the semester. She also makes sure that all questions are answered, and gives extra help to those in need. Get yourself acquainted with calculus beforehand though.

Professor Douglass is a great professor who really cares about her students and is always willing to help! AST 142 is a really cool class and she is very enthusiastic about the material. Questions were always welcome and encouraged. Tests were difficult, but no more than to be expected. Homeworks could be more clear, but help is always available

Due to the online lectures, Sumpter is always behind and classes often go overtime. The approach of his lecture is confusing as in the beginning, he introduced three physics models with no context. His handwriting is unbearable and his practice exam solutions are full of mistakes.

Dr. Sumpter was a very boring lecturer. He told us the night before classes that the semester was going to be online, and he read word for word from the textbook. His handwriting was illegible. He seemed very bored. He was also horrible with communication and often was behind other sections. Would not take his class again.

Sumpter is not a good zoom lecturer, and he sent an email 12 hours before the first class that the whole semester would be online... He copied word for word from textbook, with little explanation, and made a lot of mistakes. He also randomly went completely silent for a few minutes often, and went 10-15 minutes over class time every single lecture.

He's a pretty good professor and helpful during office hours, but his lectures have been online the past few semesters (even though the original course listings said they'd be in person). If you don't like online lectures, I recommend picking a different section. I'd take his class again if it wasn't virtual.

He is a kind and friendly professor who is willing to help. But his lecture is more like reading and copying his notes to the whiteboard and I need to self-teach after class, and the worst part is that we had Zoom class without knowing it before the class began. Besides, the written homework was hard but it's helpful for exams.
Good lectures and clear notes. Posts extra notes to help learning. Also posts recordings of lectures. If you take notes and watch his lectures, class isn't too bad.

Taught Probability really well, prepared us adequately for exams. Only issues in the course were that Written HW assignments were very hard for no reason, not super related to class, but webworks were fine. Content was rushed at the end though which sucked. Tests were pretty fair but final was brutal for some reason. Other than that good class.
He is caring and willing to answer questions. But his lecture is almost like reading and copying textbooks. He made writing mistakes on the board some times but he is willing to correct them.

He's alright. Lectures are kinda monotonous, easy to fall asleep in the morning, but at least he gets the information out and if you copy it all down you can usually sort it out later. Lectures directly from his notes so it's generally put together, but also not very inspired. It's calc, it's difficult, but he'll help you out in office hours.

Prof Sumpter's lecture pace is quite slow, so it was boring at first. But as the coursework got harder, his lecture was extremely helpful. He touched on all the strategies needed to approach a topic, and the lecture helped with homework, which eventually help with exams. Prof is nice and accessible outside of class, overall very recommended.
He's very fair and his lectures are helpful and worthwhile. The notes he writes during lectures are really good and all you need to do well on the exams.

Joshie is a technically fine professor, but he does very little to make the content particularly interesting or go above and beyond. He's basically just a textbook. 2 stars seems harsh because you could definitely do worse than Josh, but he's not great. Super boring but he will prepare you decently for the exam

He really gets straight to the point and does not waste time lecturing on topic that are irrelevant and/or will not be on the exam. Always clear about if a topic will or will not covered on an exam. He is a bit monotone in his voice while lecturing, so its a bit tough to stay engaged at times. Felt very prepared for exams and would take him again.

A great professor with the best intention for people to learn. Accessible outside of class. Sometimes goes into too abstract concepts but that could be a good or bad thing depending on what kind of student you are.

His lectures are boring, but I don't really think that's his fault- the material is pretty dull. He is accessible outside of class, and is willing to help with hw problems during office hours. He doesn't have any sort of ego, which I really appreciated.

His lectures were slow and boring. He made mistakes often when writing on the board, but was very willing to admit being wrong if someone pointed it out. He spends more time on defining ideas than showing examples of how to solve the problems. He was patient and willing to answer questions. Grading and test expectations were fair.

As someone who took Calc 1 in high school, this class was very boring for me. In the end, we got to some new things and I had very little comprehension despite putting in the effort to learn. I'm glad I already knew some calc otherwise I would probably have failed. On a good note, he is very approachable and takes time to answer questions.

MATH 201, conceptually, isn't that bad. Professor Sumpter sort of assumes that you're keeping up with the very mathematically dense definitions of stuff that he gives in class, but sort of clarifies after. Nice guy though. Keep in mind that nothing in the class really goes beyond the difficulty level of a calculus course; go to office hours too.
great lectures

Professor Sumpter is one of the best math teachers I have had not only at UR but in general. He is beyond funny and keeps you interested in what is usually a simple, boring math lecture. He is extremely caring and accessible outside of class, great guy!

I was wondering why Prof Sumpter receives so few reviews! Definitely one of the best professors at U of R, he is very funny and easily approachable. He responds to emails quickly and his office hours are helpful. His lectures are well organized and easy to understand if you pay enough attention and he goes over the materials really carefully.
Professor Sumpter is one of the greatest Math professors that I've ever had. His office hours were beyond helpful.
Worst teacher in college. Talks like he is going to pass out. Terrible handwriting. Just so bad. How does he become a professor?

he is one of the worst professors I've ever had. he constatly messes up proofs, forgets where he is and makes simple material confusing and mundane. it has gotten to the point where I exclusively rely on the teaching assistants to understand the material. Cohen might have been a good teacher at some point but that was at least 20 years ago

"I hear: I forget. I see: I remember. I do: I understand."  Dr. Cohen is brilliant, and always willing to help students. He subscribes to the Moore Method; that is, class is instructive for developing basic intuition for concepts, but true knowledge is gained through homework completion and conversation in his office hours. Amazing experience!
Obviously does not prepare for class.

Nice guy, but terribly disorganized. Can't finish half of his proofs. Frequently begins teaching a topic after homework on that topic is already handed in, which makes going to class pretty pointless. He is a brilliant guy, however, and very willing to help.

This is the best professor I had all my freshmen year, this guy is great. You can go to him for everything at any time and he really cares about your understanding of the topic regardless of your grade or whatever else, he just wants you to learn. He might seem a bit tough at first, but then HE RULES!

Loved this class, mostly because of him. I entertained my friends with his ridiculous math metaphors, I am now a math major because of the class. He expects a LOT out of you at first, but eases up after the first test.  Very responsive to our homework woes.  Assumes that you want to know the whole back story for every proof. Sweetest prof ever!

He tells very corny jokes and sometimes gets lost in his own proofs. He assumes his students know most of the material and doesn't help much when he ends class in the middle of a proof. It also doesn't help when he gives a proof in class, asks you to prove it on an exam, and marks it wrong, even when you copied it straight from the board.

He's a really nice guy and legitimately wants to see his students succeed but he's really horrible at explaining key subjects and tends to lose focus of what he's talking about and then get the example problem wrong and then he'll tell the students to finish it by themselves when he hasn't taught them how to do it.

Nice guy. Corney Jokes. Makes lots of mistakes on the board but just arithmatic usually. I have found that most of the non honors low level math professors are poor so I would say that he is above average in comparison but I still don't think he was a good teacher.

Better than Harper.  Decent at explaining the material.  Follows the book mostly.  The course isn't fun; webwork is a killer.  Cohen is a considerate professor.  He rewrites, redraws, uses different colored chalk to indicate things.  Not a bad experience overall.
Would not reccomend this teacher.  Very bad at explaining things.  I do not know what the other reviewers are thinking.  I'm an excellent math student and I think this guy shouldn't be teaching.
Very nice guy, very helpful. Go to his office hrs, talk about life. He's great!
I learned a lot in the course but not everything that was probably intended.  Cohen is a great teacher, although sometimes he is too overly concerned maybe with how everyone is doing.
Hard to follow sometimes... especially for theoretical material.  Is happy and very willing to revisit material to help comprehension, though.  Overall not a bad experience.
Great Professor, he is enthusiastic and cares.
Good teacher.  He's very concerned about his students and is very enthusiastic about what he teaches.
Excellent professor.  Really enthusiastic about mathematics, and makes it clear in his teaching.  Teaches calculus without boring you, as he tells funny anecdotes and draws pictures on the board.
Has an odd obsession with bugs.  Very helpful and concerned about my progress.
Doesn't cover the intended course material, but still a decent teacher. Has a few lame jokes and uses the same ones daily.
FredProCoh!
very helpful

T's lectures were almost incomprehensible if you didn't read the textbook before class. He does not explain things at a level that someone who doesn't already grasp the gist can understand. However, HW was fair, exams were alright, and so was grading (exh. A). T does not teach intuition in 236H, only definitions... which hurts all of his students.

comment: His lectures had to have been the worst thing possible. Would do the easiest problems in class and give extremely challenging problems for homework. His lecturing style was definitely not for me, as it felt unorganized and like he barely knew what he was talking about. The exams were a nightmare. Would not recommend.

Tucker is great, lectures can be a little boring, but his explanations and examples are often helpful. I strongly recommend going to any review lectures before exams, as they're extremely helpful. Overall a nice guy as well.

Easy class, harsh exam.
Countless homework, valueless feedback. 
Great effort, average score.

Professor Tucker is really a caring teacher. I switched into his math 141 lecture after dropping from 161. He was always nice and open to meeting and helping with homework. All around, a nice guy and worth taking!

He is definitely one of my favorite math professors at u of r. The content is really hard, but he managed to taught the materials in a way that students may better understand. Haven't gone to his office hour yet, but will definitely do when I have time

Tucker is a great guy, but I struggled to click with him as a professor. I did not take ap calc (I only took precalc) which made the class difficult. His handwriting can be hard to read, so ask if you cannot for clarification. I did find the other professors for 141 easier to understand, but again Tucker is a good person and not an awful professor.
Professor Tucker is a very nice guy and a decent lecturer. My only problem with him was his hand writing is a little hard to read.

Pretty awful calc class. I took calc in high school and if I didn't have that knowledge I'd be pretty up a creek. Do the homework - it's free points, and it teaches you the material better than the lecture. Or watch Khan Academy.

Always a pleasant experience to take his course. Took his MATH201 and 280. Though some minor mistakes are frequent in lecture, he has been one of the most reponsible and caring professor in the department. OFFICE HOUR helps a lot, 100% recommend

Really, really good professor. Presents foreign concepts very readily in a digestible form and the exams (bar the final, which was fair) weren't that hard, just understand the concepts and study the class examples/homework and recitations and you're good.
Truly gained a lot and made me prepared for MTH203. I almost got full score in final!

He makes MTH217 very interesting. The material is pretty dry, but can be confusing and he clears up the common issues. Exams are on the material and if your do good HW, you will do well on exams. Highly recommend.

comment: He gives clear and understandable proofs. Also, he is very nice and willing to answer any question about math. Nice grading and curve.
Awesome professor. He gives very clear, structured, and intuitive explanations of abstract concepts.
No matter how hard 171Q is, Prof. Tucker saved my day multiple times.
His voice is the sweetest of lullabies. It is impossible to stay awake in his class if it starts before noon.
His exams and homework problems are never easy but the curve is generous (but fair too). He is definitely one of the better professors in Math Department.

He was a very nice, adorable kind of professor. He was not intimidating at all, which I liked and took away pressure. He made simple mistakes a lot, but explained things well when asked a question. Material may be confusing if you didn't take AP Calc, but it was easy because I did and I'm not even that great at math. I got an A and enjoyed 141.

Difficult material, relatively easy grading. Pretty good lectures, but it's advisable to prepare before class, because he does tend to get a little confusing when jumping between different theorems. TAs are very helpful.

Makes a few minor mistakes while writing the proofs and ideas on the board. Doesnt rarely affects his teaching. Good guy. If youre taking 171q for the first time and youre not from china, good luck understanding all of it. Its really hard to pick up but once you have it its godly.

I could barely read his hand-writing, so it made going to class kind of pointless.  He seemed to get very confused while doing examples, which made me even more confused than he was.  Nice guy though, and very fair.  I didn't go to class a whole month and still managed to get a good grade.
He is great.  big fan
Nice guy and he makes the grading nice and easy for ya.

really nice guy. very good teacher, connects with the students alot. takes some time out of the class to talk about more fun things than math which helps because this class can get very boring after all the proofs
Quite a character.  Cares about his students.

Classes can get rather dry, with theorems and the proofs presented one after another, but what do you expect from algebra? Read ahead of class class. I find it hard to follow his proofs when I see them the first time. Going to office hours helps too. He frowns on students who skip his classes =).

Laura Givens is a great professor. I started taking Russian classes with the 150 series since I'm a heritage speaker and while it is tough to understand some grammatical concepts I never learned, she is very approachable and open to answer any questions. She grades tough but fair, and is very passionate about the Russian language!

Professor Givens is a wonderful professor, especially for a course in Russian. I appreciate the high quality and interactive nature of the lectures. While there is a lot of homework, it helps learn the language and prepares you very well for the exams and quizzes. I highly recommend Prof. Givens to anyone interested in learning Russian.

A good professor for Russian, you will most likely have her at one point or another. Russian is a hard language, but she teaches well enough and it's not too bad of a course if you put in the work. Upsides, generally small course, and lots of resources if you need it, and she's always happy to help.

comment: Professor Givens is one of my favorite professors at this university. She makes learning fun and teaches russian in a way that is conducive for learning a language. She is very caring and is willing to talk to you outside of class if you need help or advice. Taking russian was probably the best decision I made in college.

Professor Givens is an amazing Russian professor. Her lectures are organized and straight forward. As a person, she is very kind and always willing to help or talk to you. I would definitely recommend her classes to anyone.
Genuinely caring, one of the best
I LOVED THIS PROFESSOR!!!

I was shocked to see the the things some people said about Laura on this site. She is easily one of the most caring people and professors I have ever met and she was the best professor Ive ever had at U of R. She really cares about her students and is very knowledgeable in Russian and can explain complex grammatical rules with ease. Helpful always

Laura Givens is an incredible Russian teacher. Her courses are well laid out, and assignments and class expectations are clear. Russian is not an easy language to learn, but Laura explains things simply and extremely effectively explains difficult grammar topics. I have enjoyed every class with her.

Professor Givens is amazing. Both Laura and John. She always gives help when you need it and responds to emails in a timely manner with grammar explanations, even if you're on summer vacation! Her class is friendly, and she encourages frequent use of Russian.
Helpful if you ask questions. Grades a little harsh.

People on this site give Laura a bad rap. She does have a dry personality, but she also has a good sense of humor and really does care about her students, after you get to know her (and assuming you put the effort in for her class)! She's tough, but she does care.
One of the best professors I have had at the University of Rochester. Easy to follow in class and is always willing to help her students.
Great professor! Very knowledgable.
She's really not as bad as a lot of people make her out to be. She's approachable, funny, and really helpful. I enjoyed class with her.

Not nearly as engaging as her husband(I LOVE HIM). She's a nice woman, kind and helpful if you come to her, but DRY DRY DRY and intimidating in class. Hard as hell grader, too. But, she knows her Russian. If you're there to learn grammar and not be entertained, she's good, but I don't think I'd take a class with her again unless I audited.

This professor does not smile, does not make you feel welcome, and keeps the class in constant fear. There is no way to improve if you have fallen behind. Class doesn't effectively help with Russian communication.
Not as good as her husband, she seems to not have as structured classes and is definitely not a warm person, i wish i had a professor who truly cared about her students.

This professor taught my physics/chemistry advanced lab course. He did very well in giving us freedom to explore the science. I can imagine he would be better for upper-level courses, but I did not have him for any 100/200s to compare. He can be rough around the edges, but I found him to be very helpful in preparing for graduate studies in physics.

Have you ever wondered what it would be like to be taught Thermodynamics by a Part-Time, Assistant Professor? Well... wonder no more! Take PHY 227 for the low price of ~$50,000 a year! Seriously, you will learn everything you wanted to know about nothing... And Nothing is well worth the price! Actually, I lied... Do not take Boersma's courses!

He is the worst professor I've ever had.  I never went to class because he was too useless as a lecturer.  Worse still was his grading system: his tests were straight memorization and sign errors would cost you letter grades.  Do NOT take any course he teaches.

I was very disgusted in this class!! Professor Boersma did a terrible job teaching. Half of the semester was spent on learning trivial probability and the other was spent regurgitating equations from the textbook on homework and exams without learning any physics. It was evident that he had minimal understanding of the subject. Desecrated thermo!!

Professor Boersma is one of the most incompetent teachers I have ever had. I did not learn a single thing in his "class" that I hadn't seen in non-AP high school physics, nor did anybody. Even an A in his class still meant that you knew nothing. His grading system was asinine. Lectures verbatim from text. Don't ever take his classes!!!

Professor Weber is extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the topic at hand. The class can get boring at times, but overall I had a fulfilling time; Professor Weber was always accessible outside of class and always gave a lot of time to finish the work assigned. All in all, it was an enjoyable class, but be prepared to read!

comment: I loved Professor Weber. Passionate about the book we read, super knowledgeable, always open to other perspectives and additions, plus her assignments were fun and interesting. She was so careful not to give us too much work and really considerate about personal circumstances. A really fun and engaging professor

Simply the best professor I've had. Class discussions were incredibly engaging with great dialogue, as Prof. Weber really facilitated a classroom community that made it enjoyable to speak. Feedback on papers was helpful and specific, and more than anything, the readings we did were fascinating. Great course, even better professor.

comment: Professor Weber is awesome. She usually has a lot of energy, and is very eager to answer any question that you might have. She's also very flexible as long as you talk to her. The course is structured around lessons and for each lesson, there are 2 quizzes and 1 test. As long as you put in a bit of effort and do your work, you'll be fine.

Grading was random and based on arbitrary participating measures, you can get As in all the assignments and get a B in the class at the professors whim. Course material was interesting but you could just read the books and wouldnt miss much.

comment: Really enjoyed this class! The content was super interesting and Professor Weber is very approachable.

comment: Professor Wojat tries to make auditing more interesting. His auditing stories actually help me remember concepts better. He is obviously really smart and will do anything to make time for his students! He is a good professor!

comment: GO TO LECTURE and make sure he knows your name/face, he's been known to bump grades. HW isn't graded, but very similar to Exams, some exactly the same with different #'s. He is the only Prof. for FIN 205, so take his 201 so you can get used to his style before FIN 205. FIN 205 will be impossible if you take ACC 201 w/ another prof.

The WORST professor I have ever had. Goes on too many tangents during class. Very bad at explaining concepts in class. Very hard to know how to study for tests because they are all multiple choice. Do the homeworks to study for the test.

Biggest waste of time. Didn't learn anything about accounting with him besides his rants of how much his life sucks. If I were the University I would probably fire him except he probably hides all the bad numbers and raise in tuition for them. Oh yeah, if you love learning through transparencies in a large auditorium, he's perfect.

Very knowledgeable professor. Excited in the material. Taught very well. Was available meet and go over questions on the material outside of class. Test questions were based on the lecture notes. Easy to do well in this class if you went and did the problems assigned.

He really care about his students and want them to learn but has standards. The notes are overwhelming but his format is straightforward. It was one of my favorite classes at the school. I'd like to take a class with him again.

REALLY energetic prof.  he even admits that ACC material is dry, but he makes the best of it.  Even though he has over 150 students a semester, he makes it his duty to get to know every last one of them--->he's very passionate about teaching and is an overall great person.  Tests are right out of notes.
Extremely boring class and likes to call on random people. Reads off his lecture notes on the overhead and talks way too loudly. Subject is way too boring to get through reading the book.

he is all over the place when he talks, not too interesting, tries to get really into the lectures but they are still boring and confusing, tells random, unrelated stories over and over. likes to learn his students names and get to know you, gives out lecture notes, tests are all multiple choice.

the man loves to teach and he DOES care if you learn or not which is good...class can be real boring...he's easy to understand though and he gives out notes and his tests are multiple choice...very similar to ECO 211 if you've taken that before

Makes an effort to get to know each student, gives great lecture notes, and very fair exams. The course is a very general overview of finance that makes a few too many generalizations, but Wodjat does a good job teaching it. Occassional tangents can be strange, but he's a nice guy and a great prof.
Spends a lot of time preparing lectures and genuinly tries to make sure the material is understood.
Wojdat is a really sharp guy who cares a lot about teaching. He works hard to make sure he gets the material across to his classes. Accounting and Finance can be boring, but Wojdat makes it fun!
excellent notes give out, straight forward exams if you do the hwk and attend class
Excellent teacher.  It is nice to have a professor who goes out of his way to get to know his students.  He is genuinely concerned about seeing his students doing well.
He's an awesome prof. It seems he spends a long time preparing before his lectures and he gives out his notes as well which makes studying easier. He's also a generally funny and cool guy.
Excellent prof, wished he taught more classes for undergrad.

Professor Ruskin is a really lovely professor. In the class I'm in, there are only 2 short assignments, 3 exams and weekly quizzes (usually 5 questions). Taught "The Peaceful Warrior." The job of teaching WRT courses is often given to terrible starting profs who don't know what they're doing, but I found Marshall's class quite good, and the material quite interesting - even though I didn't want to be there and was only taking the course to fulfill my long-overdue freshman writing req. Good prof.
There's no clear grading criteria
Boring class

From the lectures I feel like the professor doesnt know the material that well. But from the test you understand that he understands it really well. He teaches at a level that assumes you have ALOT of background.
His lectures are confusing, PowerPoints are barebones, tests cover things that were never taught, textbook is no help. He doesnt record lectures, post notes, or allow for pictures.

Difficult class content-wise if you don't have an anatomy/physiology background. Difficult to predict what will actually be tested on. An easy-going professor with plenty of office hours.

This class was asynchronous, so everything was online and you do it at your own pace. Doesn't know how to teach and feels good about himself. Difficult homework that relate to nothing learned in class. Doesn't explain easy concepts well. Now he's teaching BME 295 and BME 260, both are required for BME majors at UR, so it sucks a lot.

Homework is a crazy ton and has nothing to do with what's taught in lectures. Exams are difficult. Man is not a good lecturer as well. Feels like easy concepts are being taught with more difficulty. Mandatory class for BME majors so it legitimately sucks.

There are classes I have taken as an upper-level BME that have truly shown me the wonders of the field. Having taken other anatomy and physiology classes, I felt well prepared for this class. This professor has a great awareness of students' needs in class and ensures that every student is appropriately addressed according to their needs. Professor Sefkow knows the material of the course very well and provided reasonable material to go along with it. However, he is very disorganized; often late to class, completely changed the syllabus in the last two weeks of class. Was his first time teaching it so it might be easier for him to plan for things in the future.

Professor Sefkow is an extremely caring and accommodating person. He regularly asked students how they were feeling about the course and welcomed feedback. Lectures were a bit hit-and-miss. Very reasonable with assignments and exams, just don't try to use the bills as a excuse for a homework extension.

Super nice person, however, lacked in being a great professor. The professionalism has been all over the place this semester with the syllabus changing and often showed up late for class. His tests, weren't very reflective of the homework problems/review given to us. Throughout the semester he's also changed the grading scheme multiple times which seems nice, but with doing this has also made an optional project required with only 2 weeks left in the semester. Prof Sefkow had great intentions, but the way he did it wasn't the best.

Professor Sefkow genuinely cares for the success of his student. He always make sure to ask if students have questions during lecture and is readily available with office hours. The class can sometimes be a bit disorganized since he may occasionally cancel lectures. The recitations are also lackluster since you are just given solutions to problems.

The class is not too bad overall as long as you do the work. Most material is directly from the textbook. I wish he added more practice problems to go over in class. You can tell he cares about his students and gave multiple opportunities to help grades out throughout the semester, even though a few of his test questions were unfair/unclear.

I was pretty nervous about taking fluid dynamics at first, but Dr. Sefkow was able to explain concepts very well and was very accommodating. It's very clear he cares about students actually learning the content and wants everyone to do well. He is very positive and enthusiastic about the subject. He is definitely my favorite engineering professor.

The content is difficult due to the nature of fluid dynamics, particularly the derivation of equations and concepts, but HW & test problems rely less on hard calculus.

Professor Sefkow is always willing to listen to feedback and truly does carefully consider each student's input when given. He teaches the material effectively and is clear on what material is important during his lectures which is then reflected in the assignments and exams. He is always willing to clarify anything during office hours or by email.

very approachable and helpful professor. exams were really conceptual and hard for me. I did ask for help and he responds well over email and gave some advice. Lots of opportunities for improving grade.

Professor Sefkow takes time go deeper into questions presented in class and reflects an ethusiam over thoughtful questions that I haven't encouned often as a student. He makes an effort to memorize all the names of students in his class which made me feel more seen. It is clear that he enjoys teaching the subject.

Professor Sefkow is incredibly catering towards students. He is constantly offering extra office hours and other resources to help his students. The TA lead recitations are somewhat useless as it heavily relies on the quality of the TA leading. The course grading scheme has changed multiple times throughout the course which has been a bit annoying.

Professor Sefkow is very open to student feedback and answering questions during class. He was easy to talk to and would take student's concerns into consideration when making decisions about the course. The only problem I saw was that things seemed a bit disorganized sometimes.

He is a very respectful professor that cares about his students and their outside commitments. However, he shows up late to almost every class or right at the time lecture starts. He loves to hear feedback from students which is unlike most professors but he had a lack of structure in the course. Overall, I would have him again.

I thought that professor Sefkow did a good job teaching Fluids. He was very respectful and listened to the students. The only complaint I have about this course was that it lacked structure so one could not plan accordingly. Overall I enjoyed this course and learned a lot.

As a lecturer he did an effective job teaching us the information and would check to make sure we got the concepts and you can tell he cares.

Professor Sefkow does a good job of explaining all of the material necessary for the course. comment: I had a really good time in this class. He was clear about the subject and found that I enjoyed taking the course far more than I was expecting. It's nice to see a professor that actually cares about the subject matter they're teaching.

Great professor, very personable and easy to talk to. Very accommodating and understands that students have a lot on their plate. Lots of homework, lots of reading quizzes. Reading quizzes really tested knowledge of the material. Homework tended to be more difficult than the exams.

Very approachable, and was open to feedback regarding the course and teaching. Difficult course in terms of content, but recitations were helpful on the homework and further understanding of the course. Attending lecture and reading helps a lot on some otherwise difficult concepts.

Wasn't clear about course structure and exam dates, but was very flexible and accomodating. Lectures were very focused on derviations of equations rather than their applications. Overall, super nice guy but could have been more organized and structured.
Willing to take feedback and adjust course accordingly

Kai teaches very well. He relates basic concepts to real world  applications and problems. The assignment are well designed, very hands-on though maybe a little bit tough.

There is just no connection between the lecture and the work to be done. He can teach and has a good standing of the stuff. But the test and homework is too difficult by just knowing what he taught in the lecture.

Kai Shen really knows his stuff. He has a bit of an accent, but he is perfectly understandable, and his accent actually became a large source of entertainment for me in the class. interesting lectures. very hard exams

Aslin is amazing. Clear, crisp, and presents just the right depth of material for a 100-level class.

comment: I took Development of the Mind & Brain with him in spring 2015. He co-taught with Celeste Kidd, and she was good, but I loved lecture days with him. A wonderful, funny guy really passionate about the topic.  I learned SO MUCH. He talked to all of us almost as if we were colleagues, and he valued our opinions.  Take his class! Wonderful professor!

Amazing professor, and he talks to all the students, regardless of previous experience or background, just the same way he talks to other faculty members. He's clear, knowledgable, and, you'd never guess from how much time he makes for all his students... a really productive, famous research scientist on top of everything!  Amazing class.
Best prof I've ever had. Speaks to even intro students as though they are peers and respects their ideas accordingly.

Awesome! A leader in his field, but i don't care about that. What I do care is how nice he is when you go to his office hours and he even helped me and a friend find research labs to work in for the summer. What prof. will go out of there way like that? very rare!
He is a very clear and precise lecturer, and is very fair with students.
Sometimes a little boring in lecture, but overall a great teacher.

Prof makes the class, I think. He's very nice though, wants to be your friend and very eager to help. Plus points for that.
Great professor - one of my favorites in the math dept. Always willing to help and very approachable.
extremely willing to give help if you ask for it. cool guy with quirks you'd expect from a math professor. very approachable if you need help.

He tends to talk directly at the whiteboard which makes it hard to hear/understand if you're not in the first 2 rows of the class. He's okay. The material isn't that challenging. He gets defensive when you ask questions, though. Ask anyway.
A terrible teacher.  He talks very quietly, mumbles, and has heavy accent.  Unable to answer questions or explain the material.  Luckily, he pretty much follows the book

Professor Ziv is a very nice person and engaging lecturer, and always answers student's questions during the lectures. Still have trauma even after taking his course for half a year. Take care.

Wow, worst professor I think I've ever heard. The entire class is just him writing down theorems and proofs then when it comes time for homework you have no idea how to solve a problem because he's never even worked out one in front of you. Avoid at all costs

Hands on optical fabrication course, show up for an engaging and good time. He's super knowledgeable on the topic due to years in the field professionally. He teaches concepts clearly, and will take as much time as needed to make sure everyone is on the same page.

He's chill but horrible professor. Unclear, very unorganized, cares only about research and has said so himself. He takes off a million points on your exams. You may have not said anything incorrect, but because someone else in the class had a slightly better worded answer, you can lose points. Long story short, it doesn't reflect what you know.

One of the best lecturers I've encountered. He shows genuine interest in his teaching and is highly engaging. Don't buy the textbook; all info is in his lectures which are all posted online. There's a lot of material, but if you memorize the lectures, you will do well. He doesn't curve, but there are opportunities for extra credit. Great class!
He did not videotape lectures for our class and he's pretty boring. Tests are ok, but he asks some pretty random questions. Also be prepared to study really hard and not do well.

Holtzman acts like he cares but he's such an ****. He'll be rude in class if he doesn't like your question, he'll lower your grade after the test, his tests cover material that is irrelevant, and his class is generally painfully boring. I'm a good student but found it hard to do well in his class and definitely do NOT recommend him

Not only are his lectures extremely comprehensive, they are VIDEOTAPED and put online so you NEVER have to show up! (and he makes the lectures as interesting as possible if you do want to show up). Memorize the lectures the night before the test, guranteed A.  So much better than the previous professor from what I've heard

Crystal clear lectures. Very, very organized. 3 test - all count, not curve, no extra credit. Memorize everything in lecture and will do fine. (BTW - when Nordeen teaches this class - it absolutely blows, or so I've heard).
Holtzman is a fabulous professor who is very helpful and knows how to keep students engaged! once he brought a boa constrictor into class :)

Good professor, knows his stuff and had some good stories to share.  His tests were manageable.  I found myself studying alot and all I got were B's.  I thought he should've given some extra credit of some sort since our whole grade was based on exams.
studied constantly and ended up with 60's every time...
Great lecturer, exams were a bit tough and he does not like to curve, so that is not cool, but he is one of the best lecturers I have had.

So much material; the most notes I've ever taken.  But the information was fascinating particularly when augmented by Holtzmann's outstanding (and for the most part very interesting) lectures.  Fair tests-only hard because of the amount of material they cover.  Doesn't really curve.

Holtzman definitely gives out some tough exams.  The good thing is that he has very interesting lectures and does a great job guiding you through the material.  He also puts all the power points onlin, so if you miss a class no big deal.  Just make sure you study your butt off.  He's pretty funny and approachable to

You have to put in a lot of work but its worth it. Andrew is very knowledgeable and more than help to help students in his free time understand difficult concepts.
Very good course

Advanced pathophysiology is a very challenging course. Andrew did not dumb it down, but was able to explain complex concepts in a way that I could understand and learn. If you really want to learn pathophysiology, he's the professor for you.
Described complex concepts VERY clearly; had fun and creative assignments that were relevant to practice.
Amazing.

Overall amazing professor, would take again. Very informative and will 100% support your learning if you are motivated. Also great guy in general. If you have the option to have him as a professor for a course, pick him.
Class was pretty easy, he's very lenient on due dates. Extremely friendly and gives good feedback
The nicest and most understanding professor ever. If you're going to take a Spanish class or cluster at UR take at least one class with him

Prof. Kirt is such a sweetheart. Really passionate and knowledgeable about the Spanish language. Amazing for absolute beginners. Super engaging and wants everyone to feel included.
