My favorite professor! He was always really caring, understanding, and makes class very enjoyable in order to make 9am class very engaging. The best professor for language class. He genuinely helps his students and wants them to succeed. Wish he taught more Spanish classes!

Amazing professor! He truly cares for his students and always gives the best feedback on hw/essays.
Very kind and knowledgable in his class too. I never felt bored in class as he'll find a way to make class fun. As long as you put in effort and are present in class you will be all set! I encourage anyone to take this class for sure :).
Very charismatic. He's really knowledgeable about the subtleties of Spanish such as the grammar rules and regional differences. Class is super easy to get an A in
Easy to understand, and an easy class overall.

The best Spanish teacher at the University!! He truly cares about his students and is so accommodating for any problems you may be facing outside of class. Super kind and patient, I really recommend taking him as. professor over the other ones if you have the option to.

Kirt is so amazing. The most caring professor on this campus. Please talk to him if you're struggling, he is soooo accommodating. Spanish is the third language I am learning and English is my second language so I often struggled to keep up in this class but he was soo helpful and always had such a good attitude everyday. Loved him and this class.

By far the nicest and most understanding professor I've ever had. He is excited to teach and always welcoming. Assignments are very manageable with fairly frequent, yet understandable quizzes. Each class is discussion-oriented and he is always helpful and judgement-free if you get stuck while speaking in Spanish. Great feedback too!

Professor Komocki comes to class prepared and excited to teach. He is always enthusiastic about the subject matter at hand and makes everything extremely clear. There are quite a few quizzes, but they are all pretty easy and straightforward as long as you review the notes he posts. He is extremely accessible, kind, and accommodating.

Amazing professor. He makes going to class enjoyable and even though participation is important, you're never scared of getting something wrong. Probably the kindest and happiest professor you'll ever have. Do yourself a favor and take this class if he's the professor, he'll make your day every class.

Professor Komocki is one of the best professors I have ever had. He makes Spanish class fun through his positive energy, exciting lectures, and his creative ties. He's always available outside of class for help, and if you're willing to put in the work, you will succeed. I looked forward going to his class every day, and am going to miss his class.

Kirt Kimocki is that old memory of a teacher who showed up to class excited to be teaching others. He's charismatic, respectful, and accommodating. He's not afraid to adapt or even embarrass himself if it means that his students may learn the course's content better. A class-act professor and a decent human being. Also impeccable taste in ties.

Be prepared to speak a lot of Spanish, but also learn a lot! This class is super collaborative and you will get a lot of practice speaking and reading Spanish. The class is not homework heavy and if you do have questions about the work, Prof. Komocki is very helpful. It's obvious that he cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed.

comment: By far the best Spanish professor I've ever had. Class is pretty participation-heavy, but he doesn't make you feel judged for getting something wrong, which I really appreciated. He's very accommodating and easy to contact if you need any help or have questions.

My favorite professor, super accommodating and overall really cares for his students. As long as you show up and make an effort you will get a good grade. Super nice guy who genuinely cares for his students, ESPECIALLY during covid.
Super great guy. If you put in the work he will help you.
Great Professor. Cares about his students and is willing to discuss your grades. Would always take him again.

Kirt is an amazing professor and he really cares about his students. He might seem like a tough grader but he puts a lot of effort into grading, and gives you a chance to write a draft/ final. Very enthusiastic, very detailed notes

One of the best Spanish professors I've ever had! Very patient, genuinely cares that everyone feels comfortable speaking in Spanish, and makes his class relatively easy as long as you put in the work. Always available for extra help during office hours and before and after class.

Kirt is honestly one of my favorite professors I've ever had, period. One of the best professors I've ever had. Super nice and funny with interesting lectures. Very approachable and gives clear feedback. The tests and papers are easy as long as you put in the work.
He's really sweet and is willing to slow down. He doesn't make anyone feel stupid and he is very open-minded. A great professor with lots of enthusiasm.

Kirt is a super great teacher, very enthusiastic about Spanish which makes it all the more fun to learn. Very clear and helpful to students. You won't do bad if you put in the work and show a real passion for learning Spanish.

keeps students really involved. always enthusiastic.

Very great teacher! Always super enthusiastic and helpful. You will never be bored in this class, professor Komocki always incorporates individuality and freedom in this Advanced Spanish Composition class!

He takes his time with explanations and examples to help students follow easily. He was never impatient and seemed to truly want students to succeed. Clear in class notes, which are really important in this circumstance.

West African dance was SO much fun! You will not learn much. but it will be a workout, and Karen will definitely have you laughing. Grading was easy. Any class with Karen is a must take dance class!

Karen is a nice person, but has very poor teaching skills.  She is more interested in making sure the front row looks good for our performances rather than actually helping us learn african dance.  she grades very easily, though.
West african dance with karen is an absolute blast! a great workout, and a really fun class overall.

Lovely person and great professor. I genuinely enjoyed this class and am so glad I took it in lieu of 111.

Rabeling is such a great professor. His exams are very representative of the lectures and he is very fair. He wants to see everyone do great in his class. I personally know a couple student in the Bio 111 or Bio 113 courses who wish that they took this professor. You won't regret taking him.
This was an amazing class. Sadly, Professor Paauw passed away last year.

This class was incredibly easy, and almost guaranteed A as long as you show up occasionally and do your homework.

He's a super friendly guy who really cares both for his students and for linguistics. His passion shows when he teaches, and he does an amazing job engaging students and making the material interesting. A must-have and one of the best professors I've had here!

Very engaging, great professor. Really cares about his students and always willing to help. Attend class, do the HW, and you'll do well on the tests and get an A. Wasn't expecting to enjoy it, but loved the class solely because of how great he is.

smart, very caring, very helpful. He'll learn everyone's names who are in his class. 2 tests and one final project. passionate about the subject. I'm by no means interested in linguistics, but loved his class!

One of the best professors I've ever had. Loves his subject and loves to teach. Show up and pay attention and you'll get an A. The textbook helps and you need it for homeworks. Two tests and one project.

Prof. Pauuw, probably more than any teacher I've had at the UR, genuinely cares about his students. Always willing to help. Tests were pretty easy, the homework was the only part that was occasionally difficult. For the most part though, extremely nice guy leading an interesting class.
Extremely smart and helpful teacher. Definitely come to his OH, as he will always help you. Also, he makes the effort to remember each student's name, which is extremely remarkable.

His teaching style is not restricted nor influenced by tests. He engages the class in dialogues often and assigns practical projects applicable to daily life. Thus one is not highly pressured to perform and rather, really learns. Fun teacher to listen to. Overall, good professor.

Prof. Garzione is one of the best geology profs at the UofR. Her lectures are clear and concise and she's a very nice person. If you have any interest in geology at the UofR, take EES 101. comment: I liked this class because I learned a lot, and the exams required high level thinking not just memorization. I actually learned a lot during the exams because it was open note. I definitely would read the textbook thoroughly if it is not open note.

comment: The class was very tough due to the sheer amount of material covered, but Dr. Fu is excellent at teaching and helping students to understand what hes talking about no matter how you learn best. Lots of examples and graphics. Powerpoints were super helpful.

comment: Dr. Chin is perhaps the best professor I have had yet at U of R. She is very empathetic and the coursework is definitely interesting. One thing for sure is that the class is graded by a few things and it is pretty hard to secure an A. She definitely sparked my interest in public health and the guest lectures are also very interesting.

Prof. Chin is a respectable, kind, and knowledgeable professor. She really cares about student's mental health and values our needs. The guest speakers she brings in are actually really interesting and relevant to coursework.The short in class writing assignments and blog posts are rather simple-just make sure your points are clear.Learned a lot!

Dr. Chin is one of the few professors at the UofR that genuinely cares about their students well-being outside of class. One of my favorite professors at UR! Very nice person and a great lecturer. Got me interested in public health!

The class is really hard with heavy class notes. Tests are 85% of the grades, and the class note is not assembled with the lecture slides he posts. Attendance is not required but if you miss one class is hard to catch up. His office hour is not helpful, but he has responsible TAs. If you think you are smart enough then you can take this class.
Dude's a genius, probably the best professor in the ECON department.
very prestigious and knowledgeable professor
You will realize how amazing and well-organized his lectures are when you go to a grad school. Excellent professor!
If you miss one lecture you will be lost for the rest of the semester.

comment: Asen has method of lecturing that is very easy to follow, which is useful for a class that can get very dense at times. He will spend more time on certain topics of he sees that the class hasnt grasped the concepts. He makes his notes available, and they are clear and organized. Overall amazing professor.

Prof Kochov is a cool guy. His classes are interesting. This was a new class, and wow did he impress. His lecture notes are amazing, well organized and clear. No textbook, because there is no textbook for this subject of economics. He made his own course out of nothing and deserves serious credit. Innovative! Take him, accommodating and reasonable!
Very clear lecturer with a sense of humor
He's great!

Very passionate about the topic and an engaging lecturer. He posts his own notes online which are very helpful for doing homework problems and reviewing for exams. It's a very interesting topic, but I definitely had to work for my grade. However, it's been the most rewarding ECO class I've ever taken. Would definitely recommend.

The class is mind-blowing, but can be very hard, especially if you don't know multivariable calculus. (Not too hard to pick up if you know univariable calculus.) I thought this was just going to be applied psych; it's not, it's like advanced micro. A grad student suspects Asen will get picked up by Harvard; I can see why.
I like him, really interesting. Tests/homeworks fair enough.

He loves what he is teaching, but since he is new it is sometimes hard to follow but the hw's and tests are very fair and the material interesting, although not easy. This is not a blow off class. Would recommend!
Little bit wacky sense of humor, long labs, and overall lecture vocabulary based exams. Penny is great

Dr. Higgins is awesome! Her love of Geology is infectious, and she is lively and funny lecturer, although at times she would drag on with jokes when she should have been lecturing. If you pay attention in class and take notes, you'll do fine on the tests. Overall she's a really nice and accommodating woman. I highly recommend her!
Penny is awesome. Her classes are never too hard, but always pretty fun. She's friendly and helpful, and also good at making animal noises. Like, really good.
Great, funny professor! Very organized and clear. Easy to contact with even after class. Exam is not hard and totally follow her lectures. I like her!
Good.

Penny gives enough information to understand the topic in class, yet still gives you room to think about a scenario that could arise. Her exams are very straight forward and offer extra credit. Used twitter for the first time and answered almost every tweet within an hour of it being sent out. Take this class if you can!! Worth it!!

The course itself was mediocre. Lectures were boring and uninspired. Homework assignments were uninteresting but at least they were aligned with the lecture material. Readings were interesting -- most likely the only good attribute from the course. Can I get my tuition refunded?
Professor Tresan is always willing to help during office hours and after lectures. The lectures were a bit boring but he explained materials thoroughly.

There are 22+6+331 journal entries for three assigned books in this course, but you seem to receive full credits easily as long as you read and write carefully, and only materials in the first book (with 22 journal entries) are discussed in class and tested on exams (there are study guides and online revision sessions helping you to review).

This is the worst organized college class I've ever taken. Unclear lectures and expectations, there are journal entries from different books that are due in class but other entries from other books due by email with no due dates just all due by a certain date and you can't submit more than one every 48 hours-yes it's as confusing as it sounds.

comment: Terrible, boring lectures. The class is way too hard for what the class should be.
Hilarious is the descriptor that would best work for describing the man's talent at interrupting himself and other students from talking. He repeats and drones on with filler words "um" and "like".

He assigns a lot of reading, yet he never goes over the material in class. He would much rather discuss topics that aren't in the reading. Jon doesn't make himself available and left Rochester before he assigned an exam. This class has so much potential to be better than it presently is and the University should revisit the topic of keeping him.

Jon generally doesn't understand how to teach. He seems like a nice enough professor, however, he goes off on unwanted tangents and never explicitly addresses what he expects from you. It seem as though he doesn't even value his own thoughts on subjects, as his tests are open note and will mark your answers wrong for repeating concepts he taught.

He gives notes for almost every class and specific study guides before every exam. He always makes himself available after classes. Even if you are not in this class, he is happy to talk to you about some topics interesting. His feedback is clear and useful. And the grade is fair.

"Umm uhhh." -  Professor Tresan. He's a great guy and cares deeply for philosophy but his class is extremely unorganized. I really appreciate him as a professor and you can tell he's very good at viewing things from a different view. The tests are difficult but its possible to earn an A if you work for it. I'd take him once if you have the chance.
I wouldn't take a class with him again. Likes to hear himself talk, his study guides and reviews are just endless thoughts he writes down but never gets to the point.
Great guy- very helpful outside of class but lectures are extremely unorganized and hard to follow. Hard to keep up with the material if you do not attend class regularly.

He's undeniably a little eccentric (as many philosophy professors are) but he definitely grows on you when you get to know him better - I particularly recommend meeting with him one-on-one - he has a lot if interesting perspectives and insights.

He may not deliver his thoughts clear to every student and he could be hard to follow some times, but the lecture material he put in the study guide is logical, clear, and easy to understand. He is super helpful. Definitely talk to him about your thoughts or ideas. He will provide you a lot of related materials to enrich your view.
Do NOT do this to yourself. "Right, um, okay, yeah" and study guides the night before that are as unclear as he is. Terrible experience. Just. No.

Loves to hear himself talk - half of every lecture is nothing more than him walking back and forth, muttering "Right, hmmmmm..." over and over again. Makes you take a midterm the day after spring break ends and often times fails to reason properly. Pretentious, and obviously thinks he's brilliant, even though his doctorate is in a humanities.

He is all over the place, super unorganized, really laid back, is interesting though, kinda makes we want to keep attending just to see what he will do. I kinda like him, as a person but not so much as a professor.  Seems really smart though and is super nice.

Professor Terlazzo is my favorite professor I have ever had. She is extremely well informed in all of her subjects she teaches, she is easily reached, connected and kind. Grading can be tough depending on TAs but go to office hours to discuss paper outlines and you will do more than fine.  Highly recommend any and all courses with Rosa.

She is inspiring, clearheaded & has a straight-to-the-point attitude. If you review the syllabus, & plan accordingly, you will pass the class. Weekly readings are very quick to become tiresome, as she assigns two professional-level philosophy readings per week, and corresponding required responses; however, thoroughness is not required for these.

PHIL223 was a challenging philosophy course but hugely rewarding. Marking is tough but entirely fair. Lots of readings as well. You'll learn a lot from doing all of it, however, and she is immensely knowledgeable, thoughtful and articulate. One of the best profs I've had in uni and one of the best classes I've taken.

shes very nice, HOLY READINGS, new reading for every class and most were 10+ pages. classes are spent going over and conversing about the paper that was due before it. must annotate readings online and is graded. end of the year group presentations, you pick which topic you want but are randomly put into groups, would take again
Rosa is an incredible teacher! Very down to earth and approachable. The class itself was reading heavy, but easy to understand if you made an effort to attend class.

disclaimer: for PSCI 293, not PHIL 226
Rosa is the kindest, most well-educated and empathetic human being; engaging and insightful professor who truly cares about her students. 11/10
LOTS of reading and in-depth class discussion about them, def go to class bc it helps a lot with the 3 take home essays (only 2 pages and thats the hardest part)

I had Professor Terlazzo for Phil 226 and she did a brilliant job. She never failed to make students feel welcome to share even if they were way off base with their response. She's a great professor, so much so that I took another one of her classes because she was teaching it (and for credit too, but she's a benefit of that course)

Really great lectures and insightful connections of how the content she teaches connects to the real world. The readings are difficult and can take a bit of effort to understand. But the grading is fair and as long as you understand what's being discussed in class, you should do fine on the exams. Take the class!

comment: Rosa is amazing! I wish every class was structured like Philosophy of Law. She is genuinely caring about the students, provides so many opportunities to engage with the course content both in and outside of lectures, and she is very knowledgeable about her subject. Unlike most philosophy profs, Rosa always connects theory to reality.

Some of the texts are challenging, but the program she uses makes it easier to understand since you can access other students' comments on the reading. She's very accessible and easy to talk to, so I never felt bad asking for help. If you're curious, definitely sit in on a lecture or two.
tags: ['Gives good feedback', 'Accessible outside class', 'Get ready to read']

comment: Rosa was amazing at explaining all the concepts in the readings, and really broke everything down to make it super clear. She padded the grades a lot with easy completion grades for the reading and gave extra credit, and the papers weren't graded too harshly. Highly recommend!!
tags: ['Get ready to read', 'Participation matters', 'Clear grading criteria']

comment: Professor Terlazzo is a good soul. She is so kind, non-judgmental, and asks thoughtful questions. Loves to make the students do the philosophy instead of lecturing at us. Make sure you show up, participate, and do the readings. Amazing course and professor - one of the best at UofR.

Such a horrible/difficult class to take. Nothing against Prof Terlazzo tho, she seems like a perfectly nice lady. But the class requires huge amounts of hours of reading and the TA who grades the exam is sooooo harsh. Make me wanna hang myself. Honestly, this is way too much work. Dont choose this class for ur own sake, unless you LOVE philosophy.

Rosa was very understanding and easy on students, especially during the pandemic. Did not demand a whole lot. Used a program that allowed us to discuss philosophical readings with other students, which helped me because some readings were hard for me to understand. Willing to add extensions, and is usually available for help.

If you draw a Venn diagram of someone who is smart and someone who is nice, there's really no much overlap. But Professor Terlazzo is definitely in the overlap. She was very supportive under this online circumstance--genuinely cared about students' mental well-being. She always came super prepared for class and respected students' opinions.

comment: She exaggerates her lack of knowledge in the field. Whenever someone asked simple questions in class regarding the material, she froze, gave a confusing answer, then emailed me later giving me an answer from Wikipedia. Her tests are terribly worded and she refuses to admit she is wrong. The TA at the time was awful! DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HER!

She clearly is new and her skills as a teacher shows it. Her lectures are disorganized, her explanations are poor at best, she can't admit when she's wrong, she doesn't give exams back neither does she explain why answers are wrong. Going to her office hours is useless, and the TA at the time didnt even understand the material well enough to teach.

I enjoy interacting with Dr. Kline out of class, but in class, it's very clear that she's a brand new professor. Powerpoints, exams, and assignments are badly made, and she holds an attitude towards her teaching and course that feels unnecessary and unprofessional. In talking with her outside, I must reiterate that she is a wonderful person!

Really nice person, but kind of a mess as a professor. She is often late for class and always seems a bit unprepared and flustered. Definitely has trouble commanding attention of a big lecture class, so I feel like she would do better in a smaller class setting. Lots of errors on tests, and sometimes really confusing examples in class.

The content of 281 is minimal, and paying $2k+ for it would be a total scam if not for HA's amazing lectures. He really tries to teach the intuition! But 281 is a rough class... The projects are obscurely graded and impossible to complete well without seeing the TAs. Fourier methods are all it covers. But again, HA does a great and caring job!

Professor Aluie is one of the best professors that I have had in my entire college career. The way that he teaches truly builds an intuition for math. Rather than simply telling you how to solve problems, Professor Aluie teaches you how to think through the problems. But make sure to ATTEND LECTURE, otherwise, you will get nothing out of the class.

I would like to throw shade at other reviewers who suggest that the course is incoherent: it isn't. Lecture attendance (or recordings) and note-taking are essential in this course (as in other conceptually higher-level courses), and homework follows directly from it if you're paying attention to the elegant explanations. He clearly knows his stuff.

His courses are not organized at all, and he won't even be there for lectures sometimes. Although he doesn't have any finals, his course is not easy to get an A because 95 is an A. What's more, his homework has nothing to do with his class, toooooo hard. He also has three term projects which is also not organized, and not enough instructions.

You can tell he is incredibly smart, but not in a way where he doesn't know how to explain things in simple terms. One of the best lecturers I have ever had. There aren't any exams which is nice but weekly homeworks and 3 group projects. Give lots of time for the projects because they are sometimes not that clear what to do so you may need to ask

Prof Aluie is great with his lectures, hard class! As long as you understand his lectures, you should be able to do the homework, no exams. Projects are rough but I did not have any CS background. It would be very helpful to know some coding. If you need extensions, better to ask him in person! He recognizes where you sit if you go to class often.
I really enjoyed the lectures and found them very stimulating. I've never had a professor who could answer complicated questions so quickly and in such an intuitive way.

Prof. Aluie is very knowledgable and very willing to help students. The subject material itself is difficult with long tedious homeworks and grueling group projects, but Prof. Aluie knows this and gives students plenty of time to tackle these. Do not procrastinate, and reach out for help, and he will be amazing.

He's a pretty good lecturer and explains concepts well. Homework and exams are challenging for sure but the lecture material is directly relevant, plus- Aluie is the nicest person and incredibly helpful in office hours!
Homeworks and tests are difficult, but the class and concepts are taught well.

Professor Aluie is exciting and full of energy. He always has useful ideas and made connections between math and physics. He is also very friendly. Sometimes I could guess he did not prepare well but I always enjoyed his lectures. I think this was the first time he teached this course.
An awesome Professor, passionate and very friendly. He has a strong understanding of the course and tried hard to make us understand what he was teaching. He is good at explaining difficult concepts.

I worked hard for this class but I liked it the most. Lectures are great even though they are at 9am :( Perfect teacher for this class. Tries to guess the answer before solving the math which is very helpful. Jumps a lot between big picture and small details. Good balance between theory and examples.

comment: Difficult but manageable class. The textbook is very helpful but the exams reference many in-class examples and demonstrations he does, so it's important to go to class. He's very helpful one and one (more so than in lecture) and definitely rewards effort and initative.

comment: Great guy! values intuition, shows demos and exams are fair. MCQ's makes you think and are tricky but are identical to practice exams except for subtle differences. It's good that he uses the textbook for notes because you don't have to spend much time reading it. If you are a Physics major, probably one of the easiest PHY classes out there.
+1 Truther here. Average class at best, lectures straight from the book, certainly not as great as the reviews say. The book was really good thankfully.
By far the best professor I ever had in all of my courses. He is so cool and gives very interesting examples from the real world.
Good lecturer, very intelligent guy, for my personal learning more examples and less derivation would have been helpful. Would have been nice if tests were curved slightly.
Good Professor,  very helpful but expects quite a bit from his students.
great guy!!!!!
Professor Aluie is by far one of the best professors I have met in college. He is one of the smartest people I have met he is a good person and he is HOT!!!
One of the best professors I had. He values intuition and is tough but fair.
He is an awesome professor. He really cares about the students and his lectures are fun a lot of the time.
His tests are very different than most professors. It really tests you if you can apply the material to real life and articles.

comment: Best professor of the MBA, I learned a lot he is an amazing human being who cares about you learning the reality of the Canadian market, he even helped to improve my resume, I would 1000%. HRMT has bad reputation but he made it so easy that I would totally repeat again.

Too bad he's currently full time at RIT, it's really our loss. F I guess this page has no use anymore. Bobby if you're reading this, come home!! Your lectures were the golden days. 1/2 the class was restarting the Apache server and all nighters but I think that was my fault. You always called out front row dorks for their pointless questions.
Amazing teacher. Great lectures. Chill dude.
He was an amazing professor. Loved his lecture, tons of examples. He did make the class harder than it had been in previous years but we were prepared for it.

Great lecturer, clear grading criteria and awesome powerpoints. The projects he gave us were a little bit challenging but I had so much fun working on them. You can really learn a lot from him. Strongly recommend!!!
Had him for the one semester he taught this class and it was awesome. Really nice guy that gives good lectures.

The Prof is very engaging in lectures and enthusiastic about the content. I've taken multiple courses with her, and every class was fun and had a comfortable environment. The courses can be a bit content (reading&film) heavy at times, but Prof Rosenow is very understanding and open to extensions as long as she has a forewarning.

James cares about her students. Sometimes expects students to do lots of reading and watch several movies in a week for her comics class particularly. She's very loose with projects/presentations/papers which are easy to do well in. Participation is a large part of the final grade. She's very knowledgable and passionate about the field.

One of the few college courses where the professor genuinely treats you like an equal and not only respects, but actively encourages joining into a discussion and sharing your perspective on things. You can clearly tell that she knows so much about what she's talking about and her enthusiasm is fantastic!
James Rosenow is god-tier. I love her. Best lecturer at UR.

Professor was nice and accessible for the most part, clearly knew what she was talking about but the class was incredibly disorganized. I have little to no complaints about the professor herself, but the way she organized the class was one of the worst things I've seen at my time at UofR.

I've greatly enjoyed both classes I took with Professor Rosenow. While young, she's clearly very experienced and knowledgeable about film. She wants all of her students to share in her passion and conveys so through her lectures. My only gripes would be ambiguity around assignments though she's far from a tough grader so it doesn't matter much.

Ok i found it really annoying how there were pop quizzes so you absolutely had to show up to every class. Wasn't fond of his teaching style, his final exam had 19 multiple choice questions so your grade can easily fall down to a B with just a few questions wrong on the exam. Couple of hw assignments nothing too bad.
Great professor. Even if you do not enjoy finance or if it is your first time studying, he makes it seem easy.
Great class, great guy. Would recommend.
He could teach a class on 100 ways to tie your shoe and I'd take it.
Great guy, easy class, show up and you'll be good

Prof. Jordan is clearly extremely intelligent, and as is often the case, this makes understanding him at time difficult. I think Jordan would help society more if he was completely be dedicated to research. The lectures varied in their difficulty; some I loved, some I hated (from frustration and being lost).

Jordan rarely explained topics in a way that was clear to those who had never taken Physics. The class was not meant as a class for physics majors, but rather was full of mostly students in other disciplines who were required to take it. He was unclear, and would focus on discussing the theoretical aspects of the problems, instead of how to do them

Not a good professor at all. His lectures are really confusing and the math he uses is well beyond the scope of the course. You 100% need to read the book to learn anything. The HW assignments are long and tedious. 1st midterm was easy, 2nd was challenging but fair, the final exam was RIDICULOUSLY HARD and very unfair. Pray for a good workshop TA.
His instruction will leave you confused. His tests will leave you angry. Avoid at all costs.

Be prepared for long grueling homework assignments. Oh and the TA's will grade at most 2 problems of the 20 asked to turn in. So if you mess up only 2 questions on the 20 question assignment and they only grade those 2 questions you get a 0, for literally hours of work.

Jordan isn't that bad. He only uses variables in lecture so that can be hard to get used to, but it really does help in the end if you put in the effort to follow it. Physics is just a tough subject, there's not going to be an easy way to teach it. You really have to change your way of thinking to be successful. Try to really learn the CONCEPTS.

He seems like a nice guy but I think 90% of the class would appreciate it if he "came down to our level" a few times per lecture instead of zooming through so much material and examples on the board. Get a tutor.

Not the greatest at making lecture interesting though he does have his moments. Does a lot of derivations in class that are not necessary for passing the class. I definitely suggest knowing the homework very well, tests are heavily based on them
A smart guy, but feels the need to derive and integrate everything. Take this course if you like the greek alphabet, as you will be seeing a lot of it.

Prof Jordan is a terrible teacher. He may be good at physics but he can't convey his understanding to students at all. Going to class was useless as well as the book. His tests were mostly unfair and difficult.
I took AP Mechanics in high school, so the class hasn't pushed me too hard. I've done pretty well. Other students with little previous physics experience tend to struggle, though.

Professor Jordan thinks that everyone is a calculus super star and that we all scored 5's on our AP exams. His lectures are extremely boring and his tests are ridiculous. He likes to say they're possible maybe because he's the professor. If at all possible stay away.

Jordan is one of the worst professors here. I understand physics is a challenging subject, but this guy can't teach it to save his life. If more then a 3rd of the class continually fails, then it's HIS fault! We study hard! He might possibly be worse then the intro to French professor here, Madame Lutkus. Both need to be fired. NOW!
awful class. very difficult, no review in or outside of class. goes quickly and assumes everyone is a calc genius. class did not help me or my gpa. lab is awful as well & is included in your grade.

I survived, this guy is tough and his lectures are almost useless, spends the a lot of time deriving formulas but no time on how to use them.  Real world examples are nice though.  Though when I started studying for MCAT's wow he did a better job than I thought.  Still tough though.
blamed us when the whole class didn't do well on a test
Jordan was not very clear and quite boring.  I consider him to be the worst professor I had during my freshman year.  Would not recommend taking a class with him.

This professor needs to improve his teaching skills and make the class more interesting in a way where the students understand the work and also have fun. More than half the class has failed both of his exams, and he's not to blame???

AVOID AT ALL COST!! lectures are useless! homework is differernt from lectures and the exams are 100% different than the lectures and homework!!...dont even ask about workshops.......He is without a doubt the worst professor I have ever had. Do your GPA a favor and dont take Jordan!! ...take it over the summer if u had to

His first midterm wasnt extremely hard but the second one was off the charts crappy. 45% is not a good average. He said something along the lines of "I can't believe you did so poorly when I gave you all spring break to do your homework and study." in regards to our lack of knowledge on a certain type of problem. Avoid him if possible  for you gpa.

Jordan is the most arrogant person I have ever met. He knows physics well but is horrible at teaching it and doesn't listen to students at all when they make suggestions or complain. The average grade on our last test was 47.5 and he told us that we clearly weren't studying enough. Never take a class with him if you can avoid it.

The material is simple but very engaging. Prof. Pazda uses great examples to explain his material and although class isn't mandatory it's fun to attend anyways.  He's a great guy.  As long as you read as well as review the slides from class, you should be okay test-wise.
This class is pretty easy as long as you go to class and then study by going through the powerpoint lectures. The material is straight-forward and I never needed to use the book.
Really awesome professor!:)  Super sweet
Interesting lectures and very good at explaining material. Tests were fairly simple with a lot of multiple choice.
Great Class.  Professor is very clear with his lectures and exams.  Can be dull at times, but his examples and stories are great.
He's an amazing professor. Class isn't necessary but very interesting, he uses great examples to explain material. The exams are simple but you do need to read the textbook for a few questions.
He is really willing to help you with your questions and grades !!! And there are many ways to get extra credits!

I took this class my freshman year and it was my favorite class of the year, mainly because of him. The material taught is pretty easy and the tests are usually multiple choice questions and short answers but you need to know all the stuff to score well in  his class.
I have no clue why he's rated so low. The class was structured well, he taught coherently and assignments were graded fairly. He's a very nice person.

comment: Randall Curren's philosophy classes were unbearable. His lectures were consistently biased, prioritizing his own viewpoints over balanced discussion. Rather than teaching critical thinking, he preferred hearing himself speak, shutting down any real debate. Avoid his courses if you actually want to learn philosophy.

I don't understand the grading system and he absolutely has no business assigning such low of grades for this class. He is stuck to his ways and is willing to debate anything BUT his grading system...

Way too much work for an ECE core course. Two presentations a week, random group calls—so you always have to prep. Spent more time on this than on my ECE core classes. Tough grading, trash course, trash prof. He doesn't care about your opinions at all. WORST COURSE FOREVER

manditory in the sense that you had to go there to be prepared for this useless debates. not in the sense that the lecture was. graded exams so harshly that U barely got points. main thing is that you learn NOTHING. like we all know this stuff is wrong. graded my reports all wrong. took all points off. He is a SHA BI

The trashest course ever manditory for ECE. Gave me a C, had three big tests, and useless non-stop debates on those useless Engineering Ethics stories. Why would you have us debate on something that had no opposite sides. Like we all agree with the stories on one side. There were no arguments to be made. Talked non stop. Harsh grading on everything

PHIL120 shouldn't be mandatory for ECE majors. The case studies are general engineering, not ECE-specific. If required, it should be for all engineering students. The 4-credit load is too much—I'd rather focus on senior design. The workload is heavy with exams, presentations, and strict grading. Feels like a waste of time.

Dr. Curren is a very kind professor who is quite passionate about what he teaches. While his lectures can be boring at times, I found his tangents as incredibly interesting and surprisingly funny. He truly cares about his students actually LEARNING and is willing to put this over the letter grade you receive.

comment: I found his lectures extremely hard to follow, he tended to ramble and didn't make it clear what was actual material and what was fluff. We had a guest lecturer for one week and it was the only time I felt clear on the material, and his review sessions were pretty much useless. It made it very difficult to study for the final exam

Curren is a very nice person. However, classes are mind-numbingly boring, so much that I needed to chug an energy drink before class to stay awake. He has no slide shows so if you don't go to class/aren't paying attention, ur screwed. I took this as an elective and it was my biggest mistake of that semester. Can't not recommend this class enough.

Prof Curren is really cute like gives Bernie Sanders, but he is not a phenomenal professor. comment: Curren included quality readings, excluding his own writings, throughout the course, but it was a shame we never really got the chance to talk about them. Professor Curren frequently goes on topics that are tangential to the readings we have due in class and assumes that we haven't read them. He's very narcissistic and this slows his class down.

Professor Curren frequently interrupts students. This causes students to retreat inward and discontinue discussion. Curren personifies the Professor that doesn't care about the opinions of his students; instead, he blatantly disregards the views we have that differ from his own.

This course is about the ethics of technology and the amount of information that Curren lacks on technology is quite staggering. It's amazing that the University of Rochester hasn't replaced him with someone more knowledgeable about the subjects discussed within the course. Overall, I would strongly recommend staying away from this course and him.

I feel sorry for him. I guess he over invested his resources into the wrong field and is now trying to compensate for his many shortcomings. To cite a few examples, he, often, highlights his own personal life, his travels, and his leftist views on many subjects. There're some good articles included, however, these are ignored.
